Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company collects data for temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure in cities across multiple continents. The average volume of data that the company collects from each site daily is 500 GB.

Each site has a high-speed Internet connection. The company wants to aggregate the data from all these global sites as quickly as possible in a single Amazon S3 bucket.

The solution must minimize operational complexity.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration on the destination S3 bucket. Use multipart uploads to directly upload site data to the destination S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses AWS edge locations to accelerate uploads into a single S3 bucket from globally distributed sites. Multipart upload is appropriate for very large objects and keeps the design operationally simple.

choices.solution:
Upload the data from each site to an S3 bucket in the closest Region. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy objects to the destination S3 bucket.

Then remove the data from the origin S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Regional staging buckets add replication configuration, intermediate storage, and cleanup. That is more operational work than uploading directly to the destination bucket with Transfer Acceleration.

choices.solution: Schedule AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device jobs daily to transfer data from each site to the closest Region. Use S3 Cross- Region Replication to copy objects to the destination S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Physical devices must be ordered, loaded, and shipped. Daily device jobs add logistical delays and operational work despite the sites already having high-speed internet connections.

choices.solution:
Upload the data from each site to an Amazon EC2 instance in the closest Region. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume.

At regular intervals, take an EBS snapshot and copy it to the Region that contains the destination S3 bucket. Restore the EBS volume in that Region.
choices.explanation: EBS snapshots restore block volumes, not objects in the destination S3 bucket. This also adds EC2 management, snapshot copying, and another transfer step before the data reaches S3.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company wants to improve its ability to clone large amounts of production data into a test environment in the same AWS Region. The data is stored in Amazon EC2 instances on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.

Modifications to the cloned data must not affect the production environment. The software that accesses this data requires consistently high I/O performance.

A solutions architect needs to minimize the time that is required to clone the production data into the test environment.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Restore the snapshots onto EC2 instance store volumes in the test environment.
choices.explanation: EBS snapshots restore to EBS volumes, not directly to EC2 instance-store volumes. Copying restored data into instance store would add a separate transfer and initialization step.

choices.solution:
Configure the production EBS volumes to use the EBS Multi-Attach feature. Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes.

Attach the production EBS volumes to the EC2 instances in the test environment.
choices.explanation: Multi-Attach exposes the same production volume to multiple instances. Test writes could therefore alter production data, directly violating the isolation requirement.

choices.solution:
Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Create and initialize new EBS volumes.

Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment before restoring the volumes from the production EBS snapshots.
choices.explanation: A volume is created from a snapshot; there is no subsequent in-place snapshot restore into an already created and attached blank volume. Manually reading restored blocks also takes time that fast snapshot restore avoids.

choices.solution:
Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Turn on the EBS fast snapshot restore feature on the EBS snapshots.

Restore the snapshots into new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment.
choices.explanation: EBS Fast Snapshot Restore creates volumes from snapshots that are fully initialized at creation, eliminating first-read latency and immediately delivering provisioned performance. That directly matches the need to clone data quickly while keeping production and test volumes independent.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A development team runs monthly resource-intensive tests on its general purpose Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with Performance Insights enabled. The testing lasts for 48 hours once a month and is the only process that uses the database.

The team wants to reduce the cost of running the tests without reducing the compute and memory attributes of the DB instance.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Stop the DB instance when tests are completed. Restart the DB instance when required.
choices.explanation: A stopped RDS DB instance automatically restarts after seven days. With tests occurring only once a month, it would resume incurring compute charges well before the next test.

choices.solution: Use an Auto Scaling policy with the DB instance to automatically scale when tests are completed.
choices.explanation: RDS for MySQL does not offer the proposed policy that automatically shuts down or scales the instance for this test schedule. Ordinary RDS storage autoscaling does not remove idle DB-instance compute charges.

choices.solution: Create a snapshot when tests are completed. Terminate the DB instance and restore the snapshot when required.
choices.explanation:
RDS automatically restarts a stopped instance after seven days, so stopping alone does not avoid compute charges for the entire month. Keep a manual snapshot, delete the instance after testing, and restore it before the next run.

Snapshot storage and restore time still apply.

choices.solution: Modify the DB instance to a low-capacity instance when tests are completed. Modify the DB instance again when required.
choices.explanation: A smaller instance still incurs compute charges throughout the idle period. Snapshotting and deleting the unused instance avoids those idle compute charges while restoring the required instance size for the next test.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company recently launched a variety of new workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in its AWS account. The company needs to create a strategy to access and administer the instances remotely and securely.

The company needs to implement a repeatable process that works with native AWS services and follows the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use the EC2 serial console to directly access the terminal interface of each instance for administration.
choices.explanation: The serial console is primarily for troubleshooting boot and network problems. It is not the scalable, routine remote-administration workflow requested for all workloads.

choices.solution: Attach the appropriate IAM role to each existing instance and new instance. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to establish a remote SSH session.
choices.explanation:
With AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, you can manage your Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances, edge devices, on-premises servers, and virtual machines (VMs). You can use either an interactive one-click browser-based shell or the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

It provides secure and auditable node management without the need to open inbound ports, maintain bastion hosts, or manage SSH keys.

choices.solution:
Create an administrative SSH key pair. Load the public key into each EC2 instance.

Deploy a bastion host in a public subnet to provide a tunnel for administration of each instance.
choices.explanation: A bastion host requires patching, availability management, network access rules, and SSH-key distribution. Session Manager avoids that additional host and key-management infrastructure.

choices.solution: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Instruct administrators to use their local on-premises machines to connect directly to the instances by using SSH keys across the VPN tunnel.
choices.explanation: A VPN introduces network provisioning and SSH-key administration. It can provide connectivity, but requires more operational setup than managed sessions authorized through instance IAM roles.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is hosting a static website on Amazon S3 and is using Amazon Route 53 for DNS. The website is experiencing increased demand from around the world.

The company must decrease latency for users who access the website.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Replicate the S3 bucket that contains the website to all AWS Regions. Add Route 53 geolocation routing entries.
choices.explanation: Replicating the entire site to every Region creates extra copies and routing administration. Geolocation selects a regional origin but does not provide CloudFront's distributed edge cache.

choices.solution:
Provision accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator. Associate the supplied IP addresses with the S3 bucket.

Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the IP addresses of the accelerators.
choices.explanation: S3 buckets are not supported Global Accelerator endpoints, so the proposed accelerator cannot target the website bucket.

choices.solution: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the CloudFront distribution.
choices.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) service that distributes content globally to reduce latency. By setting up a CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket hosting the static website, you can take advantage of its edge locations around the world to deliver content from the nearest location to the users, reducing the latency they experience.

CloudFront automatically caches and replicates content to its edge locations, resulting in faster delivery and lower latency for users worldwide. This solution is highly effective in optimizing performance while keeping costs under control because CloudFront charges are based on actual data transfer and requests, and the pay-as-you-go pricing model ensures that you only pay for what you use.

choices.solution: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the new endpoint.
choices.explanation: Transfer Acceleration is for accelerated S3 object transfers, not a website CDN that caches content near visitors. An S3 static website cannot simply be replaced with an accelerated website endpoint.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company maintains a searchable repository of items on its website. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database table that contains more than 10 million rows.

The database has 2 TB of General Purpose SSD storage. There are millions of updates against this data every day through the company's website.

The company has noticed that some insert operations are taking 10 seconds or longer. The company has determined that the database storage performance is the problem.

Which solution addresses this performance issue?

choices.solution: Change the storage type to Provisioned IOPS SSD.
choices.explanation:
Using Amazon Provisioned IOPS (PIOPS) SSD storage is the best way to solve the performance issue of insert operations taking 10 seconds or longer on an Amazon RDS for MySQL database table with more than 10 million rows and 2 TB of General Purpose SSD storage. A high-performance storage solution with reliable throughput and minimal latency is PIOPS SSD storage.

Workloads like insert operations, which demand high I/O performance, are ideally suited for it.

choices.solution: Change the DB instance to a memory optimized instance class.
choices.explanation: The diagnosed bottleneck is storage I/O, not memory capacity. A memory-optimized instance does not directly provision the required disk IOPS.

choices.solution: Change the DB instance to a burstable performance instance class.
choices.explanation: A burstable instance changes the CPU-capacity model, not the underlying storage performance. It does not address slow inserts caused by the storage bottleneck.

choices.solution: Enable Multi-AZ RDS read replicas with MySQL native asynchronous replication.
choices.explanation: Read replicas offload reads, but inserts still write to the primary database's storage. Replication does not directly increase the primary volume's IOPS.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has an on-premises application that generates a large amount of time-sensitive data that is backed up to Amazon S3. The application has grown and there are user complaints about internet bandwidth limitations.

A solutions architect needs to design a long-term solution that allows for both timely backups to Amazon S3 and with minimal impact on internet connectivity for internal users.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Establish AWS VPN connections and proxy all traffic through a VPC gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN uses the existing network path and does not remove the application's impact on internet bandwidth. S3 gateway endpoints also cannot be accessed directly from an on-premises VPN connection.

choices.solution: Establish a new AWS Direct Connect connection and direct backup traffic through this new connection.
choices.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect is a network service that allows you to establish a dedicated network connection from your on-premises data center to AWS. This connection bypasses the public Internet and can provide more reliable, lower-latency communication between your on-premises application and Amazon S3.

By directing backup traffic through the AWS Direct Connect connection, you can minimize the impact on your internet bandwidth and ensure timely backups to S3.

choices.solution: Order daily AWS Snowball devices. Load the data onto the Snowball devices and return the devices to AWS each day.
choices.explanation: Physical device delivery and return shipping introduce delays that are unsuitable for a recurring, time-sensitive backup stream. A dedicated connection supplies continuous transfer capacity.

choices.solution: Submit a support ticket through the AWS Management Console. Request the removal of S3 service limits from the account.
choices.explanation: The bottleneck is the company's internet connection, not an S3 account service limit. Changing an S3 quota cannot increase the on-premises network's available bandwidth.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company's website uses an Amazon EC2 instance store for its catalog of items. The company wants to make sure that the catalog is highly available and that the catalog is stored in a durable location.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Move the catalog to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
choices.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis is designed as an in-memory data store and cache. This option does not specify the persistence and replica configuration needed to make the catalog a durable, highly available primary store.

choices.solution: Deploy a larger EC2 instance with a larger instance store.
choices.explanation: A larger instance store is still temporary storage tied to the instance. Its data can be lost when the instance is stopped or terminated, so increasing its size does not provide durability.

choices.solution: Move the catalog from the instance store to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: Deep Archive requires an asynchronous restore before objects can be read. That retrieval delay makes it unsuitable for a live website catalog that must remain readily available.

choices.solution: Move the catalog to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
choices.explanation: EFS is fully managed, durable, highly available, and shared file system.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate its on-premises application to AWS. The application produces output files that vary in size from tens of gigabytes to hundreds of terabytes.

The application data must be stored in a standard file system structure. The company wants a solution that scales automatically. is highly available, and requires minimum operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon S3 for storage.
choices.explanation: S3 exposes objects rather than the standard mounted filesystem required here.

choices.solution: Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.
choices.explanation: EBS volumes are AZ-scoped and need capacity management; EKS adds cluster administration.

choices.solution: Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for storage.
choices.explanation: Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling replaces failed instances and adjusts capacity. EFS supplies shared file storage that remains accessible to instances in different Availability Zones.

choices.solution: Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.
choices.explanation: EBS is AZ-scoped block storage, not an automatically growing shared multi-AZ filesystem.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is running a popular social media website. The website gives users the ability to upload images to share with other users.

The company wants to make sure that the images do not contain inappropriate content. The company needs a solution that minimizes development effort.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
choices.explanation: Comprehend analyzes text, not uploaded images for visual moderation.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Rekognition to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
choices.explanation: Rekognition moderation detects potentially inappropriate image or video content. Route uncertain results for human review rather than assuming every low-confidence detection is definitive.

choices.solution: Use Amazon SageMaker to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
choices.explanation: Training and maintaining a custom SageMaker model requires more development than managed Rekognition moderation.

choices.solution: Use AWS Fargate to deploy a custom machine learning model to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
choices.explanation: A custom model on Fargate adds development, training, deployment, and container-operation responsibilities.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company wants to run its critical applications in containers to meet requirements for scalability and availability. The company prefers to focus on maintenance of the critical applications.

The company does not want to be responsible for provisioning and managing the underlying infrastructure that runs the containerized workload.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon EC2 instances, and install Docker on the instances.
choices.explanation: Installing Docker on EC2 still leaves server provisioning, patching, and capacity management to the company.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
choices.explanation: ECS manages orchestration but EC2 worker hosts still require infrastructure management.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
choices.explanation: Fargate runs ECS containers without provisioning or patching EC2 hosts, reducing operational work while preserving the container packaging.

choices.solution: Use Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)-optimized Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
choices.explanation: An optimized AMI simplifies setup but does not remove EC2 host-management responsibilities.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has more than 5 TB of file data on Windows file servers that run on premises. Users and applications interact with the data each day.

The company is moving its Windows workloads to AWS. As the company continues this process, the company requires access to AWS and on- premises file storage with minimum latency.

The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead and requires no significant changes to the existing file access patterns. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection for connectivity to AWS.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Move the on-premises file data to FSx for Windows File Server.

Reconfigure the workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS.
choices.explanation: On-premises users read across the VPN without a local cache, increasing access latency.

choices.solution:
Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the S3 File Gateway.

Reconfigure the on- premises workloads and the cloud workloads to use the S3 File Gateway.
choices.explanation: Cloud workloads would access an on-premises gateway across the VPN instead of their local AWS filesystem.

choices.solution:
Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to Amazon S3.

Reconfigure the workloads to use either Amazon S3 directly or the S3 File Gateway. depending on each workload's location.
choices.explanation: Direct S3 access changes Windows SMB access patterns instead of preserving the filesystem interface.

choices.solution:
Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Deploy and configure an Amazon FSx File Gateway on premises.

Move the on-premises file data to the FSx File Gateway. Configure the cloud workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS.

Configure the on- premises workloads to use the FSx File Gateway.
choices.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides cloud SMB storage, and FSx File Gateway historically provided local caching for on-premises clients. FSx File Gateway has been unavailable to new customers since October 28, 2024; this choice applies only to eligible existing customers.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing a new hybrid architecture to extend a company's on-premises infrastructure to AWS. The company requires a highly available connection with consistent low latency to an AWS Region.

The company needs to minimize costs and is willing to accept slower traffic if the primary connection fails.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a VPN connection as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
choices.explanation: Direct Connect provides the primary dedicated path with consistent network performance. A Site-to-Site VPN supplies a cheaper backup path over the internet if that connection fails.

choices.solution: Provision a VPN tunnel connection to a Region for private connectivity. Provision a second VPN tunnel for private connectivity and as a backup if the primary VPN connection fails.
choices.explanation: VPN traffic traverses the internet and cannot provide Direct Connect's consistent primary-path latency.

choices.solution: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a second Direct Connect connection to the same Region as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
choices.explanation: A second dedicated connection costs more than the slower VPN backup the company accepts.

choices.solution: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Use the Direct Connect failover attribute from the AWS CLI to automatically create a backup connection if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
choices.explanation: Direct Connect has no CLI failover attribute that automatically provisions a physical backup connection.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company receives 10 TB of instrumentation data each day from several machines located at a single factory. The data consists of JSON files stored on a storage area network (SAN) in an on-premises data center located within the factory.

The company wants to send this data to Amazon S3 where it can be accessed by several additional systems that provide critical near-real-time analytics. A secure transfer is important because the data is considered sensitive.

Which solution offers the MOST reliable data transfer?

choices.solution: AWS DataSync over public internet
choices.explanation: Public-internet transfer remains subject to the bandwidth variability affecting this sustained 10 TB daily flow.

choices.solution: AWS DataSync over AWS Direct Connect
choices.explanation: DataSync automates validated, encrypted data transfer, while Direct Connect provides a dedicated network path. Direct Connect alone does not encrypt traffic, but DataSync uses TLS.

choices.solution: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over public internet
choices.explanation: DMS migrates database data, not arbitrary JSON files stored on a SAN.

choices.solution: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over AWS Direct Connect
choices.explanation: Direct Connect improves transport but does not make DMS a SAN-file transfer service.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in an on-premises data center. The company needs the ability to use Lustre clients to access data.

The solution must be fully managed.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol.

Connect the application server to the file share.
choices.explanation: Storage Gateway shares use SMB or NFS, not the Lustre client protocol.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance.

Connect the application server to the file share.
choices.explanation: A self-managed Windows SMB server is neither managed Lustre storage nor protocol-compatible.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server.

Connect the application server to the file system.
choices.explanation: EFS supports NFS and cannot be configured as a Lustre filesystem.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server.

Connect the application server to the file system.
choices.explanation: FSx for Lustre provides a managed Lustre file system accessible to supported clients over private network connectivity from on premises.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A social media company allows users to upload images to its website. The website runs on Amazon EC2 instances.

During upload requests, the website resizes the images to a standard size and stores the resized images in Amazon S3. Users are experiencing slow upload requests to the website.

The company needs to reduce coupling within the application and improve website performance. A solutions architect must design the most operationally efficient process for image uploads.

Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Configure the application to upload images to S3 Glacier.
choices.explanation: Glacier archival storage requires retrieval before normal processing and is unsuitable for immediately resizing uploaded images.

choices.solution: Configure the web server to upload the original images to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Routing uploads through the web servers preserves the upload bottleneck instead of offloading transfers to S3.

choices.solution: Configure the application to upload images directly from each user's browser to Amazon S3 through the use of a presigned URL
choices.explanation: Presigned URLs let browsers upload original images directly to S3, removing upload traffic from the web servers.

choices.solution: Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when an image is uploaded. Use the function to resize the image.
choices.explanation: S3 object-created notifications invoke Lambda to resize images asynchronously, removing image processing from the upload request.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function on a schedule to resize uploaded images.
choices.explanation: Scheduled processing delays resizing and does not react immediately to each uploaded image.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company hosts a containerized web application on a fleet of on-premises servers that process incoming requests. The number of requests is growing quickly.

The on-premises servers cannot handle the increased number of requests. The company wants to move the application to AWS with minimum code changes and minimum development effort.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS Fargate on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run the containerized web application with Service Auto Scaling. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.
choices.explanation: ECS on Fargate runs the existing containers without host administration. ECS Service Auto Scaling adjusts tasks and the ALB distributes incoming requests.

choices.solution: Use two Amazon EC2 instances to host the containerized web application. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the incoming requests.
choices.explanation: A fixed pair of EC2 instances requires server management and does not automatically scale the container workload as demand grows.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Lambda with a new code that uses one of the supported languages. Create multiple Lambda functions to support the load.

Use Amazon API Gateway as an entry point to the Lambda functions.
choices.explanation: Migrating containers to Lambda requires adapting the application to the function execution model.

choices.solution: Use a high performance computing (HPC) solution such as AWS ParallelCluster to establish an HPC cluster that can process the incoming requests at the appropriate scale.
choices.explanation: An HPC configuration adds unnecessary infrastructure for ordinary application containers.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company uses 50 TB of data for reporting. The company wants to move this data from on premises to AWS.

A custom application in the company's data center runs a weekly data transformation job. The company plans to pause the application until the data transfer is complete and needs to begin the transfer process as soon as possible.

The data center does not have any available network bandwidth for additional workloads. A solutions architect must transfer the data and must configure the transformation job to continue to run in the AWS Cloud.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to move the data. Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.
choices.explanation: DataSync transfers data over a network connection; the available bandwidth cannot move this dataset quickly enough.

choices.solution: Order an AWS Snowcone device to move the data. Deploy the transformation application to the device.
choices.explanation: Snowcone has much less capacity than this 50-TB dataset and would require multiple devices and transfers.

choices.solution:
Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Copy the data to the device.

Create a custom transformation job by using AWS Glue.
choices.explanation:
Shipping the bulk data avoids the exhausted network connection. Glue supplies managed transformation after import.

Snowball Edge is now restricted to eligible existing customers; a new customer needs another physical-transfer option.

choices.solution:
Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device that includes Amazon EC2 compute. Copy the data to the device.

Create a new EC2 instance on AWS to run the transformation application.
choices.explanation: Running custom transformations on EC2 requires managing processing infrastructure; Glue provides the managed transformation workflow.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has created an image analysis application in which users can upload photos and add photo frames to their images. The users upload images and metadata to indicate which photo frames they want to add to their images.

The application uses a single Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon DynamoDB to store the metadata. The application is becoming more popular, and the number of users is increasing.

The company expects the number of concurrent users to vary significantly depending on the time of day and day of week. The company must ensure that the application can scale to meet the needs of the growing user base.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos and metadata in DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB items have a 400-KB size limit, making it unsuitable for storing arbitrary photo files directly.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to process the photos and to store the photos and metadata.
choices.explanation: Firehose delivers streaming records to destinations; it does not replace the required image-processing application and photo storage.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos in Amazon S3.

Retain DynamoDB to store the metadata.
choices.explanation: S3 is durable object storage for images, DynamoDB stores metadata, and Lambda scales image processing without maintaining application instances.

choices.solution: Increase the number of EC2 instances to three. Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to store the photos and metadata.
choices.explanation: A fixed EC2 fleet still requires server management and scaling, while attached EBS volumes do not provide a shared object store for the frames.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A media company is evaluating the possibility of moving its systems to the AWS Cloud. The company needs at least 10 TB of storage with the maximum possible I/O performance for video processing, 300 TB of very durable storage for storing media content, and 900 TB of storage to meet requirements for archival media that is not in use anymore.

Which set of services should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
choices.explanation: EBS uses network-attached storage; local instance store is the intended choice for the highest temporary video-processing I/O performance in this scenario.

choices.solution: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
choices.explanation: This selects network-attached EBS for temporary processing and pays for EFS file-system features when durable object storage is sufficient.

choices.solution: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 for archival storage
choices.explanation: EFS adds file-system cost for media objects, while S3 Standard is more expensive than archival storage for the unused archive.

choices.solution: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
choices.explanation:
Local instance-store storage suits high-I/O temporary video processing; select instances with at least the required local capacity. Use S3 for durable media and S3 Glacier storage classes for archives.

Instance-store data is ephemeral, so durable inputs and outputs must be stored elsewhere.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is running a multi-tier web application on premises. The web application is containerized and runs on a number of Linux hosts connected to a PostgreSQL database that contains user records.

The operational overhead of maintaining the infrastructure and capacity planning is limiting the company's growth. A solutions architect must improve the application's infrastructure.

Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to accomplish this? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora.
choices.explanation: Aurora PostgreSQL provides a managed PostgreSQL-compatible database with replication and failover, reducing database administration.

choices.solution: Migrate the web application to be hosted on Amazon EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Moving the containers onto EC2 retains server maintenance and capacity-planning responsibilities.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the web application content.
choices.explanation: CloudFront can improve content delivery but does not remove the container-host or database administration burden.

choices.solution: Set up Amazon ElastiCache between the web application and the PostgreSQL database.
choices.explanation: ElastiCache can reduce database reads but introduces another component and does not manage the existing servers or database.

choices.solution: Migrate the web application to be hosted on AWS Fargate with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
choices.explanation: ECS on Fargate runs and scales the existing Linux containers without managing EC2 hosts.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company recently started using Amazon Aurora as the data store for its global ecommerce application. When large reports are run, developers report that the ecommerce application is performing poorly.

After reviewing metrics in Amazon CloudWatch, a solutions architect finds that the ReadIOPS and CPUUtilization metrics are spiking when monthly reports run.

What is the MOST cost-effective solution?

choices.solution: Migrate the monthly reporting to Amazon Redshift.
choices.explanation: Redshift requires a separate warehouse and data-loading workflow when an Aurora reader can run the existing report queries directly.

choices.solution: Migrate the monthly reporting to an Aurora Replica.
choices.explanation: An Aurora Replica serves the reporting queries separately from the writer, reducing CPU and read load on the instance processing ecommerce transactions.

choices.solution: Migrate the Aurora database to a larger instance class.
choices.explanation: Increasing the writer's capacity costs more and leaves reporting CPU and read work competing with production transactions.

choices.solution: Increase the Provisioned IOPS on the Aurora instance.
choices.explanation: Aurora storage does not expose the proposed instance-level provisioned-IOPS adjustment, and extra storage IOPS would not isolate reporting CPU usage.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is migrating an application from on-premises servers to Amazon EC2 instances. As part of the migration design requirements, a solutions architect must implement infrastructure metric alarms.

The company does not need to take action if CPU utilization increases to more than 50% for a short burst of time. However, if the CPU utilization increases to more than 50% and read IOPS on the disk are high at the same time, the company needs to act as soon as possible.

The solutions architect also must reduce false alarms.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create Amazon CloudWatch composite alarms where possible.
choices.explanation: A CloudWatch composite alarm combines child alarm states with a Boolean rule, allowing notification only when CPU and memory conditions occur together. Memory metrics require an agent or custom publishing.

choices.solution: Create Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to visualize the metrics and react to issues quickly.
choices.explanation: A dashboard displays metrics but does not enforce the required condition that both alarms be in the alarm state.

choices.solution: Create Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to monitor the application and raise an alarm.
choices.explanation: Synthetics tests application behavior; it does not combine CPU and storage alarms into the specified condition.

choices.solution: Create single Amazon CloudWatch metric alarms with multiple metric thresholds where possible.
choices.explanation: Multiple thresholds on one metric do not combine the independent CPU and IOPS conditions.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company uses a three-tier web application to provide training to new employees. The application is accessed for only 12 hours every day.

The company is using an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance to store information and wants to minimize costs.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Configure an IAM policy for AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. Create an IAM role for the policy.

Update the trust relationship of the role. Set up automatic start and stop for the DB instance.
choices.explanation: Session Manager manages interactive access to instances; its trust policy does not create a schedule for starting and stopping RDS.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache cluster that gives users the ability to access the data from the cache when the DB instance is stopped. Invalidate the cache after the DB instance is started.
choices.explanation: An extra Redis cluster adds cost and does not provide a general replacement for the relational database while it is stopped.

choices.solution:
Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Create an IAM role that grants access to Amazon RDS.

Attach the role to the EC2 instance. Configure a cron job to start and stop the EC2 instance on the desired schedule.
choices.explanation: The cron job starts and stops the EC2 instance, not the RDS database whose costs must be reduced.

choices.solution:
Create AWS Lambda functions to start and stop the DB instance. Create Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled rules to invoke the Lambda functions.

Configure the Lambda functions as event targets for the rules.
choices.explanation: EventBridge schedules Lambda calls to stop and start the RDS instance during predictable idle periods. Stopped instances still incur storage charges and restart automatically after seven days.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A large media company hosts a web application on AWS. The company wants to start caching confidential media files so that users around the world will have reliable access to the files.

The content is stored in Amazon S3 buckets. The company must deliver the content quickly, regardless of where the requests originate geographically.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
choices.explanation: DataSync transfers datasets between storage locations; it does not provide an edge cache for global viewers.

choices.solution: Deploy AWS Global Accelerator to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator does not cache media and cannot use an S3 bucket directly as its endpoint.

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon CloudFront to connect the S3 buckets to CloudFront edge servers.
choices.explanation: CloudFront caches S3 content at edge locations close to viewers, providing global delivery with reduced origin traffic.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
choices.explanation: SQS queues messages; it does not serve or cache media content for users.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company produces batch data that comes from different databases. The company also produces live stream data from network sensors and application APIs.

The company needs to consolidate all the data into one place for business analytics. The company needs to process the incoming data and then stage the data in different Amazon S3 buckets.

Teams will later run one-time queries and import the data into a business intelligence tool to show key performance indicators (KPIs).

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Use Amazon Athena for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
choices.explanation: Athena queries the staged S3 data on demand, and QuickSight presents the results as dashboards without a dedicated warehouse.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
choices.explanation: Kinesis analytics processes streams; Athena is the query service for one-time SQL analysis of the staged S3 dataset.

choices.solution: Create custom AWS Lambda functions to move the individual records from the databases to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
choices.explanation: Custom per-record Lambda ingestion and a Redshift cluster add maintenance and do not implement the requested S3 staging workflow.

choices.solution: Use an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the data into JSON format. Load the data into multiple Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) clusters.
choices.explanation: Multiple OpenSearch clusters add managed-compute and indexing overhead and do not stage the consolidated dataset in S3.

choices.solution: Use blueprints in AWS Lake Formation to identify the data that can be ingested into a data lake. Use AWS Glue to crawl the source, extract the data, and load the data into Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format.
choices.explanation: Lake Formation blueprints generate Glue workflows to ingest database data into S3. Glue processes and catalogs data in Parquet format for efficient analytics.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is optimizing a website for an upcoming musical event. Videos of the performances will be streamed in real time and then will be available on demand.

The event is expected to attract a global online audience.

Which service will improve the performance of both the real-time and on-demand streaming?

choices.solution: Amazon CloudFront
choices.explanation: CloudFront is the CDN in these choices and can accelerate both live HTTP-based streaming and video-on-demand for a global audience. Global Accelerator improves network paths to regional endpoints but is not a CDN/cache for this use case.

choices.solution: AWS Global Accelerator
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator routes traffic but does not provide the edge caching and HTTP video distribution needed for both live and on-demand content.

choices.solution: Amazon Route 53
choices.explanation: Route 53 resolves and routes DNS queries; it does not deliver or cache video segments.

choices.solution: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
choices.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes transfers to and from S3 rather than providing a video content-distribution cache.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has a small Python application that processes JSON documents and outputs the results to an on-premises SQL database. The application runs thousands of times each day.

The company wants to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company needs a highly available solution that maximizes scalability and minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Run the Python code on multiple Amazon EC2 instances to process the documents.

Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
choices.explanation: An EC2 fleet needs server maintenance and capacity management, increasing overhead relative to event-driven Lambda.

choices.solution:
Place the JSON documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs the Python code to process the documents as they arrive in the S3 bucket.

Store the results in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
choices.explanation: S3 events trigger managed Lambda document processing and Aurora stores results in a managed relational database. Size and configure the Lambda workload within its execution limits.

choices.solution:
Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use the EBS Multi-Attach feature to attach the volume to multiple Amazon EC2 instances.

Run the Python code on the EC2 instances to process the documents. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.
choices.explanation: EBS Multi-Attach requires coordinated concurrent access and remains AZ-scoped; managing EC2 workers adds overhead.

choices.solution:
Place the JSON documents in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as messages. Deploy the Python code as a container on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that is configured with the Amazon EC2 launch type.

Use the container to process the SQS messages. Store the results on an Amazon RDS DB instance.
choices.explanation: The ECS EC2 launch type requires maintaining worker instances instead of using serverless execution for these small event-driven jobs.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company wants to use high performance computing (HPC) infrastructure on AWS for financial risk modeling. The company's HPC workloads run on Linux.

Each HPC workflow runs on hundreds of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances, is short-lived, and generates thousands of output files that are ultimately stored in persistent storage for analytics and long-term future use. The company seeks a cloud storage solution that permits the copying of on-premises data to long-term persistent storage to make data available for processing by all EC2 instances.

The solution should also be a high performance file system that is integrated with persistent storage to read and write datasets and output files.

Which combination of AWS services meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Amazon FSx for Lustre integrated with Amazon S3
choices.explanation: FSx for Lustre supplies high-performance shared storage and can import and export data through linked S3 storage for persistent inputs and outputs.

choices.solution: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server integrated with Amazon S3
choices.explanation: FSx for Windows uses SMB and does not provide the Lustre parallel file system and S3-linked HPC workflow required here.

choices.solution: Amazon S3 Glacier integrated with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
choices.explanation: Glacier is archival storage requiring restoration, and EBS is not a shared parallel file system for hundreds of workers.

choices.solution: Amazon S3 bucket with a VPC endpoint integrated with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume
choices.explanation: A VPC endpoint supplies connectivity, not a shared HPC file system; a gp2 EBS volume cannot supply the proposed distributed access.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A gaming company hosts a browser-based application on AWS. The users of the application consume a large number of videos and images that are stored in Amazon S3.

This content is the same for all users. The application has increased in popularity, and millions of users worldwide accessing these media files.

The company wants to provide the files to the users while reducing the load on the origin.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the web servers.
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator does not cache images and videos or use the S3 bucket as a direct endpoint.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: CloudFront caches media at nearby edge locations and serves repeated requests without repeatedly retrieving the same objects from the S3 origin.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance in front of the web servers.
choices.explanation: Redis adds a regional application cache requiring integration; it does not directly supply a worldwide S3 media distribution network.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance in front of the web servers.
choices.explanation: Memcached requires an application-managed cache and does not provide global edge delivery of S3 objects.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company has an order-processing application that uses Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. The application stores data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database.

During a recent sales event, a sudden surge in customer orders occurred. Some customers experienced timeouts, and the application did not process the orders of those customers.

A solutions architect determined that the CPU utilization and memory utilization were high on the database because of a large number of open connections. The solutions architect needs to prevent the timeout errors while making the least possible changes to the application.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function. Modify the database to be a global database in multiple AWS Regions.
choices.explanation: Provisioned concurrency can increase simultaneous database connections, and a global database does not pool connections to the writer.

choices.solution: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a proxy for the database. Modify the Lambda function to use the RDS Proxy endpoint instead of the database endpoint.
choices.explanation: RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections, reducing connection churn from concurrent Lambda invocations. It does not increase the database's underlying query-processing capacity.

choices.solution: Create a read replica for the database in a different AWS Region. Use query string parameters in API Gateway to route traffic to the read replica.
choices.explanation: Order writes cannot be routed to a read replica, and an API query parameter does not implement database connection pooling.

choices.solution: Migrate the data from Aurora PostgreSQL to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Modify the Lambda function to use the DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation: Migrating to DynamoDB changes the data model and application significantly instead of addressing connection pressure with a proxy endpoint.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
An entertainment company is using Amazon DynamoDB to store media metadata. The application is read intensive and experiencing delays.

The company does not have staff to handle additional operational overhead and needs to improve the performance efficiency of DynamoDB without reconfiguring the application.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
choices.explanation: Redis requires application-specific cache lookup, population, and invalidation logic rather than DynamoDB-compatible DAX access.

choices.solution: Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
choices.explanation: DAX supplies an API-compatible cache for eventually consistent DynamoDB reads, reducing read latency and table load. Strongly consistent reads bypass the cache, and applications need a DAX-compatible client.

choices.solution: Replicate data by using DynamoDB global tables.
choices.explanation: Global tables improve geographic availability but do not cache repeated reads to reduce their latency.

choices.solution: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with Auto Discovery enabled.
choices.explanation: Memcached requires explicit application cache integration; Auto Discovery discovers nodes, not DynamoDB records.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has an AWS account used for software engineering. The AWS account has access to the company's on-premises data center through a pair of AWS Direct Connect connections.

All non-VPC traffic routes to the virtual private gateway. A development team recently created an AWS Lambda function through the console.

The development team needs to allow the function to access a database that runs in a private subnet in the company's data center.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure the Lambda function to run in the VPC with the appropriate security group.
choices.explanation: A Lambda function must be configured for VPC access so its ENIs can use the VPC routing to the virtual private gateway and existing Direct Connect path. No additional VPN or public IP is required.

choices.solution: Set up a VPN connection from AWS to the data center. Route the traffic from the Lambda function through the VPN.
choices.explanation: Another VPN does not attach the Lambda function to the private network; the existing Direct Connect route can be used once Lambda is VPC-connected.

choices.solution: Update the route tables in the VPC to allow the Lambda function to access the on-premises data center through Direct Connect.
choices.explanation: Changing VPC routes cannot give a function outside the VPC access to its private routing domain.

choices.solution: Create an Elastic IP address. Configure the Lambda function to send traffic through the Elastic IP address without an elastic network interface.
choices.explanation: An Elastic IP cannot be assigned directly to a Lambda function; private connectivity requires VPC network interfaces and routing.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs an application using Amazon ECS. The application creates resized versions of an original image and then makes Amazon S3 API calls to store the resized images in Amazon S3.

How can a solutions architect ensure that the application has permission to access Amazon S3?

choices.solution: Update the S3 role in AWS IAM to allow read/write access from Amazon ECS, and then relaunch the container.
choices.explanation: S3 has no generic ECS role that automatically grants container credentials; the application needs a task role assigned in its task definition.

choices.solution: Create an IAM role with S3 permissions, and then specify that role as the taskRoleArn in the task definition.
choices.explanation: The ECS task role, configured as taskRoleArn, gives the code in the container its S3 permissions. The execution role is used by ECS to start and manage the task.

choices.solution: Create a security group that allows access from Amazon ECS to Amazon S3, and update the launch configuration used by the ECS cluster.
choices.explanation: Security groups control network traffic, not authorization for S3 API calls.

choices.solution: Create an IAM user with S3 permissions, and then relaunch the Amazon EC2 instances for the ECS cluster while logged in as this account.
choices.explanation: Logging in as an IAM user does not supply persistent, automatically rotated credentials to ECS tasks; a task role does.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs a containerized application on a Kubernetes cluster in an on-premises data center. The company is using a MongoDB database for data storage.

The company wants to migrate some of these environments to AWS, but no code changes or deployment method changes are possible at this time. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and MongoDB on EC2 for data storage.
choices.explanation: ECS changes the Kubernetes deployment method, and MongoDB on EC2 requires operating database servers.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage
choices.explanation: ECS changes deployment methods and DynamoDB requires database API and data-model changes.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage.
choices.explanation: EKS preserves Kubernetes, but DynamoDB is not a MongoDB-compatible replacement and requires application changes.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) for data storage.
choices.explanation: EKS preserves the Kubernetes deployment model, Fargate removes worker-node management, and DocumentDB provides MongoDB-compatible APIs. This combination minimizes code, deployment, and infrastructure changes.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company owns an asynchronous API that is used to ingest user requests and, based on the request type, dispatch requests to the appropriate microservice for processing. The company is using Amazon API Gateway to deploy the API front end, and an AWS Lambda function that invokes Amazon DynamoDB to store user requests before dispatching them to the processing microservices.

The company provisioned as much DynamoDB throughput as its budget allows, but the company is still experiencing availability issues and is losing user requests.

What should a solutions architect do to address this issue without impacting existing users?

choices.solution: Add throttling on the API Gateway with server-side throttling limits.
choices.explanation: Throttling rejects requests and impacts users instead of durably buffering accepted requests for later processing.

choices.solution: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: DAX is a read cache; it is not a durable write buffer that absorbs excess DynamoDB write demand.

choices.solution: Create a secondary index in DynamoDB for the table with the user requests.
choices.explanation: A secondary index does not increase the base table's write capacity and can add further write consumption.

choices.solution: Use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.
choices.explanation:
SQS buffers incoming requests so temporary DynamoDB write-capacity pressure does not lose requests. Lambda can drain the queue at a sustainable rate.

DAX is primarily a read cache and API Gateway throttling would reject requests rather than preserve them.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has a web server running on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet with an Elastic IP address. The default security group is assigned to the EC2 instance.

The default network ACL has been modified to block all traffic. A solutions architect needs to make the web server accessible from everywhere on port 443.

Which combination of steps will accomplish this task? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: A stateful security group allows inbound HTTPS on port 443 and automatically allows the corresponding response traffic.

choices.solution: Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: An outbound security-group rule does not allow incoming HTTPS connections.

choices.solution: Update the network ACL to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: Network ACLs are stateless; allowing only inbound port 443 still blocks return traffic to client ephemeral ports.

choices.solution: Update the network ACL to allow inbound/outbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and to destination 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: HTTPS response traffic is addressed to the client's ephemeral port, not destination port 443, so this outbound ACL rule blocks responses.

choices.solution: Update the network ACL to allow inbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and outbound TCP port 32768-65535 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: A stateless network ACL must allow inbound port 443 and outbound client ephemeral ports. Use the client port range specified by the question; some clients require 1024-65535.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing a new API using Amazon API Gateway that will receive requests from users. The volume of requests is highly variable; several hours can pass without receiving a single request.

The data processing will take place asynchronously, but should be completed within a few seconds after a request is made.

Which compute service should the solutions architect have the API invoke to deliver the requirements at the lowest cost?

choices.solution: An AWS Glue job
choices.explanation: Glue jobs are intended for data integration and have startup overhead unsuitable for these few-second API tasks.

choices.solution: An AWS Lambda function
choices.explanation: AWS Lambda supports asynchronous invocation, which is suitable for scenarios where data processing can take place independently of the API request and complete within a few seconds. This aligns with the requirement of processing data asynchronously.

choices.solution: A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
choices.explanation: An EKS service adds cluster and workload management costs during long idle periods.

choices.solution: A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2
choices.explanation: The EC2-backed ECS service incurs instance costs and host management even when no requests arrive.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs an application on a group of Amazon Linux EC2 instances. For compliance reasons, the company must retain all application log files for 7 years.

The log files will be analyzed by a reporting tool that must be able to access all the files concurrently.

Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
choices.explanation: EBS requires provisioned block volumes and attached compute rather than inexpensive shared object storage for seven years of logs.

choices.solution: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
choices.explanation: EFS provides filesystem features at a higher storage cost when the reporting tool can read log objects from S3.

choices.solution: Amazon EC2 instance store
choices.explanation: Instance store is ephemeral and loses data when its instance is stopped or terminated, violating long-term retention.

choices.solution: Amazon S3
choices.explanation:
S3 is a highly durable and scalable object storage service. It is designed for high availability and can store large amounts of data.

S3 is cost-effective for long-term storage, and its pricing is based on the amount of data stored.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company manages its own Amazon EC2 instances that run MySQL databases. The company is manually managing replication and scaling as demand increases or decreases.

The company needs a new solution that simplifies the process of adding or removing compute capacity to or from its database tier as needed. The solution also must offer improved performance, scaling, and durability with minimal effort from operations.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL.
choices.explanation:
Amazon Aurora Serverless: Aurora Serverless is an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration for Amazon Aurora. It automatically adjusts the database capacity based on actual consumption, enabling seamless scaling without manual intervention.

It is a fully managed service, reducing operational overhead.

choices.solution: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora PostgreSQL.
choices.explanation: Aurora PostgreSQL changes the database engine and SQL compatibility unnecessarily when Aurora MySQL preserves the existing engine family.

choices.solution: Combine the databases into one larger MySQL database. Run the larger database on larger EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: A larger self-managed EC2 database still requires replication management and manual vertical scaling.

choices.solution: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group for the database tier. Migrate the existing databases to the new environment.
choices.explanation: Auto Scaling EC2 instances does not configure database replication or safely add and remove MySQL writer capacity.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is moving its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database has several applications that write to the same tables.

The applications need to be migrated one by one with a month in between each migration. Management has expressed concerns that the database has a high number of reads and writes.

The data must be kept in sync across both databases throughout the migration.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
choices.explanation: DataSync transfers files and objects; it does not perform the relational Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration and schema conversion.

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
choices.explanation: DataSync cannot provide the proposed database initial load, and the workflow omits heterogeneous schema conversion.

choices.solution: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a memory optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
choices.explanation: Oracle-to-Aurora PostgreSQL is heterogeneous, so use AWS Schema Conversion Tool for schema conversion and AWS DMS with full load plus CDC to keep source and target synchronized while applications migrate gradually. A memory-optimized replication instance is appropriate for a high read/write workload.

choices.solution: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a compute optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select the largest tables.
choices.explanation: Replicating only the largest tables leaves other shared tables unsynchronized; the high-change workload also benefits from memory for DMS buffering.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company previously migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection.

Corporate office users query the data warehouse using a visualization tool. The average size of a query returned by the data warehouse is 50 MB and each webpage sent by the visualization tool is approximately 500 KB.

Result sets returned by the data warehouse are not cached.

Which solution provides the LOWEST data transfer egress cost for the company?

choices.solution: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.
choices.explanation: This transfers the roughly 50-MB query result over internet egress instead of rendering it in AWS into a much smaller page.

choices.solution: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.
choices.explanation: Rendering in AWS reduces the payload, but internet egress costs more than the available same-Region Direct Connect path.

choices.solution: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same AWS Region.
choices.explanation: This still transfers the full roughly 50-MB result to the on-premises visualization tool instead of sending only the roughly 500-KB rendered page.

choices.solution: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.
choices.explanation: Hosting the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and accessing it over a Direct Connect connection within the same Region minimizes data transfer costs. Since the data warehouse and the visualization tool are in the same Region, the data transfer between them doesn't incur the usual costs associated with data leaving the AWS network.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company plans to use Amazon ElastiCache for its multi-tier web application. A solutions architect creates a Cache VPC for the ElastiCache cluster and an App VPC for the application's Amazon EC2 instances.

Both VPCs are in the us-east-1 Region. The solutions architect must implement a solution to provide the application's EC2 instances with access to the ElastiCache cluster.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution:
Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Add a route table entry for the peering connection in both VPCs.

Configure an inbound rule for the ElastiCache cluster's security group to allow inbound connection from the application's security group.
choices.explanation:
Creating a peering connection allows communication between the Cache VPC and the App VPC. Adding a route table entry in both VPCs for the peering connection ensures that traffic can flow between them.

Inbound Rule in ElastiCache Security Group: Configuring an inbound rule in the ElastiCache cluster's security group to allow connections from the application's security group enables the EC2 instances in the App VPC to access the ElastiCache cluster.

choices.solution:
Create a Transit VPC. Update the VPC route tables in the Cache VPC and the App VPC to route traffic through the Transit VPC.

Configure an inbound rule for the ElastiCache cluster's security group to allow inbound connection from the application's security group.
choices.explanation: A transit VPC introduces additional routing infrastructure and cost for a connection between just two VPCs.

choices.solution:
Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Add a route table entry for the peering connection in both VPCs.

Configure an inbound rule for the peering connection's security group to allow inbound connection from the application's security group.
choices.explanation: A VPC peering connection has no security group; the inbound rule belongs on the ElastiCache cluster's security group.

choices.solution:
Create a Transit VPC. Update the VPC route tables in the Cache VPC and the App VPC to route traffic through the Transit VPC.

Configure an inbound rule for the Transit VPC's security group to allow inbound connection from the application's security group.
choices.explanation: A VPC itself has no security group, and operating a transit VPC adds unnecessary cost.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is building an application that consists of several microservices. The company has decided to use container technologies to deploy its software on AWS.

The company needs a solution that minimizes the amount of ongoing effort for maintenance and scaling. The company cannot manage additional infrastructure.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster.
choices.explanation: An ECS cluster provides the logical environment for managing container tasks and services.

choices.solution: Deploy the Kubernetes control plane on Amazon EC2 instances that span multiple Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: A self-managed Kubernetes control plane requires operating and maintaining additional EC2 infrastructure.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service with an Amazon EC2 launch type. Specify a desired task number level of greater than or equal to 2.
choices.explanation: The ECS EC2 launch type requires managing container hosts even when multiple tasks provide application redundancy.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service with a Fargate launch type. Specify a desired task number level of greater than or equal to 2.
choices.explanation: A Fargate service with at least two tasks across Availability Zones provides managed compute, task replacement, and service scaling without EC2 host management.

choices.solution: Deploy Kubernetes worker nodes on Amazon EC2 instances that span multiple Availability Zones. Create a deployment that specifies two or more replicas for each microservice.
choices.explanation: EC2 Kubernetes workers require node provisioning, patching, and capacity management.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A gaming company has a web application that displays scores. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer.

The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Users are starting to experience long delays and interruptions that are caused by database read performance.

The company wants to improve the user experience while minimizing changes to the application's architecture.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database.
choices.explanation:
The stated bottleneck is database read performance. ElastiCache reduces repeated reads and latency.

RDS Proxy addresses connection pooling and connection storms, not a read-I/O bottleneck.

choices.solution: Use RDS Proxy between the application and the database.
choices.explanation: RDS Proxy pools connections but does not cache repeated score queries or remove their database read work.

choices.solution: Migrate the application from EC2 instances to AWS Lambda.
choices.explanation: Changing the compute platform does not solve the database's read bottleneck and requires substantial application changes.

choices.solution: Migrate the database from Amazon RDS for MySQL to Amazon DynamoDB.
