Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Deploy AWS DataSync agents on premises. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
choices.explanation: DataSync copies SMB file data to FSx for Windows File Server and can preserve Windows ACLs when the required permissions are configured.

choices.solution: Copy the shares on each file server into Amazon S3 buckets by using the AWS CLI. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
choices.explanation: Ordinary CLI S3 copies do not preserve Windows security descriptors and ACLs required at the FSx destination.

choices.solution:
Remove the drives from each file server. Ship the drives to AWS for import into Amazon S3.

Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
choices.explanation: Shipping bare drives to AWS is not the supported managed import workflow, and S3 staging does not preserve the required Windows ACLs.

choices.solution:
Order an AWS Snowcone device. Connect the device to the on-premises network.

Launch AWS DataSync agents on the device. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
choices.explanation: Historically, a Snowcone device could run a DataSync agent for an online SMB transfer that preserves ACLs. This is an older alternative; use a supported DataSync agent host for new deployments.

choices.solution:
Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Connect the device to the on-premises network.

Copy data to the device by using the AWS CLI. Ship the device back to AWS for import into Amazon S3.

Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
choices.explanation: CLI copying through Snowball's S3 interface does not retain the Windows security metadata as DataSync's SMB-to-FSx transfer does.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs a website that uses a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2. The CMS runs on a single EC2 instance and uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance for the data tier.

Website images are stored on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is mounted inside the EC2 instance.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the performance and resilience of the website? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Move the website images into an Amazon S3 bucket that is mounted on every EC2 instance
choices.explanation: S3 is object storage rather than the existing shared POSIX filesystem; using a mount adapter can change filesystem semantics.

choices.solution: Share the website images by using an NFS share from the primary EC2 instance. Mount this share on the other EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: An NFS share hosted on the original instance preserves that instance as a single failure point.

choices.solution: Move the website images onto an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on every EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: EFS provides one shared image repository that all application instances can mount concurrently.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group.

Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator for the website
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator routes traffic but does not cache website content to offload repeated image requests as CloudFront does.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group.

Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the website.
choices.explanation: A Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group replaces failed instances and scales the website behind an ALB; CloudFront improves delivery and reduces origin load.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company provides an API interface to customers so the customers can retrieve their financial information. Ehe company expects a larger number of requests during peak usage times of the year.

The company requires the API to respond consistently with low latency to ensure customer satisfaction. The company needs to provide a compute host for the API.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use an Application Load Balancer and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
choices.explanation: An ECS service requires task and capacity management when provisioned Lambda concurrency supplies ready compute for the API.

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency.
choices.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale. AWS Lambda is a serverless computing service that automatically scales based on demand.

Provisioned concurrency in AWS Lambda allows you to set a specific number of concurrent executions to ensure that the function is ready to respond quickly to incoming requests.

choices.solution: Use an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.
choices.explanation: EKS adds Kubernetes platform and workload administration.

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with reserved concurrency.
choices.explanation: Reserved concurrency allocates a concurrency limit but does not pre-initialize functions to eliminate cold starts.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
An application uses an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The RDS database is becoming low on disk space.

A solutions architect wants to increase the disk space without downtime.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?

choices.solution: Enable storage autoscaling in RDS
choices.explanation: Enabling storage autoscaling allows Amazon RDS to automatically adjust the storage capacity of the database without requiring manual intervention. With autoscaling, the storage capacity can increase dynamically based on the actual usage, preventing the need for manual adjustments.

choices.solution: Increase the RDS database instance size
choices.explanation: Changing the instance class increases compute and memory, not the allocated database storage.

choices.solution: Change the RDS database instance storage type to Provisioned IOPS
choices.explanation: Changing storage type does not itself add the required disk capacity.

choices.solution: Back up the RDS database, increase the storage capacity, restore the database, and stop the previous instance
choices.explanation: Backup/restore and database cutover add work and downtime risk compared with online storage autoscaling.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company's workload is not consistent throughout the day.

The company wants Amazon EKS to scale in and out according to the workload.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster.
choices.explanation: A custom Lambda cluster scaler adds code and duplicates Kubernetes autoscaling components.

choices.solution: Use the Kubernetes Metrics Server to activate horizontal pod autoscaling.
choices.explanation: The Kubernetes Metrics Server supplies CPU and memory metrics to the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, which changes pod replica counts. Custom metrics require a separate metrics adapter.

choices.solution: Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
choices.explanation: Cluster Autoscaler changes EC2 node-group capacity when pods cannot be scheduled or nodes are underutilized.

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway and connect it to Amazon EKS.
choices.explanation: API Gateway does not scale Kubernetes pods or worker nodes.

choices.solution: Use AWS App Mesh to observe network activity.
choices.explanation: App Mesh observes and controls service networking, not the number of pods or cluster nodes.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs a microservice-based serverless web application. The application must be able to retrieve data from multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables A solutions architect needs to give the application the ability to retrieve the data with no impact on the baseline performance of the application.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.solution: AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers
choices.explanation:
AppSync pipeline resolvers coordinate multiple DynamoDB data-source operations in a managed GraphQL request. This avoids adding table orchestration to the existing application compute.

Appropriate table capacity is still needed; no option guarantees zero impact on database load.

choices.solution: Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge functions
choices.explanation: Lambda@Edge requires custom orchestration and remote database calls. CloudFront does not itself retrieve and combine records from multiple DynamoDB tables; AppSync pipeline resolvers provide that coordination with less application code.

choices.solution: Edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions
choices.explanation: API Gateway plus Lambda can work but requires custom multi-table orchestration code that AppSync pipeline resolvers provide declaratively.

choices.solution: Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector
choices.explanation: Athena federation targets analytical queries and adds query startup and connector overhead to an interactive application.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is reviewing the resilience of an application. The solutions architect notices that a database administrator recently failed over the application's Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database writer instance as part of a scaling exercise.

The failover resulted in 3 minutes of downtime for the application.

Which solution will reduce the downtime for scaling exercises with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create more Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas in the cluster to handle the load during failover.
choices.explanation: Additional readers do not prevent writer connections from dropping or resolve reconnection delays during failover.

choices.solution: Set up a secondary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in the same AWS Region. During failover, update the application to use the secondary cluster's writer endpoint.
choices.explanation: A separate cluster requires replication and custom cutover handling rather than a stable managed proxy endpoint.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to handle the load during failover.
choices.explanation: Memcached cannot serve database writes or preserve database connection continuity during writer failover.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon RDS proxy for the database. Update the application to use the proxy endpoint.
choices.explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy is a fully managed, highly available database proxy for Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service). It provides connection pooling, read/write splitting, and automatic failover, helping to improve the availability and scalability of database workloads.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has an online gaming application that has TCP and UDP multiplayer gaming capabilities. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to point the application traffic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions.

The company needs to improve application performance and decrease latency for the online game in preparation for user growth.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.
choices.explanation: CloudFront does not proxy arbitrary TCP and UDP game protocols.

choices.solution: Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.
choices.explanation: An ALB cannot support UDP or arbitrary TCP game traffic.

choices.solution: Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.
choices.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator is a service that uses anycast IP addresses to route traffic over the AWS global network to optimal endpoints based on health, geography, and routing policies.

choices.solution:
Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching.

Override method caching for the different stages.
choices.explanation: API Gateway handles supported API protocols, not the game's arbitrary UDP communications.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A global video streaming company uses Amazon CloudFront as a content distribution network (CDN). The company wants to roll out content in a phased manner across multiple countries.

The company needs to ensure that viewers who are outside the countries to which the company rolls out content are not able to view the content.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Add geographic restrictions to the content in CloudFront by using an allow list. Set up a custom error message.
choices.explanation:
CloudFront allows you to set up geographic restrictions by creating an allow list. This allows you to specify the countries from which viewers are allowed to access your content.

Viewers from countries not in the allow list will be restricted from accessing the content.

choices.solution:
Set up a new URL tor restricted content. Authorize access by using a signed URL and cookies.

Set up a custom error message.
choices.explanation: Signed access grants are not geographic allowlists; authorized links could still be used from excluded countries without an additional location restriction.

choices.solution: Encrypt the data for the content that the company distributes. Set up a custom error message.
choices.explanation: Encryption does not determine the viewer's country or enforce a country rollout.

choices.solution: Create a new URL for restricted content. Set up a time-restricted access policy for signed URLs.
choices.explanation: Time-based URL expiration limits when content is accessible, not the countries from which it can be viewed.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company's SAP application has a backend SQL Server database in an on-premises environment. The company wants to migrate its on-premises application and database server to AWS.

The company needs an instance type that meets the high demands of its SAP database. On-premises performance data shows that both the SAP application and the database have high memory utilization.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use the compute optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.
choices.explanation: Compute-optimized application instances do not address the application's measured high memory utilization.

choices.solution: Use the storage optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
choices.explanation: Storage-optimized instances target local disk I/O rather than the memory bottleneck in both components.

choices.solution: Use the memory optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
choices.explanation: Memory optimized instances are designed to provide a high memory-to-CPU ratio, which aligns well with workloads that have significant memory requirements, such as SAP applications with backend databases.

choices.solution: Use the high performance computing (HPC) optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.
choices.explanation: HPC-optimized application instances target specialized compute workloads instead of the identified high memory demand.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has two VPCs that are located in the us-west-2 Region within the same AWS account. The company needs to allow network traffic between these VPCs.

Approximately 500 GB of data transfer will occur between the VPCs each month.

What is the MOST cost-effective solution to connect these VPCs?

choices.solution: Implement AWS Transit Gateway to connect the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the transit gateway for inter-VPC communication.
choices.explanation: Transit Gateway adds attachment and data-processing charges unnecessary for connecting just two VPCs.

choices.solution: Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPN tunnel for inter-VPC communication.
choices.explanation: A VPN requires gateways or appliances and tunnel management that direct VPC peering avoids.

choices.solution: Set up a VPC peering connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPC peering connection for inter-VPC communication.
choices.explanation:
VPC peering allows communication between VPCs within the same AWS account. It is a cost-effective solution, especially when the VPCs are located in the same region.

In this case, both VPCs are in the us-west-2 region.

choices.solution: Set up a 1 GB AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the Direct Connect connection for inter-VPC communication.
choices.explanation: Direct Connect connects an external network to AWS, not a physical connection directly between two AWS VPCs.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company's website handles millions of requests each day, and the number of requests continues to increase. A solutions architect needs to improve the response time of the web application.

The solutions architect determines that the application needs to decrease latency when retrieving product details from the Amazon DynamoDB table.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

choices.solution: Set up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Route all read requests through DAX.
choices.explanation:
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, highly available, and in-memory cache for DynamoDB. It is designed to improve the response time of read-intensive DynamoDB workloads by caching frequently accessed data.

Using DAX helps reduce the read latency as it retrieves data from an in-memory cache instead of the DynamoDB table.

choices.solution: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Redis.
choices.explanation: Redis requires explicit cache population and invalidation code rather than DynamoDB-compatible cached requests.

choices.solution: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Memcached.
choices.explanation: Memcached requires custom cache integration and does not directly implement the DynamoDB API.

choices.solution: Set up Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table, and have AWS Lambda read from the table and populate Amazon ElastiCache. Route all read requests through ElastiCache.
choices.explanation: A stream-to-cache Lambda pipeline adds custom synchronization and failure-handling work.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs its applications on both Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters and on-premises Kubernetes clusters. The company wants to view all clusters and workloads from a central location.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect and group the cluster information.
choices.explanation: Container Insights provides telemetry but is not the direct unified EKS console registration and workload-view mechanism.

choices.solution: Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.
choices.explanation:
Amazon EKS Connector is designed to help centralize the management of multiple Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) clusters. It allows you to register and connect multiple EKS clusters, providing a unified view of the clusters from the AWS Management Console.

This solution aligns well with the requirement of managing clusters and workloads from a central location with the least operational overhead.

choices.solution: Use AWS Systems Manager to collect and view the cluster information.
choices.explanation: Systems Manager manages nodes and operations rather than registering arbitrary Kubernetes clusters for the EKS console.

choices.solution: Use Amazon EKS Anywhere as the primary cluster to view the other clusters with native Kubernetes commands.
choices.explanation: EKS Anywhere manages deployment of clusters and does not act as a native central control plane for all other independent clusters.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has an on-premises MySQL database that handles transactional data. The company is migrating the database to the AWS Cloud.

The migrated database must maintain compatibility with the company's applications that use the database. The migrated database also must scale automatically during periods of increased demand.

Which migration solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use native MySQL tools to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Configure elastic storage scaling.
choices.explanation: RDS storage autoscaling grows disk space, not database compute or read capacity for increased demand.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift by using the mysqldump utility. Turn on Auto Scaling for the Amazon Redshift cluster.
choices.explanation: Redshift is an analytical engine rather than a compatible MySQL transactional replacement; mysqldump cannot directly restore it.

choices.solution: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon Aurora. Turn on Aurora Auto Scaling.
choices.explanation:
AWS DMS is a fully managed service that helps you migrate databases to AWS easily and securely. It supports homogeneous and heterogeneous database migrations.

Amazon Aurora is a fully managed relational database service that is compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL. It provides high performance and availability with compatibility for MySQL, making it a seamless choice for migrating MySQL databases.

choices.solution: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure an Auto Scaling policy.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB requires a different data model and APIs, violating compatibility with the existing MySQL applications.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC across two Availability Zones. The instances host applications that use a hierarchical directory structure.

The applications need to read and write rapidly and concurrently to shared storage.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Allow access from all the EC2 instances in the VPC.
choices.explanation: S3 object APIs do not provide the shared directory filesystem expected by the unchanged applications.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system from each EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: Amazon EFS is a fully managed, scalable file storage service designed to provide shared access to files across multiple Amazon EC2 instances. It is particularly well-suited for use cases that require concurrent access from multiple instances.

choices.solution: Create a file system on a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Attach the EBS volume to all the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: EBS Multi-Attach is limited to one AZ and requires coordinated block access, not cross-AZ shared filesystem access.

choices.solution: Create file systems on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are attached to each EC2 instance. Synchronize the EBS volumes across the different EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Separate replicated filesystems require custom synchronization and concurrent-write conflict handling.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing the storage architecture for a new web application used for storing and viewing engineering drawings. All application components will be deployed on the AWS infrastructure.

The application design must support caching to minimize the amount of time that users wait for the engineering drawings to load. The application must be able to store petabytes of data.

Which combination of storage and caching should the solutions architect use?

choices.solution: Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront
choices.explanation:
It is suitable for storing petabytes of data and is designed to provide low-latency access. Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) service that securely delivers data, videos, applications, and APIs to customers globally with low latency and high transfer speeds.

By integrating CloudFront with S3, you can distribute the engineering drawings to edge locations worldwide, reducing the latency for users and improving load times.

choices.solution: Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache
choices.explanation: Glacier requires restore operations, while ElastiCache is not a global object content-delivery cache.

choices.solution: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Amazon CloudFront
choices.explanation: EBS is provisioned block storage rather than an economical petabyte-scale object origin directly usable by CloudFront.

choices.solution: AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache
choices.explanation: Storage Gateway adds an appliance and hybrid storage layer unnecessary for components entirely in AWS, and ElastiCache is not a global CDN.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs an application on AWS. The application receives inconsistent amounts of usage.

The application uses AWS Direct Connect to connect to an on-premises MySQL-compatible database. The on-premises database consistently uses a minimum of 2 GiB of memory.

The company wants to migrate the on-premises database to a managed AWS service. The company wants to use auto scaling capabilities to manage unexpected workload increases.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

choices.solution: Provision an Amazon DynamoDB database with default read and write capacity settings.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB is not a MySQL-compatible relational database.

choices.solution: Provision an Amazon Aurora database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
choices.explanation: A provisioned Aurora instance is sized by DB instance class, not a minimum Serverless ACU setting.

choices.solution: Provision an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
choices.explanation: Aurora Serverless is designed for applications with variable or unpredictable workloads. With Aurora Serverless v2, you can set the minimum capacity to 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU), and it will automatically scale based on the actual workload.

choices.solution: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL database with 2 GiB of memory.
choices.explanation: A fixed 2-GiB RDS instance does not automatically adjust database compute capacity as workload changes.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company wants to use an event-driven programming model with AWS Lambda. The company wants to reduce startup latency for Lambda functions that run on Java 11.

The company does not have strict latency requirements for the applications. The company wants to reduce cold starts and outlier latencies when a function scales up.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency.
choices.explanation: Provisioned concurrency incurs standing charges for ready execution environments that the relaxed latency requirements do not justify.

choices.solution: Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions.
choices.explanation: A larger timeout does not reduce initialization latency.

choices.solution: Increase the memory of the Lambda functions.
choices.explanation: More memory can improve CPU-dependent initialization but increases execution cost and does not reuse a SnapStart initialized snapshot.

choices.solution: Configure Lambda SnapStart.
choices.explanation:
Lambda Cold Start: When a Lambda function is invoked, it may take a bit of time for the system to set up everything needed to run the function. This initial setup time is called a "cold start." Cold starts can add some delay, especially if the function hasn't been used recently.

Lambda SnapStart: SnapStart is a feature in AWS Lambda designed to make these cold starts faster, specifically for functions written in Java. Instead of starting from scratch every time a function is called, SnapStart pre-warms the environment.

It's like getting things ready in advance so that when your function is called, it can start quickly without much delay.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company deployed a serverless application that uses Amazon DynamoDB as a database layer. The application has experienced a large increase in users.

The company wants to improve database response time from milliseconds to microseconds and to cache requests to the database.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
choices.explanation:
DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers fast response times for DynamoDB queries. It can be seamlessly integrated with existing DynamoDB applications, requiring minimal code changes.

DAX allows you to cache frequently accessed data, reducing the need to read from the DynamoDB table and improving response times.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift.
choices.explanation: Redshift changes the database model and targets analytical queries rather than cached DynamoDB key reads.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS.
choices.explanation: RDS requires changing the application's database engine and does not provide the DAX cache integration.

choices.solution: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
choices.explanation: Redis requires custom cache population and invalidation rather than DynamoDB-compatible cached access.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company uses locally attached storage to run a latency-sensitive application on premises. The company is using a lift and shift method to move the application to the AWS Cloud.

The company does not want to change the application architecture.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to run the application.
choices.explanation: Lustre changes local block-storage access into a network filesystem and adds unnecessary filesystem cost.

choices.solution: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 volume to run the application.
choices.explanation: gp2 generally costs more per GB and ties IOPS to volume size, whereas gp3 provides a predictable baseline independently.

choices.solution: Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to run the application.
choices.explanation: OpenZFS introduces a network filesystem and managed-filesystem charges instead of preserving simple attached block storage.

choices.solution: Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 volume to run the application.
choices.explanation: Amazon EC2 Instance with GP3 Volume (Option D): Amazon EBS GP3 volumes are designed to provide cost savings compared to GP2 volumes while still offering good performance for a broad range of workloads. GP3 volumes allow you to provision the IOPS (input/output operations per second) and throughput that your application needs, giving you flexibility and cost-effectiveness.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is deploying an application that processes large quantities of data in parallel. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload.

The network architecture must be configurable to prevent groups of nodes from sharing the same underlying hardware.

Which networking solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Run the EC2 instances in a partition placement group, placing each node group in a separate logical partition.
choices.explanation:
Partition placement ensures that node groups in different partitions do not share the same underlying hardware. This supports large distributed deployments with hundreds of instances.

Spread placement is intended for small groups and has a seven-instance-per-AZ limit for rack-level spread.

choices.solution: Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
choices.explanation: Account boundaries do not control which physical hosts the instances share.

choices.solution: Configure the EC2 instances with dedicated tenancy.
choices.explanation: Dedicated tenancy isolates hardware from other customers but does not separate the company's own node groups into distinct failure domains.

choices.solution: Configure the EC2 instances with shared tenancy.
choices.explanation: Shared tenancy supplies no guarantee that node groups avoid shared hardware.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company migrated a MySQL database from the company's on-premises data center to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company sized the RDS DB instance to meet the company's average daily workload.

Once a month, the database performs slowly when the company runs queries for a report. The company wants to have the ability to run reports and maintain the performance of the daily workloads.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a read replica of the database. Direct the queries to the read replica.
choices.explanation:
Read Replica: Creating a read replica of the database allows you to offload read queries to a replica instance. This helps in distributing the workload and prevents the additional load from impacting the performance of the primary database.

Direct Queries to the Read Replica: By directing the queries for the monthly reports to the read replica, you ensure that the heavy reporting workload doesn't affect the performance of the primary database handling daily workloads. Read replicas are designed to handle read-intensive workloads, providing a scalable solution.

choices.solution:
Create a backup of the database. Restore the backup to another DB instance.

Direct the queries to the new database.
choices.explanation: A restored backup is a point-in-time dataset and requires repeated backup, restore, and synchronization work.

choices.solution: Export the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Exporting to S3 requires a new reporting pipeline and queries instead of reusing the existing MySQL reports on a replica.

choices.solution: Resize the DB instance to accommodate the additional workload.
choices.explanation: A larger writer increases ongoing cost and leaves reporting queries competing with the daily transactional workload.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
An ecommerce application uses a PostgreSQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. During a monthly sales event, database usage increases and causes database connection issues for the application.

The traffic is unpredictable for subsequent monthly sales events, which impacts the sales forecast. The company needs to maintain performance when there is an unpredictable increase in traffic.

Which solution resolves this issue in the MOST cost-effective way?

choices.solution: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2.
choices.explanation:
Aurora Serverless is a serverless relational database engine provided by Amazon. It automatically adjusts its capacity based on actual usage, allowing it to scale up or down as needed.

Aurora Serverless v2 builds upon the original Aurora Serverless model with additional features for even more efficient scaling.

choices.solution: Enable auto scaling for the PostgreSQL database on the EC2 instance to accommodate increased usage.
choices.explanation: An EC2 Auto Scaling group does not automatically configure shared PostgreSQL state and elastic database compute.

choices.solution: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with a larger instance type.
choices.explanation: A fixed larger RDS instance incurs idle capacity cost and still needs manual resizing for unpredictable demand.

choices.solution: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Redshift to accommodate increased usage.
choices.explanation: Redshift is an analytics warehouse, not a compatible PostgreSQL transactional application database.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company hosts an internal serverless application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The company's employees report issues with high latency when they begin using the application each day.

The company wants to reduce latency.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Increase the API Gateway throttling limit.
choices.explanation: A higher throttling limit does not remove Lambda cold starts at the beginning of the day.

choices.solution: Set up a scheduled scaling to increase Lambda provisioned concurrency before employees begin to use the application each day.
choices.explanation: Lambda Provisioned Concurrency: Provisioned concurrency is the number of simultaneous executions that your function can handle. By setting up a scheduled scaling to increase Lambda provisioned concurrency before employees begin using the application, you are proactively ensuring that there are enough resources available to handle the expected load.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to initiate a Lambda function as a target for the alarm at the beginning of each day.
choices.explanation: An alarm is not a daily prewarming schedule, and a one-time invocation does not guarantee sufficient initialized environments.

choices.solution: Increase the Lambda function memory.
choices.explanation: More memory can speed execution but does not proactively create initialized environments before employees arrive.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters and Amazon RDS DB instances to build and run a payment processing application. The company will run the application in its on-premises data center for compliance purposes.

A solutions architect wants to use AWS Outposts as part of the solution. The solutions architect is working with the company's operational team to build the application.

Which activities are the responsibility of the company's operational team? (Choose three.)

choices.solution: Providing resilient power and network connectivity to the Outposts racks
choices.explanation: The customer provides the site power and network connectivity needed by Outposts.

choices.solution: Managing the virtualization hypervisor, storage systems, and the AWS services that run on Outposts
choices.explanation: AWS operates the Outposts virtualization, underlying storage systems, and managed AWS service infrastructure.

choices.solution: Physical security and access controls of the data center environment
choices.explanation: The customer controls physical security and access to the data center housing the racks.

choices.solution: Availability of the Outposts infrastructure including the power supplies, servers, and networking equipment within the Outposts racks
choices.explanation: AWS maintains the hardware components within the racks; the customer supplies facility power and network connections.

choices.solution: Physical maintenance of Outposts components
choices.explanation: Physical maintenance and replacement of Outposts components are AWS responsibilities.

choices.solution: Providing extrafficapacity for Amazon ECS clusters to mitigate server failures and maintenance events
choices.explanation: The customer plans sufficient application capacity to tolerate server failures and maintenance; AWS manages the Outposts hardware itself.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has several on-premises Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (ISCSI) network storage servers. The company wants to reduce the number of these servers by moving to the AWS Cloud.

A solutions architect must provide low-latency access to frequently used data and reduce the dependency on on-premises servers with a minimal number of infrastructure changes.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway.
choices.explanation: File Gateway supplies NFS/SMB rather than preserving the applications' iSCSI block interfaces.

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage with backups to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: EBS is attached to AWS compute and does not directly supply a locally cached on-premises iSCSI storage interface.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with stored volumes.
choices.explanation: Stored volumes retain the entire primary dataset locally, so they do not reduce local storage dependency as much as cached volumes.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with cached volumes.
choices.explanation: A volume gateway with cached volumes is a good fit when you want to keep frequently accessed data on-premises for low-latency access while still having a copy in the AWS Cloud. Cached volumes store the entire dataset in Amazon S3 while retaining the most frequently accessed data locally.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has migrated a two-tier application from its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The data tier is a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for Oracle with 12 TB of General Purpose SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage.

The application is designed to process and store documents in the database as binary large objects (blobs) with an average document size of 6 MB. The database size has grown over time, reducing the performance and increasing the cost of storage.

The company must improve the database performance and needs a solution that is highly available and resilient.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution:
Reduce the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiB.

Change the storage type to Magnetic.
choices.explanation: A smaller instance and magnetic disks reduce processing and I/O capacity while keeping large binaries in expensive database storage.

choices.solution: Increase the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiChange the storage type to Provisioned IOPS.
choices.explanation: Increasing compute and provisioned IOPS increases cost without removing document binaries from the database.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the application to store documents in the S3 bucket.

Store the object metadata in the existing database.
choices.explanation: Amazon S3 is highly scalable, durable, and cost-effective for storing objects, making it well-suited for binary large objects (blobs) such as documents. It provides low-latency access and is designed to handle large volumes of data.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Update the application to use DynamoDB.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate data from the Oracle database to DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB's 400-KB item limit cannot hold the average 6-MB documents directly.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company deploys Amazon EC2 instances that run in a VPC. The EC2 instances load source data into Amazon S3 buckets so that the data can be processed in the future.

According to compliance laws, the data must not be transmitted over the public internet. Servers in the company's on- premises data center will consume the output from an application that runs on the EC2 instances.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EC2. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
choices.explanation: An EC2 API endpoint does not supply private S3 access, and Site-to-Site VPN traffic still traverses public internet paths.

choices.solution: Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and the VPC.
choices.explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint allows communication between resources in your VPC and Amazon S3 without traversing the public internet. AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection from the on-premises data center to the VPC.

This dedicated connection enhances security and ensures a reliable and consistent connection between on-premises servers and the EC2 instances in the VPC.

choices.solution: Set up an AWS Transit Gateway connection from the VPC to the S3 buckets. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
choices.explanation: A transit gateway does not attach directly to S3 buckets, and an internet VPN does not meet the no-public-internet path requirement.

choices.solution: Set up proxy EC2 instances that have routes to NAT gateways. Configure the proxy EC2 instances to fetch S3 data and feed the application instances.
choices.explanation: Proxy servers and NAT add operations and public endpoint routing instead of direct private S3 connectivity.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts a storage server that stores data in an NFS-based file system.

The storage server holds 200 GB of data. The company needs to migrate the data without interruption to existing services.

Multiple resources in AWS must be able to access the data by using the NFS protocol.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
choices.explanation: Lustre requires its own client protocol rather than providing the requested NFS interface.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
choices.explanation: EFS provides managed shared NFS storage that multiple Linux EC2 instances can mount concurrently.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to receive the data.
choices.explanation: S3 is object storage rather than a natively mountable shared NFS filesystem.

choices.solution: Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data into the AWS destination.
choices.explanation: Manual copying requires custom scheduling and verification and does not provide managed incremental synchronization while source services continue running.

choices.solution: Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center. Use a DataSync task between the on-premises location and AWS.
choices.explanation: An on-premises DataSync agent transfers the existing NFS data to EFS without writing a custom migration tool.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is planning to deploy a business-critical application in the AWS Cloud. The application requires durable storage with consistent, low- latency performance.

Which type of storage should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Instance store volume
choices.explanation: Instance store is ephemeral and loses data during relevant instance lifecycle events.

choices.solution: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster
choices.explanation: Memcached is an in-memory cache without the durable block-storage guarantee required here.

choices.solution: Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
choices.explanation: Provisioned IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second) SSD volumes are designed to deliver predictable, consistent, and low-latency performance for critical applications. These volumes allow you to specify the amount of IOPS you need, providing a consistent level of performance regardless of the volume size.

choices.solution: Throughput Optimized HDD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
choices.explanation: Throughput-optimized HDD targets large sequential transfers rather than consistent low-latency transactional I/O.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company stores its data on premises. The amount of data is growing beyond the company's available capacity.

The company wants to migrate its data from the on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs a solution that will automatically validate the integrity of the data after the transfer.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Configure the Snowball Edge device to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
choices.explanation: Snowball's standard workflow is offline device shipment, not the specified managed online migration and validation task.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on premises. Configure the DataSync agent to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
choices.explanation:
AWS DataSync is a service designed for fast and secure online data transfer between on-premises storage and Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, or Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. DataSync automatically performs integrity validation by ensuring that the data transferred to S3 matches the source data.

It uses checksums to validate the integrity of the files.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises Configure the S3 File Gateway to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
choices.explanation: File Gateway supplies cached file access; it does not provide DataSync's migration task and source/destination verification workflow.

choices.solution: Configure an accelerator in Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on premises. Configure the accelerator to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Transfer Acceleration is enabled on an S3 bucket, not an on-premises accelerator, and does not manage end-to-end dataset validation.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is creating a data processing job that runs once daily and can take up to 2 hours to complete. If the job is interrupted, it has to restart from the beginning.

How should the solutions architect address this issue in the MOST cost-effective manner?

choices.solution: Create a script that runs locally on an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance that is triggered by a cron job.
choices.explanation: A reservation incurs a long-term commitment for a job running only two hours daily and requires server management.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
choices.explanation: Lambda cannot run a single two-hour job because its invocation limit is 15 minutes.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Fargate task triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
choices.explanation:
ECS Fargate is a serverless container service, and it abstracts away the underlying infrastructure. With Fargate, you don't need to manage or provision EC2 instances directly.

You can run containers without worrying about the infrastructure, and AWS takes care of scaling and resource allocation.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task running on Amazon EC2 triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
choices.explanation: EC2-backed ECS requires operating the worker instances and their capacity instead of paying for an isolated scheduled Fargate task.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is creating a new application that will store a large amount of data. The data will be analyzed hourly and will be modified by several Amazon EC2 Linux instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zones.

The needed amount of storage space will continue to grow for the next 6 months.

Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Store the data in Amazon S3 Glacier. Update the S3 Glacier vault policy to allow access to the application instances.
choices.explanation: Glacier archival data must be restored before frequent analysis and cannot be modified as a shared live filesystem.

choices.solution: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on the application instances.
choices.explanation: An ordinary EBS volume cannot be concurrently shared by instances across Availability Zones.

choices.solution: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the file system on the application instances.
choices.explanation:
Amazon EFS is a scalable and fully managed file storage service that can be mounted on multiple Amazon EC2 instances simultaneously. It provides a shared file system that can be accessed concurrently from different instances.Amazon EFS can automatically scale its file system capacity to accommodate growing data sets.

It can handle a large amount of data and is designed to grow and shrink as needed.

choices.solution: Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS volume shared between the application instances.
choices.explanation: Provisioned IOPS does not remove EBS Multi-Attach's same-AZ restriction or provide a managed concurrent shared filesystem.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A development team is creating an event-based application that uses AWS Lambda functions. Events will be generated when files are added to an Amazon S3 bucket.

The development team currently has Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) configured as the event target from Amazon S3.

What should a solutions architect do to process the events from Amazon S3 in a scalable way?

choices.solution: Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) before the event runs in Lambda.
choices.explanation: ECS is not a direct SNS subscription endpoint; adding a container processing stage requires more integration.

choices.solution: Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) before the event runs in Lambda
choices.explanation: EKS is not a direct SNS subscription endpoint and introduces Kubernetes processing infrastructure.

choices.solution: Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure the SQS queue to trigger a Lambda function.
choices.explanation: An SNS subscription to SQS durably buffers the notifications. A Lambda event source mapping polls SQS and retries failures, decoupling publication from processing.

choices.solution: Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure the Lambda function to poll from the SMS event.
choices.explanation: Server Migration Service is unrelated to event buffering and cannot be polled as the proposed SNS event queue.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing a new service behind Amazon API Gateway. The request patterns for the service will be unpredictable and can change suddenly from 0 requests to over 500 per second.

The total size of the data that needs to be persisted in a backend database is currently less than 1 GB with unpredictable future growth. Data can be queried using simple key-value requests.

Which combination ofAWS services would meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: AWS Fargate
choices.explanation: Fargate containers require service/task orchestration and startup capacity compared with request-driven Lambda for this small key-value service.

choices.solution: AWS Lambda
choices.explanation: Lambda scales application code with request-driven invocations without maintaining compute hosts.

choices.solution: Amazon DynamoDB
choices.explanation: DynamoDB provides a managed key-value database; use on-demand capacity for unpredictable traffic.

choices.solution: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
choices.explanation: EC2 scaling requires host maintenance and launch time during sudden spikes from zero.

choices.solution: MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora
choices.explanation: Aurora adds relational database capacity and schema management unnecessary for simple unpredictable key-value requests.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to host a high performance computing (HPC) workload in the AWS Cloud. The workload will run on hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances and will require parallel access to a shared file system to enable distributed processing of large datasets.

Datasets will be accessed across multiple instances simultaneously. The workload requires access latency within 1 ms.

After processing has completed, engineers will need access to the dataset for manual postprocessing.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) as a shared file system. Access the dataset from Amazon EFS.
choices.explanation: EFS supplies a general-purpose NFS filesystem rather than Lustre's parallel HPC architecture and sub-millisecond target performance.

choices.solution: Mount an Amazon S3 bucket to serve as the shared file system. Perform postprocessing directly from the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 object storage is not a native shared parallel filesystem, and mount adapters cannot guarantee the required semantics and latency.

choices.solution: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre as a shared file system. Link the file system to an Amazon S3 bucket for postprocessing.
choices.explanation: FSx for Lustre is designed for high-performance computing workloads that require fast and scalable shared storage. It provides low-latency access to data and is well-suited for parallel processing across multiple instances.

choices.solution: Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share an Amazon S3 bucket so that it can be mounted to all instances for processing and postprocessing.
choices.explanation: RAM does not turn an S3 bucket into a mountable low-latency parallel filesystem.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A weather forecasting company needs to process hundreds of gigabytes of data with sub-millisecond latency. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) environment in its data center and wants to expand its forecasting capabilities.

A solutions architect must identify a highly available cloud storage solution that can handle large amounts of sustained throughput. Files that are stored in the solution should be accessible to thousands of compute instances that will simultaneously access and process the entire dataset.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre scratch file systems.
choices.explanation: Scratch filesystems lack the replicated storage and automatic recovery of persistent Lustre filesystems.

choices.solution: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file systems.
choices.explanation:
Persistent file systems in FSx for Lustre are designed for longer-term storage needs. They provide a durable and highly available solution for your data.

This is important for the weather forecasting company's requirement to handle large amounts of sustained throughput.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Bursting Throughput mode.
choices.explanation: EFS bursting depends on filesystem throughput credits and does not target this sustained sub-millisecond parallel HPC workload.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Provisioned Throughput mode.
choices.explanation: Provisioning EFS throughput does not provide Lustre's optimized sub-millisecond parallel access architecture.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company runs a PostgreSQL database on premises. The database stores data by using high IOPS Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) block storage.

The daily peak I/O transactions per second do not exceed 15,000 IOPS. The company wants to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and provision disk IOPS performance independent of disk storage capacity.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
choices.explanation: gp2 IOPS scale with storage size and cannot be independently provisioned as proposed.

choices.solution: Configure the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
choices.explanation: io1 can meet the performance but costs more than gp3 for this IOPS target.

choices.solution: Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
choices.explanation: Amazon EBS gp3 volumes are designed for general-purpose workloads and offer a balance of price and performance. They allow you to provision IOPS independently of storage capacity, similar to io1 volumes.

choices.solution: Configure the EBS magnetic volume type to achieve maximum IOPS.
choices.explanation: Magnetic storage cannot provide the required predictable 15,000-IOPS performance.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company uses an on-premises network-attached storage (NAS) system to provide file shares to its high performance computing (HPC) workloads. The company wants to migrate its latency-sensitive HPC workloads and its storage to the AWS Cloud.

The company must be able to provide NFS and SMB multi-protocol access from the file system.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST latency? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a cluster placement group.
choices.explanation: A cluster placement group places compute instances close together within one Availability Zone to reduce inter-instance network latency.

choices.solution: Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a partition placement group.
choices.explanation: Partition placement favors hardware fault isolation rather than the tightly packed lowest-latency networking of a cluster placement group.

choices.solution: Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
choices.explanation: Lustre does not provide the required SMB and NFS multiprotocol interface.

choices.solution: Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system.
choices.explanation: FSx for OpenZFS provides NFS access, not the required SMB interface.

choices.solution: Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system.
choices.explanation: FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides shared NFS and SMB access to the same storage, meeting the multiprotocol requirement.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company is relocating its data center and wants to securely transfer 50 TB of data to AWS within 2 weeks. The existing data center has a Site-to- Site VPN connection to AWS that is 90% utilized.

Which AWS service should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: AWS DataSync with a VPC endpoint
choices.explanation: A private endpoint does not increase the available bandwidth of the nearly saturated VPN connection.

choices.solution: AWS Direct Connect
choices.explanation: A new Direct Connect circuit requires provisioning lead time and cost for a one-time two-week transfer deadline.

choices.solution: AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized
choices.explanation: A Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device avoids consuming the already 90%-utilized VPN and is designed for secure offline transfer of tens of terabytes within a migration window like this. Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.

choices.solution: AWS Storage Gateway
choices.explanation: Storage Gateway adds hybrid storage access but does not overcome the saturated transfer path.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company runs applications on AWS that connect to the company's Amazon RDS database. The applications scale on weekends and at peak times of the year.

The company wants to scale the database more effectively for its applications that connect to the database.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon DynamoDB with connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the DynamoDB endpoint.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB is not an RDS connection-pooling proxy and requires a different database model.

choices.solution: Use Amazon RDS Proxy with a target group for the database. Change the applications to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
choices.explanation: RDS Proxy pools application connections and reduces database connection overhead during bursts. It does not independently scale database compute or solve query bottlenecks.

choices.solution: Use a custom proxy that runs on Amazon EC2 as an intermediary to the database. Change the applications to use the custom proxy endpoint.
choices.explanation: A self-managed EC2 proxy requires patching, availability, and connection-management operations.

choices.solution: Use an AWS Lambda function to provide connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: A Lambda function is not a persistent managed database connection-pool endpoint and requires custom proxy logic.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company has a web application that runs on premises. The application experiences latency issues during peak hours.

The latency issues occur twice each month. At the start of a latency issue, the application's CPU utilization immediately increases to 10 times its normal amount.

The company wants to migrate the application to AWS to improve latency. The company also wants to scale the application automatically when application demand increases.

The company will use AWS Elastic Beanstalk for application deployment.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
choices.explanation:
The workload has rare, abrupt CPU spikes. Burstable instances in unlimited mode can absorb short spikes cost-effectively, and request-based scaling reacts automatically to actual demand.

Scheduled scaling cannot predict irregular twice-monthly events.

choices.solution: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
choices.explanation: Compute-optimized instances can scale and are technically viable, but provision their compute continuously rather than exploiting the low baseline with occasional unlimited bursting. The prompt does not provide enough sizing data to prove one family always performs better.

choices.solution: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale on a schedule.
choices.explanation: Scheduled scaling cannot respond to an issue's actual start unless its timing is known in advance.

choices.solution: Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale on predictive metrics.
choices.explanation: Predictive scaling depends on learnable recurrence and does not react directly to the unpredictable request surge.

Design High-Performing Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to run an application. The company creates one snapshot of each EBS volume every day to meet compliance requirements.

The company wants to implement an architecture that prevents the accidental deletion of EBS volume snapshots. The solution must not change the administrative rights of the storage administrator user.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort?

choices.solution:
Create an IAM role that has permission to delete snapshots. Attach the role to a new EC2 instance.

Use the AWS CLI from the new EC2 instance to delete snapshots.
choices.explanation: An EC2-attached role does not prevent the existing storage administrator from deleting snapshots.

choices.solution: Create an IAM policy that denies snapshot deletion. Attach the policy to the storage administrator user.
choices.explanation: A deny policy changes the administrator's existing rights, contrary to the requirement.

choices.solution: Add tags to the snapshots. Create retention rules in Recycle Bin for EBS snapshots that have the tags.
choices.explanation: Recycle Bin allows deletion followed by possible recovery; snapshot locking directly prevents deletion during the retention period.

choices.solution: Lock the EBS snapshots to prevent deletion.
choices.explanation: EBS Snapshot Lock prevents deletion of a locked snapshot without changing the storage administrator's IAM rights. Compliance mode enforces the retention period after any cooling-off interval; governance locks can be removed by authorized users.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company needs the ability to analyze the log files of its proprietary application. The logs are stored in JSON format in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Queries will be simple and will run on-demand. A solutions architect needs to perform the analysis with minimal changes to the existing architecture.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Redshift to load all the content into one place and run the SQL queries as needed.
choices.explanation: Loading the logs into Redshift introduces a separate data-loading pipeline and warehouse configuration. Simple on-demand SQL over the existing S3 files does not require that additional architecture.

choices.solution: Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to store the logs. Run SQL queries as needed from the Amazon CloudWatch console.
choices.explanation: The logs would need to be ingested into CloudWatch Logs first. Even though CloudWatch supports query languages, moving the existing S3 data introduces changes that direct Athena queries avoid.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Athena directly with Amazon S3 to run the queries as needed.
choices.explanation: Amazon Athena queries data directly in S3 with standard SQL and is serverless, so it requires the least architectural change and operational overhead for simple on-demand queries.

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue to catalog the logs. Use a transient Apache Spark cluster on Amazon EMR to run the SQL queries as needed.
choices.explanation: The Glue catalog can help describe the data, but provisioning and operating an EMR Spark cluster is unnecessary for these simple queries. Athena can query the existing S3 files without a cluster.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts for different departments. The management account has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains project reports.

The company wants to limit access to this S3 bucket to only users of accounts within the organization in AWS Organizations.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

choices.solution: Add the aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key with a reference to the organization ID to the S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: Scalability: DynamoDB and Amazon Kinesis are both extremely scalable technologies that can manage enormous data volumes and adjust to the workload.

choices.solution: Create an organizational unit (OU) for each department. Add the aws:PrincipalOrgPaths global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: PrincipalOrgPaths can restrict access by organizational path, but creating departmental OUs and maintaining path conditions is unnecessary when the requirement is simply organization-wide membership.

choices.solution: Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the CreateAccount, InviteAccountToOrganization, LeaveOrganization, and RemoveAccountFromOrganization events. Update the S3 bucket policy accordingly.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail reports account changes; it does not itself enforce bucket access. Maintaining a custom policy-update process for membership events adds overhead and potential delays before access is revoked.

choices.solution: Tag each user that needs access to the S3 bucket. Add the aws:PrincipalTag global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: Principal tags identify attributes assigned to principals, not organization membership. Tagging every user adds ongoing administration and does not automatically exclude an account that leaves the organization.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a VPC. The application processes logs that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket.

The EC2 instance needs to access the S3 bucket without connectivity to the internet.

Which solution will provide private network connectivity to Amazon S3?

choices.solution: Create a gateway VPC endpoint to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation:
Keywords: - EC2 in VPC - EC2 instance needs to access the S3 bucket without connectivity to the internet VPC endpoint allows you to connect to AWS services using a private network instead of using the public Internet. With a gateway endpoint, you can access Amazon S3 from your VPC, without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device for your VPC, and with no additional cost.

However, gateway endpoints do not allow access from on-premises networks, from peered VPCs in other AWS Regions, or through a transit gateway.

choices.solution: Stream the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export the logs to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Exporting logs changes where the data is stored but does not give the EC2 application a private network route to its existing S3 bucket.

choices.solution: Create an instance profile on Amazon EC2 to allow S3 access.
choices.explanation: An instance profile grants permissions. It does not provide network connectivity, so the instance still needs a reachable S3 endpoint.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon API Gateway API with a private link to access the S3 endpoint.
choices.explanation: API Gateway is not a direct VPC endpoint for S3. A private API requires additional integration configuration; the proposed private link alone does not provide the required S3 connection.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon Aurora database. The EC2 instances connect to the database by using user names and passwords that are stored locally in a file.

The company wants to minimize the operational overhead of credential management.

What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this goal?

choices.solution: Use AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation.
choices.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is a secrets management service that helps you protect access to your applications, services, and IT resources. This service enables you to rotate, manage, and retrieve database credentials, API keys, and other secrets throughout their lifecycle.

choices.solution: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation.
choices.explanation: Parameter Store can store encrypted values but does not provide a built-in switch for automatic database-password rotation. Implementing rotation separately adds the operational work this requirement seeks to avoid.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store objects that are encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Migrate the credential file to the S3 bucket.

Point the application to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 and KMS protect the stored credential file but do not rotate the database password or synchronize the application with a new value. Credential lifecycle management remains a custom responsibility.

choices.solution:
Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for each EC2 instance. Attach the new EBS volume to each EC2 instance.

Migrate the credential file to the new EBS volume. Point the application to the new EBS volume.
choices.explanation: EBS encryption protects the volume at rest but leaves separate credential files on the instances. Password rotation and updating every copy still require additional management.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company performs monthly maintenance on its AWS infrastructure. During these maintenance activities, the company needs to rotate the credentials for its Amazon RDS for MySQL databases across multiple AWS Regions.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution:
Store the credentials as secrets in AWS Secrets Manager. Use multi-Region secret replication for the required Regions.

Configure Secrets Manager to rotate the secrets on a schedule.
choices.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager allows you to store, manage, and rotate secrets, such as database credentials, across multiple AWS Regions. By enabling multi-Region secret replication, you can replicate the secrets across the required Regions to allow for seamless rotation of the credentials during maintenance activities.

Additionally, Secrets Manager provides automatic rotation of secrets on a schedule, which would minimize the operational overhead of rotating the credentials on a monthly basis.

choices.solution:
Store the credentials as secrets in AWS Systems Manager by creating a secure string parameter. Use multi-Region secret replication for the required Regions.

Configure Systems Manager to rotate the secrets on a schedule.
choices.explanation: Parameter Store does not offer the Secrets Manager combination of multi-Region secret replication and managed database-secret rotation. Those behaviors would require additional custom automation.
