choices.explanation: STS generates temporary AWS credentials, not one-time SSH keys.

choices.solution: Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
choices.explanation: Shared keys on bastion hosts still violate the requirement to remove all shared keys.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.
choices.explanation: A Cognito authorizer and custom key-generation function add unnecessary credential and access-management code.

Design Secure Architectures.question: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?

choices.solution: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.
choices.explanation: The ACL header controls permissions, not object encryption.

choices.solution: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.
choices.explanation: A private ACL does not select or enforce encryption.

choices.solution: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.
choices.explanation: SecureTransport controls HTTPS transport rather than encryption of the stored object.

choices.solution: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.
choices.explanation: To enforce server-side encryption on uploads, the bucket policy can deny PutObject requests that do not include the x-amz-server-side-encryption header (or otherwise fail the required encryption condition). ACL and SecureTransport conditions do not enforce encryption at rest.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is hosting a web application from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon Cognito as an identity provider to authenticate users and return a JSON Web Token (JWT) that provides access to protected resources that are stored in another S3 bucket.

Upon deployment of the application, users report errors and are unable to access the protected content. A solutions architect must resolve this issue by providing proper permissions so that users can access the protected content.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.
choices.explanation:
Amazon Cognito Identity Pool: When users authenticate through Amazon Cognito, they assume roles that determine their access to AWS resources. By updating the Cognito identity pool, you can configure it to assume the proper IAM role that has the necessary permissions to access the protected content stored in the S3 bucket.

IAM Role Permissions: The IAM role associated with the identity pool should have the required permissions (e.g., S3 getObject permissions) to access the protected content in the S3 bucket.

choices.solution: Update the S3 ACL to allow the application to access the protected content.
choices.explanation: An ACL does not exchange Cognito tokens for IAM credentials and risks granting access more broadly than the intended users.

choices.solution: Redeploy the application to Amazon S3 to prevent eventually consistent reads in the S3 bucket from affecting the ability of users to access the protected content.
choices.explanation: S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency; redeployment does not resolve missing IAM permissions.

choices.solution: Update the Amazon Cognito pool to use custom attribute mappings within the identity pool and grant users the proper permissions to access the protected content.
choices.explanation: Attribute mappings alone do not grant S3 access; the assumed IAM role must carry the required bucket permissions.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect must secure a VPC network that hosts Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances contain highly sensitive data and run in a private subnet.

According to company policy, the EC2 instances that run in the VPC can access only approved third-party software repositories on the internet for software product updates that use the third party's URL. Other internet traffic must be blocked.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Update the route table for the private subnet to route the outbound traffic to an AWS Network Firewall firewall. Configure domain list rule groups.
choices.explanation: Route internet egress through Network Firewall and enforce an allowlist of approved domains with stateful domain rules. Route both traffic directions consistently through the firewall and use NAT where needed.

choices.solution: Set up an AWS WAF web ACL. Create a custom set of rules that filter traffic requests based on source and destination IP address range sets.
choices.explanation: WAF protects inbound HTTP requests to supported front ends; it is not a VPC-wide outbound domain filter.

choices.solution: Implement strict inbound security group rules. Configure an outbound rule that allows traffic only to the authorized software repositories on the internet by specifying the URLs.
choices.explanation: Security-group rules accept IP ranges, prefix lists, and security groups, not arbitrary repository URLs.

choices.solution:
Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances. Direct all outbound traffic to the ALB.

Use a URL-based rule listener in the ALB's target group for outbound access to the internet.
choices.explanation: An ALB routes inbound HTTP requests to targets and is not an outbound internet filtering proxy.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A security audit reveals that Amazon EC2 instances are not being patched regularly. A solutions architect needs to provide a solution that will run regular security scans across a large fleet of EC2 instances.

The solution should also patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule and provide a report of each instance's patch status.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Set up Amazon Macie to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up a cron job on each EC2 instance to patch the instance on a regular schedule.
choices.explanation: Macie discovers sensitive S3 data, not EC2 vulnerabilities, and per-instance cron jobs add management overhead.

choices.solution:
Turn on Amazon GuardDuty in the account. Configure GuardDuty to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities.

Set up AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
choices.explanation: GuardDuty is not the vulnerability scanner, and Session Manager does not schedule patch installation.

choices.solution: Set up Amazon Detective to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
choices.explanation: Detective investigates security findings rather than scanning packages; an EventBridge schedule alone does not perform patch management.

choices.solution:
Turn on Amazon Inspector in the account. Configure Amazon Inspector to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities.

Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
choices.explanation: Inspector detects EC2 software vulnerabilities; Systems Manager Patch Manager applies updates on a schedule. Scanning and patching are separate functions.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is planning to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must encrypt the data at rest.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
choices.explanation:
By creating a key in AWS KMS and enabling encryption for the RDS DB instances, you ensure that the data at rest is encrypted using the specified key. AWS RDS supports encryption at rest, and you can use AWS KMS to manage the encryption keys.

When you enable encryption for an RDS DB instance, you can specify a KMS key to use for encryption.

choices.solution:
Create an encryption key. Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager.

Use the key to encrypt the DB instances.
choices.explanation: Secrets Manager stores secrets but does not provide the KMS key integration used by RDS storage encryption.

choices.solution: Generate a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
choices.explanation: TLS encrypts database network connections, not stored database pages and backups.

choices.solution: Generate a certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
choices.explanation: An IAM certificate does not configure RDS storage encryption; TLS addresses data in transit only.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company needs to provide its employees with secure access to confidential and sensitive files. The company wants to ensure that the files can be accessed only by authorized users.

The files must be downloaded securely to the employees' devices. The files are stored in an on-premises Windows file server.

However, due to an increase in remote usage, the file server is running out of capacity. .

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Migrate the file server to an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet. Configure the security group to limit inbound traffic to the employees' IP addresses.
choices.explanation: A public file server increases exposure and requires server management; IP filtering alone does not preserve AD-based file authorization or secure remote connectivity.

choices.solution:
Migrate the files to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Integrate the Amazon FSx file system with the on-premises Active Directory.

Configure AWS Client VPN.
choices.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server: It is a fully managed file storage service built on Windows Server. It is designed to be integrated with on-premises Active Directory, allowing for a seamless extension of your existing directory and authentication infrastructure to the AWS Cloud.

Integrate with On-Premises Active Directory: With Amazon FSx, you can integrate the file system with your on-premises Active Directory, ensuring that the same user accounts and permissions are used both on-premises and in the cloud.

choices.solution: Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a private VPC endpoint. Create a signed URL to allow download.
choices.explanation: A signed URL is a transferable bearer credential, and a private endpoint also requires a network path for remote employees; this does not preserve Windows AD file-share access.

choices.solution: Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a public VPC endpoint. Allow employees to sign on with AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
choices.explanation: There is no public VPC endpoint of the proposed type, and IAM Identity Center login alone does not authorize arbitrary S3 downloads.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to give a customer the ability to use on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to download files that are stored in Amazon S3. The customer's application uses an SFTP client to download the files.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead and no changes to the customer's application?

choices.solution: Set up AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
choices.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3: AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed service that allows you to set up an SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol) service for Amazon S3. It enables you to transfer files directly to and from Amazon S3 using the SFTP protocol.

Integrated Active Directory Authentication: AWS Transfer Family allows you to configure authentication with Microsoft Active Directory. By integrating with Active Directory, you can provide users with seamless access to S3 resources using their existing credentials without modifying their applications.

choices.solution: Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to synchronize the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
choices.explanation: DMS migrates databases; it does not present an AD-authenticated SFTP interface to S3.

choices.solution: Set up AWS DataSync to synchronize between the on-premises location and the S3 location by using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
choices.explanation: DataSync runs managed transfers rather than exposing the unchanged client's SFTP download endpoint.

choices.solution: Set up a Windows Amazon EC2 instance with SFTP to connect the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Integrate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
choices.explanation: A self-managed SFTP server requires maintenance, and IAM integration alone does not preserve the customer's AD authentication.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company hosts a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances.

The company's IT security guidelines mandate that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.solution:
Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials.

Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.
choices.explanation:
A proposes to create a new AWS KMS encryption key and use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Then, the secret will be associated with the Aurora DB cluster, and a custom rotation period of 14 days will be configured.

AWS Secrets Manager will automate the process of rotating the database credentials, which will reduce the operational effort required to meet the IT security guidelines.

choices.solution:
Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier.

Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.
choices.explanation: Parameter Store requires custom password-rotation code and scheduling compared with Secrets Manager's rotation integration.

choices.solution:
Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier.

Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.
choices.explanation: An EFS credential file adds filesystem access management and custom rotation/synchronization work.

choices.solution:
Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used.

Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: An S3 credential file requires custom refresh and rotation logic and risks stale downloaded credentials.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has a custom application with embedded credentials that retrieves information from an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. Management says the application must be made more secure with the least amount of programming effort.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create keys. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS.

Enable automatic key rotation.
choices.explanation: KMS rotates encryption-key material, not database passwords, and is not a database-credential storage service.

choices.solution:
Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager.

Create an AWS Lambda function that rotates the credentials in Secret Manager.
choices.explanation: Writing a custom rotation function adds work when Secrets Manager supplies the RDS rotation workflow and scheduling.

choices.solution:
Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager.

Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Secrets Manager.
choices.explanation:
C is a valid solution for securing the custom application with the least amount of programming effort. It involves creating credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and storing them in AWS Secrets Manager.

The application can then be configured to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Additionally, the solution includes setting up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Secrets Manager, which will automatically rotate the credentials at a specified interval without requiring any programming effort.

choices.solution:
Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store.

Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Parameter Store.
choices.explanation: Parameter Store has no native database-password rotation schedule; implementing it requires additional automation.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A media company hosts its website on AWS. The website application's architecture includes a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a database that is hosted on Amazon Aurora.

The company's cybersecurity team reports that the application is vulnerable to SQL injection.

How should the company resolve this issue?

choices.solution: Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
choices.explanation:
AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall): AWS WAF is designed to protect web applications from common web exploits, including SQL injection. It allows you to create web access control lists (web ACLs) to define rules that filter and monitor HTTP traffic to your application.

Associating Web ACLs with AWS WAF: By using AWS WAF in front of the ALB, you can define rules to block or allow web requests based on conditions that you specify. This includes protection against SQL injection attempts.

AWS WAF provides a range of conditions and rulesets that you can use to mitigate common security threats.

choices.solution: Create an ALB listener rule to reply to SQL injections with a fixed response.
choices.explanation: ALB listener rules do not implement SQL-injection payload inspection as a WAF managed rule does.

choices.solution: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
choices.explanation: Shield Advanced is DDoS protection; it does not automatically block every SQL-injection attempt.

choices.solution: Set up Amazon Inspector to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
choices.explanation: Inspector reports vulnerabilities rather than filtering incoming SQL-injection requests.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has an Amazon S3 data lake that is governed by AWS Lake Formation. The company wants to create a visualization in Amazon QuickSight by joining the data in the data lake with operational data that is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL database.

The company wants to enforce column-level authorization so that the company's marketing team can access only a subset of columns in the database.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon EMR to ingest the data directly from the database to the QuickSight SPICE engine. Include only the required columns.
choices.explanation: An EMR ingestion pipeline adds infrastructure and does not provide centralized column-level permissions for the lake.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Glue Studio to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Attach an IAM policy to the QuickSight users to enforce column-level access control.

Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.
choices.explanation: IAM policies control AWS resource access, not individual columns within the lake's tables.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Glue Elastic Views to create a materialized view for the database in Amazon S3. Create an S3 bucket policy to enforce column- level access control for the QuickSight users.

Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.
choices.explanation: An S3 bucket policy cannot authorize individual table columns inside object contents.

choices.solution:
Use a Lake Formation blueprint to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Use Lake Formation to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users.

Use Amazon Athena as the data source in QuickSight.
choices.explanation: A Lake Formation blueprint ingests Aurora data into the S3 lake using Glue. Lake Formation enforces column permissions when QuickSight queries through Athena; S3 bucket policies cannot restrict individual table columns.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company stores confidential data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database in the ap-southeast-3 Region. The database is encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key.

The company was recently acquired and must securely share a backup of the database with the acquiring company's AWS account in ap-southeast-3.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create a database snapshot. Copy the snapshot to a new unencrypted snapshot.

Share the new snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
choices.explanation: An encrypted Aurora snapshot cannot be copied into an unencrypted snapshot, and sharing plaintext would defeat secure sharing.

choices.solution:
Create a database snapshot. Add the acquiring company's AWS account to the KMS key policy.

Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
choices.explanation:
sharing encrypted snapshots involves granting permission not only on the snapshot itself but also on the underlying AWS Key Management Service (KMS) key used for encryption. By adding the acquiring company's AWS account to the KMS key policy, you ensure that they have the necessary permissions to decrypt and access the snapshot.

Sharing the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account completes the process, allowing them to restore the database from the shared snapshot.

choices.solution:
Create a database snapshot that uses a different AWS managed KMS key. Add the acquiring company's AWS account to the KMS key alias.

Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
choices.explanation: AWS managed KMS keys cannot have their policy edited for this cross-account sharing, and adding an account to an alias does not grant key use.

choices.solution:
Create a database snapshot. Download the database snapshot.

Upload the database snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the acquiring company's AWS account.
choices.explanation: RDS snapshots cannot be downloaded and uploaded as ordinary restorable snapshot files through S3.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is designing the network for an online multi-player game. The game uses the UDP networking protocol and will be deployed in eight AWS Regions.

The network architecture needs to minimize latency and packet loss to give end users a high-quality gaming experience.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Setup a transit gateway in each Region. Create inter-Region peering attachments between each transit gateway.
choices.explanation: Transit gateways connect private networks but do not provide the global edge entry points and user-path optimization of Global Accelerator.

choices.solution: Set up AWS Global Accelerator with UDP listeners and endpoint groups in each Region.
choices.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator is designed to improve the availability and performance of applications by using static IP addresses (Anycast) and directing traffic over the AWS global network. It provides low-latency and high-performance routing, making it well-suited for applications with a global user base, such as multi-player games.

By setting up UDP listeners and endpoint groups in each Region with AWS Global Accelerator, you can efficiently route traffic to the nearest game servers, reducing latency and improving the overall gaming experience.

choices.solution: Set up Amazon CloudFront with UDP turned on. Configure an origin in each Region.
choices.explanation: CloudFront does not support arbitrary UDP traffic; there is no UDP enablement option.

choices.solution: Set up a VPC peering mesh between each Region. Turn on UDP for each VPC.
choices.explanation: VPC peering connects private VPC networks rather than accelerating internet users into the nearest healthy regional game endpoint.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A hospital needs to store patient records in an Amazon S3 bucket. The hospital's compliance team must ensure that all protected health information (PHI) is encrypted in transit and at rest.

The compliance team must administer the encryption key for data at rest.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create a public SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Associate the certificate with Amazon S3.

Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
choices.explanation: An ACM certificate cannot be attached to the S3 service endpoint as proposed; enforce S3 HTTPS with a bucket-policy condition.

choices.solution:
Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3).

Assign the compliance team to manage the SSE-S3 keys.
choices.explanation: SSE-S3 keys are controlled by S3 and cannot be administered by the hospital's compliance team.

choices.solution:
Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
choices.explanation: it allows the compliance team to manage the KMS keys used for server-side encryption, thereby providing the necessary control over the encryption keys. Additionally, the use of the "aws:SecureTransport" condition on the bucket policy ensures that all connections to the S3 bucket are encrypted in transit.

choices.solution:
Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Use Amazon Macie to protect the sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3.

Assign the compliance team to manage Macie.
choices.explanation: Macie discovers sensitive data but does not encrypt stored objects or give the team control of encryption keys.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon API Gateway to run a private gateway with two REST APIs in the same VPC. The BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service to ensure that enough funds are available before a stock can be purchased.

The company has noticed in the VPC flow logs that the BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service over the internet instead of through the VPC. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the APIs communicate through the VPC.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?

choices.solution: Add an X-API-Key header in the HTTP header for authorization.
choices.explanation: An API key does not change the network route or provide private connectivity.

choices.solution: Use an interface endpoint.
choices.explanation: Interface Endpoint (VPC Endpoint for API Gateway): An interface endpoint allows private connectivity to API Gateway within your VPC. By creating a VPC endpoint for API Gateway, you can ensure that the communication between the BuyStock and CheckFunds RESTful web services stays within the VPC, eliminating the need for traffic to go over the internet.

choices.solution: Use a gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: API Gateway uses interface endpoints; gateway endpoints are for S3 and DynamoDB.

choices.solution: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue between the two REST APIs.
choices.explanation: Introducing a queue changes the synchronous API interaction and does not itself supply a private API endpoint.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A hospital is designing a new application that gathers symptoms from patients. The hospital has decided to use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) and Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) in the architecture.

A solutions architect is reviewing the infrastructure design. Data must be encrypted at rest and in transit.

Only authorized personnel of the hospital should be able to access the data.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.
choices.explanation: This does not enforce encrypted transport or explicitly select a customer-managed key whose policy the hospital controls.

choices.solution: Turn on server-side encryption on the SNS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply a key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.
choices.explanation: SNS server-side encryption with a customer managed KMS key protects message data at rest and gives control over key use.

choices.solution:
Turn on encryption on the SNS components. Update the default key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.

Set a condition in the topic policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.
choices.explanation: An AWS-managed/default key policy cannot be customized as proposed; choose a customer-managed KMS key for explicit principal restrictions.

choices.solution:
Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply a key policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.

Set a condition in the queue policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.
choices.explanation: SQS SSE-KMS protects queued message data at rest. A queue policy that denies aws:SecureTransport=false enforces TLS in transit.

choices.solution:
Turn on server-side encryption on the SQS components by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Apply an IAM policy to restrict key usage to a set of authorized principals.

Set a condition in the queue policy to allow only encrypted connections over TLS.
choices.explanation: An IAM allow policy alone does not establish the key's permitted principals and cannot override other key-policy grants; the selected design directly configures the KMS key policy.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company's web application consists of an Amazon API Gateway API in front of an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB database. The Lambda function handles the business logic, and the DynamoDB table hosts the data.

The application uses Amazon Cognito user pools to identify the individual users of the application. A solutions architect needs to update the application so that only users who have a subscription can access premium content.

Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Enable API caching and throttling on the API Gateway API.
choices.explanation: Caching and throttling control performance and request rates, not subscription entitlement.

choices.solution: Set up AWS WAF on the API Gateway API. Create a rule to filter users who have a subscription.
choices.explanation: WAF inspects request patterns; it does not natively verify a user's subscription record.

choices.solution: Apply fine-grained IAM permissions to the premium content in the DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB IAM permissions alone do not enforce the subscription check at this Cognito-authenticated application API.

choices.solution: Use a Cognito user-pool authorizer in API Gateway and require a premium-content OAuth scope that is issued only to users with an active subscription. Enforce subscription entitlement when issuing or refreshing tokens.
choices.explanation:
Cognito verifies the user token and API Gateway enforces the required premium scope. Subscription state must govern which users receive that scope.

API keys and usage plans can meter usage, but must not be used as the sole authentication or authorization mechanism.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect wants all new users to have specific complexity requirements and mandatory rotation periods for IAM user passwords.

What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

choices.solution: Set an overall password policy for the entire AWS account.
choices.explanation:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) allows you to set an account-wide password policy using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). This policy defines the rules and requirements for all IAM users in the AWS account.

It's a centralized approach to enforce security measures consistently across all users. In this case, the solutions architect can set the specific complexity requirements and mandatory rotation periods by configuring the password policy at the AWS account level.

choices.solution: Set a password policy for each IAM user in the AWS account.
choices.explanation: IAM password complexity and expiration settings are an account-level policy, not individual per-user policies.

choices.solution: Use third-party vendor software to set password requirements.
choices.explanation: Third-party software adds unnecessary management when IAM provides the password policy directly.

choices.solution: Attach an Amazon CloudWatch rule to the Create_newuser event to set the password with the appropriate requirements.
choices.explanation: Custom event automation is unnecessary and does not establish the account's ongoing password complexity and expiration requirements.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company runs a public three-tier web application in a VPC. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones.

The EC2 instances that run in private subnets need to communicate with a license server over the internet. The company needs a managed solution that minimizes operational maintenance.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Provision a NAT instance in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
choices.explanation: A NAT instance requires patching and capacity management instead of the requested managed service.

choices.solution: Provision a NAT instance in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT instance.
choices.explanation: A NAT instance in a private subnet has no direct internet egress and still requires server maintenance.

choices.solution: Provision a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
choices.explanation:
NAT Gateway: A NAT gateway is a managed service provided by AWS that allows EC2 instances in private subnets to initiate outbound traffic to the internet while preventing unsolicited inbound traffic from reaching those instances. NAT gateways are fully managed, highly available, and require minimal maintenance.

Public Subnet: Placing the NAT gateway in a public subnet allows it to have access to the internet, fulfilling the requirement for private instances to communicate with a license server over the internet. Default Route: Modifying each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway ensures that traffic from private instances is directed through the NAT gateway for outbound communication.

choices.solution: Provision a NAT gateway in a private subnet. Modify each private subnet's route table with a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: A NAT gateway must be in a public subnet with internet-gateway routing to provide public internet egress.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company needs to create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster to host a digital media streaming application. The EKS cluster will use a managed node group that is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes for storage.

The company must encrypt all data at rest by using a customer managed key that is stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

Which combination of actions will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Use a Kubernetes plugin that uses the customer managed key to perform data encryption.
choices.explanation: A filesystem plugin adds custom encryption management instead of using native EBS encryption.

choices.solution: After creation of the EKS cluster, locate the EBS volumes. Enable encryption by using the customer managed key.
choices.explanation: Encryption cannot be enabled in place on an existing unencrypted EBS volume; new encrypted volumes must be created.

choices.solution: Enable EBS encryption by default in the AWS Region where the EKS cluster will be created. Select the customer managed key as the default key.
choices.explanation: Enable EBS encryption by default in the target Region and select the customer managed key before creating the managed node group.

choices.solution: Create the EKS cluster and managed node group. Grant the node group's Auto Scaling service-linked role the required permissions and grants for the customer managed KMS key.
choices.explanation: Authorize the managed node group's Auto Scaling service-linked role to use the KMS key, including grant creation. Attaching a KMS policy only to the EKS cluster role is insufficient for encrypted node volumes.

choices.solution: Store the customer managed key as a Kubernetes secret in the EKS cluster. Use the customer managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: KMS key material is not exported into Kubernetes secrets; applications use KMS permissions and key identifiers.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has a three-tier application on AWS that ingests sensor data from its users' devices. The traffic flows through a Network Load Balancer (NLB), then to Amazon EC2 instances for the web tier, and finally to EC2 instances for the application tier.

The application tier makes calls to a database.

What should a solutions architect do to improve the security of the data in transit?

choices.solution: Configure a TLS listener. Deploy the server certificate on the NLB.
choices.explanation: TLS Listener on NLB: By configuring a TLS (Transport Layer Security) listener on the NLB, you can encrypt the traffic between the users' devices and the web tier EC2 instances. This helps protect the data in transit from eavesdropping and other potential security threats.

choices.solution: Configure AWS Shield Advanced. Enable AWS WAF on the NLB.
choices.explanation: Shield protects against DDoS rather than encrypting connections, and WAF cannot be directly associated with an NLB.

choices.solution: Change the load balancer to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Enable AWS WAF on the ALB.
choices.explanation: WAF filters requests but does not by itself configure TLS encryption for the application's traffic.

choices.solution: Encrypt the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instances by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
choices.explanation: EBS encryption protects data at rest, not data traveling between clients and application tiers.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is creating a new VPC design. There are two public subnets for the load balancer, two private subnets for web servers, and two private subnets for MySQL.

The web servers use only HTTPS. The solutions architect has already created a security group for the load balancer allowing port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.

Company policy requires that each resource has the least access required to still be able to perform its tasks.

Which additional configuration strategy should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
choices.explanation: Allowing HTTPS from every address admits sources beyond the load balancer and violates least privilege.

choices.solution: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
choices.explanation: Network ACLs cannot reference a security group as a source, and the broad HTTPS rule does not restrict traffic to the load balancer.

choices.solution: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
choices.explanation: Security-group references restrict HTTPS to traffic from the load balancer and MySQL to traffic from the web tier, instead of opening database ports to arbitrary hosts.

choices.solution: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
choices.explanation: Network ACLs cannot use security-group references; security groups can identify the application tiers directly.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A new employee has joined a company as a deployment engineer. The deployment engineer will be using AWS CloudFormation templates to create multiple AWS resources.

A solutions architect wants the deployment engineer to perform job activities while following the principle of least privilege.

Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Have the deployment engineer use AWS account root user credentials for performing AWS CloudFormation stack operations.
choices.explanation: Root credentials grant unrestricted account access and violate least privilege.

choices.solution: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the PowerUsers IAM policy attached.
choices.explanation: PowerUserAccess grants far broader permissions than the particular stack deployment requires.

choices.solution: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the AdministratorAccess IAM policy attached.
choices.explanation: AdministratorAccess grants unrestricted permissions rather than narrowly scoped stack operations and a service role.

choices.solution: Grant the deployment engineer only the required CloudFormation stack actions and narrowly scoped iam:PassRole permission for the stack's service role.
choices.explanation: Give the deployment identity only the required CloudFormation stack actions and narrowly scoped iam:PassRole permission.

choices.solution: Create a CloudFormation service role with only the permissions needed for the stack's resources, and specify that role when launching the stack.
choices.explanation: Use a CloudFormation service role with only the permissions needed to create stack resources. CloudFormation assumes this role instead of requiring broad permissions on the deployment user.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is deploying a two-tier web application in a VPC. The web tier is using an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with public subnets that span multiple Availability Zones.

The database tier consists of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in separate private subnets. The web tier requires access to the database to retrieve product information.

The web application is not working as intended. The web application reports that it cannot connect to the database.

The database is confirmed to be up and running. All configurations for the network ACLs, security groups, and route tables are still in their default states.

What should a solutions architect recommend to fix the application?

choices.solution: Add an explicit rule to the private subnet's network ACL to allow traffic from the web tier's EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: The default network ACL already permits traffic, so an additional ACL rule does not fix the missing database security-group permission.

choices.solution: Add a route in the VPC route table to allow traffic between the web tier's EC2 instances and the database tier.
choices.explanation: The VPC's local route already connects its subnets; no additional intra-VPC route is needed.

choices.solution: Deploy the web tier's EC2 instances and the database tier's RDS instance into two separate VPCs, and configure VPC peering.
choices.explanation: Splitting the tiers into separate VPCs adds complexity and does not remove the need for the database ingress rule.

choices.solution: Add an inbound rule to the security group of the database tier's RDS instance to allow traffic from the web tiers security group.
choices.explanation:
Security Groups: Security groups act as virtual firewalls for your instances to control inbound and outbound traffic. By default, they deny all inbound traffic.

In this scenario, the default security group associated with the RDS instance is likely denying incoming traffic from the web tier. Inbound Rule: To allow traffic from the web tier's EC2 instances to the database tier's RDS instance, you need to add an inbound rule to the security group associated with the RDS instance.

This rule should permit traffic from the security group associated with the web tier's EC2 instances.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to deploy a new public web application on AWS. The application includes a web server tier that uses Amazon EC2 instances.

The application also includes a database tier that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The application must be secure and accessible for global customers that have dynamic IP addresses.

How should a solutions architect configure the security groups to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from the security group of the web servers.
choices.explanation: Public HTTPS access reaches the web tier, while a security-group reference permits MySQL access only from the web servers.

choices.solution: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from the IP addresses of the customers. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from the security group of the web servers.
choices.explanation: A static customer IP allowlist fails as globally distributed customers' addresses change.

choices.solution: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from the IP addresses of the customers. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from the IP addresses of the customers.
choices.explanation: Customer IP allowlists are unsuitable for dynamic addresses, and customers should not connect directly to the database.

choices.solution: Configure the security group for the web servers to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Configure the security group for the DB instance to allow inbound traffic on port 3306 from 0.0.0.0/0.
choices.explanation: Allowing MySQL from every IPv4 address exposes the database beyond the application tier.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
An IAM user made several configuration changes to AWS resources in their company's account during a production deployment last week. A solutions architect learned that a couple of security group rules are not configured as desired.

The solutions architect wants to confirm which IAM user was responsible for making changes.

Which service should the solutions architect use to find the desired information?

choices.solution: Amazon GuardDuty
choices.explanation: GuardDuty detects suspicious activity but is not the authoritative API audit trail identifying the principal for this change.

choices.solution: Amazon Inspector
choices.explanation: Inspector reports workload vulnerabilities, not the user who changed a security-group rule.

choices.solution: AWS CloudTrail
choices.explanation: AWS CloudTrail is a service provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS) that allows you to monitor and log AWS account activity. It records API calls made on your AWS account, capturing information such as the identity of the caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address, the request parameters, and the response elements returned by the AWS service.

choices.solution: AWS Config
choices.explanation: Config records configuration history; CloudTrail directly records the API caller and change request.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has implemented a self-managed DNS service on AWS. The solution consists of the following:
* Amazon EC2 instances in different AWS Regions
* Endpoints of a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator The company wants to protect the solution against DDoS attacks.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the accelerator as a resource to protect.
choices.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced is a managed Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) protection service provided by AWS. By subscribing to AWS Shield Advanced, you gain access to enhanced DDoS protection capabilities, including automatic detection and mitigation of DDoS attacks.

choices.solution: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the EC2 instances as resources to protect.
choices.explanation: Shield Advanced protects supported public-facing resources such as the accelerator and EC2 Elastic IPs, not arbitrary EC2 instance IDs as proposed.

choices.solution: Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the accelerator.
choices.explanation: WAF cannot be associated directly with Global Accelerator and does not inspect DNS UDP traffic.

choices.solution: Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: WAF cannot be directly associated with EC2 instances and is not a DNS protocol DDoS filter.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A financial company hosts a web application on AWS. The application uses an Amazon API Gateway Regional API endpoint to give users the ability to retrieve current stock prices.

The company's security team has noticed an increase in the number of API requests. The security team is concerned that HTTP flood attacks might take the application offiine.

A solutions architect must design a solution to protect the application from this type of attack.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the API Gateway Regional API endpoint with a maximum TTL of 24 hours.
choices.explanation: A long cache TTL neither rate-limits malicious requests nor reliably serves current stock prices.

choices.solution: Create a Regional AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the API Gateway stage.
choices.explanation:
Rate-based Rule with AWS WAF: AWS WAF provides protection against various web application attacks, including HTTP flood attacks. By using a rate-based rule, you can set thresholds for the number of requests from a client IP within a specified time period.

This helps in detecting and mitigating HTTP flood attacks effectively.

choices.solution: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the Count metric and alert the security team when the predefined rate is reached.
choices.explanation: Monitoring and alerting detect the flood but do not automatically block it.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with Lambda@Edge in front of the API Gateway Regional API endpoint. Create an AWS Lambda function to block requests from IP addresses that exceed the predefined rate.
choices.explanation: Custom edge rate-limit code adds development and operational work compared with a managed WAF rate-based rule.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A developer has an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to upload files to Amazon S3 and needs the required permissions to perform the task. The developer already has an IAM user with valid IAM credentials required for Amazon S3.

What should a solutions architect do to grant the permissions?

choices.solution: Add required IAM permissions in the resource policy of the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: The Lambda resource policy controls invocation of the function, not its outgoing S3 permissions.

choices.solution: Create a signed request using the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: Using a user's credentials embeds long-lived secrets instead of the execution role's temporary credentials.

choices.solution: Create a new IAM user and use the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: Creating another user does not provide the function with automatically managed role credentials and increases credential-management work.

choices.solution: Create an IAM execution role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: o grant the necessary permissions to an AWS Lambda function to upload files to Amazon S3, a solutions architect should create an IAM execution role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the Lambda function. This approach follows the principle of least privilege and ensures that the Lambda function can only access the resources it needs to perform its specific task.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application writes data to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.

The company needs to ensure that all data that is written to the EBS volumes is encrypted at rest.

Which solution will meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Create an IAM role that specifies EBS encryption. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: An IAM role controls permissions; attaching it does not change an EBS volume's encryption state.

choices.solution: Create the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes. Attach the EBS volumes to the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: By creating the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes, you ensure that all data written to those volumes is automatically encrypted. This provides a straightforward and effective solution for meeting the encryption-at-rest requirement.

choices.solution: Create an EC2 instance tag that has a key of Encrypt and a value of True. Tag all instances that require encryption at the EBS level.
choices.explanation: An Encrypt tag is metadata and does not activate storage encryption.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policy that enforces EBS encryption in the account. Ensure that the key policy is active.
choices.explanation: A KMS key policy controls use of that key; it does not force every new EBS volume to use encryption.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
An image-hosting company stores its objects in Amazon S3 buckets. The company wants to avoid accidental exposure of the objects in the S3 buckets to the public.

All S3 objects in the entire AWS account need to remain private.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor S3 bucket policies. Create an automatic remediation action rule that uses an AWS Lambda function to remediate any change that makes the objects public.
choices.explanation: Detecting and remediating public access after a change leaves an exposure window instead of preventing the change.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Configure email notifications in Trusted Advisor when a change is detected.

Manually change the S3 bucket policy if it allows public access.
choices.explanation: Manual remediation is delayed and permits public exposure until someone responds.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Resource Access Manager to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a change is detected.

Deploy a Lambda function that programmatically remediates the change.
choices.explanation: RAM shares supported resources; it is not the proposed S3 public-access detection and enforcement service.

choices.solution:
Use the S3 Block Public Access feature on the account level. Use AWS Organizations to create a service control policy (SCP) that prevents IAM users from changing the setting.

Apply the SCP to the account.
choices.explanation:
AWS Organizations allows you to create service control policies (SCPs) that set fine-grained permissions for member accounts. In this case, you can create an SCP that prevents IAM users from changing the S3 Block Public Access settings.

Applying this SCP to the account ensures that the configured public access settings remain in place and cannot be altered by IAM users.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions to run its application. The company has VPCs with public subnets and private subnets in its AWS account.

The EC2 instances run in a private subnet in one of the VPCs. The Lambda functions need direct network access to the EC2 instances for the application to work.

The application will run for at least 1 year. The company expects the number of Lambda functions that the application uses to increase during that time.

The company wants to maximize its savings on all application resources and to keep network latency between the services low.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan Optimize the Lambda functions' duration and memory usage and the number of invocations. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not discount Lambda usage.

choices.solution: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan Optimize the Lambda functions' duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Connect the Lambda functions to a public subnet in the same VPC where the EC2 instances run.
choices.explanation: The plan excludes Lambda, and placing a Lambda interface in a public subnet does not itself give the function public internet access or lower latency.

choices.solution:
Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions' duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred.

Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Compute Savings Plans cover both eligible EC2 and Lambda usage. Configure Lambda VPC access to the private subnets so it can reach the EC2 instances directly; a public subnet does not give Lambda a public IP.

choices.solution:
Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions' duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred.

Keep the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC.
choices.explanation: Keeping Lambda outside the customer VPC prevents direct access to the instances' private addresses.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to allow team members to access Amazon S3 buckets in two different AWS accounts: a development account and a production account. The team currently has access to S3 buckets in the development account by using unique IAM users that are assigned to an IAM group that has appropriate permissions in the account.

The solutions architect has created an IAM role in the production account. The role has a policy that grants access to an S3 bucket in the production account.

Which solution will meet these requirements while complying with the principle of least privilege?

choices.solution: Attach the Administrator Access policy to the development account users.
choices.explanation: AdministratorAccess grants far more permissions than the bucket-access and role-assumption requirements.

choices.solution: Add the development account as a principal in the trust policy of the role in the production account.
choices.explanation: By adding the development account as a principal in the trust policy of the IAM role in the production account, you enable IAM users in the development account to assume the role and gain temporary permissions to access the S3 bucket in the production account. This approach follows the principle of least privilege because it allows users in the development account to access only the specific resources (S3 bucket) defined in the trust policy of the IAM role.

choices.solution: Turn off the S3 Block Public Access feature on the S3 bucket in the production account.
choices.explanation: Disabling Block Public Access does not authenticate team members and risks exposing the bucket.

choices.solution: Create a user in the production account with unique credentials for each team member.
choices.explanation: Duplicating IAM users creates another set of long-lived credentials instead of using the existing identities to assume a scoped role.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and runs multiple Amazon EC2 workloads in the ap-southeast-2 Region. The company has a service control policy (SCP) that prevents any resources from being created in any other Region.

A security policy requires the company to encrypt all data at rest. An audit discovers that employees have created Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes for EC2 instances without encrypting the volumes.

The company wants any new EC2 instances that any IAM user or root user launches in ap-southeast-2 to use encrypted EBS volumes. The company wants a solution that will have minimal effect on employees who create EBS volumes.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: In each member account, enable EBS encryption by default in ap-southeast-2 and select a default KMS key.
choices.explanation: Enable EBS encryption by default in ap-southeast-2 in each member account and choose a default KMS key.

choices.solution:
Create an IAM permission boundary. Attach the permission boundary to the root organizational unit (OU).

Define the boundary to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
choices.explanation: A permissions boundary attaches to an IAM user or role, not an Organizations OU, and does not constrain member-account root users.

choices.solution:
Create an SCP. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU).

Define the SCP to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
choices.explanation: An SCP denies unencrypted CreateVolume requests in member accounts. Add appropriate RunInstances protections where needed; an SCP does not affect the management account.

choices.solution: Update the IAM policies for each account to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
choices.explanation: Per-identity IAM policies do not constrain root users and add maintenance across accounts and identities.

choices.solution: In the Organizations management account, specify the Default EBS volume encryption setting.
choices.explanation: Default EBS encryption is configured per account and Region; enabling it in the management account does not enable it for member accounts.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A serverless application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. The Lambda function needs permissions to read and write to the DynamoDB table.

Which solution will give the Lambda function access to the DynamoDB table MOST securely?

choices.solution:
Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table.

Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters as part of the Lambda environment variables. Ensure that other AWS users do not have read and write access to the Lambda function configuration.
choices.explanation: Environment-variable user keys are long-lived credentials that require manual rotation and are exposed to principals allowed to read configuration.

choices.solution:
Create an IAM role that includes Lambda as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table.

Update the configuration of the Lambda function to use the new role as the execution role.
choices.explanation:
IAM Role with Lambda as a Trusted Service: This approach follows the principle of least privilege. You create an IAM role that specifically grants the required permissions to access DynamoDB and makes Lambda a trusted service.

This ensures that only Lambda functions associated with this role can assume it.

choices.solution:
Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table.

Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as secure string parameters. Update the Lambda function code to retrieve the secure string parameters before connecting to the DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation: Encrypted stored user keys still require credential retrieval and rotation instead of automatically managed execution-role credentials.

choices.solution:
Create an IAM role that includes DynamoDB as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access from the Lambda function.

Update the code of the Lambda function to attach to the new role as an execution role.
choices.explanation: The role must trust Lambda to assume it; trusting DynamoDB does not allow Lambda to use it as an execution role.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
The following IAM policy is attached to an IAM group. This is the only policy applied to the group.

{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "1", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:*", "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "ec2:Region": "us-east-1" } } }, { "Sid": "2", "Effect": "Deny", "Action": [ "ec2:StopInstances", "ec2:TerminateInstances" ], "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "BoolIfExists": { "aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent": false } } } ] }

What are the effective IAM permissions of this policy for group members?

choices.solution: Group members are permitted any Amazon EC2 action within the us-east-1 Region. Statements after the Allow permission are not applied.
choices.explanation: IAM evaluates all applicable statements; an explicit deny overrides an allow regardless of statement order.

choices.solution: Group members are denied any Amazon EC2 permissions in the us-east-1 Region unless they are logged in with multi-factor authentication (MFA).
choices.explanation: Only StopInstances and TerminateInstances have the MFA-related deny, not every EC2 action.

choices.solution: Group members are allowed the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances permissions for all Regions when logged in with multi- factor authentication (MFA). Group members are permitted any other Amazon EC2 action.
choices.explanation: The allow applies only in us-east-1; satisfying MFA does not create permissions in other Regions.

choices.solution: Group members are allowed the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances permissions for the us-east-1 Region only when logged in with multi-factor authentication (MFA). Group members are permitted any other Amazon EC2 action within the us-east-1 Region.
choices.explanation:
The Allow statement permits EC2 actions only in us-east-1. The explicit Deny blocks StopInstances and TerminateInstances when MFA is absent or false.

Therefore those two actions are allowed in us-east-1 only when MFA is present, while other EC2 actions remain allowed there.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company wants to use machine learning (ML) algorithms to build and train models. The company will use the models to visualize complex scenarios and to detect trends in customer data.

The architecture team wants to integrate its ML models with a reporting platform to analyze the augmented data and use the data directly in its business intelligence dashboards.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue to create an ML transform to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
choices.explanation: Glue ML transforms target data preparation such as record matching, not the general model-development and BI integration requested.

choices.solution: Use Amazon SageMaker to build and train models. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
choices.explanation:
Amazon SageMaker: It is a fully managed service for building, training, and deploying machine learning models. SageMaker simplifies the ML workflow and reduces operational overhead.

It provides a fully managed Jupyter Notebook instance for model development and training, and it can seamlessly integrate with other AWS services. QuickSight can directly connect to Amazon SageMaker models and use the results for visualization without the need for extensive data movement or transformation.

choices.solution: Use a pre-built ML Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the AWS Marketplace to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
choices.explanation: A marketplace AMI requires managing training servers, while OpenSearch adds a separate visualization platform instead of native BI integration.

choices.solution: Use Amazon QuickSight to build and train models by using calculated fields. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
choices.explanation: QuickSight calculated fields do not train arbitrary custom ML models as SageMaker does.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is running its production and nonproduction environment workloads in multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are in an organization in AWS Organizations.

The company needs to design a solution that will prevent the modification of cost usage tags.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a custom AWS Config rule to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
choices.explanation: Config detects and reports changes after they occur rather than denying unauthorized tag modification.

choices.solution: Create a custom trail in AWS CloudTrail to prevent tag modification.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records changes but does not prevent the API actions.

choices.solution: Create a service control policy (SCP) to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
choices.explanation: SCPs in AWS Organizations are used to set fine-grained permissions on what actions AWS accounts within the organization can perform. You can create a custom SCP to specifically control access to tag modification.

choices.solution: Create custom Amazon CloudWatch logs to prevent tag modification.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch logs observe activity; they are not an authorization boundary preventing tag changes.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to share accounting data with an external auditor. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS DB instance that resides in a private subnet.

The auditor has its own AWS account and requires its own copy of the database.

What is the MOST secure way for the company to share the database with the auditor?

choices.solution: Create a read replica of the database. Configure IAM standard database authentication to grant the auditor access.
choices.explanation: A read replica remains associated with the company's environment rather than providing the auditor its own independently restored copy.

choices.solution:
Export the database contents to text files. Store the files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Create a new IAM user for the auditor. Grant the user access to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Text exports require reconstructing the database and create another IAM credential instead of scoped encrypted snapshot sharing.

choices.solution:
Copy a snapshot of the database to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an IAM user.

Share the user's keys with the auditor to grant access to the object in the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: An RDS snapshot cannot be copied into S3 as an ordinary restorable file, and sharing long-lived user keys is unnecessary.

choices.solution:
Create an encrypted snapshot of the database. Share the snapshot with the auditor.

Allow access to the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key.
choices.explanation:
Share a manual encrypted RDS snapshot and its customer managed KMS key with the auditor's account. The auditor copies the snapshot using a key it controls and restores an independent database.

Snapshots encrypted with the default AWS managed RDS key cannot be shared directly.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect configured a VPC that has a small range of IP addresses. The number of Amazon EC2 instances that are in the VPC is increasing, and there is an insufficient number of IP addresses for future workloads.

Which solution resolves this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Add an additional IPv4 CIDR block to increase the number of IP addresses and create additional subnets in the VPC. Create new resources in the new subnets by using the new CIDR.
choices.explanation: By adding an additional IPv4 CIDR block to the existing VPC, you can effectively increase the number of available IP addresses within the same VPC. Creating additional subnets using the new CIDR block allows you to organize your resources and maintain segmentation within the VPC.

choices.solution: Create a second VPC with additional subnets. Use a peering connection to connect the second VPC with the first VPC Update the routes and create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
choices.explanation: A second VPC and peering require additional network resources and routing that a secondary CIDR in the existing VPC avoids.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Transit Gateway to add a transit gateway and connect a second VPC with the first VPC. Update the routes of the transit gateway and VPCs.

Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
choices.explanation: A transit gateway adds cost and configuration for an address-capacity issue solvable inside the existing VPC.

choices.solution:
Create a second VPC. Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the first VPC and the second VPC by using a VPN-hosted solution on Amazon EC2 and a virtual private gateway.

Update the route between VPCs to the traffic through the VPN. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
choices.explanation: Self-managed VPN connectivity adds servers, routing, and failure points unnecessarily.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company stores several petabytes of data across multiple AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Lake Formation to manage its data lake.

The company's data science team wants to securely share selective data from its accounts with the company's engineering team for analytical purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution:
Copy the required data to a common account. Create an IAM access role in that account.

Grant access by specifying a permission policy that includes users from the engineering team accounts as trusted entities.
choices.explanation: Copying petabytes duplicates storage and requires ongoing synchronization across accounts.

choices.solution: Use the Lake Formation permissions Grant command in each account where the data is stored to allow the required engineering team users to access the data.
choices.explanation: Individual resource/user grants require more repeated administration than tag-based policies across many datasets.

choices.solution: Use AWS Data Exchange to privately publish the required data to the required engineering team accounts.
choices.explanation: Data Exchange adds data-publication workflows when Lake Formation already governs the shared lake.

choices.solution: Use Lake Formation tag-based access control to authorize and grant cross-account permissions for the required data to the engineering team accounts.
choices.explanation:
Lake Formation allows you to use tag-based access control to authorize and grant permissions for data in the data lake. You can apply tags to databases and tables, and then use those tags to control access to the data.

By applying tags to the relevant data and using tag-based access control, you can easily manage access to specific data sets without having to create additional IAM roles or copy data to a common account.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has two VPCs named Management and Production. The Management VPC uses VPNs through a customer gateway to connect to a single device in the data center.
