The Production VPC uses a virtual private gateway with two attached AWS Direct Connect connections. The Management and Production VPCs both use a single VPC peering connection to allow communication between the applications.

What should a solutions architect do to mitigate any single point of failure in this architecture?

choices.solution: Add a set of VPNs between the Management and Production VPCs.
choices.explanation: Additional connections between VPCs do not remove the single on-premises customer gateway device.

choices.solution: Add a second virtual private gateway and attach it to the Management VPC.
choices.explanation: Another AWS gateway does not eliminate failure of the one customer gateway device, and a VPC cannot attach multiple virtual private gateways as proposed.

choices.solution: Add a second set of VPNs to the Management VPC from a second customer gateway device.
choices.explanation: Adding a second set of VPN connections from the Management VPC to a second customer gateway device provides redundancy and eliminates this single point of failure.

choices.solution: Add a second VPC peering connection between the Management VPC and the Production VPC.
choices.explanation: VPC peering is already managed and redundant; a second connection between the same VPCs does not fix the customer gateway failure point.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is migrating its applications and databases to the AWS Cloud. The company will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), AWS Direct Connect, and Amazon RDS.

Which activities will be managed by the company's operational team? (Choose three.)

choices.solution: Management of the Amazon RDS infrastructure layer, operating system, and platforms
choices.explanation: AWS manages the RDS infrastructure and operating system; customers configure and use the database service.

choices.solution: Creation of an Amazon RDS DB instance and configuring the scheduled maintenance window
choices.explanation: The customer selects RDS configuration and schedules maintenance within the options provided by the managed service.

choices.solution: Configuration of additional software components on Amazon ECS for monitoring, patch management, log management, and host intrusion detection
choices.explanation: The customer configures application monitoring, logging, and security tools. With ECS on EC2, the customer also manages and patches the container hosts.

choices.solution: Installation of patches for all minor and major database versions for Amazon RDS
choices.explanation: AWS performs RDS engine patch installation; customers choose maintenance settings and approve or schedule applicable upgrades.

choices.solution: Ensure the physical security of the Amazon RDS infrastructure in the data center
choices.explanation: AWS is responsible for physical security of its data centers.

choices.solution: Encryption of the data that moves in transit through Direct Connect
choices.explanation: Direct Connect does not encrypt traffic by default; the customer configures TLS, a VPN, or supported MACsec encryption as required.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations. The company wants to operate some of its AWS accounts with different budgets.

The company wants to receive alerts and automatically prevent provisioning of additional resources on AWS accounts when the allocated budget threshold is met during a specific period.

Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

choices.solution: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Cost and Usage Reports section of the required AWS accounts.
choices.explanation: Cost and Usage Reports is an export/reporting configuration, not the place to establish the proposed AWS Budgets budget.

choices.solution: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Billing dashboards of the required AWS accounts.
choices.explanation: AWS Budgets tracks costs against the configured account budget threshold.

choices.solution: Create an IAM user for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.
choices.explanation: Budgets actions assume an IAM role, not a user's long-lived credentials.

choices.solution: Create an IAM role for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.
choices.explanation: A Budgets action role provides permissions to apply the chosen corrective action.

choices.solution: Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate config rule to prevent provisioning of additional resources.
choices.explanation: Config rules detect compliance states after provisioning; an SCP supplies the preventive API permission boundary.

choices.solution: Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate service control policy (SCP) to prevent provisioning of additional resources.
choices.explanation: An alert notifies the company, and a budget action applies an SCP to restrict further provisioning. Budget evaluation is delayed, so it is not a hard real-time spending cap.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to securely exchange data between its software as a service (SaaS) application Salesforce account and Amazon S3. The company must encrypt the data at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys (CMKs).

The company must also encrypt the data in transit. The company has enabled API access for the Salesforce account.

choices.solution: Create AWS Lambda functions to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Custom Lambda integration requires maintaining authentication, API pagination, transfers, and error handling.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Define the task to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Step Functions requires implementing the actual Salesforce transfer tasks and connector logic.

choices.solution: Create Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation:
Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed integration service that allows you to securely transfer data between AWS services and SaaS applications like Salesforce. It supports data encryption both in transit and at rest.

With AppFlow, you can configure the integration flow, including source (Salesforce) and destination (Amazon S3), and set up encryption options. It simplifies the data transfer process and can handle the encryption requirements without the need for custom development.

choices.solution: Create a custom connector for Salesforce to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Salesforce has a managed AppFlow connector, so building a custom connector adds unnecessary development work.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
An IoT company is releasing a mattress that has sensors to collect data about a user's sleep. The sensors will send data to an Amazon S3 bucket.

The sensors collect approximately 2 MB of data every night for each mattress. The company must process and summarize the data for each mattress.

The results need to be available as soon as possible. Data processing will require 1 GB of memory and will finish within 30 seconds.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue with a Scala job
choices.explanation: A Glue Scala job has startup and execution overhead unnecessary for a small 30-second event-driven task.

choices.solution: Use Amazon EMR with an Apache Spark script
choices.explanation: An EMR cluster adds compute and cluster management for processing just 2 MB per event.

choices.solution: Use AWS Lambda with a Python script
choices.explanation:
AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that allows you to run code without provisioning or managing servers. It automatically scales with the number of requests, making it well-suited for event-driven workloads like processing data from IoT devices.

Python is a lightweight and efficient language for data processing tasks. Lambda allows you to execute code in response to events, such as data arriving in the S3 bucket.

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue with a PySpark job
choices.explanation: Glue PySpark adds distributed ETL startup and billing overhead compared with a short Lambda function.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations. A member account has purchased a Compute Savings Plan.

Because of changes in the workloads inside the member account, the account no longer receives the full benefit of the Compute Savings Plan commitment. The company uses less than 50% of its purchased compute power.

choices.solution: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the member account that purchased the Compute Savings Plan.
choices.explanation: The Organizations management account controls consolidated discount sharing; the purchasing member account cannot enable the organization-wide setting itself.

choices.solution: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the company's Organizations management account.
choices.explanation: Savings Plans and reservation discount sharing are controlled through the management account's billing preferences and apply to eligible usage under consolidated billing.

choices.solution: Migrate additional compute workloads from another AWS account to the account that has the Compute Savings Plan.
choices.explanation: Moving workloads between accounts adds migration work when shared discounts can cover eligible usage in existing accounts.

choices.solution: Sell the excess Savings Plan commitment in the Reserved Instance Marketplace.
choices.explanation: Savings Plans cannot be resold in the Reserved Instance Marketplace.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is developing a microservices application that will provide a search catalog for customers. The company must use REST APIs to present the frontend of the application to users.

The REST APIs must access the backend services that the company hosts in containers in private VPC subnets.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet.

Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: A WebSocket API does not meet the specified REST API interface.

choices.solution:
Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet.

Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: An API Gateway VPC link connects the public API integration to a private load balancer serving ECS tasks, leaving the application infrastructure private.

choices.solution:
Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet.

Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: A WebSocket API is the wrong interface, and a security group alone does not connect API Gateway to private container targets.

choices.solution:
Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet.

Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: A security group does not establish API Gateway's private integration path; a VPC link is required.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has applications hosted on Amazon EC2 instances with IPv6 addresses. The applications must initiate communications with other external applications using the internet.

However the company's security policy states that any external service cannot initiate a connection to the EC2 instances.

What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?

choices.solution: Create a NAT gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
choices.explanation: NAT gateways provide IPv4 translation or IPv6-to-IPv4 NAT64; they are not the native outbound-only IPv6 internet gateway requested.

choices.solution: Create an internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
choices.explanation: An internet gateway permits bidirectional routing unless additional security rules restrict it; it does not inherently enforce outbound-only IPv6 connections.

choices.solution: Create a virtual private gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
choices.explanation: A virtual private gateway terminates private VPN connectivity, not general IPv6 internet egress.

choices.solution: Create an egress-only internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
choices.explanation:
An egress-only internet gateway is used for IPv6 traffic leaving the VPC to reach the internet. It allows outbound communication initiated by resources inside the VPC but prevents incoming traffic initiated from the internet.

Configuring the subnet's route table to use the egress-only internet gateway as the destination ensures that IPv6 traffic initiated from EC2 instances can reach external services while blocking unsolicited incoming traffic.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has multiple VPCs across AWS Regions to support and run workloads that are isolated from workloads in other Regions. Because of a recent application launch requirement, the company's VPCs must communicate with all other VPCs across all Regions.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?

choices.solution: Use VPC peering to manage VPC communication in a single Region. Use VPC peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
choices.explanation: An all-to-all peering mesh requires many connections and individual routes as the VPC count grows.

choices.solution: Use AWS Direct Connect gateways across all Regions to connect VPCs across regions and manage VPC communications.
choices.explanation: Direct Connect gateways connect external networks to AWS resources; they are not the proposed transitive VPC-to-VPC routing fabric.

choices.solution: Use AWS Transit Gateway to manage VPC communication in a single Region and Transit Gateway peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
choices.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway is designed for simplifying the connectivity between multiple VPCs and on-premises networks. It allows for hub-and-spoke connectivity patterns, making it easier to manage communication across multiple VPCs.

By using AWS Transit Gateway in a single Region to connect VPCs and enabling Transit Gateway peering across Regions, you can efficiently manage communication between VPCs in different Regions with centralized control and minimal administrative effort.

choices.solution: Use AWS PrivateLink across all Regions to connect VPCs across Regions and manage VPC communications
choices.explanation: PrivateLink exposes specific services rather than providing general bidirectional connectivity among all VPC networks.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is expecting rapid growth in the near future. A solutions architect needs to configure existing users and grant permissions to new users on AWS.

The solutions architect has decided to create IAM groups. The solutions architect will add the new users to IAM groups based on department.

Which additional action is the MOST secure way to grant permissions to the new users?

choices.solution: Apply service control policies (SCPs) to manage access permissions
choices.explanation: SCPs limit maximum permissions but do not grant the new users permission to perform actions.

choices.solution: Create IAM roles that have least privilege permission. Attach the roles to the IAM groups
choices.explanation: IAM roles cannot be attached to IAM groups as permission policies.

choices.solution: Create an IAM policy that grants least privilege permission. Attach the policy to the IAM groups
choices.explanation: Creating an IAM policy that grants the least privilege required for the users' tasks is a security best practice. By attaching this policy to IAM groups, you ensure that new users added to these groups inherit the specific permissions defined in the policy.

choices.solution: Create IAM roles. Associate the roles with a permissions boundary that defines the maximum permissions
choices.explanation: A permissions boundary limits a role's maximum permissions but does not grant department users access through their groups.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A group requires permissions to list an Amazon S3 bucket and delete objects from that bucket. An administrator has created the following IAM policy to provide access to the bucket and applied that policy to the group.

The group is not able to delete objects in the bucket. The company follows least-privilege access rules.

{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Action": [ "s3:ListBucket", "s3:DeleteObject" ], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name" ], "Effect": "Allow" } ] }

Which statement should a solutions architect add to the policy to correct bucket access?

choices.solution: { "Action": ["s3:*Object"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*"], "Effect": "Allow" }
choices.explanation: s3:*Object permits additional object actions beyond the required DeleteObject permission.

choices.solution: { "Action": ["s3:*"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*"], "Effect": "Allow" }
choices.explanation: s3:* grants more object permissions than the group's listing and deletion requirements.

choices.solution: { "Action": ["s3:DeleteObject"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name*"], "Effect": "Allow" }
choices.explanation: The missing slash makes the wildcard match other bucket names and their objects; bucket-name/* scopes deletion to this bucket's objects.

choices.solution: { "Action": ["s3:DeleteObject"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*"], "Effect": "Allow" }
choices.explanation:
s3:DeleteObject is an object-level action, so its Resource must be an object ARN such as arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*. The existing bucket ARN is appropriate for s3:ListBucket.

Option D adds exactly the missing least-privilege object permission.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A business application is hosted on Amazon EC2 and uses Amazon S3 for encrypted object storage. The chief information security officer has directed that no application traffic between the two services should traverse the public internet.

Which capability should the solutions architect use to meet the compliance requirements?

choices.solution: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
choices.explanation: KMS protects encryption keys but does not change the network route to S3.

choices.solution: VPC endpoint
choices.explanation: AWS provides VPC endpoints that allow you to privately connect your VPC to supported AWS services, including Amazon S3, without needing to use public IP addresses or traverse the public internet. With an S3 VPC endpoint, the traffic between your Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon S3 remains within the AWS network, providing a secure and private connection.

choices.solution: Private subnet
choices.explanation: A private subnet alone does not establish a private S3 connection; it can still route through NAT to a public endpoint.

choices.solution: Virtual private gateway
choices.explanation: A virtual private gateway connects external networks through VPN/Direct Connect, not private EC2-to-S3 service access.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to move from many standalone AWS accounts to a consolidated, multi-account architecture. The company plans to create many new AWS accounts for different business units.

The company needs to authenticate access to these AWS accounts by using a centralized corporate directory service.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Create a new organization in AWS Organizations with all features turned on. Create the new AWS accounts in the organization.
choices.explanation: An organization with all features enabled provides centralized multi-account management and policy controls.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to accept Amazon Cognito authentication.
choices.explanation: A Cognito identity pool is not the centralized workforce access configuration for AWS Organizations accounts.

choices.solution: Configure a service control policy (SCP) to manage the AWS accounts. Add AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to AWS Directory Service.
choices.explanation: SCPs constrain permissions but do not authenticate users or establish corporate directory federation.

choices.solution: Create a new organization in AWS Organizations. Configure the organization's authentication mechanism to use AWS Directory Service directly.
choices.explanation: Organizations does not itself provide direct directory authentication; IAM Identity Center supplies that integration.

choices.solution: Set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the organization. Configure IAM Identity Center, and integrate it with the company's corporate directory service.
choices.explanation: IAM Identity Center integrates with the corporate identity source and assigns access across organization accounts.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A 4-year-old media company is using the AWS Organizations all features feature set to organize its AWS accounts. According to the company's finance team, the billing information on the member accounts must not be accessible to anyone, including the root user of the member accounts.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Add all finance team users to an IAM group. Attach an AWS managed policy named Billing to the group.
choices.explanation: Granting the finance team billing access does not deny access to member-account users or roots.

choices.solution: Attach an identity-based policy to deny access to the billing information to all users, including the root user.
choices.explanation: IAM identity policies cannot be attached to a root user.

choices.solution: Create a service control policy (SCP) to deny access to the billing information. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU).
choices.explanation: SCPs in AWS Organizations allow you to set fine-grained permissions and controls over what actions can be performed in member accounts. By creating an SCP, you can explicitly deny access to billing information for all users, including the root user, under the specified organizational unit (OU).

choices.solution: Convert from the Organizations all features feature set to the Organizations consolidated billing feature set.
choices.explanation: Changing the Organizations feature set does not impose the required permission denial and removes SCP capability.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A gaming company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store user information such as geographic location, player data, and leaderboards. The company needs to configure continuous backups to an Amazon S3 bucket with a minimal amount of coding.

The backups must not affect availability of the application and must not affect the read capacity units (RCUs) that are defined for the table.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Use an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Hive job to back up the data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: An EMR scan-based export consumes table reads and requires cluster and job management.

choices.solution: Export the data directly from DynamoDB to Amazon S3 with continuous backups. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery enables managed exports of a selected table state to S3 without consuming table read capacity. An export is a point-in-time operation, not continuous streaming.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the stream and export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: A stream consumer can export changes but requires custom batching, failure handling, and file-writing code.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function to export the data from the database tables to Amazon S3 on a regular basis. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.
choices.explanation: A custom export function adds code and scheduling; PITR plus native exports avoids scanning table data through RCUs.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has multiple AWS accounts for development work. Some staff consistently use oversized Amazon EC2 instances, which causes the company to exceed the yearly budget for the development accounts.

The company wants to centrally restrict the creation of AWS resources in these accounts.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

choices.solution: Develop AWS Systems Manager templates that use an approved EC2 creation process. Use the approved Systems Manager templates to provision EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Approved templates alone do not prevent users from launching disallowed instances through other APIs.

choices.solution: Use AWS Organizations to organize the accounts into organizational units (OUs). Define and attach a service control policy (SCP) to control the usage of EC2 instance types.
choices.explanation:
AWS Organizations allows you to consolidate multiple AWS accounts into an organization that you create and centrally manage. Organizational Units (OUs) can be used to group accounts based on different criteria, such as development, production, etc.

Service Control Policies (SCPs) are used to set fine-grained permissions on AWS accounts within an organization. By defining an SCP and attaching it to the OUs containing the development accounts, you can restrict the EC2 instance types that can be launched.

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function when an EC2 instance is created. Stop disallowed EC2 instance types.
choices.explanation: Stopping instances after launch is reactive and leaves a provisioning and billing window.

choices.solution: Set up AWS Service Catalog products for the staff to create the allowed EC2 instance types. Ensure that staff can deploy EC2 instances only by using the Service Catalog products.
choices.explanation: Service Catalog needs product setup and tightly scoped provisioning permissions; an SCP directly constrains instance types across the accounts.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon EC2 instances to host its internal systems. As part of a deployment operation, an administrator tries to use the AWS CLI to terminate an EC2 instance.

However, the administrator receives a 403 (Access Denied) error message.

The administrator is using an IAM role that has the following IAM policy attached:

{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["ec2:TerminateInstances"], "Resource": ["*"] }, { "Effect": "Deny", "Action": ["ec2:TerminateInstances"], "Condition": { "NotIpAddress": { "aws:SourceIp": [ "192.0.2.0/24", "203.0.113.0/24" ] } }, "Resource": ["*"] } ] }

What is the cause of the unsuccessful request?

choices.solution: The EC2 instance has a resource-based policy with a Deny statement.
choices.explanation: EC2 instances do not expose the proposed resource policy; the shown identity policy already contains the relevant conditional deny.

choices.solution: The principal has not been specified in the policy statement.
choices.explanation: Identity-based policies omit Principal because the attached role is the identity receiving permissions.

choices.solution: The "Action" field does not grant the actions that are required to terminate the EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: ec2:TerminateInstances is the correct action; the source-IP condition causes the denial.

choices.solution: The request to terminate the EC2 instance does not originate from the CIDR blocks 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24.
choices.explanation: The explicit Deny applies when aws:SourceIp is not in 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24. An explicit Deny overrides the Allow, so a termination request from outside those CIDR blocks receives AccessDenied.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is conducting an internal audit. The company wants to ensure that the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is associated with the company's AWS Lake Formation data lake does not contain sensitive customer or employee data.

The company wants to discover personally identifiable information (PII) or financial information, including passport numbers and credit card numbers.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure AWS Audit Manager on the account. Select the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) for auditing.
choices.explanation: Audit Manager gathers compliance evidence; it does not inspect S3 content for passport or credit-card numbers.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon S3 Inventory on the S3 bucket Configure Amazon Athena to query the inventory.
choices.explanation: S3 Inventory lists object metadata rather than examining object contents for PII.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job that uses managed identifiers for the required data types.
choices.explanation: Amazon Macie is a security service that uses machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data like PII or financial information. By configuring Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job, you can use managed identifiers to search for specific types of sensitive data within the S3 bucket.

choices.solution: Use Amazon S3 Select to run a report across the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 Select is a per-object query facility, not automated bucket-wide sensitive-data discovery.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has a service that reads and writes large amounts of data from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region. The service is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances within the private subnet of a VPC.

The service communicates with Amazon S3 over a NAT gateway in the public subnet. However, the company wants a solution that will reduce the data output costs.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the public subnet. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.
choices.explanation: A NAT instance adds compute and maintenance cost when an S3 gateway endpoint has no hourly or processing fee.

choices.solution: Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the private subnet. Configure the route table for the public subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.
choices.explanation: A private NAT instance lacks direct internet access, and changing the public subnet route does not route the private workers' traffic correctly.

choices.solution: Provision a VPC gateway endpoint. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the gateway endpoint as the route for all S3 traffic.
choices.explanation: An S3 gateway endpoint installs a service-prefix route in the private subnet's route table, allowing S3 traffic to bypass a NAT gateway.

choices.solution: Provision a second NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use this NAT gateway as the destination for all S3 traffic.
choices.explanation: Another NAT gateway preserves per-GB processing charges rather than removing them with an S3 gateway endpoint.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company runs an infrastructure monitoring service. The company is building a new feature that will enable the service to monitor data in customer AWS accounts.

The new feature will call AWS APIs in customer accounts to describe Amazon EC2 instances and read Amazon CloudWatch metrics.

What should the company do to obtain access to customer accounts in the MOST secure way?

choices.solution: Ensure that the customers create an IAM role in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy to the company's account.
choices.explanation: A customer-created cross-account role provides temporary read-only permissions for EC2 and CloudWatch. Use an external ID in the trust policy for a third-party service to prevent the confused-deputy problem.

choices.solution: Create a serverless API that implements a token vending machine to provide temporary AWS credentials for a role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions.
choices.explanation: A custom token-vending service adds credential-handling code; each customer still needs a trusted scoped IAM role.

choices.solution: Ensure that the customers create an IAM user in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store customer access and secret keys in a secrets management system.
choices.explanation: Stored customer access keys are long-lived secrets requiring rotation instead of temporary AssumeRole credentials.

choices.solution: Ensure that the customers create an Amazon Cognito user in their account to use an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store the Amazon Cognito user and password in a secrets management system.
choices.explanation: Cognito usernames do not directly authorize service API calls and add unnecessary stored credentials.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company needs to connect several VPCs in the us-east-1 Region that span hundreds of AWS accounts. The company's networking team has its own AWS account to manage the cloud network.

What is the MOST operationally efficient solution to connect the VPCs?

choices.solution: Set up VPC peering connections between each VPC. Update each associated subnet's route table
choices.explanation: A peering mesh across hundreds of accounts requires many connections and individually maintained routes.

choices.solution: Configure a NAT gateway and an internet gateway in each VPC to connect each VPC through the internet
choices.explanation: NAT and internet gateways expose an internet path and do not supply centralized private inter-VPC routing.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Transit Gateway in the networking team's AWS account. Configure static routes from each VPC.
choices.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway: It is designed to simplify the connectivity between multiple VPCs. It acts as a central hub that allows you to connect multiple VPCs and on-premises networks.

This approach reduces the complexity of managing peering connections individually.

choices.solution: Deploy VPN gateways in each VPC. Create a transit VPC in the networking team's AWS account to connect to each VPC.
choices.explanation: A transit VPC and VPN gateways require managing appliances and tunnels instead of a managed transit gateway.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A global marketing company has applications that run in the ap-southeast-2 Region and the eu-west-1 Region. Applications that run in a VPC in eu-west-1 need to communicate securely with databases that run in a VPC in ap-southeast-2.

Which network design will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a VPC peering connection between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. Create an inbound rule in the eu-west-1 application security group that allows traffic from the database server IP addresses in the ap-southeast-2 security group.
choices.explanation: The rule is on the application side rather than permitting database ingress, and the option omits the required peering routes.

choices.solution:
Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables.

Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.
choices.explanation: Security-group references across VPC peering are supported within the same Region, not this inter-Region peering connection.

choices.solution:
Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables.

Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows traffic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.
choices.explanation: VPC peering connections can be established between VPCs in different AWS Regions. In this case, a VPC peering connection is set up between the VPC in ap-southeast-2 and the VPC in eu-west-1.

choices.solution: Create a transit gateway with a peering attachment between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. After the transit gateways are properly peered and routing is configured, create an inbound rule in the database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.
choices.explanation: Transit-gateway peering does not allow cross-Region security-group references as proposed.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations with resources tagged by account. The company also uses AWS Backup to back up its AWS infrastructure resources.

The company needs to back up all AWS resources.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution:
Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically.

Use tags in the backup plan.
choices.explanation:
AWS Config can be used to identify untagged resources, and it can provide a comprehensive view of the resource inventory across your AWS Organization. AWS Backup supports the use of tags in backup plans.

By utilizing tags, you can create a backup plan that automatically includes resources based on their tags.

choices.solution: Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.
choices.explanation: Running state does not determine whether persistent resource data needs backup; stopped resources can still require protection.

choices.solution: Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.
choices.explanation: Manual reviews across account owners add ongoing effort and risk missing resources.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.
choices.explanation: Inspector discovers vulnerabilities, not completeness of backup resource tagging.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is running a microservices application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for scalability.

The company must configure the Amazon EKS control plane with endpoint private access set to true and endpoint public access set to false to maintain security compliance. The company must also put the data plane in private subnets.

However, the company has received error notifications because the node cannot join the cluster.

Which solution will allow the node to join the cluster?

choices.solution: Grant the required permission in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to the AmazonEKSNodeRole IAM role.
choices.explanation: IAM permissions alone do not create network access to the private API and required AWS service endpoints.

choices.solution: Create the interface VPC endpoints required for private node access to AWS services, including ECR and EC2, plus an S3 gateway endpoint for image layers. Verify private Kubernetes API endpoint DNS and security-group access.
choices.explanation: The private Kubernetes API endpoint is managed by EKS and is different from the EKS management API PrivateLink endpoint. Nodes also require IAM permissions, DNS, security-group access to the private API, and connectivity to services such as ECR, S3, and EC2 when no internet egress exists.

choices.solution: Recreate nodes in the public subnet. Restrict security groups for EC2 nodes.
choices.explanation: Public nodes violate the required private data-plane placement.

choices.solution: Allow outbound traffic in the security group of the nodes.
choices.explanation: Outbound allow rules do not create routes or private endpoints where no egress path exists.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is migrating an on-premises application to AWS. The company wants to use Amazon Redshift as a solution.

Which use cases are suitable for Amazon Redshift in this scenario? (Choose three.)

choices.solution: Supporting data APIs to access data with traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications
choices.explanation: The Redshift Data API provides SQL access for traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications without persistent client connections.

choices.solution: Supporting client-side and server-side encryption
choices.explanation: Redshift supports encrypted storage and TLS connections. An application can encrypt sensitive fields before ingestion, though this limits server-side analytics on those fields.

choices.solution: Building analytics workloads during specified hours and when the application is not active
choices.explanation: Redshift supports scheduled analytical workloads and can pause eligible provisioned clusters between runs to reduce compute costs.

choices.solution: Caching data to reduce the pressure on the backend database
choices.explanation: Redshift is an analytics warehouse, not a cache for a transactional backend database.

choices.solution: Scaling globally to support petabytes of data and tens of millions of requests per minute
choices.explanation: Globally distributed millions-per-minute low-latency key access is not Redshift's analytical query workload model.

choices.solution: Creating a secondary replica of the cluster by using the AWS Management Console
choices.explanation: Redshift does not expose a simple cluster secondary-replica creation option as a general migration use case.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A consulting company provides professional services to customers worldwide. The company provides solutions and tools for customers to expedite gathering and analyzing data on AWS.

The company needs to centrally manage and deploy a common set of solutions and tools for customers to use for self-service purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create AWS CloudFormation templates for the customers.
choices.explanation: Templates describe deployments but do not supply the centralized governed self-service portfolio of Service Catalog.

choices.solution: Create AWS Service Catalog products for the customers.
choices.explanation: AWS Service Catalog allows you to create and manage catalogs of IT services that are approved for use on AWS. It enables you to centrally manage and distribute standardized product portfolios.

choices.solution: Create AWS Systems Manager templates for the customers.
choices.explanation: Systems Manager documents automate operations rather than exposing governed infrastructure products to customers.

choices.solution: Create AWS Config items for the customers.
choices.explanation: Config items record resource configurations; they are not self-service deployment products.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A retail company has several businesses. The IT team for each business manages its own AWS account.

Each team account is part of an organization in AWS Organizations. Each team monitors its product inventory levels in an Amazon DynamoDB table in the team's own AWS account.

The company is deploying a central inventory reporting application into a shared AWS account. The application must be able to read items from all the teams' DynamoDB tables.

Which authentication option will meet these requirements MOST securely?

choices.solution:
Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Secrets Manager in the inventory application account. Configure the application to use the correct secret from Secrets Manager to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table.

Schedule secret rotation for every 30 days.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB uses IAM-signed requests, not a database password supplied by Secrets Manager.

choices.solution:
In every business account, create an IAM user that has programmatic access. Configure the application to use the correct IAM user access key ID and secret access key to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table.

Manually rotate IAM access keys every 30 days.
choices.explanation: Long-lived cross-account user keys require storage and manual rotation instead of scoped temporary role credentials.

choices.solution:
In every business account, create an IAM role named BU_ROLE with a policy that gives the role access to the DynamoDB table and a trust policy to trust a specific role in the inventory application account. In the inventory account, create a role named APP_ROLE that allows access to the STS AssumeRole API operation.

Configure the application to use APP_ROLE and assume the cross-account role BU_ROLE to read the DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation: The application role assumes a least-privilege role in each business account. The destination role trust policy and the source sts:AssumeRole permission are both required.

choices.solution:
Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Generate identity certificates to authenticate DynamoDB.

Configure the application to use the correct certificate to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation: ACM certificates are not a supported replacement for IAM authentication to DynamoDB.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to analyze and troubleshoot Access Denied errors and Unauthorized errors that are related to IAM permissions. The company has AWS CloudTrail turned on.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
choices.explanation: Custom Glue scripts add processing and development work compared with directly querying the CloudTrail dataset with Athena.

choices.solution: Use AWS Batch and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
choices.explanation: Batch requires writing and running custom log-processing jobs.

choices.solution: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena queries to identify the errors.
choices.explanation: Amazon Athena allows you to query data directly from S3 using standard SQL queries. CloudTrail logs can be stored in Amazon S3, and Athena makes it easy to analyze the logs using SQL queries.

choices.solution: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon QuickSight. Create a dashboard to identify the errors.
choices.explanation: QuickSight needs a queryable data source and visualization setup; Athena directly searches the required error fields.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has transactional and sensitive data in its databases.

The company wants to use AWS Cloud solutions to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
choices.explanation: EC2 databases retain operating-system, database maintenance, and backup responsibilities.

choices.solution: Migrate the databases to Amazon RDS Configure encryption at rest.
choices.explanation:
Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) is a fully managed database service that simplifies database management tasks, such as hardware provisioning, patching, and backups. Encryption at Rest Amazon RDS supports encryption at rest, which means data stored in the database is automatically encrypted.

This provides an additional layer of security for sensitive data. Managed Service: Amazon RDS is a managed service, meaning AWS takes care of operational aspects such as hardware maintenance, software patching, and backups.

This reduces operational overhead for the company.

choices.solution: Migrate the data to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Macie for data security and protection
choices.explanation: S3 object storage is not a transactional database replacement, and Macie discovers sensitive data rather than supplying database functionality.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs for data security and protection.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch Logs records events but does not encrypt stored database data.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has a workload in an AWS Region. Customers connect to and access the workload by using an Amazon API Gateway REST API.

The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company wants to provide individual and secure URLs for all customers.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency? (Choose three.)

choices.solution: Register the required domain in a registrar. Create a wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone and record in the zone that points to the API Gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: Register the domain and configure a Route 53 wildcard DNS record pointing to the Regional API Gateway custom domain endpoint.

choices.solution: Request a wildcard certificate that matches the domains in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in a different Region.
choices.explanation: A Regional API custom domain uses an ACM certificate in the same Region; an arbitrary other Region is not supported.

choices.solution: Create hosted zones for each customer as required in Route 53. Create zone records that point to the API Gateway endpoint.
choices.explanation: Separate hosted zones for each customer add administration compared with one wildcard domain and certificate.

choices.solution: Request a wildcard certificate that matches the custom domain name in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region.
choices.explanation: Request an ACM wildcard certificate in the same Region as the Regional API endpoint.

choices.solution: Create multiple API endpoints for each customer in API Gateway.
choices.explanation: Separate API deployments for every customer add unnecessary duplication and management.

choices.solution: Create a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API. Import the certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
choices.explanation: Associate the ACM certificate with an API Gateway wildcard custom domain and configure the API mapping; the certificate is referenced, not imported from ACM.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is building an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for its workloads. All secrets that are stored in Amazon EKS must be encrypted in the Kubernetes etcd key-value store.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage, rotate, and store all secrets in Amazon EKS.
choices.explanation: Storing secrets in Secrets Manager does not configure encryption of Kubernetes secrets already stored in etcd.

choices.solution: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable Amazon EKS KMS secrets encryption on the Amazon EKS cluster.
choices.explanation:
EKS provides default KMS-backed envelope encryption for Kubernetes API data on clusters running Kubernetes 1.28 or later. A customer-managed KMS key can be configured when customer control is required.

Earlier supported configurations explicitly enabled KMS secrets encryption; creating a customer key is not required merely to obtain encryption on modern clusters.

choices.solution: Create the Amazon EKS cluster with default options. Use the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver as an add-on.
choices.explanation: The EBS CSI driver manages workload volumes, not encryption of the managed control-plane etcd store.

choices.solution: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key with the alias/aws/ebs alias. Enable default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption for the account.
choices.explanation: EBS defaults do not configure EKS control-plane encryption, and the AWS-managed aws/ebs alias cannot be used for a newly created customer key.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A media company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver content over the internet. The company wants only premium customers to have access to the media streams and file content.

The company stores all content in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company also delivers content on demand to customers for a specific purpose, such as movie rentals or music downloads.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Generate and provide S3 signed cookies to premium customers.
choices.explanation: S3 has presigned URLs, not the proposed viewer signed cookies; CloudFront signs the private distribution's access grants.

choices.solution: Generate and provide CloudFront signed URLs to premium customers.
choices.explanation: This solution involves generating signed URLs for the content, which allows access only to those who have the appropriate permissions. Signed URLs can be time-limited, and you can define custom policies specifying who can access the content and for how long.

choices.solution: Use origin access control (OAC) to limit the access of non-premium customers.
choices.explanation: OAC restricts origin access to CloudFront, not access by premium versus non-premium viewers.

choices.solution: Generate and activate field-level encryption to block non-premium customers.
choices.explanation: Field-level encryption protects request data fields; it does not authorize customers to download private content.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company runs Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS accounts that are individually billed. The company recently purchased a Savings Plan.

Because of changes in the company's business requirements, the company has decommissioned a large number of EC2 instances. The company wants to use its Savings Plan discounts on its other AWS accounts.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: From the AWS Account Management Console of the management account, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section.
choices.explanation: The management account controls Savings Plans discount sharing through billing preferences.

choices.solution: From the AWS Account Management Console of the account that purchased the existing Savings Plan, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section. Include all accounts.
choices.explanation: Consolidated discount sharing is controlled from the Organizations management account after accounts are joined.

choices.solution: From the AWS Organizations management account, use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Savings Plan with other accounts.
choices.explanation: RAM does not share Savings Plans; consolidated billing discount sharing does.

choices.solution: Create an organization in AWS Organizations in a new payer account. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.
choices.explanation: A new payer account can consolidate billing, but creating one adds setup when the existing purchasing account can become the management account. The question's exact account choice is not a technical restriction.

choices.solution: Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the existing AWS account with the existing EC2 instances and Savings Plan. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.
choices.explanation: Bringing the accounts into one organization enables consolidated billing and sharing of eligible Savings Plans discounts.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has separate AWS accounts for its finance, data analytics, and development departments. Because of costs and security concerns, the company wants to control which services each AWS account can use.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS Systems Manager templates to control which AWS services each department can use.
choices.explanation: Systems Manager templates do not prevent users from invoking disallowed services outside the templates.

choices.solution: Create organization units (OUs) for each department in AWS Organizations. Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the OUs.
choices.explanation: AWS Organizations and Service Control Policies (SCPs): AWS Organizations provides a way to centrally manage and organize multiple AWS accounts. By creating separate organizational units (OUs) for each department, you can apply Service Control Policies (SCPs) to control which AWS services each department's accounts can access.

choices.solution: Use AWS CloudFormation to automatically provision only the AWS services that each department can use.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation provisioning does not impose a permission boundary on other API calls.

choices.solution: Set up a list of products in AWS Service Catalog in the AWS accounts to manage and control the usage of specific AWS services.
choices.explanation: Service Catalog controls product provisioning but requires additional IAM restrictions to prevent direct use of other services.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has created a multi-tier application for its ecommerce website. The website uses an Application Load Balancer that resides in the public subnets, a web tier in the public subnets, and a MySQL cluster hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets.

The MySQL database needs to retrieve product catalog and pricing information that is hosted on the internet by a third-party provider. A solutions architect must devise a strategy that maximizes security without increasing operational overhead.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy a NAT instance in the VPC. Route all the internet-based traffic through the NAT instance.
choices.explanation: A NAT instance requires patching, scaling, and availability management.

choices.solution: Deploy a NAT gateway in the public subnets. Modify the private subnet route table to direct all internet-bound traffic to the NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: A NAT gateway is a fully managed service provided by AWS that allows instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound traffic to the internet while preventing inbound traffic from reaching those instances. It simplifies the process of enabling internet access for instances in private subnets without the need for managing a separate NAT instance.

choices.solution: Configure an internet gateway and attach it to the VPModify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the internet gateway.
choices.explanation: An internet gateway does not translate private IPv4 addresses; the private database still needs NAT for public access.

choices.solution: Configure a virtual private gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the virtual private gateway.
choices.explanation: A virtual private gateway routes VPN/Direct Connect connections, not general public internet egress.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt AWS Lambda environment variables. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the required permissions are in place to decrypt and use the environment variables.

Which steps must the solutions architect take to implement the correct permissions? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda resource policy.
choices.explanation: A Lambda resource policy grants invocation access; it does not authorize the function to decrypt with KMS.

choices.solution: Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda execution role.
choices.explanation: Grant the Lambda execution role kms:Decrypt on the specific key used for encrypted values.

choices.solution: Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda function policy.
choices.explanation: The function's incoming resource policy is not its execution identity for KMS operations.

choices.solution: Allow the Lambda execution role in the AWS KMS key policy.
choices.explanation: The KMS key policy must also permit the execution role directly or enable IAM delegation; IAM permission alone cannot override a restrictive key policy.

choices.solution: Allow the Lambda resource policy in the AWS KMS key policy.
choices.explanation: A resource policy is not an IAM principal that can be granted key use; grant the execution role in the key policy.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to review a company's Amazon S3 buckets to discover personally identifiable information (PII). The company stores the PII data in the us-east-1 Region and us-west-2 Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Macie in each Region. Create a job to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Amazon Macie is a managed data security and data privacy service that uses machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data, including personally identifiable information (PII). By configuring Amazon Macie in each region where the company stores PII data, you can create jobs to analyze the data in Amazon S3 and identify any PII.

choices.solution: Configure AWS Security Hub for all Regions. Create an AWS Config rule to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Security Hub aggregates security findings, while a Config rule does not inspect S3 object contents for PII.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Inspector scans supported compute artifacts for vulnerabilities, not S3 objects for PII.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: GuardDuty detects malicious activity, not sensitive data within S3 object contents.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company runs an application in a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC extends across multiple Availability Zones.

The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application uses an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

A solutions architect needs to design a secure solution to establish a connection between the EC2 instances and the SQS queue.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the private subnets.

Add to the endpoint a security group that has an inbound access rule that allows traffic from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.
choices.explanation: An SQS interface endpoint provides private connectivity. Allow HTTPS from application instances in the endpoint security group and restrict access through IAM and endpoint policies.

choices.solution:
Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets.

Attach to the interface endpoint a VPC endpoint policy that allows access from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.
choices.explanation: Public-subnet endpoint placement can still be private, but the proposed endpoint policy alone omits the endpoint security-group rule needed to allow instance connections.

choices.solution:
Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets.

Attach an Amazon SQS access policy to the interface VPC endpoint that allows requests from only a specified VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: An SQS resource policy belongs on the queue, not on the interface endpoint; the endpoint needs its own policy and security group.

choices.solution:
Implement a gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS. Add a NAT gateway to the private subnets.

Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instances that allows access to the SQS queue.
choices.explanation: SQS does not support gateway endpoints, and a NAT gateway for internet egress belongs in a public subnet.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is using an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a three-tier web application. The web application consists of a web tier and an application tier that stores and retrieves user data in Amazon DynamoDB tables.

The web and application tiers are hosted on Amazon EC2 instances, and the database tier is not publicly accessible. The application EC2 instances need to access the DynamoDB tables without exposing API credentials in the template.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an IAM role to read the DynamoDB tables. Associate the role with the application instances by referencing an instance profile.
choices.explanation: Read-only permissions omit the application's required DynamoDB writes.

choices.solution: Create an IAM role that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Add the role to the EC2 instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the application instances.
choices.explanation: Option B is the correct choice because it leverages IAM roles and instance profiles for EC2 instances. By creating an IAM role with the necessary permissions to access DynamoDB and associating it with the EC2 instance profile, you can securely grant permissions to the EC2 instances without exposing API credentials in the CloudFormation template.

choices.solution: Use the parameter section in the AWS CloudFormation template to have the user input access and secret keys from an already-created IAM user that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables.
choices.explanation: Template parameters introduce long-lived access keys instead of automatically supplied instance-role credentials.

choices.solution: Create an IAM user in the AWS CloudFormation template that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Use the GetAtt function to retrieve the access and secret keys, and pass them to the application instances through the user data.
choices.explanation: Embedding generated access keys in user data exposes long-lived credentials and adds rotation work.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company's solutions architect is designing an AWS multi-account solution that uses AWS Organizations. The solutions architect has organized the company's accounts into organizational units (OUs).

The solutions architect needs a solution that will identify any changes to the OU hierarchy. The solution also needs to notify the company's operations team of any changes.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use account drift notifications to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
choices.explanation:
AWS Control Tower is a service that simplifies the process of setting up and governing a secure, multi-account AWS environment based on AWS best practices. It provides a pre-defined landing zone with an organizational structure, OUs, and guardrails to enforce security and compliance. the organizational units (OUs) are established as part of the AWS Control Tower landing zone.

If there are any changes to the OU hierarchy (such as moving accounts between OUs), these changes are considered drift, and AWS Control Tower can generate account drift notifications.

choices.solution: Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use AWS Config aggregated rules to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
choices.explanation: Config aggregators combine resource compliance information; they do not supply Control Tower's direct managed OU drift notifications.

choices.solution: Use AWS Service Catalog to create accounts in Organizations. Use an AWS CloudTrail organization trail to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
choices.explanation: Custom account products and CloudTrail event analysis add provisioning and detection work.

choices.solution: Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create accounts in Organizations. Use the drift detection operation on a stack to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation drift detects changes to stack-managed resource properties, not every organization-wide hierarchy change.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to ensure that API calls to Amazon DynamoDB from Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC do not travel across the internet.

Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Create a route table entry for the endpoint.
choices.explanation: Associate the DynamoDB gateway endpoint with the relevant route tables so the service prefix-list route is installed.

choices.solution: Create a gateway endpoint for DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: A DynamoDB gateway endpoint provides access from the VPC without an internet gateway or NAT gateway.

choices.solution: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: An EC2 interface endpoint provides private EC2 API access, not DynamoDB API connectivity.

choices.solution: Create an elastic network interface for the endpoint in each of the subnets of the VPC.
choices.explanation: A DynamoDB gateway endpoint uses route-table entries rather than endpoint network interfaces in each subnet.

choices.solution: Create a security group entry in the endpoint's security group to provide access.
choices.explanation: Gateway endpoints have no security group; access uses routing, endpoint policies, and relevant instance security rules.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the ability to complete purchase transactions on the website.

The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from database administrators.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution:
Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data.

Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.
choices.explanation: EBS encryption protects physical storage but a database administrator can read plaintext through the database engine.

choices.solution: Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.
choices.explanation:
Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) for MySQL is a managed relational database service that makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale a MySQL database in the cloud. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) provides a way to create and control encryption keys.

In the context of client-side encryption, the application (in this case, the ecommerce application) handles the encryption and decryption of data before it is stored in or retrieved from the database.

choices.solution:
Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data.

Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.
choices.explanation: Server-side S3 encryption decrypts data for authorized readers and is not the transactional relational storage requested.

choices.solution:
Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers.

Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.
choices.explanation: File permissions do not cryptographically protect sensitive fields against privileged administrators.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is creating a REST API. The company has strict requirements for the use of TLS.

The company requires TLSv1.3 on the API endpoints. The company also requires a specific public third-party certificate authority (CA) to sign the TLS certificate.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Obtain a certificate signed by the required third-party CA and import it into ACM. Create an API Gateway Regional REST API with a custom domain using the certificate and a TLS-1.3-only enhanced security policy.
choices.explanation:
Importing an externally issued certificate preserves the required CA. For current API Gateway REST APIs, the SecurityPolicy_TLS13_1_3_2025_09 policy rejects TLS 1.2 and accepts TLS 1.3; configure it on the applicable endpoint and custom domain.

Merely using an HTTP API does not establish the stated TLS-1.3-only requirement.

choices.solution:
Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain.

Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.
choices.explanation: ACM-issued public certificates use Amazon's CA; obtaining a specific third-party CA signature requires issuing externally and importing the certificate.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).

Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.
choices.explanation: ACM cannot issue from an arbitrary external public CA, and Lambda function URLs do not support attaching a custom certificate.

choices.solution:
Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL.

Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.
choices.explanation: A Lambda function URL cannot be configured with this custom domain certificate, and ACM does not issue through an arbitrary external CA.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is building a RESTful serverless web application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The users of this web application will be geographically distributed, and the company wants to reduce the latency of API requests to these users.

Which type of endpoint should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Private endpoint
choices.explanation: A private API endpoint is reachable through private VPC connectivity, not globally distributed public users.

choices.solution: Regional endpoint
choices.explanation: A Regional endpoint enters through its Region rather than CloudFront edge locations unless a separate distribution is added.

choices.solution: Interface VPC endpoint
choices.explanation: An interface VPC endpoint supplies private API connectivity rather than global public edge acceleration.

choices.solution: Edge-optimized endpoint
choices.explanation:
Edge-optimized endpoints use the global CloudFront network to distribute API traffic across multiple edge locations. This reduces latency for users by serving API requests from the edge locations closest to the users.

It leverages the AWS Global Accelerator and CloudFront to automatically route requests to the nearest AWS endpoint.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve content pages for its website. The company needs to ensure that clients use a TLS certificate when accessing the company's website.

The company wants to automate the creation and renewal of the TLS certificates.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.solution: Use a CloudFront security policy to create a certificate.
choices.explanation: A security policy selects TLS versions and ciphers; it does not issue certificates.

choices.solution: Use a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to create a certificate.
choices.explanation: OAC authenticates origin requests and does not create viewer TLS certificates.

choices.solution: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use DNS validation for the domain.
choices.explanation:
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM): ACM is a fully managed service that allows you to easily provision, manage, and deploy public and private Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS) certificates for use with AWS services and your internal connected resources. It is designed for automation and ease of use.

DNS Validation: DNS validation involves adding a DNS record to your domain's DNS configuration. This method is more suitable for automation as it does not require manual intervention, and it can be easily integrated into automated certificate issuance and renewal processes.

choices.solution: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use email validation for the domain.
choices.explanation: Email validation requires domain-owner email approval and renewal handling; persistent DNS validation enables simpler automated renewal.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has five organizational units (OUs) as part of its organization in AWS Organizations. Each OU correlates to the five businesses that the company owns.

The company's research and development (R&D) business is separating from the company and will need its own organization. A solutions architect creates a separate new management account for this purpose.

What should the solutions architect do next in the new management account?

choices.solution: Have the R&D AWS account be part of both organizations during the transition.
choices.explanation: An AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time.

choices.solution: Invite the R&D AWS account to be part of the new organization after the R&D AWS account has left the prior organization.
choices.explanation: An AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time. Leave the previous organization before accepting the new organization's invitation.

choices.solution: Create a new R&D AWS account in the new organization. Migrate resources from the prior R&D AWS account to the new R&D AWS account.
choices.explanation: Creating a replacement account and migrating resources adds unnecessary work when the existing account can join the new organization.

choices.solution: Have the R&D AWS account join the new organization. Make the new management account a member of the prior organization.
choices.explanation: The new management account cannot also act as a member of the previous organization while managing its own organization.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS and sells access to copyrighted images. The company's global customer base needs to be able to access these images quickly.

The company must deny access to users from specific countries. The company wants to minimize costs as much as possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
