Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and public bucket access.

Provide customers with a link to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Public bucket access bypasses paid authorization, and MFA does not add geographic viewer restrictions.

choices.solution:
Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Create an IAM user for each customer.

Add the users to a group that has permission to access the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Per-customer IAM users add credential administration and do not provide edge caching or country restrictions.

choices.solution:
Use Amazon EC2 instances that are behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) to store the images. Deploy the instances only in the countries the company services.

Provide customers with links to the ALBs for their specific country's instances.
choices.explanation: Regional web-server placement does not prevent users in excluded countries from accessing public ALB URLs and adds compute costs.

choices.solution:
Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute the images with geographic restrictions.

Provide a signed URL for each customer to access the data in CloudFront.
choices.explanation: By using CloudFront, you can cache and serve the images from edge locations around the world, improving access speed for global customers. Geographic Restrictions in CloudFront: CloudFront allows you to set up geographic restrictions to deny access to users from specific countries.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has an application that serves clients that are deployed in more than 20,000 retail storefront locations around the world. The application consists of backend web services that are exposed over HTTPS on port 443.

The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The retail locations communicate with the web application over the public internet.

The company allows each retail location to register the IP address that the retail location has been allocated by its local ISP. The company's security team recommends to increase the security of the application endpoint by restricting access to only the IP addresses registered by the retail locations.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Use IP-set rules to allow only registered retail-location IP addresses and update the sets as registrations change.

Split the addresses across multiple IP sets as required by quotas.
choices.explanation: WAF IP-set rules filter HTTP requests at the ALB. More than 20,000 addresses require multiple IP sets under the standard per-set quota; configure the web ACL to block requests that match none of the approved sets.

choices.solution:
Deploy AWS Firewall Manager to manage the ALB. Configure firewall rules to restrict traffic to the ALB.

Modify the firewall rules to include the registered IP addresses.
choices.explanation: Firewall Manager centrally manages policies but still needs an actual WAF policy/web ACL; it does not directly inspect ALB requests through unspecified firewall rules.

choices.solution: Store the IP addresses in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure an AWS Lambda authorization function on the ALB to validate that incoming requests are from the registered IP addresses.
choices.explanation: ALBs do not provide an arbitrary Lambda request-authorizer hook as proposed.

choices.solution: Configure the network ACL on the subnet that contains the public interface of the ALB. Update the ingress rules on the network ACL with entries for each of the registered IP addresses.
choices.explanation: A rule per location exceeds practical network ACL limits and requires extensive rule administration.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is building a data analysis platform on AWS by using AWS Lake Formation. The platform will ingest data from different sources such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS.

The company needs a secure solution to prevent access to portions of the data that contain sensitive information.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create an IAM role that includes permissions to access Lake Formation tables.
choices.explanation: IAM table permissions do not by themselves restrict particular rows or cells containing sensitive information.

choices.solution: Create data filters to implement row-level security and cell-level security.
choices.explanation: AWS Lake Formation allows you to create data filters that can be used for row-level security and cell-level security.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function that removes sensitive information before Lake Formation ingests the data.
choices.explanation: Pre-ingestion redaction adds transformation code and removes data rather than selectively restricting its visibility.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive information from Lake Formation tables.
choices.explanation: Deleting sensitive content with a periodic function creates an exposure window and custom data-maintenance work.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to process sensitive information from an Amazon S3 bucket.

The application must not use the internet to connect to the S3 bucket.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Configure an internet gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the internet gateway.

Update the application to use the new internet gateway.
choices.explanation: An internet gateway uses public routing and cannot be named as the authenticated source identity in an S3 bucket policy.

choices.solution:
Configure a VPN connection. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPN connection.

Update the application to use the new VPN connection.
choices.explanation: A bucket cannot terminate a VPN connection; a VPN alone does not create the private AWS service endpoint.

choices.solution:
Configure a NAT gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the NAT gateway.

Update the application to use the new NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: NAT uses the public service endpoint and does not establish the requested private endpoint path.

choices.solution:
Configure a VPC endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPC endpoint.

Update the application to use the new VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: VPC Endpoint for S3: A VPC endpoint allows you to privately connect your VPC to supported AWS services, including Amazon S3, without traversing the public internet. This ensures secure and direct access to S3 from within your VPC.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run a container application. The EKS cluster stores sensitive information in the Kubernetes secrets object.

The company wants to ensure that the information is encrypted.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use the container application to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
choices.explanation: Application encryption requires changing code rather than enabling managed encryption for the secrets store.

choices.solution: Enable secrets encryption in the EKS cluster by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
choices.explanation:
Use EKS managed KMS-backed envelope encryption for Kubernetes secrets. Clusters running Kubernetes 1.28 or later provide this by default, with an optional customer-managed key.

This avoids application-side encryption code and external secret migration.

choices.solution: Implement an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
choices.explanation: A custom encryption function adds invocation and secret-handling orchestration.

choices.solution: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
choices.explanation: Moving secrets to Parameter Store changes the application retrieval model and does not encrypt existing Kubernetes secret objects in etcd.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company runs a critical, customer-facing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application has a microservices architecture.

The company needs to implement a solution that collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from the application in a centralized location.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Run the Amazon CloudWatch agent in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
choices.explanation: A generic agent installation alone lacks Container Insights' Kubernetes discovery and curated aggregation of container metrics and logs.

choices.solution: Run AWS App Mesh in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the App Mesh console.
choices.explanation: App Mesh is a service networking layer; it does not independently provide the requested metrics/log storage dashboard.

choices.solution: Configure AWS CloudTrail to capture data events. Query CloudTrail by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records AWS API activity, not all application metrics and logs from the containers.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch Container Insights is specifically designed for monitoring containerized applications on Amazon EKS and ECS. It provides visibility into the performance of containers, clusters, and microservices.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has deployed its newest product on AWS. The product runs in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer.

The company stores the product's objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company recently experienced malicious attacks against its systems.

The company needs a solution that continuously monitors for malicious activity in the AWS account, workloads, and access patterns to the S3 bucket. The solution must also report suspicious activity and display the information on a dashboard.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Macie to monitor and report findings to AWS Config.
choices.explanation: Macie discovers sensitive S3 data rather than comprehensively detecting malicious workload and account activity.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Inspector to monitor and report findings to AWS CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: Inspector discovers software vulnerabilities, and CloudTrail is not a security-findings dashboard.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor and report findings to AWS Security Hub.
choices.explanation:
Amazon GuardDuty: GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior in your AWS account. It analyzes events, such as API calls and network traffic, to detect potentially malicious activity.

AWS Security Hub: AWS Security Hub is a comprehensive security service that aggregates and prioritizes security findings from various AWS services, including GuardDuty. It provides a centralized dashboard for security alerts and findings.

choices.solution: Configure AWS Config to monitor and report findings to Amazon EventBridge.
choices.explanation: Config tracks resource configuration compliance rather than detecting malicious access patterns and runtime threats.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing a security solution for a company that wants to provide developers with individual AWS accounts through AWS Organizations, while also maintaining standard security controls. Because the individual developers will have AWS account root user-level access to their own accounts, the solutions architect wants to ensure that the mandatory AWS CloudTrail configuration that is applied to new developer accounts is not modified.

Which action meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an IAM policy that prohibits changes to CloudTrail. and attach it to the root user.
choices.explanation: An IAM identity policy cannot be attached to an account root user.

choices.solution: Create a new trail in CloudTrail from within the developer accounts with the organization trails option enabled.
choices.explanation: Member-account roots cannot create an organization trail; the organization trail is managed centrally from the authorized organization account.

choices.solution: Create a service control policy (SCP) that prohibits changes to CloudTrail, and attach it the developer accounts.
choices.explanation: SCPs are used in AWS Organizations to set fine-grained permissions and restrictions on AWS accounts within the organization. By creating an SCP that explicitly prohibits changes to CloudTrail settings, you can enforce this restriction across all developer accounts.

choices.solution: Create a service-linked role for CloudTrail with a policy condition that allows changes only from an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the management account.
choices.explanation: A service-linked role does not impose a deny on all developer and root API calls that could change their trails.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon API Gateway to manage its REST APIs that third-party service providers access. The company must protect the REST APIs from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks.

What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure AWS Shield.
choices.explanation: Shield addresses DDoS protection rather than SQL-injection and cross-site-scripting request inspection.

choices.solution: Configure AWS WAF.
choices.explanation: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) is specifically designed to protect web applications from common web exploits like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. By configuring AWS WAF with API Gateway, you can create rules to filter and allow or block requests based on defined conditions, providing protection against various types of attacks.

choices.solution: Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS Shield in CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Adding CloudFront and Shield does not supply the missing WAF application exploit rules.

choices.solution: Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS WAF in CloudFront.
choices.explanation: A separate CloudFront distribution and WAF association add configuration when a Regional WAF web ACL can protect the REST API stage directly.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to provide users with access to AWS resources. The company has 1,500 users and manages their access to on-premises resources through Active Directory user groups on the corporate network.

However, the company does not want users to have to maintain another identity to access the resources. A solutions architect must manage user access to the AWS resources while preserving access to the on- premises resources.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an IAM user for each user in the company. Attach the appropriate policies to each user.
choices.explanation: Creating 1,500 IAM users duplicates the existing workforce identities and adds password and lifecycle management.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Cognito with an Active Directory user pool. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached.
choices.explanation: Cognito has no native Active Directory user-pool type; workforce SAML federation preserves the existing directory identities.

choices.solution: Define cross-account roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
choices.explanation: Cross-account role trust alone does not authenticate the on-premises AD users; a federation provider must issue the trusted identity assertions.

choices.solution: Configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2 0-based federation. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
choices.explanation: using SAML 2.0-based federation, which allows you to integrate AWS with your existing Active Directory infrastructure. This approach enables single sign-on (SSO) for users, meaning they can use their existing corporate credentials to access both on-premises and AWS resources without maintaining separate identities.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A global company runs its applications in multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The company's applications use multipart uploads to upload data to multiple Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions.

The company wants to report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost compliance purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Configure AWS Config with a rule to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
choices.explanation: Config rules do not supply the built-in organization-wide incomplete multipart-upload count dashboard.

choices.solution: Create a service control policy (SCP) to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
choices.explanation: An SCP controls permissions and cannot generate metrics or cost-compliance reports.

choices.solution: Configure S3 Storage Lens to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
choices.explanation:
S3 Storage Lens is a feature in Amazon S3 that provides a comprehensive view of your storage usage and activity across multiple accounts. It helps you understand, analyze, and optimize your storage usage.

You can use S3 Storage Lens to generate reports on various metrics, including the incomplete multipart upload object count.

choices.solution: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
choices.explanation: A Multi-Region Access Point routes requests to buckets; it does not report incomplete upload counts.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company collects 10 GB of telemetry data daily from various machines. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket in a source data account.

The company has hired several consulting agencies to use this data for analysis. Each agency needs read access to the data for its analysts.

The company must share the data from the source data account by choosing a solution that maximizes security and operational efficiency.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure S3 global tables to replicate data for each agency.
choices.explanation: S3 does not have a global tables feature; DynamoDB global tables are unrelated to this object-sharing requirement.

choices.solution: Make the S3 bucket public for a limited time. Inform only the agencies.
choices.explanation: A public bucket exposes telemetry to anyone who discovers it, not just the agencies.

choices.solution: Configure cross-account access for the S3 bucket to the accounts that the agencies own.
choices.explanation: By configuring cross-account access, you can grant permissions to specific AWS accounts (owned by the consulting agencies) to access the S3 bucket. This allows you to share the data securely with the agencies without making the data public or creating additional IAM users in the source data account.

choices.solution: Set up an IAM user for each analyst in the source data account. Grant each user access to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Separate analyst users require managing long-lived credentials in the source account instead of trusting scoped identities in agency accounts.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company collects and shares research data with the company's employees all over the world. The company wants to collect and store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket and process the data in the AWS Cloud.

The company will share the data with the company's employees. The company needs a secure solution in the AWS Cloud that minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use an AWS Lambda function to create an S3 presigned URL. Instruct employees to use the URL.
choices.explanation: A presigned S3 URL grants temporary access to a specific operation without distributing AWS credentials. Its effective permissions and expiry are bounded by the signing identity and credentials.

choices.solution:
Create an IAM user for each employee. Create an IAM policy for each employee to allow S3 access.

Instruct employees to use the AWS Management Console.
choices.explanation: Per-employee IAM users and policies create unnecessary identity and credential administration.

choices.solution:
Create an S3 File Gateway. Create a share for uploading and a share for downloading.

Allow employees to mount shares on their local computers to use S3 File Gateway.
choices.explanation: File Gateway requires network mounts and appliance management across globally distributed employee devices.

choices.solution:
Configure AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoints. Select the custom identity provider options.

Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage the user credentials Instruct employees to use Transfer Family.
choices.explanation: SFTP endpoints and custom identity-provider credentials add protocol and authentication administration compared with scoped expiring links.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has an application workflow that uses an AWS Lambda function to download and decrypt files from Amazon S3. These files are encrypted using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys.

A solutions architect needs to design a solution that will ensure the required permissions are set correctly.

Which combination of actions accomplish this? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Attach the kms:decrypt permission to the Lambda function's resource policy
choices.explanation: The Lambda resource policy controls who can invoke the function, not its permission to decrypt data.

choices.solution: Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda IAM role in the KMS key's policy
choices.explanation: Authorize the Lambda execution role in the KMS key policy to decrypt with the key.

choices.solution: Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda resource policy in the KMS key's policy.
choices.explanation: A resource policy is not an IAM principal to name in the KMS key policy; use the execution role.

choices.solution: Create a new IAM policy with the kms:decrypt permission and attach the policy to the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: IAM permission policies attach to the function's execution role, not directly to the Lambda resource.

choices.solution: Create a Lambda execution role with kms:Decrypt on the specific KMS key and s3:GetObject on the required objects, and attach the role to the function.
choices.explanation: Attach an execution role with kms:Decrypt and the required S3 read permissions to the function.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to monitor its AWS costs for financial review. The cloud operations team is designing an architecture in the AWS Organizations management account to query AWS Cost and Usage Reports for all member accounts.

The team must run this query once a month and provide a detailed analysis of the bill.

Which solution is the MOST scalable and cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver reports to Amazon Kinesis.

Use Amazon EMR for analysis.
choices.explanation: Cost and Usage Reports are delivered to S3, not directly to Kinesis, and EMR adds unnecessary cluster cost.

choices.solution: Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Athena for analysis.
choices.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service that allows you to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using SQL queries.

choices.solution: Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Redshift for analysis.
choices.explanation: Per-member reports and a Redshift warehouse add management and running cost compared with querying the consolidated S3 report.

choices.solution:
Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon Kinesis.

Use Amazon QuickSight for analysis.
choices.explanation: The reports are not delivered directly to Kinesis, and QuickSight still needs a queryable data source.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company runs several websites on AWS for its different brands. Each website generates tens of gigabytes of web traffic logs each day.

A solutions architect needs to design a scalable solution to give the company's developers the ability to analyze traffic patterns across all the company's websites. This analysis by the developers will occur on demand once a week over the course of several months.

The solution must support queries with standard SQL.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena for analysis.
choices.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service that allows you to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL queries. It is cost-effective because you pay only for the queries you run, and there is no need to provision or manage infrastructure.

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon RDS. Use a database client for analysis.
choices.explanation: A continuously provisioned relational database adds ingestion and compute cost for weekly analytical queries over raw logs.

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Use OpenSearch Service for analysis.
choices.explanation: Maintaining search indexes and cluster capacity costs more for occasional SQL analysis directly over stored objects.

choices.solution: Store the logs in an Amazon EMR cluster Use a supported open-source framework for SQL-based analysis.
choices.explanation: An EMR cluster requires execution and lifecycle management when Athena provides serverless on-demand SQL.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
An international company has a subdomain for each country that the company operates in. The subdomains are formatted as example.com, country1.example.com, and country2.example.com.

The company's workloads are behind an Application Load Balancer. The company wants to encrypt the website data that is in transit.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Request an ACM public certificate with example.com and *.example.com as subject alternative names, and associate it with the ALB HTTPS listener.
choices.explanation: Request an ACM public certificate covering example.com and *.example.com. A wildcard does not cover the apex domain or multiple subdomain levels.

choices.solution: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a private certificate for the apex top domain example.com and a wildcard certificate for *.example.com.
choices.explanation: Private certificates are not trusted by ordinary public browsers without distributing the private CA trust chain.

choices.solution: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a public and private certificate for the apex top domain example.com.
choices.explanation: A certificate only for the apex does not cover country subdomains, and a private certificate does not add public browser trust.

choices.solution: Validate domain ownership by email address. Switch to DNS validation by adding the required DNS records to the DNS provider.
choices.explanation: An issued certificate cannot switch validation method in place; requesting DNS validation initially avoids duplicate validation work.

choices.solution: Validate domain ownership for the domain by adding the required DNS records to the DNS provider.
choices.explanation: DNS validation proves domain ownership and supports automated renewal while the validation records and certificate usage remain valid. ACM also supports email validation for public wildcard certificates.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is required to use cryptographic keys in its on-premises key manager. The key manager is outside of the AWS Cloud because of regulatory and compliance requirements.

The company wants to manage encryption and decryption by using cryptographic keys that are retained outside of the AWS Cloud and that support a variety of external key managers from different vendors.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS CloudHSM key store backed by a CloudHSM cluster.
choices.explanation: CloudHSM key material resides inside AWS, violating the requirement to retain keys in the external on-premises manager.

choices.solution: Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) external key store backed by an external key manager.
choices.explanation: A KMS external key store keeps key material and cryptographic operations in an external key manager while retaining compatible KMS integrations. The customer is responsible for external availability and latency.

choices.solution: Use the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) managed key store.
choices.explanation: The default KMS store retains key material in AWS rather than the mandated external key manager.

choices.solution: Use a custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster.
choices.explanation: A CloudHSM-backed custom store still uses HSMs hosted in AWS rather than the external vendor key manager.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company maintains an Amazon RDS database that maps users to cost centers. The company has accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations.

The company needs a solution that will tag all resources that are created in a specific AWS account in the organization. The solution must tag each resource with the cost center ID of the user who created the resource.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Move the specific AWS account to a new organizational unit (OU) in Organizations from the management account. Create a service control policy (SCP) that requires all existing resources to have the correct cost center tag before the resources are created.

Apply the SCP to the new OU.
choices.explanation: An SCP denies API operations but does not look up the creator's cost center or add tags to resources.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources after the Lambda function looks up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function.
choices.explanation:
CloudTrail events can trigger EventBridge, which invokes Lambda immediately after resource creation. Lambda can look up the creator's cost center in RDS and apply the correct tag.

SCPs cannot dynamically derive tag values from a database.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS CloudFormation stack to deploy an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to look up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database and to tag resources.

Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the CloudFormation stack.
choices.explanation: A scheduled rule cannot invoke a CloudFormation stack as the proposed resource-tagging target and does not react directly to each creation event.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources with a default value. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function when a resource is missing the cost center tag.
choices.explanation: A default tag value does not identify the creating user's actual cost center from RDS.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has multiple AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations that different business units use. The company has multiple offices around the world.

The company needs to update security group rules to allow new office CIDR ranges or to remove old CIDR ranges across the organization. The company wants to centralize the management of security group rules to minimize the administrative overhead that updating CIDR ranges requires.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Create VPC security groups in the organization's management account. Update the security groups when a CIDR range update is necessary.
choices.explanation: A security group is VPC-scoped and does not automatically update independent security groups in every account.

choices.solution:
Create a VPC customer managed prefix list that contains the list of CIDRs. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the prefix list across the organization.

Use the prefix list in the security groups across the organization.
choices.explanation: A customer-managed VPC prefix list centralizes the office CIDRs. Sharing it through AWS RAM lets security groups in multiple accounts reference the same list, so a CIDR change is made once.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS managed prefix list. Use an AWS Security Hub policy to enforce the security group update across the organization.

Use an AWS Lambda function to update the prefix list automatically when the CIDR ranges change.
choices.explanation: AWS-managed prefix lists cannot be edited with the company's office CIDRs, and Security Hub does not enforce this rule-update workflow.

choices.solution:
Create security groups in a central administrative AWS account. Create an AWS Firewall Manager common security group policy for the whole organization.

Select the previously created security groups as primary groups in the policy.
choices.explanation: Firewall Manager can manage common security groups but adds policy administration and cost when a shared customer-managed prefix list directly solves CIDR maintenance.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is developing a new application on AWS. The application consists of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster, an Amazon S3 bucket that contains assets for the application, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL database that contains the dataset for the application.

The dataset contains sensitive information. The company wants to ensure that only the ECS cluster can access the data in the RDS for MySQL database and the data in the S3 bucket.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt both the S3 bucket and the RDS for MySQL database. Ensure that the KMS key policy includes encrypt and decrypt permissions for the ECS task execution role.
choices.explanation: The execution role is for ECS infrastructure operations, not the application task's data access; encryption alone does not restrict MySQL connections.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key to encrypt both the S3 bucket and the RDS for MySQL database. Ensure that the S3 bucket policy specifies the ECS task execution role as a user.
choices.explanation: AWS managed key policies cannot be customized this way, and granting an execution role does not establish application task and database network isolation.

choices.solution:
Restrict S3 bucket access to the ECS application task role. Place the RDS database in private subnets and allow MySQL traffic only from the ECS tasks' security group.

Give tasks only the required S3 and database credentials or IAM permissions.
choices.explanation:
The ECS task role supplies application AWS permissions; the task execution role is used by ECS to launch tasks. Restrict S3 authorization to the task role and RDS network access to the tasks' security group.

An RDS API interface endpoint does not provide private database SQL connectivity.

choices.solution:
Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon RDS for MySQL. Update the RDS for MySQL security group to allow access from only the subnets that the ECS cluster will generate tasks in.

Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from only the S3 VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: An RDS API endpoint does not provide private MySQL SQL connectivity, and restricting S3 to a VPC endpoint still allows other authorized clients using that endpoint.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company has customers located across the world. The company wants to use automation to secure its systems and network infrastructure.

The company's security team must be able to track and audit all incremental changes to the infrastructure.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
choices.explanation: Organizations manages accounts and policies, not deployment of the application's network and resource infrastructure.

choices.solution: Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation defines reproducible infrastructure deployments. Config records supported resource configuration history and evaluates compliance rules to audit changes.

choices.solution: Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
choices.explanation: Organizations does not deploy arbitrary infrastructure, and Service Catalog is not a configuration-change audit recorder.

choices.solution: Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
choices.explanation: Service Catalog governs provisioning products; Config records ongoing resource configuration changes.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company is moving its data and applications to AWS during a multiyear migration project. The company wants to securely access data on Amazon S3 from the company's AWS Region and from the company's on-premises location.

The data must not traverse the internet. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between its Region and its on-premises location.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the gateway endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
choices.explanation: S3 gateway endpoints cannot be accessed directly from on-premises networks over Direct Connect.

choices.solution: Create a gateway in AWS Transit Gateway to access Amazon S3 securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
choices.explanation: Transit Gateway alone does not expose an S3 service endpoint to on-premises clients.

choices.solution: Create interface endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the interface endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
choices.explanation: S3 interface endpoints are reachable from on-premises networks over Direct Connect. Gateway endpoints cannot be used from on premises; ensure private routing, DNS resolution, and endpoint policies are configured.

choices.solution: Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key to access the data securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
choices.explanation: KMS provides encryption operations and authorization, not the private network path to S3.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has multiple accounts for the company's development teams.

The development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each of the company's applications, the development teams must use a predefined application name to tag resources that are created.

A solutions architect needs to design a solution that gives the development team the ability to create resources only if the application name tag has an approved value.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specified for resources to be created.
choices.explanation: Identity Center users assume roles rather than IAM groups, and the policy checks only tag presence rather than approved values.

choices.solution: Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
choices.explanation: Denying any tagged resource blocks compliant requests as well as incorrect ones.

choices.solution: Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in all accounts.
choices.explanation: Resource Groups organizes resources but does not prevent creation requests with missing or invalid tags.

choices.solution: Use an enforced Organizations tag policy for approved application-name values and an SCP that denies supported resource-creation requests when the required application-name tag is missing or invalid.
choices.explanation: An enforced tag policy validates values on supported tagged resources, but does not block all untagged creation. Pair it with request-tag conditions in an SCP for supported creation APIs to require the tag across accounts.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company runs its databases on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company wants a secure solution to manage the master user password by rotating the password every 30 days.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a custom AWS Lambda function to rotate the password every 30 days.
choices.explanation: A custom rotation function and schedule add code and password synchronization work.

choices.solution: Use the modify-db-instance command in the AWS CLI to change the password.
choices.explanation: An ad hoc CLI password change does not provide automatic secure 30-day rotation.

choices.solution: Integrate AWS Secrets Manager with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
choices.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager integrates with RDS and can rotate database credentials automatically on a schedule, avoiding custom Lambda scheduling or manual CLI changes.

choices.solution: Integrate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
choices.explanation: Parameter Store does not natively rotate RDS passwords; additional automation is required.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company stores sensitive data in Amazon S3. A solutions architect needs to create an encryption solution.

The company needs to fully control the ability of users to create, rotate, and disable encryption keys with minimal effort for any data that must be encrypted.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use default server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) to store the sensitive data.
choices.explanation: SSE-S3 keys are managed by S3; the company cannot create, disable, and rotate them itself.

choices.solution: Create a customer managed key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use the new key to encrypt the S3 objects by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
choices.explanation: A customer-managed KMS key gives the company control over key policies, enable/disable state, and rotation while keeping key management managed by AWS. SSE-S3 and AWS-managed keys do not provide the same control.

choices.solution: Create an AWS managed key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Use the new key to encrypt the S3 objects by using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
choices.explanation: AWS managed keys do not give the company full lifecycle and rotation control.

choices.solution:
Download S3 objects to an Amazon EC2 instance. Encrypt the objects by using customer managed keys.

Upload the encrypted objects back into Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Downloading and reuploading every object adds transfer and encryption-code work compared with native SSE-KMS.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and stores data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company must ensure that all data is encrypted at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

The company must be able to control rotation of the encryption keys.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create a customer managed key. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: A customer-managed KMS key can encrypt EBS volumes and gives the company control over key rotation. AWS-owned keys are not customer-controlled, and imported key material adds operational overhead.

choices.solution: Use an AWS managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes. Use the key to configure automatic key rotation.
choices.explanation: AWS controls rotation of AWS managed keys; the company cannot configure its own rotation policy.

choices.solution: Create an external KMS key with imported key material. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: Imported material adds external generation and rotation operations rather than the simple automatic rotation of an AWS-generated customer-managed key.

choices.solution: Use an AWS owned key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: AWS owned keys are controlled by AWS and do not provide customer lifecycle or rotation control.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company needs a solution to enforce data encryption at rest on Amazon EC2 instances. The solution must automatically identify noncompliant resources and enforce compliance policies on findings.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

choices.solution: Use an IAM policy that allows users to create only encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Config and AWS Systems Manager to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: Use IAM conditions to prevent unencrypted volume creation and Config rules with Systems Manager Automation for detection and remediation. Existing EBS volumes cannot be encrypted in place; remediation creates an encrypted snapshot copy and replacement volume, then arranges a safe cutover.

choices.solution: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage access to encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Lambda and Amazon EventBridge to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: KMS permissions do not ensure newly created volumes are encrypted, and custom event detection/remediation adds more code than Config and Systems Manager integration.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Macie to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: Macie discovers sensitive S3 data, not unencrypted EBS volumes; existing EBS volumes also cannot be encrypted in place.

choices.solution: Use Amazon inspector to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: Inspector detects vulnerabilities, not EBS encryption compliance; encryption remediation requires replacing unencrypted volumes with encrypted copies.

Design Secure Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate its web applications from on premises to AWS. The company is located close to the eu-central-1 Region.

Because of regulations, the company cannot launch some of its applications in eu-central-1. The company wants to achieve single-digit millisecond latency.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to an edge location in Amazon CloudFront.
choices.explanation: CloudFront edge locations do not host arbitrary EC2 application workloads or extend VPC subnets, and the application remains in the prohibited Region.

choices.solution: Deploy the applications in AWS Local Zones by extending the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Local Zone.
choices.explanation: Local Zones extend an AWS Region to locations closer to users and can provide single-digit millisecond latency. The selected Local Zone must satisfy the regulation and support the needed services; placing compute in a Local Zone does not automatically remove all dependency on its parent Region.

choices.solution: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the regional edge caches in Amazon CloudFront.
choices.explanation: Regional edge caches cache HTTP content; they do not host application servers or accept extended VPC subnets.

choices.solution: Deploy the applications in AWS Wavelength Zones by extending the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Wavelength Zone.
choices.explanation: Wavelength is designed for applications at participating mobile-carrier 5G edges, not a general low-latency local deployment for the company's location.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is hosting a web application on AWS using a single Amazon EC2 instance that stores user-uploaded documents in an Amazon EBS volume. For better scalability and availability, the company duplicated the architecture and created a second EC2 instance and EBS volume in another Availability Zone, placing both behind an Application Load Balancer.

After completing this change, users reported that, each time they refreshed the website, they could see one subset of their documents or the other, but never all of the documents at the same time.

What should a solutions architect propose to ensure users see all of their documents at once?

choices.solution: Copy the data so both EBS volumes contain all the documents
choices.explanation: A one-time copy aligns the volumes only temporarily. New uploads can still reach different servers and leave their independent EBS volumes inconsistent.

choices.solution: Configure the Application Load Balancer to direct a user to the server with the documents
choices.explanation: Session affinity can keep a user on one server, but it does not combine documents stored on both servers. A server failure or a different session can expose the same inconsistency.

choices.solution: Copy the data from both EBS volumes to Amazon EFS. Modify the application to save new documents to Amazon EFS
choices.explanation:
Option C, which involves copying the data to Amazon EFS and modifying the application to use Amazon EFS for document storage, is the most appropriate solution to ensure users can see all their documents at once in the duplicated architecture. Amazon EFS provides scalability, availability, and shared access, allowing both EC2 instances to access and synchronize the documents seamlessly.

Unlike EBS volumes or snapshots, which cannot be shared in real time across multiple instances and Availability Zones, Amazon EFS allows both EC2 instances to access the same file system simultaneously, ensuring all users see the same set of documents regardless of which instance serves their request.

choices.solution: Configure the Application Load Balancer to send the request to both servers. Return each document from the correct server
choices.explanation: An Application Load Balancer forwards each request to a selected target; it does not broadcast the request and merge documents from multiple responses.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has an application that ingests incoming messages. Dozens of other applications and microservices then quickly consume these messages.

The number of messages varies drastically and sometimes increases suddenly to 100,000 each second. The company wants to decouple the solution and increase scalability.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Persist the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Configure the consumer applications to read and process the messages.
choices.explanation: Kinesis Data Analytics processes streams; it is not a persistent fan-out message queue for each consumer. The option omits the independent message buffers needed to decouple all the consuming applications.

choices.solution: Deploy the ingestion application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to scale the number of EC2 instances based on CPU metrics.
choices.explanation: Scaling the ingestion servers addresses compute capacity but does not provide durable buffering or decouple producers from the dozens of consumers.

choices.solution:
Write the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard. Use an AWS Lambda function to preprocess messages and store them in Amazon DynamoDB.

Configure the consumer applications to read from DynamoDB to process the messages.
choices.explanation: One provisioned Kinesis shard cannot accept a burst of 100,000 records per second. Preprocessing into DynamoDB also introduces extra components instead of providing an independent delivery queue for each consumer.

choices.solution: Publish the messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) subscriptions. Configure the consumer applications to process the messages from the queues.
choices.explanation:
SNS fans out messages to independent SQS standard queues, decoupling each consumer and buffering bursts. Standard SQS queues support nearly unlimited API throughput.

SNS publish quotas are Regional, so provision sufficient throughput and make consumers idempotent.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is migrating a distributed application to AWS. The application serves variable workloads.

The legacy platform consists of a primary server that coordinates jobs across multiple compute nodes. The company wants to modernize the application with a solution that maximizes resiliency and scalability.

How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group.

Configure EC2 Auto Scaling to use scheduled scaling.
choices.explanation: Scheduled scaling follows predetermined times, so it cannot reliably respond to an unpredictable backlog. Queue-based scaling adjusts worker capacity to the outstanding jobs.

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination for the jobs. Implement the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group.

Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the size of the queue.
choices.explanation:
Option B: This option provides a decoupled architecture where the jobs are sent to an SQS queue. The compute nodes (EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group) can then process these jobs.

Scaling based on the size of the SQS queue (the number of messages) allows the architecture to adapt to variable workloads, scaling out when the queue depth increases and scaling in when the depth decreases.

choices.solution:
Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure AWS CloudTrail as a destination for the jobs.

Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the primary server.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records AWS API activity; it is not a destination for application jobs. Retaining the coordinating primary server also preserves a central point of failure.

choices.solution:
Implement the primary server and the compute nodes with Amazon EC2 instances that are managed in an Auto Scaling group. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) as a destination for the jobs.

Configure EC2 Auto Scaling based on the load on the compute nodes.
choices.explanation: This retains the coordinating primary server instead of replacing it with a durable work queue. EventBridge event routing alone does not supply the proposed workers with an SQS-style backlog for resilient job processing.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is building an ecommerce web application on AWS. The application sends information about new orders to an Amazon API Gateway REST API to process.

The company wants to ensure that orders are processed in the order that they are received.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use an API Gateway integration to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the application receives an order. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the topic to perform processing.
choices.explanation: The option specifies an ordinary SNS topic, which does not guarantee the FIFO ordering required here. A directly subscribed Lambda consumer does not add that ordering guarantee.

choices.solution: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS FIFO queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.
choices.explanation: A FIFO queue preserves order within each message group. A Lambda event source mapping polls the queue and processes each group in order; use one group if strict order across all orders is required.

choices.solution: Use an API Gateway authorizer to block any requests while the application processes an order.
choices.explanation: An API Gateway authorizer decides whether a request is authorized; it is not an order-processing lock or queue. Blocking requests would reject orders instead of durably preserving their arrival order.

choices.solution: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS standard queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.
choices.explanation: SQS standard queues provide best-effort ordering, so messages can be delivered out of order. The application requires a FIFO queue with a consistent message group for ordered processing.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A global company hosts its web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The web application has static data and dynamic data.

The company stores its static data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to improve performance and reduce latency for the static data and dynamic data.

The company is using its own domain name registered with Amazon Route 53.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket and the ALB as origins. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.
choices.explanation:
CloudFront with Multiple Origins: CloudFront allows you to set up multiple origins for your distribution, so you can use both the ALB (for dynamic content) and the S3 bucket (for static content) as origins. This means that both your dynamic and static content can be served through CloudFront, which will cache content at edge locations to reduce latency.

Route 53 Integration with CloudFront: Amazon Route 53 can be easily configured to route traffic for your domain to a CloudFront distribution. Users will access your domain, and Route 53 will direct them to the nearest CloudFront edge location.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.
choices.explanation: An S3 bucket is not a supported Global Accelerator endpoint. The static-content portion of this design therefore cannot be configured as proposed.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the ALB and the CloudFront distribution as endpoints.

Create a custom domain name that points to the accelerator DNS name. Use the custom domain name as an endpoint for the web application.
choices.explanation: CloudFront distributions are not supported Global Accelerator endpoints. The accelerator can target the ALB, but not the proposed CloudFront distribution.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint.

Create two domain names. Point one domain name to the CloudFront DNS name for dynamic content.

Point the other domain name to the accelerator DNS name for static content. Use the domain names as endpoints for the web application.
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator cannot use an S3 bucket as an endpoint. Adding separate domain names does not resolve that service limitation or provide edge caching for the static S3 content.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs an ecommerce application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.

The Auto Scaling group scales based on CPU utilization metrics. The ecommerce application stores the transaction data in a MySQL 8.0 database that is hosted on a large EC2 instance.

The database's performance degrades quickly as application load increases. The application handles more read requests than write transactions.

The company wants a solution that will automatically scale the database to meet the demand of unpredictable read workloads while maintaining high availability.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Redshift with a single node for leader and compute functionality.
choices.explanation: Redshift is an analytical warehouse, not a drop-in MySQL transactional database. A single-node design also does not supply the requested highly available, automatically scaled read replicas.

choices.solution: Use Amazon RDS with a Single-AZ deployment Configure Amazon RDS to add reader instances in a different Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: The proposed database is Single-AZ, so it lacks the requested high availability. Ordinary RDS MySQL does not provide Aurora Auto Scaling's automatic addition and removal of reader instances.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Aurora with a Multi-AZ deployment. Configure Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas.
choices.explanation:
Option C: Using Amazon Aurora with a Multi-AZ deployment and configuring Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas is the most appropriate solution. Aurora is a MySQL-compatible relational database engine that provides high performance and scalability.

With Multi-AZ deployment, the database is automatically replicated across multiple Availability Zones for high availability. Aurora Auto Scaling allows the database to automatically add or remove Aurora Replicas based on the workload, ensuring that read requests can be distributed effectively and the database can scale to meet demand.

This provides both high availability and automatic scaling to handle unpredictable read workloads.

choices.solution: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with EC2 Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: Memcached is a cache, not a durable replacement for the transactional MySQL database. Spot capacity can be interrupted and does not establish a highly available database with automatically scaled readers.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An application development team is designing a microservice that will convert large images to smaller, compressed images. When a user uploads an image through the web interface, the microservice should store the image in an Amazon S3 bucket, process and compress the image with an AWS Lambda function, and store the image in its compressed form in a different S3 bucket.

A solutions architect needs to design a solution that uses durable, stateless components to process the images automatically.

Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the S3 bucket to send a notification to the SQS queue when an image is uploaded to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 object-created notifications put image-processing jobs into a durable SQS queue, decoupling uploads from processing.

choices.solution: Configure an SQS event source mapping for the Lambda function. Allow Lambda to delete messages from the queue after successful processing.
choices.explanation: A Lambda event source mapping polls SQS, invokes the function, and deletes messages after successful processing. Failed messages become visible again; processing must be idempotent.

choices.solution: Configure the Lambda function to monitor the S3 bucket for new uploads. When an uploaded image is detected, write the file name to a text file in memory and use the text file to keep track of the images that were processed.
choices.explanation: Lambda does not continuously monitor S3 as a persistent process. An in-memory text file is not durable across execution environments, so it cannot reliably track processing or preserve pending work.

choices.solution: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to monitor an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. When items are added to the queue, log the file name in a text file on the EC2 instance and invoke the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: The EC2 instance and its local tracking file add state and a failure point. Lambda's SQS event source mapping already performs managed polling without a dedicated monitoring server.

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) event to monitor the S3 bucket. When an image is uploaded, send an alert to an Amazon ample Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with the application owner's email address for further processing.
choices.explanation: Sending an email asks a person to process the image; it does not automatically invoke the compression workflow. EventBridge could route to compute targets, but this option specifies an email destination instead.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company wants to launch a one-deal-a-day website on AWS. Each day will feature exactly one product on sale for a period of 24 hours.

The company wants to be able to handle millions of requests each hour with millisecond latency during peak hours.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution:
Use Amazon S3 to host the full website in different S3 buckets. Add Amazon CloudFront distributions.

Set the S3 buckets as origins for the distributions. Store the order data in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: S3 static website hosting cannot run the dynamic order-processing APIs. Storing orders as S3 objects does not supply the low-latency transactional backend proposed by the serverless design.

choices.solution:
Deploy the full website on Amazon EC2 instances that run in Auto Scaling groups across multiple Availability Zones. Add an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute the website traffic.

Add another ALB for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
choices.explanation: This requires managing EC2 fleets, operating systems, load balancers, and database capacity. It can host the application, but adds significantly more infrastructure administration than the serverless option.

choices.solution:
Migrate the full application to run in containers. Host the containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS).

Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to increase and decrease the number of pods to process bursts in traffic. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
choices.explanation: EKS introduces Kubernetes cluster and workload administration. The Cluster Autoscaler adjusts worker-node capacity, not the number of application pods as stated in this option.

choices.solution:
Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host the website's static content. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution.

Set the S3 bucket as the origin. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions for the backend APIs.

Store the data in Amazon DynamoDB.
choices.explanation:
Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host the website's static content, deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution, set the S3 bucket as the origin, and use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon DynamoDB.

Using Amazon S3 to host static content and Amazon CloudFront to distribute the content can provide high performance and scale for websites with millions of requests each hour. Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda can be used to build scalable and highly available backend APIs to support the website, and Amazon DynamoDB can be used to store the data.

This solution requires minimal operational overhead as it leverages fully managed services that automatically scale to meet demand.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is designing an application. The application uses an AWS Lambda function to receive information through Amazon API Gateway and to store the information in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database.

During the proof-of-concept stage, the company has to increase the Lambda quotas significantly to handle the high volumes of data that the company needs to load into the database. A solutions architect must recommend a new design to improve scalability and minimize the configuration effort.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Refactor the Lambda function code to Apache Tomcat code that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Connect the database by using native Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) drivers.
choices.explanation: Rewriting the function as a Tomcat application adds server provisioning, scaling, patching, and code migration. It does not introduce a managed buffer between ingestion and database writes.

choices.solution: Change the platform from Aurora to Amazon DynamoDProvision a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Use the DAX client SDK to point the existing DynamoDB API calls at the DAX cluster.
choices.explanation: Replacing Aurora with DynamoDB requires a database and application redesign. DAX accelerates DynamoDB reads; it does not solve the Aurora ingestion bottleneck described here.

choices.solution:
Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information.

Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
choices.explanation: An SNS subscription invokes processing as messages arrive rather than providing a separately managed SQS work backlog. SQS allows database-writing consumers to process and retry buffered work at a controlled rate.

choices.solution:
Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information.

Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.
choices.explanation: "By dividing the functionality into two Lambda functions, one for receiving the information and the other for loading it into the database, you can independently scale and optimize each function based on their specific requirements. This approach allows for more efficient resource allocation and reduces the potential impact of high volumes of data on the overall system.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company provides a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) service that uses UDP connections. The service consists of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group.

The company has deployments across multiple AWS Regions. The company needs to route users to the Region with the lowest latency.

The company also needs automated failover between Regions.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group.

Use the NLB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
choices.explanation:
Answer A does not mention service Global Accelerator, it mentions the NLB would act like one. Not sure if the wording is wrong or not. ' Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group.

Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the NLB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.

choices.solution:
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group.

Use the ALB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
choices.explanation: An Application Load Balancer supports HTTP and HTTPS, not the UDP traffic used by this VoIP service. Global Accelerator cannot make an ALB handle an unsupported protocol.

choices.solution:
Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group.

Create an Amazon Route 53 latency record that points to aliases for each NLB. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the latency record as an origin.
choices.explanation: CloudFront is an HTTP and HTTPS content distribution service; it cannot proxy this UDP VoIP traffic. Putting a latency-based DNS record behind CloudFront does not resolve that limitation.

choices.solution:
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group.

Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted record that points to aliases for each ALB. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the weighted record as an origin.
choices.explanation: Both ALB and CloudFront are unsuitable for UDP VoIP traffic. A weighted Route 53 policy also divides traffic by weights rather than choosing the lowest-latency Region.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A development team needs to host a website that will be accessed by other teams. The website contents consist of HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript, and images.

Which method is the MOST cost-effective for hosting the website?

choices.solution: Containerize the website and host it in AWS Fargate.
choices.explanation: Fargate runs containers, so it introduces compute charges and deployment management for content that needs no server-side execution.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and host the website there.
choices.explanation:
Explanation: The website is a static website because it consists only of HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript, and images. The most cost-effective method is to create an Amazon S3 bucket and host the website there.

Amazon S3 is a highly scalable and cost-effective object storage service. It is suitable for hosting static websites because no web servers, containers, or backend compute resources are required.

To host the website on Amazon S3, the development team would create an S3 bucket, upload the website files to the bucket, and configure the bucket for static website hosting. Option A is incorrect because AWS Fargate is used to run containers and is unnecessary for a static website.

Option C is incorrect because an EC2 web server would add compute cost and operational overhead. Option D is incorrect because using an Application Load Balancer with Lambda and Express.js is overly complex for static content.

choices.solution: Deploy a web server on an Amazon EC2 instance to host the website.
choices.explanation: An EC2 web server adds instance charges, patching, and administration. S3 can serve these static files without a running server.

choices.solution: Configure an Application Load Balancer with an AWS Lambda target that uses the Express.js framework.
choices.explanation: An ALB and Lambda-based web server add request-processing components and costs that are unnecessary for serving static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs an online marketplace web application on AWS. The application serves hundreds of thousands of users during peak hours.

The company needs a scalable, near-real-time solution to share the details of millions of financial transactions with several other internal applications. Transactions also need to be processed to remove sensitive data before being stored in a document database for low-latency retrieval.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Store the transactions data into Amazon DynamoDB. Set up a rule in DynamoDB to remove sensitive data from every transaction upon write.

Use DynamoDB Streams to share the transactions data with other applications.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB does not have the proposed built-in rule that removes sensitive fields before a write. Streams record changes after storage, so this option also stores the sensitive transaction before the required sanitization.

choices.solution:
Stream the transactions data into Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to store data in Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon S3. Use AWS Lambda integration with Kinesis Data Firehose to remove sensitive data.

Other applications can consume the data stored in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB is not a native Firehose delivery destination as proposed here. Reading delivered S3 objects also substitutes buffered files for the independent near-real-time stream consumers.

choices.solution:
Stream the transactions data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use AWS Lambda integration to remove sensitive data from every transaction and then store the transactions data in Amazon DynamoDB.

Other applications can consume the transactions data off the Kinesis data stream.
choices.explanation:
Kinesis Data Streams durably ingests high-volume transactions and allows independent consumers. Lambda transforms records and writes sanitized data to DynamoDB.

Downstream applications must consume sanitized output if they are not authorized to see the original sensitive stream.

choices.solution:
Store the batched transactions data in Amazon S3 as files. Use AWS Lambda to process every file and remove sensitive data before updating the files in Amazon S3.

The Lambda function then stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB. Other applications can consume transaction files stored in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Batching transactions into S3 files introduces delay and requires each consumer to discover and process files. That is a weaker fit for the required near-real-time sharing than a multi-consumer stream.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is preparing to launch a public-facing web application in the AWS Cloud. The architecture consists of Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC behind an Elastic Load Balancer (ELB).

A third-party service is used for the DNS. The company's solutions architect must recommend a solution to detect and protect against large-scale DDoS attacks.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Enable Amazon GuardDuty on the account.
