choices.explanation: EventBridge does not guarantee ordered delivery of events.

choices.solution: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topics
choices.explanation: SNS FIFO also can send events or messages cocurrently to many subscribers while maintaining the order it receives. SNS fanout pattern is set in standard SNS which is commonly used to fan out events to large number of subscribers and usually for duplicated messages.

choices.solution: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topics
choices.explanation: SNS standard topics do not guarantee ordering or deduplicated delivery.

choices.solution: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues
choices.explanation: One FIFO queue distributes work among consumers rather than broadcasting each event concurrently to all three services.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a web application that is backed by Amazon RDS. A new database administrator caused data loss by accidentally editing information in a database table.

To help recover from this type of incident, the company wants the ability to restore the database to its state from 5 minutes before any change within the last 30 days.

Which feature should the solutions architect include in the design to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Read replicas
choices.explanation: Read replicas also replicate accidental changes and do not supply historical point-in-time restoration.

choices.solution: Manual snapshots
choices.explanation: Manual snapshots recover only to their capture times, not arbitrary points five minutes before an incident.

choices.solution: Automated backups
choices.explanation:
Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) can automatically create backups of your database every day. These backups are like snapshots of your entire database, capturing all the data.

They happen automatically, so you don't have to remember to do it. You can decide how long you want to keep these backup snapshots.

For example, you might choose to keep them for up to 35 days. This is like saying, "I want to keep the pictures of my database for the last 35 days."

choices.solution: Multi-AZ deployments
choices.explanation: A Multi-AZ standby replicates the accidental edit rather than preserving the earlier logical database state.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is using Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to its UDP-based application for users around the world. The application is hosted on redundant servers in the company's on-premises data centers in the United States, Asia, and Europe.

The company's compliance requirements state that the application must be hosted on premises. The company wants to improve the performance and availability of the application.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Configure an NLB in each of three AWS Regions with supported UDP relay targets inside its VPC. Have the relays forward traffic over private connections to the on-premises application servers.

Register the NLBs with Global Accelerator and point a CNAME to the accelerator DNS name.
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator and Regional NLBs support UDP routing, but an NLB UDP target cannot be an on-premises IP outside its VPC. This imported answer is incomplete: use supported in-VPC UDP relay targets with private connectivity to the on-premises servers, or revise the architecture.

choices.solution:
Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the ALBs as its endpoints.

Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.
choices.explanation: An Application Load Balancer does not support UDP traffic.

choices.solution:
Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three NLBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution.

Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.
choices.explanation: CloudFront cannot proxy this application's arbitrary UDP protocol even if NLBs are used as origins.

choices.solution:
Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three ALBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution.

Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.
choices.explanation: Neither CloudFront nor an ALB supports the required UDP application traffic.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has migrated an application to Amazon EC2 Linux instances. One of these EC2 instances runs several 1-hour tasks on a schedule.

These tasks were written by different teams and have no common programming language. The company is concerned about performance and scalability while these tasks run on a single instance.

A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to resolve these concerns.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS Batch to run the tasks as jobs. Schedule the jobs by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
choices.explanation:
AWS Batch: AWS Batch is a fully managed service for running batch computing workloads. It dynamically provisions the optimal quantity and type of compute resources based on the volume and specific resource requirements of the batch jobs.

It allows you to run tasks written in different programming languages with minimal operational overhead.

choices.solution: Convert the EC2 instance to a container. Use AWS App Runner to create the container on demand to run the tasks as jobs.
choices.explanation: App Runner hosts request-driven services rather than acting as a scheduled one-hour batch-job engine.

choices.solution: Copy the tasks into AWS Lambda functions. Schedule the Lambda functions by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
choices.explanation: Lambda's maximum invocation duration is 15 minutes, shorter than these one-hour tasks.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the EC2 instance that runs the tasks. Create an Auto Scaling group with the AMI to run multiple copies of the instance.
choices.explanation: Duplicating the whole instance requires custom scheduling and task placement and does not supply Batch's job queue and resource management.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate an Oracle database to AWS. The database consists of a single table that contains millions of geographic information systems (GIS) images that are high resolution and are identified by a geographic code.

When a natural disaster occurs, tens of thousands of images get updated every few minutes. Each geographic code has a single image or row that is associated with it.

The company wants a solution that is highly available and scalable during such events.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Store the images and geographic codes in a database table. Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.
choices.explanation: Keeping large image binaries in Oracle adds database storage and compute cost that scalable S3 object storage avoids.

choices.solution: Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Use Amazon DynamoDB with the geographic code as the key and the image S3 URL as the value.
choices.explanation: Explanation: Each geographic code maps to a single image/row - a simple key-value access pattern - and updates arrive in spiky bursts during disasters. DynamoDB is built for exactly that: high, unpredictable write throughput with simple key lookups, scaling more cost-effectively than a relational Oracle-on-RDS table for this access pattern.

choices.solution: Store the images and geographic codes in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) during times of high load.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB's 400-KB item limit is unsuitable for high-resolution images, and DAX does not fix that storage limit.

choices.solution:
Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Store geographic codes and image S3 URLs in a database table.

Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.
choices.explanation: S3 separates images efficiently, but a provisioned Oracle database adds licensing and capacity costs for a simple key-to-object lookup.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company is building a distributed application that involves several serverless functions and AWS services to complete order- processing tasks. These tasks require manual approvals as part of the workflow.

A solutions architect needs to design an architecture for the order-processing application. The solution must be able to combine multiple AWS Lambda functions into responsive serverless applications.

The solution also must orchestrate data and services that run on Amazon EC2 instances, containers, or on-premises servers.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS Step Functions to build the application.
choices.explanation: Step Functions provide a way to coordinate and orchestrate multiple AWS services, including AWS Lambda functions, in a serverless workflow. They allow you to build applications by connecting various serverless functions and services without managing the underlying infrastructure.

choices.solution: Integrate all the application components in an AWS Glue job.
choices.explanation: Glue orchestrates data-integration jobs rather than general application tasks with human approval callbacks.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to build the application.
choices.explanation: SQS provides queues but requires custom orchestration for state transitions, branching, retries, and approvals.

choices.solution: Use AWS Lambda functions and Amazon EventBridge events to build the application.
choices.explanation: Custom functions and events require implementing workflow state and approval coordination that Step Functions supplies.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company recently deployed a new auditing system to centralize information about operating system versions, patching, and installed software for Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect must ensure all instances provisioned through EC2 Auto Scaling groups successfully send reports to the auditing system as soon as they are launched and terminated.

Which solution achieves these goals MOST efficiently?

choices.solution: Use a scheduled AWS Lambda function and run a script remotely on all EC2 instances to send data to the audit system.
choices.explanation: Scheduled polling is delayed and may miss information from an instance that has already terminated.

choices.solution: Use EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to run a custom script to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
choices.explanation: Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks can run custom audit work during launch or termination, but they pause the lifecycle transition until completion or timeout. Use EventBridge notifications when pausing is unacceptable.

choices.solution: Use an EC2 Auto Scaling launch configuration to run a custom script through user data to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
choices.explanation: User data runs at launch and does not provide a termination lifecycle hook.

choices.solution: Run a custom script on the instance operating system to send data to the audit system. Configure the script to be invoked by the EC2 Auto Scaling group when the instance starts and is terminated.
choices.explanation: An ordinary startup/shutdown script lacks the explicit Auto Scaling wait-and-complete lifecycle coordination needed to send reports before termination.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is developing a real-time multiplayer game that uses UDP for communications between the client and servers in an Auto Scaling group. Spikes in demand are anticipated during the day, so the game server platform must adapt accordingly.

Developers want to store gamer scores and other non-relational data in a database solution that will scale without intervention.

Which solution should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Route 53 for traffic distribution and Amazon Aurora Serverless for data storage.
choices.explanation: DNS does not provide per-flow UDP load balancing, and Aurora is a relational database rather than the requested non-relational store.

choices.solution: Use a Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon DynamoDB on-demand for data storage.
choices.explanation:
Think of an NLB like a traffic cop for your game. It helps distribute and manage the incoming traffic from players to your game servers.

It ensures that the load is balanced across your servers, which is crucial for handling the expected spikes in demand. DynamoDB is a type of database that can store data for your game, such as gamer scores. "On-demand" means that DynamoDB automatically scales to handle the amount of data and traffic your game is experiencing.

choices.solution: Use a Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon Aurora Global Database for data storage.
choices.explanation: An Aurora global database targets cross-Region relational replication and does not automatically scale non-relational capacity.

choices.solution: Use an Application Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon DynamoDB global tables for data storage.
choices.explanation: An ALB cannot handle arbitrary UDP traffic.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The company already uses several Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances.

The company wants a solution that automatically starts and stops the EC2 instances and DB instances outside of business hours. The solution must minimize cost and infrastructure maintenance.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Scale the EC2 instances by using elastic resize. Scale the DB instances to zero outside of business hours.
choices.explanation: Elastic resize is not EC2 instance scheduling, and provisioned RDS instances cannot be scaled to zero as proposed.

choices.solution: Explore AWS Marketplace for partner solutions that will automatically start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
choices.explanation: A partner solution may work but adds acquisition, configuration, and possible licensing cost compared with native scheduled Lambda automation.

choices.solution: Launch another EC2 instance. Configure a crontab schedule to run shell scripts that will start and stop the existing EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
choices.explanation: An extra always-running EC2 scheduler adds server cost and maintenance.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function that will start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.
choices.explanation:
AWS Lambda Function: Create a Lambda function that contains the logic to start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances. Lambda is a serverless compute service that allows you to run code without provisioning or managing servers.

It is a cost-effective and maintenance-free solution. Amazon EventBridge: Configure EventBridge (formerly CloudWatch Events) to invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.

EventBridge provides a reliable and scalable way to schedule the execution of Lambda functions at specified intervals, such as starting and stopping instances during business hours.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company hosts a three-tier web application that includes a PostgreSQL database. The database stores the metadata from documents.

The company searches the metadata for key terms to retrieve documents that the company reviews in a report each month. The documents are stored in Amazon S3.

The documents are usually written only once, but they are updated frequently. The reporting process takes a few hours with the use of relational queries.

The reporting process must not prevent any document modifications or the addition of new documents. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to speed up the reporting process.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the application code?

choices.solution: Set up a new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) cluster that includes a read replica. Scale the read replica to generate the reports.
choices.explanation: DocumentDB changes the database interface and data model, requiring significant application-query changes.

choices.solution: Set up a new Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster that includes an Aurora Replica. Issue queries to the Aurora Replica to generate the reports.
choices.explanation: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster that includes an Aurora Replica. Issue queries to the Aurora Replica to generate the reports) is the best option for speeding up the reporting process for a three-tier web application that includes a PostgreSQL database storing metadata from documents, while not impacting document modifications or additions, with the least amount of change to the application code.

choices.solution: Set up a new Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the reporting module to query the secondary RDS node so that the reporting module does not affect the primary node.
choices.explanation: The standby in a traditional RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment cannot serve reporting queries.

choices.solution:
Set up a new Amazon DynamoDB table to store the documents. Use a fixed write capacity to support new document entries.

Automatically scale the read capacity to support the reports.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB requires a different data model and queries and does not preserve the PostgreSQL reporting code.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has a large dataset for its online advertising business stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in a single Availability Zone. The company wants business reporting queries to run without impacting the write operations to the production DB instance.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy RDS read replicas to process the business reporting queries.
choices.explanation:
Amazon RDS provides the ability to create read replicas of a source DB instance. Read replicas can be used to offload read traffic from the primary (write) DB instance, allowing you to scale read operations horizontally.

This is particularly useful for scenarios where you want to run reporting queries without affecting the write performance of the production DB instance.

choices.solution: Scale out the DB instance horizontally by placing it behind an Elastic Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: An ELB does not horizontally replicate an RDS writer or turn copies into synchronized reporting databases.

choices.solution: Scale up the DB instance to a larger instance type to handle write operations and queries.
choices.explanation: Vertical scaling leaves reporting queries competing with production writes on the same instance.

choices.solution: Deploy the DB instance in multiple Availability Zones to process the business reporting queries.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby is for failover and cannot serve reporting queries.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company hosts a three-tier ecommerce application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).

All ecommerce data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MariaDB Multi-AZ DB instance. The company wants to optimize customer session management during transactions.

The application must store session data durably.

Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Turn on the sticky sessions feature (session affinity) on the ALB.
choices.explanation: Sticky sessions keep users on one instance but lose local session state if that instance terminates.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store customer session information.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB stores sessions centrally so requests can reach any application instance without losing session state.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon Cognito user pool to manage user session information.
choices.explanation: A Cognito user pool manages identity tokens rather than arbitrary durable shopping-session state.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to store customer session information.
choices.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis provides a shared low-latency session store; replication and Multi-AZ failover improve availability.

choices.solution: Use AWS Systems Manager Application Manager in the application to manage user session information.
choices.explanation: Application Manager manages application resources and operations, not per-customer session data.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company needs a backup strategy for its three-tier stateless web application. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group with a dynamic scaling policy that is configured to respond to scaling events.

The database tier runs on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The web application does not require temporary local storage on the EC2 instances.

The company's recovery point objective (RPO) is 2 hours. The backup strategy must maximize scalability and optimize resource utilization for this environment.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Take snapshots of Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes of the EC2 instances and database every 2 hours to meet the RPO.
choices.explanation: RDS storage is managed and cannot be backed up through customer EBS snapshots; repeatedly snapshotting stateless workers also wastes resources.

choices.solution: Configure a snapshot lifecycle policy to take Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS to meet the RPO.
choices.explanation: Snapshotting every stateless instance adds unnecessary storage and scheduling compared with retaining the deployment AMIs.

choices.solution: Retain the latest Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) of the web and application tiers. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS and use point-in-time recovery to meet the RPO.
choices.explanation:
Snapshots of EBS volumes would be necessary if you want to back up the entire EC2 instance, including any applications and temporary data stored on the EBS volumes attached to the instances. When you take a snapshot of an EBS volume, it backs up the entire contents of that volume.

This ensures that you can restore the entire EC2 instance to a specific point in time more quickly. However, if there is no temporary data stored on the EBS volumes, then snapshots of EBS volumes are not necessary.

choices.solution: Take snapshots of Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes of the EC2 instances every 2 hours. Enable automated backups in Amazon RDS and use point-in-time recovery to meet the RPO.
choices.explanation: Per-instance snapshots every two hours are redundant for stateless compute that can be recreated from its current AMI.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A payment processing company records all voice communication with its customers and stores the audio files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to capture the text from the audio files.

The company must remove from the text any personally identifiable information (PII) that belongs to customers.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Process the audio files by using Amazon Kinesis Video Streams. Use an AWS Lambda function to scan for known PII patterns.
choices.explanation: Kinesis Video Streams transports media but does not itself transcribe speech or redact PII.

choices.solution: When an audio file is uploaded to the S3 bucket, invoke an AWS Lambda function to start an Amazon Textract task to analyze the call recordings.
choices.explanation: Textract extracts text from documents, not speech from audio recordings.

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon Transcribe transcription job with PII redaction turned on. When an audio file is uploaded to the S3 bucket, invoke an AWS Lambda function to start the transcription job.

Store the output in a separate S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Amazon Transcribe is a fully managed service provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS) that enables automatic speech recognition (ASR). It allows developers to convert spoken language into written text, making it useful for various applications such as transcription services, voice analytics, and content indexing.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Connect contact flow that ingests the audio files with transcription turned on. Embed an AWS Lambda function to scan for known PII patterns.

Use Amazon EventBridge to start the contact flow when an audio file is uploaded to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: A contact flow is not the proposed batch-file transcription mechanism, and custom PII pattern scanning adds work compared with Transcribe redaction.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company needs to run a scheduled daily job to aggregate and filter sales records for analytics. The company stores the sales records in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Each object can be up to 10 GB in size. Based on the number of sales events, the job can take up to an hour to complete.

The CPU and memory usage of the job are constant and are known in advance. A solutions architect needs to minimize the amount of operational effort that is needed for the job to run.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function that has an Amazon EventBridge notification. Schedule the EventBridge event to run once a day.
choices.explanation: The job can run for an hour, exceeding Lambda's 15-minute invocation limit.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Lambda function. Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API, and integrate the API with the function.

Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that calls the API and invokes the function.
choices.explanation: Adding API Gateway does not extend Lambda's 15-minute execution limit.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.
choices.explanation: An EventBridge schedule launches an ECS Fargate task without managing a scheduler or worker hosts. Fargate supports long-running container jobs beyond the Lambda execution timeout.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type and an Auto Scaling group with at least one EC2 instance. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.
choices.explanation: The EC2 launch type retains host capacity and maintenance work that a scheduled Fargate task avoids.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A meteorological startup company has a custom web application to sell weather data to its users online. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store its data and wants to build a new service that sends an alert to the managers of four internal teams every time a new weather event is recorded.

The company does not want this new service to affect the performance of the current application.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use DynamoDB transactions to write new event data to the table. Configure the transactions to notify internal teams.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB transactions do not directly publish notifications to the teams.

choices.solution: Have the current application publish a message to four Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Have each team subscribe to one topic.
choices.explanation: Publishing to four topics modifies and adds network work to the current application; a stream-triggered single-topic fan-out avoids that coupling.

choices.solution: Enable Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table. Use triggers to write to a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to which the teams can subscribe.
choices.explanation:
Using a single SNS topic simplifies the notification process. The trigger can publish a message to this topic, and each internal team can subscribe to this topic.

This reduces the operational overhead compared to managing multiple SNS topics (Option B).

choices.solution: Add a custom attribute to each record to flag new items. Write a cron job that scans the table every minute for items that are new and notifies an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to which the teams can subscribe.
choices.explanation: Repeated table scans consume capacity and add polling delay; SQS also distributes messages rather than broadcasting each event to all teams.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to make an existing application highly available and resilient. The current version of the application resides in the company's data center.

The application recently experienced data loss after a database server crashed because of an unexpected power outage. The company needs a solution that avoids any single points of failure.

The solution must give the application the ability to scale to meet user demand.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ configuration.
choices.explanation: Auto Scaling Across Multiple Availability Zones: Deploying application servers using EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) helps avoid a single point of failure. If one AZ experiences an issue, the application can continue to operate in another AZ.

choices.solution:
Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone. Deploy the database on an EC2 instance.

Enable EC2 Auto Recovery.
choices.explanation: A single AZ remains a common failure point, and EC2 recovery does not replicate database data or handle an AZ-wide outage.

choices.solution:
Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance with a read replica in a single Availability Zone.

Promote the read replica to replace the primary DB instance if the primary DB instance fails.
choices.explanation: A same-AZ read replica shares the AZ failure risk and asynchronous replication can lose recent writes; manual promotion adds recovery work.

choices.solution:
Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Deploy the primary and secondary database servers on EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones.

Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach to create shared storage between the instances.
choices.explanation: EBS Multi-Attach works only within one Availability Zone and cannot supply the proposed shared cross-AZ volume.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company needs to ingest and handle large amounts of streaming data that its application generates. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and sends data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, which is configured with default settings.

Every other day, the application consumes the data and writes the data to an Amazon S3 bucket for business intelligence (BI) processing. The company observes that Amazon S3 is not receiving all the data that the application sends to Kinesis Data Streams.

What should a solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

choices.solution: Update the Kinesis Data Streams default settings by modifying the data retention period.
choices.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams retains data for 24 hours by default. Increase retention beyond the every-other-day consumer interval, with recovery margin, so records are not expired before consumption.

choices.solution: Update the application to use the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL) to send the data to Kinesis Data Streams.
choices.explanation: KPL optimizes producers but does not extend the default 24-hour retention that expires before the two-day consumer interval.

choices.solution: Update the number of Kinesis shards to handle the throughput of the data that is sent to Kinesis Data Streams.
choices.explanation: More shards improve throughput but do not prevent records aging out before consumption.

choices.solution: Turn on S3 Versioning within the S3 bucket to preserve every version of every object that is ingested in the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 Versioning cannot recover records that already expired in Kinesis before they reached S3.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has deployed a serverless application that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses the Lambda function to process the documents.

After a recent marketing campaign, the company noticed that the application did not process many of the documents.

What should a solutions architect do to improve the architecture of this application?

choices.solution: Set the Lambda function's runtime timeout value to 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: A longer timeout does not create a durable backlog or solve concurrent processing limits.

choices.solution: Configure an S3 bucket replication policy. Stage the documents in the S3 bucket for later processing.
choices.explanation: Replication copies documents but does not ensure failed processing requests are retried by workers.

choices.solution: Deploy an additional Lambda function. Load balance the processing of the documents across the two Lambda functions.
choices.explanation: Adding a second function requires custom routing and does not supply a durable, controlled processing queue.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Send the requests to the queue.

Configure the queue as an event source for Lambda.
choices.explanation: Introducing Amazon SQS as a queue allows for better decoupling between the S3 events and the document processing. This ensures that the Lambda function is not overwhelmed with spikes in incoming events, leading to missed document processing.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing the architecture for a software demonstration environment. The environment will run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).

The system will experience significant increases in traffic during working hours but is not required to operate on weekends.

Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to ensure that the system can scale to meet demand? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Use AWS Auto Scaling to adjust the ALB capacity based on request rate.
choices.explanation: ALB capacity is managed by AWS; the proposed policy does not scale the application instances.

choices.solution: Use AWS Auto Scaling to scale the capacity of the VPC internet gateway.
choices.explanation: An internet gateway has no user-configurable Auto Scaling capacity.

choices.solution: Launch the EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions to distribute the load across Regions.
choices.explanation: A single Auto Scaling group is regional, and a multi-Region deployment adds unnecessary complexity for this capacity requirement.

choices.solution: Use a target tracking scaling policy to scale the Auto Scaling group based on instance CPU utilization.
choices.explanation: Target tracking adjusts application instance capacity to maintain the chosen utilization metric.

choices.solution: Use scheduled scaling to change the Auto Scaling group minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to zero for weekends. Revert to the default values at the start of the week.
choices.explanation: Scheduled scaling sets capacity to zero when the application is not needed and restores it before work resumes.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs an application that receives data from thousands of geographically dispersed remote devices that use UDP. The application processes the data immediately and sends a message back to the device if necessary.

No data is stored. The company needs a solution that minimizes latency for the data transmission from the devices.

The solution also must provide rapid failover to another AWS Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions.

Configure the NLB to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the data.
choices.explanation: An NLB cannot use Lambda as its UDP processing target, and DNS failover is affected by cached resolutions.

choices.solution: Use AWS Global Accelerator with an NLB endpoint in each of two Regions. Run the processing application as an ECS service on Fargate and register the tasks in each NLB's UDP target group.
choices.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator: AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses that act as a fixed entry point to your application. It routes traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal AWS endpoint based on health, geography, and routing policies.

Network Load Balancer (NLB): NLB is well-suited for UDP-based traffic, and it's designed for high-performance, low-latency applications. In this case, it can efficiently handle the thousands of geographically dispersed remote devices sending UDP traffic.

Amazon ECS with Fargate Launch Type: Using ECS with Fargate allows you to deploy and run containers without managing the underlying infrastructure. This setup can efficiently handle the immediate processing of data without the need to manage the underlying servers.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Global Accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions as an endpoint.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster.

Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: An ALB does not support arbitrary UDP traffic.

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster.

Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
choices.explanation: An ALB cannot handle UDP, and DNS failover does not provide Global Accelerator's rapid endpoint rerouting.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A solutions architect must migrate a Windows Internet Information Services (IIS) web application to AWS. The application currently relies on a file share hosted in the user's on-premises network-attached storage (NAS).

The solutions architect has proposed migrating the IIS web servers to Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones that are connected to the storage solution, and configuring an Elastic Load Balancer attached to the instances.

Which replacement to the on-premises file share is MOST resilient and durable?

choices.solution: Migrate the file share to Amazon RDS.
choices.explanation: RDS is a relational database, not a Windows file-share replacement.

choices.solution: Migrate the file share to AWS Storage Gateway.
choices.explanation: Storage Gateway adds an appliance and cache layer rather than directly providing the managed multi-AZ Windows filesystem for the AWS servers.

choices.solution: Migrate the file share to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
choices.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server: Amazon FSx is a fully managed file storage service that is compatible with Windows file systems. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is specifically designed for Windows workloads, including IIS web applications.

It provides a highly available and durable file system that can be accessed by multiple EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.

choices.solution: Migrate the file share to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).
choices.explanation: EFS provides NFS rather than the Windows SMB filesystem expected by this IIS application.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has a web application with sporadic usage patterns. There is heavy usage at the beginning of each month, moderate usage at the start of each week, and unpredictable usage during the week.

The application consists of a web server and a MySQL database server running inside the data center. The company would like to move the application to the AWS Cloud, and needs to select a cost-effective database platform that will not require database modifications.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Amazon DynamoDB
choices.explanation: DynamoDB uses a different data model and APIs from MySQL and requires application changes.

choices.solution: Amazon RDS for MySQL
choices.explanation: Provisioned RDS capacity must be sized and paid for despite highly variable usage; Aurora Serverless adjusts compute capacity.

choices.solution: MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora Serverless
choices.explanation:
Aurora Serverless is a serverless option for MySQL-compatible databases. It automatically adjusts the database capacity based on actual usage, making it suitable for sporadic usage patterns.

It is MySQL-compatible, so it won't require significant database modifications.

choices.solution: MySQL deployed on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group
choices.explanation: An EC2 Auto Scaling group does not safely implement MySQL database replication and scaling without custom management.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company is experiencing an increase in user traffic. The company's store is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances as a two-tier web application consisting of a web tier and a separate database tier.

As traffic increases, the company notices that the architecture is causing significant delays in sending timely marketing and order confirmation email to users. The company wants to reduce the time it spends resolving complex email delivery issues and minimize operational overhead.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing.
choices.explanation: Dedicated email servers retain mail delivery, patching, and capacity-management work.

choices.solution: Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
choices.explanation: Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) is a fully managed email sending service. By configuring the web instances to send emails through Amazon SES, the ecommerce company can offload the complexity of email delivery to a reliable and scalable service.

choices.solution: Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
choices.explanation: SNS email subscriptions are notification delivery, not a transactional and marketing email platform like SES.

choices.solution: Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing. Place the instances in an Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: An Auto Scaling email fleet still requires managing mail servers and deliverability instead of using managed SES.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A rapidly growing global ecommerce company is hosting its web application on AWS. The web application includes static content and dynamic content.

The website stores online transaction processing (OLTP) data in an Amazon RDS database The website's users are experiencing slow page loads.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon Redshift cluster.
choices.explanation: Redshift is an analytics warehouse and does not directly improve the transactional website's existing query path.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution.
choices.explanation: CloudFront caches static content at edge locations, reducing latency and web-server load.

choices.solution: Host the dynamic web content in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: S3 cannot execute the dynamic server-side web application.

choices.solution: Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance.
choices.explanation: An RDS read replica offloads read-only queries from the primary database; route eligible queries to it explicitly.

choices.solution: Configure a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS DB instance.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby improves availability but does not offload application reads.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB cluster to simplify time-consuming database administrative tasks for production database workloads. The company wants to ensure that its database is highly available and will provide automatic failover support in most scenarios in less than 40 seconds.

The company wants to offload reads off of the primary instance and keep costs as low as possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Create one read replica and point the read workload to the read replica.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance can take longer to fail over and requires an extra read replica beyond its unreadable standby.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB duster deployment Create two read replicas and point the read workload to the read replicas.
choices.explanation: The cluster already includes two readable instances; creating two more replicas adds unnecessary capacity and cost.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Point the read workload to the secondary instances in the Multi-AZ pair.
choices.explanation: The standby in a Multi-AZ DB instance pair cannot serve application reads.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment Point the read workload to the reader endpoint.
choices.explanation: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB Cluster Deployment: This provides high availability by automatically replicating data to a standby instance in a different Availability Zone. In case of a failure, Amazon RDS automatically fails over to the standby instance.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is developing a new machine learning (ML) model solution on AWS. The models are developed as independent microservices that fetch approximately 1 GB of model data from Amazon S3 at startup and load the data into memory.

Users access the models through an asynchronous API. Users can send a request or a batch of requests and specify where the results should be sent.

The company provides models to hundreds of users. The usage patterns for the models are irregular.

Some models could be unused for days or weeks. Other models could receive batches of thousands of requests at a time.

Which design should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Direct the requests from the API to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by the NLB.
choices.explanation: An NLB cannot invoke Lambda targets, and the direct endpoint lacks a durable batch-request buffer.

choices.solution:
Direct the requests from the API to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

Use AWS App Mesh to scale the instances of the ECS cluster based on the SQS queue size.
choices.explanation: App Mesh handles service networking; it does not scale ECS capacity based on queue depth as proposed.

choices.solution:
Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by SQS events.

Use AWS Auto Scaling to increase the number of vCPUs for the Lambda functions based on the SQS queue size.
choices.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling cannot dynamically adjust the vCPU allocation of Lambda functions based on SQS backlog; Lambda compute is tied to configured memory.

choices.solution:
Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue.

Enable AWS Auto Scaling on Amazon ECS for both the cluster and copies of the service based on the queue size.
choices.explanation:
Amazon ECS Services: Deploying the models as Amazon ECS services allows for flexibility in managing the containerized applications. ECS services can efficiently handle the startup process of fetching model data from Amazon S3 and loading it into memory.

Application Load Balancer (ALB): The ALB is used to direct requests from the API to the ECS services. ALB provides advanced routing capabilities and can handle the asynchronous API requirements.

AWS App Mesh: AWS App Mesh can be used to scale the instances of the ECS cluster based on the SQS queue size. This allows for dynamic scaling based on demand, helping to efficiently use resources.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is implementing a complex Java application with a MySQL database. The Java application must be deployed on Apache Tomcat and must be highly available.

What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy the application in AWS Lambda. Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to connect with the Lambda functions.
choices.explanation: Lambda does not provide the existing Tomcat application-server deployment model without restructuring the application.

choices.solution: Deploy the application by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Configure a load-balanced environment and a rolling deployment policy.
choices.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk: It is a fully managed service that simplifies the deployment and operation of applications, including web applications running Apache Tomcat. Elastic Beanstalk handles the deployment details, capacity provisioning, load balancing, auto-scaling, and application health monitoring, making it easier to deploy and manage your applications.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon ElastiCache. Configure the ElastiCache security group to allow access from the application.
choices.explanation: ElastiCache is not a MySQL relational database replacement.

choices.solution:
Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Install a MySQL server on the EC2 instance.

Configure the application on the server. Create an AMI.

Use the AMI to create a launch template with an Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: Duplicating an AMI containing MySQL does not configure replicated database state and adds self-managed application-server work.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group and with an Amazon DynamoDB table.

The company wants to ensure the application can be made available in another AWS Region with minimal downtime.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of downtime?

choices.solution:
Create an Auto Scaling group and a load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table.

Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
choices.explanation: A secondary application fleet and DynamoDB global table keep both application capacity and data available in the recovery Region. DNS failover switches traffic; plan for the chosen global-table consistency mode.

choices.solution: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, load balancers, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when needed Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
choices.explanation: Creating the entire environment during failure takes longer and does not continuously replicate the existing table data.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and a load balancer to be launched when needed. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table.

Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
choices.explanation: Replicated data helps, but launching compute only after failure increases downtime compared with pre-provisioned standby capacity.

choices.solution:
Create an Auto Scaling group and load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to trigger an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 pointing to the disaster recovery load balancer.
choices.explanation: A custom alarm/Lambda DNS update adds reaction steps and maintenance compared with configured Route 53 health-based failover.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company moved its on-premises PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company successfully launched a new product.

The workload on the database has increased. The company wants to accommodate the larger workload without adding infrastructure.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Buy reserved DB instances for the total workload. Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance larger.
choices.explanation:
When you commit to using a database instance for a longer time (with reserved instances), AWS gives you a discount compared to paying on a month-to-month basis. Imagine you have a computer, and you want to make it more powerful because you have more things to do on it.

Making the instance larger means upgrading the power of your virtual computer.

choices.solution: Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance a Multi-AZ DB instance.
choices.explanation: A Multi-AZ DB instance standby improves availability, not the writer's processing capacity.

choices.solution: Buy reserved DB instances for the total workload. Add another Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance.
choices.explanation: A separate database adds infrastructure and does not transparently increase capacity of the existing writer.

choices.solution: Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance an on-demand DB instance.
choices.explanation: Changing the purchasing model without increasing capacity does not accommodate the larger workload and misses reservation savings.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company operates an ecommerce website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in an Auto Scaling group. The site is experiencing performance issues related to a high request rate from illegitimate external systems with changing IP addresses.

The security team is worried about potential DDoS attacks against the website. The company must block the illegitimate incoming requests in a way that has a minimal impact on legitimate users.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon Inspector and associate it with the ALB.
choices.explanation: Inspector detects vulnerabilities; it does not rate-limit requests arriving at an ALB.

choices.solution: Deploy AWS WAF, associate it with the ALB, and configure a rate-limiting rule.
choices.explanation:
AWS WAF is a web application firewall service that helps protect your web applications from common web exploits. It allows you to create rules to filter and monitor HTTP and HTTPS traffic based on conditions that you define.

By associating AWS WAF with the ALB, you can inspect and filter incoming traffic before it reaches your instances, providing a layer of protection against DDoS attacks and other malicious activities.

choices.solution: Deploy rules to the network ACLs associated with the ALB to block the incomingtraffic.
choices.explanation: Static address-block rules require continuous updates as attacker IPs change and cannot inspect HTTP request rates.

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon GuardDuty and enable rate-limiting protection when configuring GuardDuty.
choices.explanation: GuardDuty detects threats but has no native rate-limiting protection setting.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company used an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance during application testing. Before terminating the DB instance at the end of the test cycle, a solutions architect created two backups.

The solutions architect created the first backup by using the mysqldump utility to create a database dump. The solutions architect created the second backup by enabling the final DB snapshot option on RDS termination.

The company is now planning for a new test cycle and wants to create a new DB instance from the most recent backup. The company has chosen a MySQL-compatible edition of Amazon Aurora to host the DB instance.

Which solutions will create the new DB instance? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Import the RDS snapshot directly into Aurora.
choices.explanation: A compatible RDS for MySQL snapshot can be migrated to a new Aurora MySQL cluster.

choices.solution: Upload the RDS snapshot to Amazon S3. Then import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
choices.explanation: An RDS snapshot cannot be uploaded to S3 as an ordinary snapshot file; Aurora supports migration from eligible RDS snapshots directly.

choices.solution: Create a new Aurora MySQL cluster. Download the mysqldump backup from Amazon S3 and restore the SQL dump into the cluster with a MySQL client.
choices.explanation: Create an Aurora MySQL cluster and replay the mysqldump SQL through a MySQL client. A logical SQL dump is not a Percona physical backup for Aurora's native S3 restore.

choices.solution: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
choices.explanation: DMS consumes running database sources or supported data formats, not an RDS snapshot as its source.

choices.solution: Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the database dump into Aurora.
choices.explanation: DMS's S3 source expects supported record files, not a mysqldump SQL script; restore that dump with a MySQL client.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company hosts a multi-tier web application on Amazon Linux Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.

The company observes that the Auto Scaling group launches more On-Demand Instances when the application's end users access high volumes of static web content. The company wants to optimize cost.

What should a solutions architect do to redesign the application MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Update the Auto Scaling group to use Reserved Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
choices.explanation: Reservations discount compute but do not remove the unnecessary web-server work for static objects.

choices.solution: Update the Auto Scaling group to scale by launching Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
choices.explanation: Spot lowers some instance cost but still routes static downloads through compute and introduces interruption handling.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to host the static web contents from an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) service that delivers static and dynamic web content, including images, videos, CSS, and JavaScript, with low latency and high transfer speeds. It can be used to cache and distribute static content globally, reducing the load on your web servers.

By creating a CloudFront distribution and hosting static web content in an Amazon S3 bucket, you offload the serving of static content to the CDN, which can significantly reduce the load on your EC2 instances.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function behind an Amazon API Gateway API to host the static website contents.
choices.explanation: Lambda and API Gateway add execution and request-processing layers when S3 and CloudFront directly serve static objects.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has hired a solutions architect to design a reliable architecture for its application. The application consists of one Amazon RDS DB instance and two manually provisioned Amazon EC2 instances that run web servers.

The EC2 instances are located in a single Availability Zone. An employee recently deleted the DB instance, and the application was unavailable for 24 hours as a result.

The company is concerned with the overall reliability of its environment.

What should the solutions architect do to maximize reliability of the application's infrastructure?

choices.solution: Delete one EC2 instance and enable termination protection on the other EC2 instance. Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.
choices.explanation: One web instance remains a failure point even with termination protection, and it cannot elastically scale.

choices.solution: Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection. Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer, and run them in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Multi-AZ RDS Instance: By updating the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, you ensure that there is a standby replica in a different Availability Zone, providing high availability and automatic failover in case of a failure in the primary zone. Deletion Protection: Enabling deletion protection for the DB instance helps prevent accidental deletion, reducing the risk of downtime caused by human error.

choices.solution:
Create an additional DB instance along with an Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. Configure the application to invoke the Lambda function through API Gateway.

Have the Lambda function write the data to the two DB instances.
choices.explanation: Custom dual database writes require coordination, failure handling, and consistency logic instead of managed Multi-AZ replication.

choices.solution:
Place the EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group that has multiple subnets located in multiple Availability Zones. Use Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.

Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the health of the instances Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.
choices.explanation: Using only interruptible Spot instances weakens guaranteed web-tier availability, and this option omits the ALB for balanced healthy-target access.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company stores data in PDF format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must follow a legal requirement to retain all new and existing data in Amazon S3 for 7 years.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution:
Turn on the S3 Versioning feature for the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Lifecycle to delete the data after 7 years.

Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete for all S3 objects.
choices.explanation: Versioning and MFA Delete do not enforce an immutable seven-year retention period against authorized permanent deletion.

choices.solution:
Turn on S3 Object Lock with governance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years.

Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
choices.explanation: Governance retention can be bypassed by privileged users, and recopying everything adds unnecessary work.

choices.solution:
Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years.

Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
choices.explanation: Compliance mode is appropriate, but manually recopying existing objects adds work compared with a Batch Operations retention job.

choices.solution:
Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years.

Use S3 Batch Operations to bring the existing data into compliance.
choices.explanation: Object Lock compliance retention protects the retained S3 versions for seven years. Batch Operations applies retention to existing versions; default retention applies only to newly written versions.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has a stateless web application that runs on AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to deploy the application across multiple AWS Regions to provide Regional failover capabilities.

What should a solutions architect do to route traffic to multiple Regions?

choices.solution: Create a Route 53 latency or weighted routing policy for the Regional API endpoints and associate health checks with each record so unhealthy Regions are excluded.
choices.explanation: Latency or weighted routing with health checks supports active-active Regional routing and excludes unhealthy records. Route 53 failover routing is active-passive, so "active-active failover" is not a failover policy setting.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin for each Region. Use CloudFront health checks to route traffic.
choices.explanation: CloudFront does not provide the proposed periodic origin health-check routing; origin-group failover also has method and failure-condition limitations.

choices.solution:
Create a transit gateway. Attach the transit gateway to the API Gateway endpoint in each Region.

Configure the transit gateway to route requests.
choices.explanation: Transit gateways connect private networks and cannot attach directly to API Gateway endpoints.

choices.solution: Create an Application Load Balancer in the primary Region. Set the target group to point to the API Gateway endpoint hostnames in each Region.
choices.explanation: An ALB target group does not accept arbitrary API Gateway endpoint hostnames as targets.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs its application on an Oracle database. The company plans to quickly migrate to AWS because of limited resources for the database, backup administration, and data center maintenance.

The application uses third-party database features that require privileged access.

Which solution will help the company migrate the database to AWS MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Replace third-party features with cloud services.
choices.explanation: Standard RDS restricts privileged access; replacing the third-party features requires application changes and delays the migration.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
choices.explanation: RDS Custom for Oracle provides managed automation while allowing supported host and database customization needed for third-party features.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
choices.explanation: Oracle on EC2 supports customization but leaves database backup, patching, and infrastructure administration to the company.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by rewriting the application code to remove dependency on Oracle APEX.
choices.explanation: Rewriting Oracle dependencies for PostgreSQL requires substantial development instead of a quick compatible migration.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has a three-tier web application that is in a single server. The company wants to migrate the application to the AWS Cloud.

The company also wants the application to align with the AWS Well-Architected Framework and to be consistent with AWS recommended best practices for security, scalability, and resiliency.

Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

choices.solution:
Create a VPC across two Availability Zones with the application's existing architecture. Host the application with existing architecture on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet in each Availability Zone with EC2 Auto Scaling groups.

Secure the EC2 instance with security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs).
choices.explanation: Replicating the original single-server stack keeps the tiers coupled and does not establish managed database replication.

choices.solution: Set up security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs) to control access to the database layer. Set up a single Amazon RDS database in a private subnet.
choices.explanation: A single database instance remains a failure point despite network access controls.

choices.solution:
Create a VPC across two Availability Zones. Refactor the application to host the web tier, application tier, and database tier.

Host each tier on its own private subnet with Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and application tier.
choices.explanation: Separate the application tiers into private subnets across two Availability Zones and scale the web and application tiers independently.

choices.solution: Use a single Amazon RDS database. Allow database access only from the application tier security group.
choices.explanation: Restricting database access is good practice, but a single-instance database lacks the required Multi-AZ resilience.

choices.solution: Use Elastic Load Balancers in front of the web tier. Control access by using security groups containing references to each layer's security groups.
choices.explanation: An internet-facing load balancer in public subnets fronts the private web tier; security-group references restrict traffic between tiers.

choices.solution: Use an Amazon RDS database Multi-AZ cluster deployment in private subnets. Allow database access only from application tier security groups.
choices.explanation: An RDS Multi-AZ database in private subnets provides failover and accepts database traffic only from the application tier.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to implement a backup strategy for Amazon EC2 data and multiple Amazon S3 buckets. Because of regulatory requirements, the company must retain backup files for a specific time period.

The company must not alter the files for the duration of the retention period.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in governance mode. Create the required backup plan.
choices.explanation: Privileged users can remove a governance-mode vault lock; compliance mode provides the required immutable retention after its grace period.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create the required automated snapshot policy.
choices.explanation: DLM manages EBS snapshots but does not supply immutable backups across both EC2 and S3.

choices.solution: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway to create the backup. Configure the appropriate S3 Lifecycle management.
choices.explanation: File Gateway and S3 Lifecycle do not implement immutable retention for the combined EC2 and S3 backup strategy.

choices.solution: Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in compliance mode. Create the required backup plan.
choices.explanation:
AWS Backup provides a centralized solution for managing backups across various AWS services, including Amazon EC2. By creating a backup vault with a vault lock in compliance mode, the company ensures that the backup files are retained and cannot be altered for the duration of the retention period.

Compliance mode is designed to meet regulatory requirements for data retention.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has resources across multiple AWS Regions and accounts. A newly hired solutions architect discovers a previous employee did not provide details about the resources inventory.

The solutions architect needs to build and map the relationship details of the various workloads across all accounts.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.solution: Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory to generate a map view from the detailed view report.
choices.explanation: Systems Manager Inventory focuses on managed-node configuration, not complete multi-account workload relationship diagrams.

choices.solution: Use AWS Step Functions to collect workload details. Build architecture diagrams of the workloads manually.
choices.explanation: Custom collection and manually drawn diagrams require substantially more ongoing work.

choices.solution: Use Workload Discovery on AWS to generate architecture diagrams of the workloads.
choices.explanation:
AWS has a service called AWS Well-Architected Tool, which includes Workload Discovery. Workload Discovery automatically discovers and visualizes the architecture of your workloads.

It provides architecture diagrams, best practice recommendations, and insights into your workloads.

choices.solution: Use AWS X-Ray to view the workload details. Build architecture diagrams with relationships.
choices.explanation: X-Ray traces instrumented application requests; it does not automatically inventory every resource and relationship across accounts.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The company wants to back up the EC2 instances to a second Region.

The company also wants to provision EC2 resources in the second Region and manage the EC2 instances centrally from one AWS account.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Create a disaster recovery (DR) plan that has a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Configure data replication.
choices.explanation: Keeping a comparable fleet running in the second Region incurs unnecessary compute cost for backup-based recovery.

choices.solution: Create point-in-time Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the EC2 instances. Copy the snapshots to the second Region periodically.
choices.explanation: Separate snapshot copy schedules require custom orchestration and omit centralized full-instance backup management.

choices.solution: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup. Configure cross-Region backup to the second Region for the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation:
AWS Backup is a centralized backup service that allows you to create backup plans for various AWS resources, including EC2 instances. With AWS Backup, you can configure cross-Region backups, meaning you can replicate backups from one AWS Region to another.

This provides a cost-effective and centralized solution for backup.

choices.solution: Deploy a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data from the source Region to the second Region.
choices.explanation: A duplicate running fleet and DataSync add compute and synchronization operations rather than managed backup copies.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is developing a mobile gaming app in a single AWS Region. The app runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group.

The company stores the app data in Amazon DynamoDB. The app communicates by using TCP traffic and UDP traffic between the users and the servers.

The application will be used globally. The company wants to ensure the lowest possible latency for all users.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports.

Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB.
choices.explanation: An ALB cannot handle the required arbitrary UDP traffic.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports.

Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB.
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator supplies stable entry IPs and optimized routing to NLB endpoints. NLB supports both TCP and UDP and integrates with the application Auto Scaling group.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports.

Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB. Update CloudFront to use the NLB as the origin.
choices.explanation: CloudFront handles HTTP/HTTPS, not arbitrary TCP and UDP game traffic.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports.

Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB. Update CloudFront to use the ALB as the origin.
choices.explanation: Both CloudFront and an ALB lack support for the game's arbitrary UDP traffic.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has an application that processes customer orders. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that saves the orders to an Amazon Aurora database.

Occasionally when traffic is high the workload does not process orders fast enough.

What should a solutions architect do to write the orders reliably to the database as quickly as possible?

choices.solution:
Increase the instance size of the EC2 instance when traffic is high. Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic.
choices.explanation: An Aurora database endpoint cannot subscribe directly to an SNS topic to insert orders.

choices.solution: Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.
choices.explanation:
Amazon SQS, which is a fully managed message queuing service. Writing orders to an SQS queue allows for decoupling the EC2 instances processing the orders from the application writing the orders.
