EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group can then read from the SQS queue, ensuring that the processing scales with demand. Using an Auto Scaling group ensures that you can dynamically adjust the number of EC2 instances based on the workload.

This can help handle high traffic efficiently.

choices.solution:
Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic.

Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SNS topic.
choices.explanation: SNS cannot be polled as a work queue, and Aurora does not accept an SNS subscription as a database ingestion interface.

choices.solution: Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when the EC2 instance reaches CPU threshold limits. Use scheduled scaling of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.
choices.explanation: Waiting until overload to queue requests risks losing earlier work, while scheduled scaling does not respond to unpredictable demand.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company hosts an online shopping application that stores all orders in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instance. Management wants to eliminate single points of failure and has asked a solutions architect to recommend an approach to minimize database downtime without requiring any changes to the application code.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Convert the existing database instance to a Multi-AZ deployment by modifying the database instance and specifying the Multi-AZ option.
choices.explanation:
By converting the existing RDS instance to a Multi-AZ deployment, you enable high availability with automatic failover. Amazon RDS will automatically replicate the database to a standby instance in a different Availability Zone (AZ).

In the event of a failure, Amazon RDS will automatically promote the standby to the primary, minimizing downtime.

choices.solution: Create a new RDS Multi-AZ deployment. Take a snapshot of the current RDS instance and restore the new Multi-AZ deployment with the snapshot.
choices.explanation: Restoring into a new deployment requires coordinating cutover and can introduce more downtime than modifying the existing instance's deployment.

choices.solution: Create a read-only replica of the PostgreSQL database in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across the databases.
choices.explanation: A read replica is not writable, and weighted DNS does not perform safe database failover for order writes.

choices.solution: Place the RDS for PostgreSQL database in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum group size of two. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across instances.
choices.explanation: RDS instances cannot be placed into an EC2 Auto Scaling group, and independent instances would not share a consistent writer state.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company designed a stateless two-tier application that uses Amazon EC2 in a single Availability Zone and an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. New company management wants to ensure the application is highly available.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Configure the application to use Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling and create an Application Load Balancer
choices.explanation: A Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group provides redundant instances and automatic replacement, while an ALB routes requests only to healthy application targets.

choices.solution: Configure the application to take snapshots of the EC2 instances and send them to a different AWS Region
choices.explanation: Snapshots provide recovery artifacts, not a running application tier able to survive an AZ outage immediately.

choices.solution: Configure the application to use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to feed requests to the application
choices.explanation: DNS routing cannot compensate for all application instances residing in one failed AZ.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Route 53 rules to handle incoming requests and create a Multi-AZ Application Load Balancer
choices.explanation: A multi-AZ ALB does not make single-AZ application instances highly available; the compute fleet must span AZs too.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content.

Website traffic is increasing, and the company is concerned about a potential increase in cost.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache static files at edge locations.
choices.explanation: By creating a CloudFront distribution and configuring it to cache static files, you can offload the delivery of static content to the CDN, reducing the load on the ALB and potentially lowering data transfer costs. CloudFront helps improve website performance and can be cost-effective due to its caching mechanism.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Connect the ALB to the ElastiCache cluster to serve cached files
choices.explanation: An ALB cannot directly connect to ElastiCache to serve files; this requires application-managed caching logic.

choices.solution: Create an AWS WAF web ACL and associate it with the ALB. Add a rule to the web ACL to cache static files
choices.explanation: WAF filters requests and has no rule that caches static content.

choices.solution: Create a second ALB in an alternative AWS Region. Route user traffic to the closest Region to minimize data transfer costs
choices.explanation: Another ALB adds cost and does not cache static files or reduce repeated origin processing.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is designing a containerized application that will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application needs to access a shared file system that is highly durable and can recover data to another AWS Region with a recovery point objective (RPO) of 8 hours.

The file system needs to provide a mount target m each Availability Zone within a Region. A solutions architect wants to use AWS Backup to manage the replication to another Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ deployment
choices.explanation: FSx for Windows does not provide an EFS-style mount target in each AZ of the Region.

choices.solution: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with a Multi-AZ deployment
choices.explanation: FSx for ONTAP uses its filesystem endpoints and HA topology, not a mount target in each AZ as specified.

choices.solution: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with the Standard storage class
choices.explanation: Regional EFS Standard supplies shared file access across Availability Zones, unlike a single-AZ block volume or local instance store.

choices.solution: Amazon FSx for OpenZFS
choices.explanation: FSx for OpenZFS does not provide EFS's regional mount-target model across all required AZs.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A law firm needs to share information with the public. The information includes hundreds of files that must be publicly readable.

Modifications or deletions of the files by anyone before a designated future date are prohibited.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?

choices.solution: Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket until the designated date.
choices.explanation: Read-only user policies can be changed and do not enforce immutable time-bound retention against administrators.

choices.solution:
Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date.

Configure the S3 bucket for static website hosting. Set an S3 bucket policy to allow read-only access to the objects.
choices.explanation:
S3 Versioning helps maintain multiple versions of an object over time. With S3 Object Lock, you can enforce retention periods during which the objects cannot be modified or deleted.

This aligns with the requirement to prohibit modifications or deletions before a designated future date.

choices.solution:
Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an event trigger to run an AWS Lambda function in case of object modification or deletion.

Configure the Lambda function to replace the objects with the original versions from a private S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Restoring objects after deletion leaves an exposure window and does not prevent the prohibited operation.

choices.solution:
Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Select the folder that contains the files.

Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 has object-key prefixes rather than lockable folders; Object Lock requires bucket versioning and retention on object versions.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is making a prototype of the infrastructure for its new website by manually provisioning the necessary infrastructure. This infrastructure includes an Auto Scaling group, an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon RDS database.

After the configuration has been thoroughly validated, the company wants the capability to immediately deploy the infrastructure for development and production use in two Availability Zones in an automated fashion.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS Systems Manager to replicate and provision the prototype infrastructure in two Availability Zones
choices.explanation: Systems Manager does not automatically replicate arbitrary ALB, Auto Scaling, and RDS infrastructure from a prototype.

choices.solution: Define the infrastructure as a template by using the prototype infrastructure as a guide. Deploy the infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation.
choices.explanation: AWS CloudFormation is a service specifically designed for defining and deploying AWS infrastructure as code using templates. In this case, you can create a CloudFormation template based on the validated prototype infrastructure, and then use CloudFormation to deploy and manage the infrastructure in an automated and repeatable way.

choices.solution: Use AWS Config to record the inventory of resources that are used in the prototype infrastructure. Use AWS Config to deploy the prototype infrastructure into two Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Config records configurations and compliance; it does not deploy the recorded architecture.

choices.solution: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk and configure it to use an automated reference to the prototype infrastructure to automatically deploy new environments in two Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk does not automatically reference and clone this manually provisioned arbitrary infrastructure.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that is integrated with an on-premises warehouse solution. The company uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send order messages to an on-premises HTTPS endpoint so the warehouse application can process the orders.

The local data center team has detected that some of the order messages were not received. A solutions architect needs to retain messages that are not delivered and analyze the messages for up to 14 days.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream target with a retention period of 14 days.
choices.explanation: An SNS subscription dead-letter queue must be an SQS queue, not a Kinesis data stream.

choices.solution: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue with a retention period of 14 days between the application and Amazon SNS.
choices.explanation: A queue before SNS does not capture messages whose delivery from SNS to the HTTPS subscriber ultimately fails.

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) target with a retention period of 14 days.
choices.explanation:
Amazon SNS allows you to set up a dead letter queue to capture and retain messages that cannot be delivered to the intended endpoint. When configuring a DLQ, you can specify an Amazon SQS queue as the target for messages that fail to be delivered.

Amazon SQS provides message retention settings, and in this case, you can set the retention period to 14 days.

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon DynamoDB target with a TTL attribute set for a retention period of 14 days.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB cannot be configured as an SNS subscription dead-letter queue.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing an asynchronous application to process credit card data validation requests for a bank. The application must be secure and be able to process each request at least once.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution:
Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source.

Use AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.
choices.explanation: An SQS standard queue provides durable at-least-once delivery with low operational overhead. The Lambda execution role requires queue permissions and kms:Decrypt for the encrypted messages.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source.

Use SQS managed encryption keys (SSE-SQS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: SSE-SQS does not require a KMS invocation permission, and FIFO adds ordering overhead that is not required.

choices.solution:
Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source.

Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.
choices.explanation: FIFO is more expensive than Standard when only at-least-once processing is needed; Lambda processing still requires idempotency.

choices.solution:
Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source.

Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: The consumer needs kms:Decrypt on its execution role, not an undefined encryption-key invocation permission.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon S3 to store high-resolution pictures in an S3 bucket. To minimize application changes, the company stores the pictures as the latest version of an S3 object.

The company needs to retain only the two most recent versions of the pictures. The company wants to reduce costs.

The company has identified the S3 bucket as a large expense.

Which solution will reduce the S3 costs with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use S3 Lifecycle to delete expired object versions and retain the two most recent versions.
choices.explanation: Retain the current version and one newer noncurrent version with NoncurrentVersionExpiration, using NewerNoncurrentVersions=1 and a noncurrent-age threshold. Older versions are removed asynchronously only after both conditions are met; lifecycle rules do not impose an instantaneous two-version limit.

choices.solution: Use an AWS Lambda function to check for older versions and delete all but the two most recent versions.
choices.explanation: Custom Lambda enumeration and deletion require code, scheduling, and failure handling compared with native Lifecycle retention.

choices.solution: Use S3 Batch Operations to delete noncurrent object versions and retain only the two most recent versions.
choices.explanation: Batch Operations requires creating and maintaining manifests and jobs; Lifecycle automatically handles future versions.

choices.solution: Deactivate versioning on the S3 bucket and retain the two most recent versions.
choices.explanation: Suspending versioning does not prune older versions or automatically retain exactly the two most recent versions.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to ingest customer payment data into the company's data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives payment data every minute on average.

The company wants to analyze the payment data in real time. Then the company wants to ingest the data into the data lake.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
choices.explanation: Custom Lambda analysis requires implementing stream processing and S3 delivery rather than using managed analysis and delivery services.

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
choices.explanation: Glue is not the proposed real-time ingestion endpoint, and this option does not specify delivery of analyzed data into the S3 lake.

choices.solution: Ingest data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for real-time analysis and Amazon Data Firehose to deliver the stream or analysis output into the S3 data lake.
choices.explanation:
Kinesis Data Streams durably ingests the data, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink provides managed stream processing. Use Firehose where the design requires delivery to S3.

The former Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL service was discontinued in January 2026.

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
choices.explanation: API Gateway and custom Lambda processing require implementing ingestion handling and reliable S3 delivery.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has a web application for travel ticketing. The application is based on a database that runs in a single data center in North America.

The company wants to expand the application to serve a global user base. The company needs to deploy the application to multiple AWS Regions.

Average latency must be less than 1 second on updates to the reservation database. The company wants to have separate deployments of its web platform across multiple Regions.

However, the company must maintain a single primary reservation database that is globally consistent.

Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Convert the application to use Amazon DynamoDB. Use a global table for the center reservation table.

Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment.
choices.explanation:
DynamoDB global tables support multiple regional deployments, but the default eventually consistent mode does not meet globally consistent reservation semantics. This answer is only valid with a supported strong-consistency configuration and deliberate single-Region writes.

Aurora Global Database is the single-writer alternative; no configuration guarantees subsecond latency between arbitrary Regions.

choices.solution: Migrate the reservation database to an Aurora MySQL global database with one primary writer and read-only secondary clusters in the application Regions. Direct reservation writes to the primary writer and reads to the appropriate Regional endpoint.
choices.explanation:
Aurora global database retains one primary writer and replicates to Regional readers with typically sub-second lag. All reservation writes use the primary to preserve a single authoritative database.

Replication latency is not a guaranteed sub-second bound; reads requiring the latest committed reservation must also use the writer.

choices.solution:
Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Deploy MySQL read replicas in each Region.

Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.
choices.explanation: Cross-Region RDS MySQL read replicas are asynchronous and read-only; each Regional endpoint cannot accept reservation updates.

choices.solution:
Migrate the application to an Amazon Aurora Serverless database. Deploy instances of the database to each Region.

Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment to access the database. Use AWS Lambda functions to process event streams in each Region to synchronize the databases.
choices.explanation: Independent databases synchronized with Lambda require custom conflict and consistency logic and do not establish one globally consistent primary.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has migrated multiple Microsoft Windows Server workloads to Amazon EC2 instances that run in the us-west-1 Region. The company manually backs up the workloads to create an image as needed.

In the event of a natural disaster in the us-west-1 Region, the company wants to recover workloads quickly in the us-west-2 Region. The company wants no more than 24 hours of data loss on the EC2 instances.

The company also wants to automate any backups of the EC2 instances.

Which solutions will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily.

Copy the image on demand.
choices.explanation: Copying only on demand leaves no automatic second-Region copy if the source Region fails.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily.

Configure the copy to the us-west-2 Region.
choices.explanation: Data Lifecycle Manager can create tagged EBS-backed AMIs on a schedule and copy them to the recovery Region.

choices.solution:
Create backup vaults in us-west-1 and in us-west-2 by using AWS Backup. Create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values.

Create an AWS Lambda function to run as a scheduled job to copy the backup data to us-west-2.
choices.explanation: A custom Lambda copy scheduler adds code when AWS Backup supports copy actions natively.

choices.solution:
Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values.

Define the destination for the copy as us-west-2. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily.
choices.explanation: AWS Backup schedules tagged EC2 backups and cross-Region copies, preserving recovery points outside the primary Region.

choices.solution:
Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values.

Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily. Copy on demand to us-west-2.
choices.explanation: Manual on-demand copying does not guarantee the required up-to-date recovery copy in the second Region.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company operates a two-tier application for image processing. The application uses two Availability Zones, each with one public subnet and one private subnet.

An Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the web tier uses the public subnets. Amazon EC2 instances for the application tier use the private subnets.

Users report that the application is running more slowly than expected. A security audit of the web server log files shows that the application is receiving millions of illegitimate requests from a small number of IP addresses.

A solutions architect needs to resolve the immediate performance problem while the company investigates a more permanent solution.

What should the solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Modify the inbound security group for the web tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
choices.explanation: Security groups do not support explicit deny rules.

choices.solution: Modify the network ACL for the web tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
choices.explanation: A network ACL can explicitly deny the abusive source IP ranges. Put deny rules before matching allow rules and account for stateless return-traffic rules.

choices.solution: Modify the inbound security group for the application tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
choices.explanation: Security groups do not support deny rules, and filtering after traffic reaches the application tier misses the front-end resource consumption.

choices.solution: Modify the network ACL for the application tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
choices.explanation: Behind the ALB, network traffic reaches targets from ALB addresses; blocking original client addresses in target subnet ACLs does not reliably block the public requests.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A social media company wants to allow its users to upload images in an application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs a solution that automatically resizes the images so that the images can be displayed on multiple device types.

The application experiences unpredictable traffic patterns throughout the day. The company is seeking a highly available solution that maximizes scalability.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a static website hosted in Amazon S3 that invokes AWS Lambda functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation:
Hosting a static website in Amazon S3 is a cost-effective and highly available solution. Amazon S3 provides scalable and durable object storage.

A static website in S3 can serve as the front end for user interactions. In this option, Lambda functions can be triggered by events (e.g., new image uploads to an S3 bucket) to perform image resizing.

Lambda can efficiently handle sporadic and unpredictable workloads.

choices.solution: Create a static website hosted in Amazon CloudFront that invokes AWS Step Functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon RDS database.
choices.explanation: CloudFront needs a content origin, Step Functions needs an actual image-processing task, and RDS adds unnecessary image-storage overhead.

choices.solution: Create a dynamic website hosted on a web server that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a process that runs on the EC2 instance to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: One EC2 web and resizing server is a failure point and lacks elastic processing capacity.

choices.solution: Create a dynamic website hosted on an automatically scaling Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that creates a resize job in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Set up an image-resizing program that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance to process the resize jobs.
choices.explanation: An independently scaling front end does not remove the single EC2 image processor's capacity and availability bottleneck.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes.

Which solution will meet this requirement with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.solution: Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.
choices.explanation: While AWS Systems Manager supports logging command output to an S3 bucket, this is primarily for storing the output of commands executed through Systems Manager, not specifically for Session Manager logs. It may not capture all the detailed session logs, including interactive session input/output and other session-specific details.

choices.solution:
Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group.

Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.
choices.explanation: Installing an agent and exporting log groups adds steps compared with Session Manager's native S3 session logging.

choices.solution: Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.
choices.explanation: A daily document to collect all server logs adds custom handling and is less direct than native session logging.

choices.solution:
Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group.

Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.
choices.explanation: A log subscription and Firehose pipeline add services and configuration when Session Manager can write directly to S3.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has a regional subscription-based streaming service that runs in a single AWS Region. The architecture consists of web servers and application servers on Amazon EC2 instances.

The EC2 instances are in Auto Scaling groups behind Elastic Load Balancers. The architecture includes an Amazon Aurora global database cluster that extends across multiple Availability Zones.

The company wants to expand globally and to ensure that its application has minimal downtime.

Which solution will provide the MOST fault tolerance?

choices.solution:
Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region.

Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.
choices.explanation: An Auto Scaling group cannot extend into another Region; separate regional groups are required.

choices.solution:
Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region.

Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.
choices.explanation: Cross-Region replica replication has more overhead and slower recovery characteristics than Aurora global database's storage-level replication.

choices.solution:
Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.
choices.explanation: DMS adds a replication service and operational complexity compared with Aurora's integrated global database replication.

choices.solution:
Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region.

Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.
choices.explanation:
An Aurora global database allows you to replicate your database across multiple AWS Regions. This ensures that you have a read-capable secondary database in the second Region, providing low-latency access to the database.

Amazon Route 53 can be configured with health checks to monitor the health of the web and application tiers in both Regions. In the event of a failure in the primary Region, Route 53 can automatically route traffic to the healthy resources in the second Region.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption.

A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must make the Lambda function available for the third party to call.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.solution: Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.
choices.explanation:
AWS Lambda supports API Gateway integration, which allows you to create an HTTP endpoint (URL) for your Lambda function. Operational Efficiency: Directly exposing the Lambda function through a URL eliminates the need for additional services, such as load balancers or message queues, for simple webhook integration.

Simplicity: This approach is straightforward and easy to implement. It provides a direct URL that the third party can use to invoke the Lambda function when the webhook is triggered.

choices.solution: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.
choices.explanation: An ALB adds load-balancer resources and configuration when a function URL directly supplies the webhook endpoint.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function.

Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.
choices.explanation: An SNS topic endpoint requires AWS Publish API authentication; it is not a generic HTTPS webhook receiver.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function.

Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.
choices.explanation: An SQS endpoint requires signed queue API requests rather than accepting an ordinary webhook callback.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company stores data in Amazon S3. According to regulations, the data must not contain personally identifiable information (PII).

The company recently discovered that S3 buckets have some objects that contain PII. The company needs to automatically detect PII in S3 buckets and to notify the company's security team.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.
choices.explanation:
Amazon Macie is a service designed for data discovery and classification. It can identify sensitive data, including personally identifiable information (PII).

By creating an EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData event type, you can specifically target PII-related findings and notify the security team using Amazon SNS.

choices.solution: Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.
choices.explanation: GuardDuty detects threats rather than inspecting object contents for PII; the proposed CRITICAL filter is not the Macie sensitive-data finding.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData:S3Object/Personal event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.
choices.explanation: A finding delivered to SQS still needs a consumer to notify human recipients; SNS directly supplies security-team notifications.

choices.solution: Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.
choices.explanation: GuardDuty does not perform the required PII discovery, and SQS does not directly notify human recipients.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to provide data scientists with near real-time read-only access to the company's production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The database is currently configured as a Single-AZ database.

The data scientists use complex queries that will not affect the production database. The company needs a solution that is highly available.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Scale the existing production database in a maintenance window to provide enough power for the data scientists.
choices.explanation: A larger writer still executes the complex analysis alongside production work and does not add database high availability.

choices.solution: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment with a larger secondary standby instance. Provide the data scientists access to the secondary instance.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby cannot serve reads and cannot be separately sized as proposed.

choices.solution: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment. Provide two additional read replicas for the data scientists.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ instance pair plus two separate read replicas provisions four database instances. The selected Multi-AZ DB cluster integrates one writer and two readable standbys, supplying availability and analytical read capacity without the extra instance.

choices.solution: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ cluster deployment with two readable standby instances. Provide read endpoints to the data scientists.
choices.explanation: An RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB cluster includes one writer and two readable standbys across three Availability Zones. Its reader endpoint isolates analytical reads, and integrated failover supplies high availability without adding separate replicas.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud that operates across three Availability Zones. The application architecture has an Application Load Balancer, an Amazon EC2 web server that hosts user session states, and a MySQL database that runs on an EC2 instance.

The company expects sudden increases in application traffic. The company wants to be able to scale to meet future application capacity demands and to ensure high availability across all three Availability Zones.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads.

Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Migrating the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment provides high availability by replicating the database across multiple Availability Zones. Using Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability ensures that session data and reads are cached effectively, improving performance

choices.solution:
Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with high availability to store session data and to cache reads.

Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Memcached lacks Redis replication and automatic failover needed for reliable shared session state.

choices.solution:
Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon DynamoDB Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache reads. Store the session data in DynamoDB.

Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Migrating MySQL to DynamoDB requires a different data model and query implementation rather than preserving relational compatibility.

choices.solution:
Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads.

Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: The single-AZ database remains a failure point despite multi-AZ compute and caching.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to improve its on-premises disaster recovery (DR) configuration. The company's core production business application uses Microsoft SQL Server Standard, which runs on a virtual machine (VM).

The application has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 30 seconds or fewer and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 60 minutes. The DR solution needs to minimize costs wherever possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure a multi-site active/active setup between the on-premises server and AWS by using Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise with Always On availability groups.
choices.explanation: SQL Server Enterprise licensing and a continuously active second site add unnecessary cost compared with replication to a small DR staging area.

choices.solution: Configure a warm standby Amazon RDS for SQL Server database on AWS. Configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to use change data capture (CDC).
choices.explanation: A warm RDS target incurs continuous database compute cost and database-only CDC does not recover the complete source VM.

choices.solution: Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery configured to replicate disk changes to AWS as a pilot light.
choices.explanation:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates block-level changes to a low-cost staging area in AWS and can launch recovery instances during a disaster. This is designed for low RPO/RTO DR while avoiding the cost of a continuously running warm standby.

Nightly backups cannot meet an RPO of 30 seconds.

choices.solution: Use third-party backup software to capture backups every night. Store a secondary set of backups in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Nightly backups allow up to a day of data loss, far exceeding the 30-second RPO.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has an on-premises server that uses an Oracle database to process and store customer information. The company wants to use an AWS database service to achieve higher availability and to improve application performance.

The company also wants to offload reporting from its primary database system.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.solution: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create an Amazon RDS DB instance in multiple AWS Regions. Point the reporting functions toward a separate DB instance from the primary DB instance.
choices.explanation: Custom DMS replication to separately created databases adds management compared with native RDS replication and failover.

choices.solution:
Use Amazon RDS in a Single-AZ deployment to create an Oracle database. Create a read replica in the same zone as the primary DB instance.

Direct the reporting functions to the read replica.
choices.explanation: The primary and replica share one AZ and do not provide the requested higher availability across failures.

choices.solution: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle with a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Create an Oracle read replica and direct reporting queries to that replica.
choices.explanation: RDS for Oracle Multi-AZ provides failover, and a separate Oracle read replica offloads reporting. Oracle does not use the RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster reader architecture; Oracle read replicas require the supported Enterprise Edition and Active Data Guard licensing.

choices.solution: Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ instance deployment to create an Amazon Aurora database. Direct the reporting functions to the reader instances.
choices.explanation: Aurora is not Oracle-compatible, so replacing the engine requires application and schema changes.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to build a web application on AWS. Client access requests to the website are not predictable and can be idle for a long time.

Only customers who have paid a subscription fee can have the ability to sign in and use the web application.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve user information from Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs.

Send the API calls to the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: API Gateway and Lambda implement the API, while DynamoDB stores user data without database server management.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer to retrieve user information from Amazon RDS. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs.

Send the API calls to the Lambda function.
choices.explanation: An always-running ECS/ALB and RDS stack adds idle-period costs, and the proposed integration inconsistently refers to a Lambda function.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate users.
choices.explanation: A Cognito user pool provides user registration and authentication.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to authenticate users.
choices.explanation: A Cognito identity pool supplies AWS credentials for already authenticated identities; a user pool provides the sign-in directory.

choices.solution: Use AWS Amplify to serve the frontend web content with HTML, CSS, and JS. Use an integrated Amazon CloudFront configuration.
choices.explanation: Amplify Hosting publishes the static frontend through CloudFront for scalable global delivery.

choices.solution: Use Amazon S3 static web hosting with PHP, CSS, and JS. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the frontend web content.
choices.explanation: S3 static hosting cannot execute PHP server-side code.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A retail company uses a regional Amazon API Gateway API for its public REST APIs. The API Gateway endpoint is a custom domain name that points to an Amazon Route 53 alias record.

A solutions architect needs to create a solution that has minimal effects on customers and minimal data loss to release the new version of APIs.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create a canary release deployment stage for API Gateway. Deploy the latest API version.

Point an appropriate percentage of traffic to the canary stage. After API verification, promote the canary stage to the production stage.
choices.explanation: A canary release deployment is a strategy in software development and release management where a new version of a software application or service is gradually rolled out to a small subset of users before making it available to the entire user base.

choices.solution:
Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI YAML file format. Use the import-to-update operation in merge mode into the API in API Gateway.

Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.
choices.explanation: Immediately merging and deploying definitions to production sends every user to the new behavior without a controlled canary trial.

choices.solution:
Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI JSON file format. Use the import-to-update operation in overwrite mode into the API in API Gateway.

Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.
choices.explanation: Overwriting and deploying the production API gives no gradual traffic exposure or easy canary rollback.

choices.solution:
Create a new API Gateway endpoint with new versions of the API definitions. Create a custom domain name for the new API Gateway API.

Point the Route 53 alias record to the new API Gateway API custom domain name.
choices.explanation: A DNS endpoint switch can be affected by cached records and does not provide API Gateway's controlled percentage-based rollout.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to direct its users to a backup static error page if the company's primary website is unavailable. The primary website's DNS records are hosted in Amazon Route 53.

The domain is pointing to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company needs a solution that minimizes changes and infrastructure overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Update the Route 53 records to use a latency routing policy. Add a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket to the records so that the traffic is sent to the most responsive endpoints.
choices.explanation: Latency routing prefers responsive locations rather than making an error page a strictly passive fallback.

choices.solution: Set up a Route 53 active-passive failover configuration. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket when Route 53 health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy.
choices.explanation:
An active-passive failover configuration in Route 53 involves designating one endpoint (primary, in this case, the ALB) as active and another endpoint (S3 bucket hosting a static error page) as passive. Route 53 health checks can be configured to monitor the health of the ALB endpoint.

If the health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy (i.e., the primary website is unavailable), Route 53 automatically directs traffic to the passive endpoint (S3 bucket with the static error page).

choices.solution: Set up a Route 53 active-active configuration with the ALB and an Amazon EC2 instance that hosts a static error page as endpoints. Configure Route 53 to send requests to the instance only if the health checks fail for the ALB.
choices.explanation: Active-active routing sends normal traffic to both endpoints and adds an unnecessary EC2 server for the error page.

choices.solution:
Update the Route 53 records to use a multivalue answer routing policy. Create a health check.

Direct traffic to the website if the health check passes. Direct traffic to a static error page that is hosted in Amazon S3 if the health check does not pass.
choices.explanation: Multivalue routing returns healthy records without modeling the required primary/secondary preference, and it cannot use S3 website aliases in the proposed way.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has data collection sensors at different locations. The data collection sensors stream a high volume of data to the company.

The company wants to design a platform on AWS to ingest and process high-volume streaming data. The solution must be scalable and support data collection in near real time.

The company must store the data in Amazon S3 for future reporting.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: It is a fully managed service for ingesting, transforming, and delivering streaming data to various destinations, including Amazon S3. Kinesis Data Firehose can scale automatically based on the volume of incoming data, and it simplifies the process of delivering data to S3 without the need for manual intervention.

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Glue streaming jobs need a streaming source and job configuration; Firehose directly supplies managed ingestion and S3 delivery.

choices.solution: Use AWS Lambda to deliver streaming data and store the data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Custom Lambda delivery requires implementing buffering, retries, and failure handling supplied by Firehose.

choices.solution: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: DMS streams database changes, not arbitrary sensor ingestion as a general-purpose streaming receiver.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A solutions architect manages an analytics application. The application stores large amounts of semistructured data in an Amazon S3 bucket.

The solutions architect wants to use parallel data processing to process the data more quickly. The solutions architect also wants to use information that is stored in an Amazon Redshift database to enrich the data.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Athena to process the S3 data. Use AWS Glue with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
choices.explanation: Athena and a separate Glue enrichment stage can work, but split processing across services instead of one parallel EMR job reading and joining both datasets.

choices.solution: Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon EMR with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
choices.explanation: EMR runs distributed processing for the S3 dataset and can join it with Redshift-derived data through supported connectors and permissions.

choices.solution: Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to move the S3 data into Amazon Redshift so that the data can be enriched.
choices.explanation: Moving the S3 dataset into Redshift through Kinesis adds ingestion infrastructure instead of enriching it in the existing parallel processing job.

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue to process the S3 data. Use AWS Lake Formation with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
choices.explanation: Lake Formation governs data access; it does not execute the proposed Redshift enrichment transformation.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing a workload that will store hourly energy consumption by business tenants in a building. The sensors will feed a database through HTTP requests that will add up usage for each tenant.

The solutions architect must use managed services when possible. The workload will receive more features in the future as the solutions architect adds independent components.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale. It acts as an entry point for HTTP requests and can handle the communication with the sensors.

In this scenario, you can use Lambda functions to process the data received from the sensors. Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database that can handle the storage of the hourly energy consumption data.

choices.solution: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the processed data.
choices.explanation: An EC2 fleet requires server management, and S3 does not directly supply tenant usage aggregation as a database.

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in a Microsoft SQL Server Express database on an Amazon EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: Self-managed SQL Server on EC2 retains patching, backup, and capacity-management responsibilities.

choices.solution: Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) shared file system to store the processed data.
choices.explanation: EC2 and EFS add running infrastructure and custom file-based aggregation instead of managed API and database services.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An Amazon EventBridge rule targets a third-party API. The third-party API has not received any incoming traffic.

A solutions architect needs to determine whether the rule conditions are being met and if the rule's target is being invoked.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Check for metrics in Amazon CloudWatch in the namespace for AWS/Events.
choices.explanation: EventBridge publishes matched-event, invocation, and failed-invocation metrics in the AWS/Events CloudWatch namespace, distinguishing rule matching from target delivery failures.

choices.solution: Review events in the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue.
choices.explanation: A dead-letter queue shows exhausted delivery failures only if configured; it does not reveal unmatched events or every invocation.

choices.solution: Check for the events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: EventBridge does not automatically place all rule matches and invocations into CloudWatch Logs without a configured logging target.

choices.solution: Check the trails in AWS CloudTrail for the EventBridge events.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail audits EventBridge API operations rather than supplying the rule's matching and target-invocation metrics.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has a large workload that runs every Friday evening. The workload runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in two Availability Zones in the us-east-1 Region.

Normally, the company must run no more than two instances at all times. However, the company wants to scale up to six instances each Friday to handle a regularly repeating increased workload.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create a reminder in Amazon EventBridge to scale the instances.
choices.explanation: A reminder still requires manual scaling or custom action wiring.

choices.solution: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.
choices.explanation: By creating an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled action, you can configure the group to automatically adjust the desired capacity based on a specified schedule. In this case, you can set up a scheduled action to increase the desired capacity to six instances every Friday evening.

choices.solution: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses manual scaling.
choices.explanation: Manual scaling requires operator intervention every Friday.

choices.solution: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses automatic scaling.
choices.explanation: Reactive automatic scaling waits for load rather than provisioning for the known recurring workload; scheduled scaling is more direct.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company deploys its applications on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) behind an Application Load Balancer in an AWS Region. The application needs to store data in a PostgreSQL database engine.

The company wants the data in the database to be highly available. The company also needs increased capacity for read workloads.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.solution: Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB does not provide a PostgreSQL engine.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby cannot serve reads, so it does not add readable capacity.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.
choices.explanation: Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ (Availability Zone) DB cluster deployment provides high availability by automatically replicating the primary database to a standby instance in a different Availability Zone. This helps ensure database availability in the event of a failure in the primary Availability Zone.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas.
choices.explanation: Cross-Region read replicas are asynchronous and require promotion for writer failover; a Multi-AZ cluster directly provides managed HA and readable standbys.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a stateful production application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application requires at least two EC2 instances to always be running.

A solutions architect needs to design a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture for the application. The solutions architect creates an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances.

Which set of additional steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy one On-Demand Instance in one Availability Zone and one On-Demand Instance in a second Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: Losing either AZ leaves only one instance, below the required two-instance minimum.

choices.solution: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two On-Demand Instances in a second Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: Four On-Demand instances, with two in each of two Availability Zones, preserve the required two running instances if one entire zone fails. Two instances total would leave only one after a zone failure.

choices.solution: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy four Spot Instances in one Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: All instances share one AZ failure risk and Spot interruptions can also remove them.

choices.solution: Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two Spot Instances in a second Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: If the On-Demand AZ fails, only interruptible Spot capacity remains, which cannot guarantee two running production instances.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company hosts its website on premises and in the AWS Cloud.

The company's on-premises data center is near the us-west-1 Region. The company uses the eu-central-1 Region to host the website.

The company wants to minimize load time for the website as much as possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Set up a geolocation routing policy. Send the traffic that is near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center.

Send the traffic that is near eu- central-1 to eu-central-1.
choices.explanation:
Geolocation routing directs traffic based on the geographic location of the user. This option would send users near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center and users near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1.

While this approach considers geographic location, it might not always result in the lowest latency.

choices.solution: Set up a simple routing policy that routes all traffic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1 and routes all traffic that is near the on-premises datacenter to the on-premises data center.
choices.explanation: Simple routing cannot choose records based on the user's geographic proximity.

choices.solution: Set up a latency routing policy. Associate the policy with us-west-1.
choices.explanation: A latency policy associated only with us-west-1 omits the European endpoint; a complete two-endpoint latency configuration would be another valid design.

choices.solution: Set up a weighted routing policy. Split the traffic evenly between eu-central-1 and the on-premises data center.
choices.explanation: An even weighted split sends some users to the distant site regardless of latency.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is designing a solution to capture customer activity in different web applications to process analytics and make predictions. Customer activity in the web applications is unpredictable and can increase suddenly.

The company requires a solution that integrates with other web applications. The solution must include an authorization step for security purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Authorization is resolved at the GWLB.
choices.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer is for network appliances and does not provide the proposed application authorization and HTTP ingestion interface.

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis data stream that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.
choices.explanation: Data Streams does not directly write records into S3; it requires a delivery consumer that this option omits.

choices.solution: Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to resolve authorization.
choices.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway: It provides a fully managed service for creating, publishing, maintaining, monitoring, and securing APIs at any scale. It allows you to expose the capabilities of your backend services as APIs.

Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: It can capture and load streaming data into storage services such as Amazon S3. It is well-suited for scenarios where you need to ingest and store large volumes of streaming data.

API Gateway Lambda Authorizer: It allows you to control access to your APIs using Lambda functions. It's used to resolve authorization before allowing access to the API.

choices.solution: Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.
choices.explanation: A GWLB is not a user-authorized HTTP API endpoint, and the proposed Lambda authorization integration is not a GWLB capability.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An ecommerce company wants a disaster recovery solution for its Amazon RDS DB instances that run Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise Edition. The company's current recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) are 24 hours.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Create a cross-Region read replica and promote the read replica to the primary instance.
choices.explanation: A continuously running cross-Region replica incurs compute and storage costs beyond what the 24-hour recovery objectives require.

choices.solution: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create RDS cross-Region replication.
choices.explanation: DMS adds a continuously running replication service and target database for a backup-based recovery requirement.

choices.solution: Use cross-Region replication every 24 hours to copy native backups to an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Automating native SQL backup export and S3 copies adds more operations than managed cross-Region snapshot copies.

choices.solution: Copy automatic snapshots to another Region every 24 hours.
choices.explanation: RDS automatically takes snapshots of your database instances. These snapshots capture the entire DB instance, including the data and the DB instance's metadata.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer that has sticky sessions enabled. The web server currently hosts the user session state.

The company wants to ensure high availability and avoid user session state loss in the event of a web server outage.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance to store the session data. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Memcached to store the session state.
choices.explanation: Memcached does not replicate cached session records or provide automatic failover preserving them after a node failure.

choices.solution: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.
choices.explanation:
ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory data store service that is well-suited for storing session data. It provides high availability and durability.

Using Redis allows the application to offload the session state from individual EC2 instances to a centralized and highly available Redis cluster.

choices.solution: Use an AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store session data. Update the application to use AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store the session state.
choices.explanation: A cached block-storage gateway is intended for hybrid volumes, not a low-latency distributed web session service.

choices.solution: Use Amazon RDS to store the session state. Update the application to use Amazon RDS to store the session state.
choices.explanation: A highly available RDS database can store shared sessions, but adds relational query and connection overhead compared with the intended Redis session store; it is not inherently incapable of meeting availability.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a container application by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application includes microservices that manage customers and place orders.

The company needs to route incoming requests to the appropriate microservices.

Which solution will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision a Network Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: An NLB cannot inspect HTTP paths to route customer and order requests to different services.

choices.solution: Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision an Application Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: This is a Kubernetes-native controller that allows you to define and manage Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers to route traffic to services in your Amazon EKS cluster. ALBs are designed for routing HTTP/HTTPS traffic and provide more advanced routing features compared to Network Load Balancers.

choices.solution: Use an AWS Lambda function to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.
choices.explanation: Custom Lambda routing adds invocation cost and development work compared with ALB path rules.

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.
choices.explanation: API Gateway adds API configuration and integration overhead when an ALB ingress directly supplies the required routing.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing a highly available Amazon ElastiCache for Redis based solution. The solutions architect needs to ensure that failures do not result in performance degradation or loss of data locally and within an AWS Region.

The solution needs to provide high availability at the node level and at the Region level.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards that contain multiple nodes.
choices.explanation:
Multi-AZ (Availability Zone) replication groups provide high availability at the node level. In a Multi-AZ setup, your data is replicated asynchronously to a standby replica in a different Availability Zone.

Using shards with multiple nodes within each Availability Zone further enhances availability and provides scalability.

choices.solution: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Redis append only files (AOF) turned on.
choices.explanation: ElastiCache Redis does not expose the proposed Redis AOF persistence configuration, and multiple same-AZ nodes alone do not provide Multi-AZ resilience.

choices.solution: Use a Multi-AZ Redis cluster with more than one read replica in the replication group.
choices.explanation: A Multi-AZ replication group with multiple readers can provide HA too; this wording does not explicitly include sharding for the selected solution's distributed capacity, so the original single-answer distinction is incomplete.

choices.solution: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Auto Scaling turned on.
choices.explanation: Autoscaling adjusts capacity but does not by itself distribute replicas across AZs or enable automatic failover.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company plans to migrate to AWS and use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances for its application. During the migration testing phase, a technical team observes that the application takes a long time to launch and load memory to become fully productive.

Which solution will reduce the launch time of the application during the next testing phase?

choices.solution: Launch two or more EC2 On-Demand Instances. Turn on auto scaling features and make the EC2 On-Demand Instances available during the next testing phase.
choices.explanation: Keeping full running instances ready incurs ongoing compute charges instead of retaining initialized state in a hibernated warm pool.

choices.solution: Launch EC2 Spot Instances to support the application and to scale the application so it is available during the next testing phase.
choices.explanation: Spot pricing does not shorten initialization and interruptions can remove prepared capacity.

choices.solution: Launch the EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools during the next testing phase.
choices.explanation: When you launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on, the instances can be hibernated and resumed rather than terminated and launched.

choices.solution: Launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Start additional EC2 instances during the next testing phase.
choices.explanation: Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity availability but do not pre-initialize the application or restore its loaded memory.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. The company notices that its applications experience sudden traffic increases on random days of the week.

The company wants to maintain application performance during sudden traffic increases.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use manual scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: Manual scaling reacts only after an operator intervenes and adds operational work.

choices.solution: Use predictive scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: Predictive scaling relies on learned recurring patterns; random sudden increases need reactive demand-based scaling.

choices.solution: Use dynamic scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation:
Dynamic Scaling: With dynamic scaling, the Auto Scaling group automatically adjusts its capacity based on real-time demand. It scales out during traffic spikes and scales in during periods of lower demand.

This ensures that your application can handle sudden increases in traffic without manual intervention.

choices.solution: Use schedule scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: Scheduled scaling cannot anticipate traffic spikes on random days.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is planning to migrate a TCP-based application into the company's VPC. The application is publicly accessible on a nonstandard TCP port through a hardware appliance in the company's data center.

This public endpoint can process up to 3 million requests per second with low latency. The company requires the same level of performance for the new public endpoint in AWS.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
choices.explanation:
Network Load Balancer (NLB): It operates at the connection level (Layer 4) and is well-suited for TCP traffic. It can handle millions of requests per second with minimal latency.

NLB allows you to configure the listener for the specific TCP port that the application requires, ensuring compatibility with the nonstandard TCP port used by the application.

choices.solution: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the ALB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
choices.explanation: An ALB handles HTTP-family requests, not arbitrary TCP protocol traffic on the application port.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that listens on the TCP port that the application requires. Use an Application Load Balancer as the origin.
choices.explanation: CloudFront supports HTTP/HTTPS on its supported ports, not this arbitrary high-throughput TCP endpoint.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon API Gateway API that is configured with the TCP port that the application requires. Configure AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency to process the requests.
choices.explanation: API Gateway does not expose arbitrary TCP listeners and cannot act as the proposed TCP load balancer.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs its critical database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime and data loss.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create a DB snapshot of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance to populate a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
choices.explanation: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy and does not continuously catch up with new writes before cutover.

choices.solution: Create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Promote the Aurora read replicate to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
choices.explanation: A compatible Aurora PostgreSQL read replica follows the RDS PostgreSQL source until cutover. Stop source writes, wait for replication to catch up, and promote the replica into an independent cluster; this minimizes data loss and downtime.

choices.solution: Use data import from Amazon S3 to migrate the database to an Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
choices.explanation: S3 import requires an export/import workflow and does not provide automatic live replication of subsequent changes.

choices.solution: Use the pg_dump utility to back up the RDS for PostgreSQL database. Restore the backup to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
choices.explanation: Dump and restore take additional time and leave changes after the dump unsynchronized unless extra replication is added.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
