A company's infrastructure consists of hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. A solutions architect must ensure that every EC2 instance can be recovered after a disaster.

What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of effort?

choices.solution: Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to launch new EC2 instances from the EBS storage.
choices.explanation: Separate snapshots and custom instance-recreation templates require more orchestration than EC2-level managed backups.

choices.solution: Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to set the environment based on the EC2 template and attach the EBS storage.
choices.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is not a general restoration service for every existing EC2 instance configuration.

choices.solution: Use AWS Backup to set up a backup plan for the entire group of EC2 instances. Use the AWS Backup API or the AWS CLI to speed up the restore process for multiple EC2 instances.
choices.explanation:
AWS Backup: AWS Backup is a fully managed backup service that centralizes and automates the backup of data across AWS services. Backup Plan: You can set up a backup plan in AWS Backup to create and manage backups of the entire group of EC2 instances.

AWS Backup provides a streamlined process for restoring data. You can use the AWS Backup console, API, or AWS CLI to initiate the restore process for multiple EC2 instances.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function to take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance and copy the Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). Create another Lambda function to perform the restores with the copied AMIs and attach the EBS storage.
choices.explanation: Custom backup and restore functions add scheduling, error-handling, and maintenance work.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company recently migrated to the AWS Cloud. The company wants a serverless solution for large-scale parallel on-demand processing of a semistructured dataset.

The data consists of logs, media files, sales transactions, and IoT sensor data that is stored in Amazon S3. The company wants the solution to process thousands of items in the dataset in parallel.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.solution: Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Inline mode to process the data in parallel.
choices.explanation: Inline Map supports at most 40 concurrent iterations, below the requested thousands of parallel items.

choices.solution: Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode to process the data in parallel.
choices.explanation:
The Map state in AWS Step Functions is designed for parallel processing. In Distributed mode, it efficiently processes items in parallel, providing a scalable solution.

This allows you to process thousands of items concurrently, achieving high throughput.

choices.solution: Use AWS Glue to process the data in parallel.
choices.explanation: Glue suits ETL processing but does not directly provide per-item distributed workflow orchestration for all these heterogeneous tasks.

choices.solution: Use several AWS Lambda functions to process the data in parallel.
choices.explanation: Manually coordinating many functions requires custom fan-out, tracking, and retry handling.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company has an application with a REST-based interface that allows data to be received in near-real time from a third-party vendor. Once received, the application processes and stores the data for further analysis.

The application is running on Amazon EC2 instances. The third-party vendor has received many 503 Service Unavailable Errors when sending data to the application.

When the data volume spikes, the compute capacity reaches its maximum limit and the application is unable to process all requests.

Which design should a solutions architect recommend to provide a more scalable solution?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Process the data using AWS Lambda functions.
choices.explanation:
Kinesis Data Streams is designed for ingesting and processing real-time streaming data at scale. It can handle large volumes of data and provides the ability to scale horizontally.

Using Lambda functions allows for serverless, event-driven processing of the data. Lambda automatically scales based on the number of incoming events, providing the needed elasticity to handle spikes in data volume without the need to manage underlying infrastructure.

choices.solution: Use Amazon API Gateway on top of the existing application. Create a usage plan with a quota limit for the third-party vendor.
choices.explanation: A usage quota rejects excess data submissions rather than retaining them for processing when capacity becomes available.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the data. Put the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: SNS pushes requests and does not provide the durable replayable streaming backlog needed to absorb ingestion bursts.

choices.solution: Repackage the application as a container. Deploy the application using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the EC2 launch type with an Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: Containerization and EC2 scaling still require startup time and do not independently buffer requests arriving faster than workers can process them.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is designing a new multi-tier web application that consists of the following components:
* Web and application servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances as part of Auto Scaling groups
* An Amazon RDS DB instance for data storage A solutions architect needs to limit access to the application servers so that only the web servers can access them.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy AWS PrivateLink in front of the application servers. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
choices.explanation: PrivateLink adds service-endpoint infrastructure unnecessary for simple tier isolation within the VPC.

choices.solution: Deploy a VPC endpoint in front of the application servers. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
choices.explanation: An endpoint alone does not provide application-layer load balancing or the intended tier-specific ALB routing.

choices.solution: Deploy a Network Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
choices.explanation: Subnet ACLs identify IP ranges rather than dynamic web-tier security-group membership, adding maintenance as Auto Scaling changes instances.

choices.solution: Deploy an Application Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
choices.explanation:
An ALB is a load balancer service provided by AWS that allows you to distribute incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances. In this scenario, the ALB is deployed in front of the application servers.

The ALB is configured with a target group that includes the application servers' Auto Scaling group instances. The target group defines where the ALB directs traffic.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for its Amazon EC2 instances that have an SMB file share mounted as a volume in the us-east-1 Region. The company has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes for planned system maintenance or unplanned service disruptions.

The company needs to replicate the file system to the us-west-2 Region. The replicated data must not be deleted by any user for 5 years.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2.

Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
choices.explanation: Single-AZ storage lacks Multi-AZ synchronous failover, and daily backup copies cannot meet a five-minute cross-Region RPO.

choices.solution:
Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2.

Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
choices.explanation: Governance Vault Lock can be removed by authorized administrators, and daily backups cannot supply a five-minute cross-Region recovery point.

choices.solution:
Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2.

Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
choices.explanation:
Multi-AZ FSx synchronously replicates within its Region and can preserve recent writes during local maintenance or an AZ failure. Compliance Vault Lock protects the copied backups for five years.

However, daily cross-Region backups allow approximately 24 hours of data loss; this option does not meet a five-minute cross-Region RPO. No listed choice meets that interpretation of the requirement.

choices.solution:
Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2.

Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
choices.explanation: Single-AZ storage lacks Multi-AZ resilience, governance retention can be bypassed, and daily copies cannot satisfy a five-minute cross-Region RPO.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
An online photo-sharing company stores its photos in an Amazon S3 bucket that exists in the us-west-1 Region. The company needs to store a copy of all new photos in the us-east-1 Region.

Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

choices.solution: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.
choices.explanation:
S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) is designed specifically for replicating objects across different AWS regions. It is a fully managed feature that automatically replicates objects from the source bucket to the destination bucket in a different region.

This requires minimal operational effort as it is a built-in S3 feature for cross-region replication, and you don't have to manually trigger actions or configure additional services.

choices.solution: Create a cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration of the existing S3 bucket. Specify us-east-1 in the CORS rule's AllowedOrigin element.
choices.explanation: CORS controls which browser origins may read responses; it does not replicate objects to another Region.

choices.solution: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1 across multiple Availability Zones. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to save photos into the second S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: S3 Lifecycle transitions or expires objects within a bucket; it does not copy them into a second bucket.

choices.solution: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 event notifications on object creation and update events to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Custom copy Lambda code adds retry, permissions, and monitoring work compared with managed Cross-Region Replication.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is creating a new web application for its subscribers. The application will consist of a static single page and a persistent database layer.

The application will have millions of users for 4 hours in the morning, but the application will have only a few thousand users during the rest of the day. The company's data architects have requested the ability to rapidly evolve their schema.

Which solutions will meet these requirements and provide the MOST scalability? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution using on-demand capacity mode.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB supports evolving item attributes, and on-demand capacity adapts to changing request volume without provisioning throughput. CloudFront and S3 independently scale delivery of the static application.

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon Aurora as the database solution. Choose the serverless DB engine mode.
choices.explanation: Aurora Serverless retains a relational schema and database engine. DynamoDB better fits rapidly evolving item attributes and highly scalable key-value or document access for this application.

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution. Ensure that DynamoDB auto scaling is enabled.
choices.explanation: Provisioned DynamoDB autoscaling can lag abrupt traffic increases and requires configured capacity limits. On-demand mode avoids managing provisioned throughput and better matches the requested scalability during the large daily demand swing.

choices.solution: Deploy the static content into an Amazon S3 bucket. Provision an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin.
choices.explanation: S3 hosts the static content and CloudFront caches it globally without operating web servers.

choices.solution: Deploy the web servers for static content across a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. Configure the instances to periodically refresh the content from an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume.
choices.explanation: Serving static files from EC2 and EFS adds server capacity management when S3 and CloudFront scale directly.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is hosting a website behind multiple Application Load Balancers. The company has different distribution rights for its content around the world.

A solutions architect needs to ensure that users are served the correct content without violating distribution rights.

Which configuration should the solutions architect choose to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure Amazon CloudFront with AWS WAF.
choices.explanation: CloudFront and WAF can block countries, but this option does not specify routing each location to the ALB serving its licensed content.

choices.solution: Configure Application Load Balancers with AWS WAF
choices.explanation: WAF can filter access but does not provide the global DNS selection of the correct regional content endpoint.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation policy
choices.explanation:
Geolocation routing in Amazon Route 53 allows you to route traffic based on the geographic location of the user. You can create different records for your website content and associate them with specific geographic locations.

This way, users from different regions will be directed to the appropriate servers or load balancers hosting the content that adheres to the distribution rights for that region.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geoproximity routing policy
choices.explanation: Geoproximity routes by distance and adjustable bias, not the explicit country or geographic boundaries used for distribution rights.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate two DNS servers to AWS. The servers host a total of approximately 200 zones and receive 1 million requests each day on average.

The company wants to maximize availability while minimizing the operational overhead that is related to the management of the two servers.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create 200 new hosted zones in the Amazon Route 53 console Import zone files.
choices.explanation: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable domain name system (DNS) web service provided by AWS. By creating 200 new hosted zones in the Amazon Route 53 console and importing the existing zone files, you can take advantage of the fully managed and highly available nature of Route 53 without the need to manage servers.

choices.solution: Launch a single large Amazon EC2 instance Import zone tiles. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
choices.explanation: One DNS instance is a failure point, and alarms do not supply redundant authoritative DNS.

choices.solution: Migrate the servers to AWS by using AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
choices.explanation: Migrating servers retains operating-system and DNS server management instead of using managed Route 53 hosting.

choices.solution:
Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones. Import zone files.

Set the desired capacity to 1 and the maximum capacity to 3 for the Auto Scaling group. Configure scaling alarms to scale based on CPU utilization.
choices.explanation: Desired capacity one leaves one running server; CPU scaling does not provide continuous redundant authoritative DNS service.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a production database on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The company wants to upgrade the database version for security compliance reasons.

Because the database contains critical data, the company wants a quick solution to upgrade and test functionality without losing any data.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create an RDS manual snapshot. Upgrade to the new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
choices.explanation: Upgrading production directly provides no isolated validation environment and makes rollback depend on snapshot restoration.

choices.solution: Use native backup and restore. Restore the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
choices.explanation: Manual backup and restore add transfer work and cutover coordination.

choices.solution: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
choices.explanation: DMS requires operating a separate replication workflow instead of the integrated Blue/Green test and switchover mechanism.

choices.solution: Use Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments to deploy and test production changes.
choices.explanation: RDS Blue/Green Deployments creates a separate synchronized environment for testing supported production changes, then switches over with reduced downtime. Confirm engine and feature support.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A social media company wants to store its database of user profiles, relationships, and interactions in the AWS Cloud. The company needs an application to monitor any changes in the database.

The application needs to analyze the relationships between the data entities and to provide recommendations to users.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
choices.explanation: Neptune Streams already captures graph changes; introducing Kinesis requires another forwarding and processing integration.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
choices.explanation:
Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database service that is designed for storing and querying highly connected data. It supports the property graph and RDF graph models, making it suitable for scenarios where relationships between data entities need to be analyzed.

Neptune Streams: Neptune Streams is a feature of Amazon Neptune that allows you to capture changes (inserts, updates, deletes) made to the graph database in a streaming fashion. This streaming capability enables you to react to changes in near real-time and trigger additional processing based on those changes.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
choices.explanation: QLDB is a ledger database rather than a graph database optimized for relationship traversal and recommendations.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
choices.explanation: Neptune Streams captures Neptune changes, not QLDB changes, and QLDB is not the graph database requested.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company manages an application that stores data on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Increases in traffic are causing performance problems.

The company determines that database queries are the primary reason for the slow performance.

What should a solutions architect do to improve the application's performance?

choices.solution: Serve read traffic from the Multi-AZ standby replica.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby is not available for read queries.

choices.solution: Configure the DB instance to use Transfer Acceleration.
choices.explanation: Transfer Acceleration is an S3 feature, not an RDS query-performance setting.

choices.solution: Create a read replica from the source DB instance. Serve read traffic from the read replica.
choices.explanation: Creating read replicas allows you to offload read traffic from the primary (master) DB instance to one or more read replicas. Read replicas can serve read-only queries, distributing the load and improving overall query performance.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose between the application and Amazon RDS to increase the concurrency of database requests.
choices.explanation: Firehose does not act as a database query proxy or scale RDS read execution.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company uses Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP in its primary AWS Region for CIFS and NFS file shares. Applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances access the file shares.

The company needs a storage disaster recovery (DR) solution in a secondary Region. The data that is replicated in the secondary Region needs to be accessed by using the same protocols as the primary Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create an AWS Lambda function to copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Replicate the S3 bucket to the secondary Region.
choices.explanation: S3 copies do not expose the required CIFS/SMB and NFS interfaces without additional filesystem infrastructure.

choices.solution:
Create a backup of the FSx for ONTAP volumes by using AWS Backup. Copy the volumes to the secondary Region.

Create a new FSx for ONTAP instance from the backup.
choices.explanation: Backup copying and restoration require recovery operations rather than maintaining an already replicated ONTAP filesystem.

choices.solution: Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the secondary Region. Use NetApp SnapMirror to replicate data from the primary Region to the secondary Region.
choices.explanation: FSx for ONTAP supports NetApp SnapMirror, which is a robust data replication technology. You can use SnapMirror to replicate data from the primary FSx for ONTAP instance in the primary Region to an FSx for ONTAP instance in the secondary Region.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Migrate the current data to the volume.

Replicate the volume to the secondary Region.
choices.explanation: EFS supplies NFS, not CIFS/SMB, and migrating filesystem platforms changes the existing protocol support.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is building a new furniture inventory application. The company has deployed the application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones.

The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in their VPC. A solutions architect has observed that incoming traffic seems to favor one EC2 instance, resulting in latency for some requests.

What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

choices.solution: Disable session affinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB
choices.explanation: Session affinity, also known as sticky sessions, directs a client's requests to the same EC2 instance, based on the client's session information. While sticky sessions can be useful in some scenarios, they can lead to uneven distribution of traffic, causing latency for some requests if one EC2 instance is overloaded.

choices.solution: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer
choices.explanation: Changing load-balancer type does not directly address persistent session affinity and may change supported application features.

choices.solution: Increase the number of EC2 instances in each Availability Zone
choices.explanation: Additional instances can remain underused if sticky sessions continue pinning traffic to the favored instance.

choices.solution: Adjust the frequency of the health checks on the ALB's target group
choices.explanation: Health-check frequency affects failure detection, not the allocation of healthy clients bound by sticky sessions.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to run a gaming application on Amazon EC2 instances that are part of an Auto Scaling group in the AWS Cloud. The application will transmit data by using UDP packets.

The company wants to ensure that the application can scale out and in as traffic increases and decreases.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Attach a Network Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: UDP is a connectionless protocol, and Network Load Balancers (NLB) support UDP, making them suitable for applications that use UDP for transmitting data.

choices.solution: Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: An ALB does not support arbitrary UDP traffic.

choices.solution: Deploy an Amazon Route 53 record set with a weighted policy to route traffic appropriately.
choices.explanation: DNS weighting does not track individual dynamic targets with NLB-style flow distribution and health checks.

choices.solution: Deploy a NAT instance that is configured with port forwarding to the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group.
choices.explanation: A NAT instance with forwarding is a self-managed bottleneck and does not automatically track the elastic target fleet.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A gaming company is building an application with Voice over IP capabilities. The application will serve traffic to users across the world.

The application needs to be highly available with an automated failover across AWS Regions. The company wants to minimize the latency of users without relying on IP address caching on user devices.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS Global Accelerator with health checks.
choices.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator is a service that provides static IP addresses (Anycast) to route traffic over the AWS global network. It routes traffic over the optimal path to the AWS endpoint, improving availability and performance.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation routing policy.
choices.explanation: Geolocation DNS depends on resolver caching and does not provide rapid health-based rerouting over a global accelerator path.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that includes multiple origins.
choices.explanation: CloudFront serves HTTP/HTTPS content rather than arbitrary real-time VoIP traffic.

choices.solution: Create an Application Load Balancer that uses path-based routing.
choices.explanation: A regional ALB cannot provide automatic multi-Region endpoint failover and does not handle arbitrary VoIP transport.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate its on-premises Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise edition database to AWS. The company's online application uses the database to process transactions.

The data analysis team uses the same production database to run reports for analytical processing. The company wants to reduce operational overhead by moving to managed services wherever possible.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Migrate to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server. Use read replicas for reporting purposes
choices.explanation: Amazon RDS supports read replicas, allowing you to offload reporting and analytical workloads to replicas without impacting the performance of the primary database. This is a cost-effective and efficient way to handle reporting without affecting transactional processing on the primary database.

choices.solution: Migrate to Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2. Use Always On read replicas for reporting purposes
choices.explanation: SQL Server on EC2 retains operating-system, backup, patching, and replication administration.

choices.solution: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB. Use DynamoDB on-demand replicas for reporting purposes
choices.explanation: DynamoDB requires a different data model and has no proposed conventional on-demand SQL reporting replicas.

choices.solution: Migrate to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Use Aurora read replicas for reporting purposes
choices.explanation: Aurora MySQL requires converting SQL Server schema, code, and application queries rather than preserving the existing engine.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company recently migrated its web application to the AWS Cloud. The company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run multiple processes to host the application.

The processes include an Apache web server that serves static content. The Apache web server makes requests to a PHP application that uses a local Redis server for user sessions.

The company wants to redesign the architecture to be highly available and to use AWS managed solutions.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to host the static content and the PHP application. Configure Elastic Beanstalk to deploy its EC2 instance into a public subnet.

Assign a public IP address.
choices.explanation: A single public Beanstalk instance does not supply redundant application capacity or a highly available shared session store.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Lambda to host the static content and the PHP application. Use an Amazon API Gateway REST API to proxy requests to the Lambda function.

Set the API Gateway CORS configuration to respond to the domain name. Configure Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to handle session information.
choices.explanation: Moving an existing PHP server directly to Lambda requires runtime packaging and application changes, and serving static content through functions is unnecessary.

choices.solution:
Keep the backend code on the EC2 instance. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that has Multi-AZ enabled.

Configure the ElastiCache for Redis cluster in cluster mode. Copy the frontend resources to Amazon S3.

Configure the backend code to reference the EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: The original backend EC2 instance remains a single failure point even after static content and Redis are moved.

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 endpoint to an S3 bucket that is configured to host the static content. Configure an Application Load Balancer that targets an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service that runs AWS Fargate tasks for the PHP application.

Configure the PHP application to use an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that runs in multiple Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: Use CloudFront + S3 for highly available static content, an ALB + ECS Fargate for the PHP application, and Multi-AZ ElastiCache for Redis sessions. This removes the single EC2/Redis failure point and uses managed services.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that has a target group. The company designed the application to work with session affinity (sticky sessions) for a better user experience.

The application must be available publicly over the internet as an endpoint. A WAF must be applied to the endpoint for additional security.

Session affinity (sticky sessions) must be configured on the endpoint.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Create a public Network Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
choices.explanation: WAF cannot be associated directly with an NLB; its transport-layer stickiness also differs from ALB cookie-based sessions.

choices.solution: Create a Gateway Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
choices.explanation: Gateway Load Balancer serves network appliances rather than a public application endpoint with WAF and HTTP session affinity.

choices.solution: Create a public Application Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
choices.explanation: An ALB provides a public HTTP endpoint and supports sticky sessions when configured on the target group.

choices.solution: Create a second target group. Add Elastic IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: A second target group and public instance addresses do not provide the required WAF-protected sticky-session endpoint.

choices.solution: Create a web ACL in AWS WAF. Associate the web ACL with the endpoint
choices.explanation: A WAF web ACL associated with the ALB filters application-layer threats before requests reach the instances.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group. Application peak hours occur at the same time each day.

Application users report slow application performance at the start of peak hours. The application performs normally 2-3 hours after peak hours begin.

The company wants to ensure that the application works properly at the start of peak hours.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic properly to the instances.
choices.explanation: Load balancing distributes existing capacity but does not launch enough instances before the predictable peak.

choices.solution: Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on memory utilization.
choices.explanation: Memory-based scaling is reactive and needs custom metrics; it does not guarantee capacity before peak hours.

choices.solution: Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on CPU utilization.
choices.explanation: CPU-based scaling begins after demand increases, leaving a startup interval with insufficient capacity.

choices.solution: Configure a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances before peak hours.
choices.explanation: Scheduled scaling launches instances before the predictable peak, giving initialization time and avoiding a delay while reactive policies detect traffic.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A startup company is hosting a website for its customers on an Amazon EC2 instance. The website consists of a stateless Python application and a MySQL database.

The website serves only a small amount of traffic. The company is concerned about the reliability of the instance and needs to migrate to a highly available architecture.

The company cannot modify the application code.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to achieve high availability for the website? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Provision an internet gateway in each Availability Zone in use.
choices.explanation: An internet gateway attaches to a VPC, not separately to each AZ, and does not replicate the application or database.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance.
choices.explanation: RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provides database failover without changing the application to a different database engine.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB, and enable DynamoDB auto scaling.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB requires data-model and query changes, violating the unchanged application-code requirement.

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to synchronize the database data across multiple EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: DataSync copies files and objects; it is not a transaction-consistent MySQL replication and failover service.

choices.solution: Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that are distributed across two Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: An ALB and an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones provide redundant application instances and automatic replacement.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A marketing company receives a large amount of new clickstream data in Amazon S3 from a marketing campaign. The company needs to analyze the clickstream data in Amazon S3 quickly.

Then the company needs to determine whether to process the data further in the data pipeline.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Create external tables in a Spark catalog. Configure jobs in AWS Glue to query the data.
choices.explanation: Glue Spark jobs add processing-job configuration for quick exploratory SQL that Athena executes directly.

choices.solution: Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Athena to query the data.
choices.explanation: AWS Glue can crawl the S3 data to build metadata, and Athena can query the files directly in S3 without provisioning a cluster. This is the lowest-operational-overhead path for quick ad-hoc analysis.

choices.solution: Create external tables in a Hive metastore. Configure Spark jobs in Amazon EMR to query the data.
choices.explanation: An EMR cluster and Hive metastore add infrastructure and management for a simple on-demand S3 analysis.

choices.solution: Configure an AWS Glue crawler to crawl the data. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to use SQL to query the data.
choices.explanation: Kinesis analytics processes streaming sources rather than querying a static S3 dataset directly as proposed.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses a database that runs on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance.

The application performs slowly when traffic increases. The database experiences a heavy read load during periods of high traffic.

Which actions should a solutions architect take to resolve these performance issues? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Turn on auto scaling for the DB instance.
choices.explanation: RDS storage autoscaling does not scale DB instance compute or offload read queries.

choices.solution: Create a read replica for the DB instance. Configure the application to send read traffic to the read replica.
choices.explanation: An RDS read replica serves read-only queries separately from the writer; the application must direct eligible reads to it.

choices.solution: Convert the DB instance to a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Configure the application to send read traffic to the standby DB instance.
choices.explanation: A traditional Multi-AZ DB instance standby cannot serve application reads.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Configure the application to cache query results in the ElastiCache cluster.
choices.explanation: ElastiCache stores reusable query results to reduce database reads; configure cache invalidation and expiry to meet freshness requirements.

choices.solution: Configure the Auto Scaling group subnets to ensure that the EC2 instances are provisioned in the same Availability Zone as the DB instance.
choices.explanation: Moving clients into the DB's AZ does not add database read capacity and reduces application AZ resilience.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company's application uses Network Load Balancers, Auto Scaling groups, Amazon EC2 instances, and databases that are deployed in an Amazon VPC. The company wants to capture information about traffic to and from the network interfaces in near real time in its Amazon VPC.

The company wants to send the information to Amazon OpenSearch Service for analysis.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group.

Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
choices.explanation: Data Streams requires a consumer to deliver records into OpenSearch; Firehose supplies that managed destination delivery.

choices.solution:
Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group.

Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
choices.explanation: VPC Flow Logs can publish to CloudWatch Logs, and Kinesis Data Firehose can deliver the log stream to OpenSearch Service with minimal custom processing. CloudTrail is not a destination for VPC Flow Logs.

choices.solution:
Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail.

Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.
choices.explanation: VPC Flow Logs cannot send network flow records into a CloudTrail trail.

choices.solution:
Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail.

Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records API activity and cannot serve as the proposed VPC Flow Logs destination.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is developing an application that will run on a production Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster has managed node groups that are provisioned with On-Demand Instances.

The company needs a dedicated EKS cluster for development work. The company will use the development cluster infrequently to test the resiliency of the application.

The EKS cluster must manage all the nodes.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Create a managed node group that contains only Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: For an infrequently used development cluster, a managed node group consisting only of Spot Instances is the most cost-effective choice while still letting EKS manage the nodes. Mixing in On-Demand capacity adds cost that the requirement does not justify.

choices.solution:
Create two managed node groups. Provision one node group with On-Demand Instances.

Provision the second node group with Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: An On-Demand baseline adds cost that is unnecessary for infrequent interruption-tolerant development resiliency tests.

choices.solution: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a launch configuration that uses Spot Instances. Configure the user data to add the nodes to the EKS cluster.
choices.explanation: A separately created Auto Scaling group is self-managed rather than an EKS managed node group.

choices.solution: Create a managed node group that contains only On-Demand Instances.
choices.explanation: All On-Demand nodes miss the Spot savings appropriate for this nonproduction test workload.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company wants to back up its on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to AWS. The company's backup solution exports on-premises backups to an Amazon S3 bucket as objects.

The S3 backups must be retained for 30 days and must be automatically deleted after 30 days.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

choices.solution: Create an S3 bucket that has S3 Object Lock enabled.
choices.explanation: Object Lock requires versioning and prevents permanent deletion of protected backup versions during retention.

choices.solution: Create an S3 bucket that has object versioning enabled.
choices.explanation: Versioning alone does not prevent authorized permanent deletion during the mandatory retention period.

choices.solution: Configure a default Object Lock compliance-mode retention period of 30 days for new backup objects.
choices.explanation: A default compliance retention period protects new backup versions for 30 days.

choices.solution: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to protect the objects for 30 days.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle expiration schedules deletion but does not prevent users from deleting an object before day 30.

choices.solution: Configure S3 Lifecycle expiration after 30 days, noncurrent-version expiration for eligible unlocked versions, and expired delete-marker cleanup. Allow asynchronous deletion after retention expires.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle expiration hides current objects with delete markers. Also configure noncurrent-version expiration and delete-marker cleanup for permanent removal after retention; deletion is asynchronous.

choices.solution: Configure the backup solution to tag the objects with a 30-day retention period
choices.explanation: An object tag is metadata and does not itself enforce retention or automatic deletion.

Design Resilient Architectures.question:
A company is migrating its multi-tier on-premises application to AWS. The application consists of a single-node MySQL database and a multi-node web tier.

The company must minimize changes to the application during the migration. The company wants to improve application resiliency after the migration.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: An ALB and Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling group provide a resilient web tier while preserving the application runtime.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer.
choices.explanation: An Auto Scaling group and NLB do not implement MySQL replication, shared state, or safe database failover.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment.
choices.explanation: RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provides a managed database standby and failover while retaining MySQL compatibility.

choices.solution: Migrate the web tier to an AWS Lambda function.
choices.explanation: Moving the existing web tier into Lambda functions changes the execution and deployment model and requires application refactoring.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB requires converting the MySQL schema and queries into a different data model and API.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company uses NFS to store large video files in on-premises network attached storage. Each video file ranges in size from 1 MB to 500 GB.

The total storage is 70 TB and is no longer growing. The company decides to migrate the video files to Amazon S3.

The company must migrate the video files as soon as possible while using the least possible network bandwidth.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create an S3 bucket. Create an IAM role that has permissions to write to the S3 bucket.

Use the AWS CLI to copy all files locally to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Copying all 70 TB over the network consumes the very bandwidth the requirement seeks to minimize. Granting an IAM role does not reduce the transfer volume.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Snowball Edge job. Receive a Snowball Edge device on premises.

Use the Snowball Edge client to transfer data to the device. Return the device so that AWS can import the data into Amazon S3.
choices.explanation:
AWS Snowball Edge is designed for offline bulk transfer of tens of terabytes. It moves the 70 TB without consuming the company's network bandwidth, which directly satisfies the requirement to use the least possible network bandwidth.

Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.

choices.solution:
Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises. Create a public service endpoint to connect to the S3 File Gateway.

Create an S3 bucket. Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway.

Point the new file share to the S3 bucket. Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.
choices.explanation: File Gateway uploads data to S3 over the network. It does not avoid transmitting the 70 TB, and deploying a gateway adds work for a one-time migration.

choices.solution:
Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and AWS. Deploy an S3 File Gateway on premises.

Create a public virtual interface (VIF) to connect to the S3 File Gateway. Create an S3 bucket.

Create a new NFS file share on the S3 File Gateway. Point the new file share to the S3 bucket.

Transfer the data from the existing NFS file share to the S3 File Gateway.
choices.explanation: Direct Connect still transfers all 70 TB over a network connection and requires connection provisioning and gateway setup. It does not meet the least-network-bandwidth objective of an offline device transfer.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is running an SMB file server in its data center. The file server stores large files that are accessed frequently for the first few days after the files are created.

After 7 days the files are rarely accessed. The total data size is increasing and is close to the company's total storage capacity.

A solutions architect must increase the company's available storage space without losing low-latency access to the most recently accessed files. The solutions architect must also provide file lifecycle management to avoid future storage issues.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
choices.explanation: DataSync copies files but does not provide a local cache-backed SMB interface or automatic S3 lifecycle management. Copying older files also does not by itself reclaim the original file-server capacity.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to extend the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
choices.explanation:
Option B: Amazon S3 File Gateway provides a hybrid cloud storage solution, integrating on-premises environments with cloud storage. Files written to the file share are automatically saved as S3 objects.

With S3 Lifecycle policies, you can transition objects between storage classes. Transitioning to Glacier Deep Archive is suitable for rarely accessed files.

This solution addresses both the storage capacity and lifecycle management requirements.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system to extend the company's storage space.
choices.explanation: FSx for Windows supplies SMB storage, but this option does not retain a local cache for low-latency on-premises access or define the requested archival lifecycle.

choices.solution: Install a utility on each user's computer to access Amazon S3. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.
choices.explanation: Per-user S3 utilities replace the existing SMB access pattern and require client administration. Direct S3 access does not provide the local cache needed for low-latency access to recent files.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is using Amazon S3 to design the storage architecture of a new digital media application. The media files must be resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone.

Some files are accessed frequently while other files are rarely accessed in an unpredictable pattern. The solutions architect must minimize the costs of storing and retrieving the media files.

Which storage option meets these requirements?

choices.solution: S3 Standard
choices.explanation: S3 Standard provides multi-AZ durability, but keeps every object at the frequent-access storage price. It does not automatically reduce storage cost for the unpredictably cold files.

choices.solution: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
choices.explanation:
Amazon S3 Intelligent Tiering is a storage class that automatically moves data to the most cost-effective storage tier based on access patterns. It can store objects in two access tiers: the frequent access tier and the infrequent access tier.

The frequent access tier is optimized for frequently accessed objects and is charged at the same rate as S3 Standard. The infrequent access tier is optimized for objects that are not accessed frequently and are charged at a lower rate than S3 Standard.

S3 Intelligent Tiering is a good choice for storing media files that are accessed frequently and infrequently in an unpredictable pattern because it automatically moves data to the most cost-effective storage tier based on access patterns, minimizing storage and retrieval costs. It is also resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone because it stores objects in multiple Availability Zones within a region.

choices.solution: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
choices.explanation: Standard-IA charges retrieval fees and assumes objects are accessed infrequently. Files that unexpectedly become hot can incur additional retrieval costs instead of being automatically moved between access tiers.

choices.solution: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, so it does not meet the requirement to withstand the loss of an Availability Zone.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is storing backup files by using Amazon S3 Standard storage. The files are accessed frequently for 1 month.

However, the files are not accessed after 1 month. The company must keep the files indefinitely.

Which storage solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically migrate objects.
choices.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering is intended for uncertain access patterns. Here the archive date is already known, so a direct lifecycle transition to Deep Archive avoids unnecessary tier monitoring and intermediate storage.

choices.solution: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month.
choices.explanation:
Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive is a secure, durable, and extremely low-cost Amazon S3 storage class for long-term retention of data that is rarely accessed and for which retrieval times of several hours are acceptable. It is the lowest-cost storage option in Amazon S3, making it a cost-effective choice for storing backup files that are not accessed after 1 month.

You can use an S3 Lifecycle configuration to automatically transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month. This will minimize the storage costs for the backup files that are not accessed frequently.

choices.solution: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 1 month.
choices.explanation: Standard-IA keeps data immediately accessible at a higher storage price than Deep Archive. That extra retrieval readiness is unnecessary for files that are never accessed after the first month.

choices.solution: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 month.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA still costs more to store than Deep Archive and sacrifices multi-AZ resilience. Its immediate access capability does not help an indefinitely retained archive with no expected reads.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company observes an increase in Amazon EC2 costs in its most recent bill. The billing team notices unwanted vertical scaling of instance types for a couple of EC2 instances.

A solutions architect needs to create a graph comparing the last 2 months of EC2 costs and perform an in-depth analysis to identify the root cause of the vertical scaling.

How should the solutions architect generate the information with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget report and compare EC2 costs based on instance types.
choices.explanation: Budgets tracks spending against configured limits and produces budget-oriented reports. Cost Explorer is the direct tool for interactive historical cost breakdowns by instance type.

choices.solution: Use Cost Explorer's granular filtering feature to perform an in-depth analysis of EC2 costs based on instance types.
choices.explanation: Cost Explorer filters historical costs by service, instance type, and usage type to identify the effect of larger EC2 instances. Use CloudTrail to identify who changed an instance type; cost data alone does not identify the actor.

choices.solution: Use graphs from the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard to compare EC2 costs based on instance types for the last 2 months.
choices.explanation: The billing dashboard provides summary views rather than the granular instance-type filtering needed for the investigation. Cost Explorer supplies that detail without creating a separate reporting system.

choices.solution: Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report and send it to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon QuickSight with Amazon S3 as a source to generate an interactive graph based on instance types.
choices.explanation: Cost and Usage Reports can support detailed analysis, but configuring report delivery and a QuickSight dataset adds setup and maintenance. The requested two-month comparison can be made directly in Cost Explorer.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company that hosts its web application on AWS wants to ensure all Amazon EC2 instances. Amazon RDS DB instances. and Amazon Redshift clusters are configured with tags.

The company wants to minimize the effort of configuring and operating this check.

What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?

choices.solution: Use AWS Config rules to define and detect resources that are not properly tagged.
choices.explanation:
Yes, you can use AWS Config to create tags for your resources. AWS Config is a service that enables you to assess, audit, and evaluate the configurations of your AWS resources.

You can use AWS Config to create rules that automatically tag resources when they are created or when their configurations change.

choices.solution: Use Cost Explorer to display resources that are not properly tagged. Tag those resources manually.
choices.explanation: Cost Explorer analyzes billing data rather than continuously evaluating every resource's tagging compliance. Manually checking and tagging resources adds ongoing effort.

choices.solution: Write API calls to check all resources for proper tag allocation. Periodically run the code on an EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: A custom EC2 polling process requires code, server administration, scheduling, and maintenance. AWS Config provides the required tagging evaluation without that custom system.

choices.solution: Write API calls to check all resources for proper tag allocation. Schedule an AWS Lambda function through Amazon CloudWatch to periodically run the code.
choices.explanation: Lambda avoids a polling server, but the team still has to develop and maintain its own tagging checks. A managed Config rule requires less implementation work.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company stores call transcript files on a monthly basis. Users access the files randomly within 1 year of the call, but users access the files infrequently after 1 year.

The company wants to optimize its solution by giving users the ability to query and retrieve files that are less than 1-year- old as quickly as possible. A delay in retrieving older files is acceptable.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Query the tags to retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
choices.explanation: Object tags are not an SQL-queryable index of transcript content. Instant Retrieval provides low-latency object access but does not supply the requested transcript query engine or an automatic archive transition after a year.

choices.solution:
Store individual files in S3 Intelligent-Tiering and catalog supported transcript formats for Amazon Athena. Transition them to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year.

Restore archived files to S3 before querying or retrieving them.
choices.explanation:
Intelligent-Tiering suits changing access patterns during the first year. Athena can query supported formats in accessible S3 storage, but it cannot query objects still archived in Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

Restore archived objects before querying; Glacier Select refers to the separate legacy vault service, not S3 Glacier storage-class objects.

choices.solution:
Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Store search metadata for each archive in Amazon S3 Standard storage.

Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files by searching for metadata from Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Keeping every first-year object in Standard lacks Intelligent-Tiering's cost adaptation to random access. Searching metadata stored as S3 objects also needs an additional indexing or query mechanism that this option does not define.

choices.solution:
Store individual files in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.

Store search metadata in Amazon RDS. Query the files from Amazon RDS.

Retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: A separate RDS metadata database requires a custom ingestion and indexing pipeline and additional database operation. It adds more infrastructure than cataloging supported S3 transcript formats for serverless Athena queries.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to store its accounting records in Amazon S3. The records must be immediately accessible for 1 year and then must be archived for an additional 9 years.

No one at the company, including administrative users and root users, can be able to delete the records during the entire 10-year period. The records must be stored with maximum resiliency.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
choices.explanation: Glacier archives require restoration, and an administrator can change an access policy permitting deletion.

choices.solution:
Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records.

After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
choices.explanation: IAM policies are mutable; administrators can remove the deletion restriction before ten years.

choices.solution: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
choices.explanation: Deep Archive reduces long-term storage costs after the first year. Object Lock compliance mode protects each retained version for ten years even against privileged deletion.

choices.solution: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.
choices.explanation: Governance retention can be bypassed with permission; One Zone-IA also sacrifices multi-AZ resilience.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs multiple Windows workloads on AWS. The company's employees use Windows file shares that are hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances.

The file shares synchronize data between themselves and maintain duplicate copies. The company wants a highly available and durable storage solution that preserves how users currently access the files.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Migrate all the data to Amazon S3. Set up IAM authentication for users to access files.
choices.explanation: S3 object access replaces the existing Windows SMB file-sharing interface.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Mount the S3 File Gateway on the existing EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: This keeps the EC2 file servers and their availability management instead of replacing them.

choices.solution: Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
choices.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides managed SMB shares and Active Directory integration. A Multi-AZ file system provides a standby and automatic failover.

choices.solution: Extend the file share environment to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to Amazon EFS.
choices.explanation: EFS uses NFS, not the Windows SMB protocol the users already require.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has an application that generates a large number of files, each approximately 5 MB in size. The files are stored in Amazon S3.

Company policy requires the files to be stored for 4 years before they can be deleted. Immediate accessibility is always required as the files contain critical business data that is not easy to reproduce.

The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of the object creation but are rarely accessed after the first 30 days.

Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

choices.solution: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
choices.explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval requires restoration, violating continuous immediate accessibility.

choices.solution: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA cannot withstand an AZ loss; these critical files are not readily reproducible.

choices.solution: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
choices.explanation: S3 Lifecycle moves eligible objects to Standard-IA after its 30-day minimum age and expires them after the required four-year retention period.

choices.solution: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier 4 years after object creation.
choices.explanation: Archiving after four years adds ongoing storage instead of deleting data after the required retention period.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to configure a real-time data ingestion architecture for its application. The company needs an API, a process that transforms data as the data is streamed, and a storage solution for the data.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution:
Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source.

Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: An EC2-hosted API adds server patching and scaling compared with managed API Gateway.

choices.solution:
Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to AWS Glue. Stop source/destination checking on the EC2 instance.

Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to send the data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Disabling source/destination checks does not create a streaming Glue ingestion API; EC2 adds administration too.

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source.

Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: API Gateway sends records to Kinesis Data Streams. Firehose invokes Lambda transformations and delivers buffered output to S3 with managed retries and scaling.

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to AWS Glue. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data.

Use AWS Glue to send the data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Sending API calls to Glue alone omits the defined stream-ingestion and Firehose delivery mechanism.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to keep user transaction data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must retain the data for 7 years.

What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Use DynamoDB point-in-time recovery to back up the table continuously.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB PITR retains at most 35 days of recovery history, not seven years.

choices.solution: Use AWS Backup to create backup schedules and retention policies for the table.
choices.explanation: AWS Backup schedules DynamoDB recovery points and applies seven-year retention, avoiding custom backup scripts. Backup retention does not itself delete live items from the table.

choices.solution:
Create an on-demand backup of the table by using the DynamoDB console. Store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB on-demand backups are managed backups, not files manually placed in a customer S3 bucket.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to back up the table and to store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Custom Lambda export and retention automation requires more maintenance than an AWS Backup plan.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is planning to use an Amazon DynamoDB table for data storage. The company is concerned about cost optimization.

The table will not be used on most mornings. In the evenings, the read and write traffic will often be unpredictable.

When traffic spikes occur, they will happen very quickly.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.solution: Create a DynamoDB table in on-demand capacity mode.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB on-demand capacity bills for actual read and write requests and handles variable traffic without maintaining provisioned capacity during idle periods.

choices.solution: Create a DynamoDB table with a global secondary index.
choices.explanation: A secondary index supports queries and incurs capacity charges; it does not solve unpredictable table capacity.

choices.solution: Create a DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity and auto scaling.
choices.explanation: Provisioned autoscaling reacts after demand changes and maintains capacity charges during idle periods.

choices.solution: Create a DynamoDB table in provisioned capacity mode, and configure it as a global table.
choices.explanation: Global tables add regional replication costs and do not resolve the proposed provisioned-capacity scaling delay.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company wants to reduce the cost of its existing three-tier web architecture. The web, application, and database servers are running on Amazon EC2 instances for the development, test, and production environments.

The EC2 instances average 30% CPU utilization during peak hours and 10% CPU utilization during non-peak hours. The production EC2 instances run 24 hours a day.

The development and test EC2 instances run for at least 8 hours each day. The company plans to implement automation to stop the development and test EC2 instances when they are not in use.

Which EC2 instance purchasing solution will meet the company's requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Spot interruptions are unsuitable for this steady production workload; Reserved Instances charge during stopped test periods.

choices.solution: Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Reserved Instances discount the steady production baseline. On-Demand instances can be stopped outside development and testing hours without a long-term usage commitment.

choices.solution: Use Spot blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: Spot blocks are not a continuous 24-hour production solution; test reservations still incur idle commitment charges.

choices.solution: Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: On-Demand pricing misses production's steady-use discount; Spot blocks are unavailable for the proposed test purchase.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has a large Microsoft SharePoint deployment running on-premises that requires Microsoft Windows shared file storage. The company wants to migrate this workload to the AWS Cloud and is considering various storage options.

The storage solution must be highly available and integrated with Active Directory for access control.

Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure Amazon EFS storage and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.
choices.explanation: EFS provides NFS rather than the required Windows SMB filesystem and native AD integration.

choices.solution: Create an SMB file share on an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in two Availability Zones.
choices.explanation: S3 File Gateway is not the native multi-AZ Windows filesystem with full SharePoint-compatible filesystem semantics.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and configure Microsoft Windows Server to mount it as a volume.
choices.explanation: Mounting S3 objects does not provide native Windows file locking, SMB semantics, and AD integration.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system on AWS and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.
choices.explanation: FSx for Windows File Server provides managed Windows SMB storage with Active Directory authentication; choose Multi-AZ for the required high availability.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts an SFTP server that stores its data on an NFS-based file system.

The server holds 200 GB of data that needs to be transferred. The server must be hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.

Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to automate this task? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Launch the EC2 instance into the same Availability Zone as the EFS file system.
choices.explanation: Choosing an Availability Zone for the EC2 instance does not automate copying the NFS files into the regional EFS file system.

choices.solution: Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center.
choices.explanation: An on-premises DataSync agent reads the existing NFS file system and transfers its data to EFS.

choices.solution: Create a secondary Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instance for the data.
choices.explanation: An EBS volume is block storage for EC2, not the required EFS destination or an automated NFS migration service.

choices.solution: Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data to the EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: Manual copying does not meet the requirement for an automated transfer.

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to configure the on-premises NFS file system behind the SFTP server as the source location and Amazon EFS as the destination location.
choices.explanation: Configure an NFS source location for the storage behind the SFTP server and an EFS destination. DataSync does not use SFTP as a source protocol.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has a highly dynamic batch processing job that uses many Amazon EC2 instances to complete it. The job is stateless in nature, can be started and stopped at any given time with no negative impact, and typically takes upwards of 60 minutes total to complete.

The company has asked a solutions architect to design a scalable and cost-effective solution that meets the requirements of the job.

What should the solutions architect recommend?

choices.solution: Implement EC2 Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: Spot Instances reduce cost for stateless jobs that tolerate interruption. Save checkpoints or retry work so an interruption does not prevent completion.

choices.solution: Purchase EC2 Reserved Instances.
choices.explanation: Reserved Instances require a commitment to capacity usage; interruptible batch processing can use cheaper spare Spot capacity.

choices.solution: Implement EC2 On-Demand Instances.
choices.explanation: On-Demand pricing is higher than Spot pricing for a workload that can safely tolerate interruptions.
