choices.solution: Implement the processing on AWS Lambda.
choices.explanation: A single Lambda invocation is limited to 15 minutes, shorter than this job's roughly hour-long execution.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to reduce a company's storage costs. All the company's data is in the Amazon S3 Standard storage class.

The company must keep all data for at least 25 years. Data from the most recent 2 years must be highly available and immediately retrievable.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately.
choices.explanation: Deep Archive requires a restore before access, so immediately archiving objects violates immediate retrieval during the first two years.

choices.solution: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
choices.explanation: Keep the recent two years in an immediately retrievable storage class and transition older objects to Deep Archive for lower long-term storage cost.

choices.solution: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Activate the archiving option to ensure that data is archived in S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: Access-based archival can move infrequently accessed recent objects out of immediate retrieval before they are two years old.

choices.solution: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately and to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA stores data in one Availability Zone and does not meet the requested highly available storage for recent data.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to help a company optimize the cost of running an application on AWS. The application will use Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda for compute within the architecture.

The EC2 instances will run the data ingestion layer of the application. EC2 usage will be sporadic and unpredictable.

Workloads that run on EC2 instances can be interrupted at any time. The application front end will run on Fargate, and Lambda will serve the API layer.

The front-end utilization and API layer utilization will be predictable over the course of the next year.

Which combination of purchasing options will provide the MOST cost-effective solution for hosting this application? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Use Spot Instances for the data ingestion layer
choices.explanation: Spot capacity reduces costs for the interruption-tolerant ingestion layer; jobs must handle interruption and retries.

choices.solution: Use On-Demand Instances for the data ingestion layer
choices.explanation: On-Demand EC2 pricing misses the Spot discounts suitable for the sporadic, interruption-tolerant work.

choices.solution: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
choices.explanation: Compute Savings Plans cover predictable eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage under an hourly spending commitment.

choices.solution: Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved instances for the data ingestion layer.
choices.explanation: Reserved Instances commit to EC2 usage that the sporadic workload cannot reliably sustain and do not cover Fargate or Lambda.

choices.solution: Purchase a 1-year EC2 instance Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
choices.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans cover EC2 usage in a particular instance family and Region, not the predictable Fargate and Lambda usage.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs a stateless web application in production on a group of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application experiences heavy usage during an 8-hour period each business day.

Application usage is moderate and steady overnight. Application usage is low during weekends.

The company wants to minimize its EC2 costs without affecting the availability of the application.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use Spot Instances for the entire workload.
choices.explanation: An entirely Spot-based fleet can lose the steady production baseline during interruptions.

choices.solution: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
choices.explanation: Reservations discount steady baseline usage and Spot lowers the cost of additional stateless capacity. Maintain sufficient reliable baseline capacity and handle Spot interruptions to preserve availability.

choices.solution: Use On-Demand Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
choices.explanation: Paying On-Demand prices for predictable baseline usage forfeits the savings available through a reservation.

choices.solution: Use Dedicated Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use On-Demand Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
choices.explanation: Dedicated Instances incur a tenancy premium that this workload does not require.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to retain application log files for a critical application for 10 years. The application team regularly accesses logs from the past month for troubleshooting, but logs older than 1 month are rarely accessed.

The application generates more than 10 TB of logs per month.

Which storage option meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: AWS Backup retention settings do not perform lifecycle transitions of the live S3 log objects into archive storage.

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: Keep recent logs in S3 for troubleshooting and transition older logs to Deep Archive for lower long-term storage cost when restore delays are acceptable.

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: AWS Backup is not a backup and archival mechanism for CloudWatch Logs log groups.

choices.solution: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: S3 Lifecycle policies apply to S3 objects, not to CloudWatch Logs log groups.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company sells ringtones created from clips of popular songs. The files containing the ringtones are stored in Amazon S3 Standard and are at least 128 KB in size.

The company has millions of files, but downloads are infrequent for ringtones older than 90 days. The company needs to save money on storage while keeping the most accessed files readily available for its users.

Which action should the company take to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage for the initial storage tier of the objects.
choices.explanation: Initially using Standard-IA incurs retrieval charges during the first 90 days when downloads are frequent.

choices.solution: Move the files to S3 Intelligent-Tiering and configure it to move objects to a less expensive storage tier after 90 days.
choices.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering adds per-object monitoring charges, and its automatic access tiers do not use a configurable 90-day object-age transition to Standard-IA.

choices.solution: Configure S3 inventory to manage objects and move them to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.
choices.explanation: S3 Inventory produces object listings; it does not transition storage classes without additional processing.

choices.solution: Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy that moves the objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.
choices.explanation: A lifecycle transition after 90 days reduces storage cost for rarely accessed older files while Standard serves the frequently accessed recent files.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs a production application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads the data from an Amazon SQS queue and processes the messages in parallel.

The message volume is unpredictable and often has intermittent traffic. This application should continually process messages without any downtime.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use Spot Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
choices.explanation: Spot interruptions can remove all processing capacity, violating the continuous-processing requirement.

choices.solution: Use Reserved Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
choices.explanation: Reserving peak capacity wastes money during intermittent low-volume periods.

choices.solution: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.
choices.explanation: Reserved capacity serves the reliable baseline and Spot workers process additional durable SQS backlog at lower cost. Consumers must handle interruptions and redelivery.

choices.solution: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.
choices.explanation: On-Demand burst capacity costs more than interruption-tolerant Spot workers while the reserved baseline maintains continuous processing.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question: A company has a Windows-based application that must be migrated to AWS. The application requires the use of a shared Windows file system attached to multiple Amazon EC2 Windows instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zone: What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

choices.solution: Configure AWS Storage Gateway in volume gateway mode. Mount the volume to each Windows instance.
choices.explanation: Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes, not a managed shared Windows SMB file system.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the Amazon FSx file system to each Windows instance.
choices.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed Windows file system that can be accessed by multiple EC2 instances. It is designed to provide shared file storage for Windows-based applications.

It supports the SMB protocol, allowing Windows instances to mount the file system. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is fully managed, highly available, and provides features like automatic backups and integration with Active Directory.

choices.solution: Configure a file system by using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS file system to each Windows instance.
choices.explanation: EFS uses NFS and is not the native shared Windows SMB file service required here.

choices.solution:
Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with the required size. Attach each EC2 instance to the volume.

Mount the file system within the volume to each Windows instance.
choices.explanation: An ordinary EBS volume cannot be shared across Availability Zones, and concurrent block-volume access is not a managed Windows file share.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has an ordering application that stores customer information in Amazon RDS for MySQL. During regular business hours, employees run one-time queries for reporting purposes.

Timeouts are occurring during order processing because the reporting queries are taking a long time to run. The company needs to eliminate the timeouts without preventing employees from performing queries.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Create a read replica. Move reporting queries to the read replica.
choices.explanation: Move reporting reads to an RDS read replica so analytical queries no longer compete with order-processing traffic on the primary database.

choices.solution: Create a read replica. Distribute the ordering application to the primary DB instance and the read replica.
choices.explanation: A read replica cannot handle order writes; reporting should move off the writer rather than distributing writable application operations to a read-only endpoint.

choices.solution: Migrate the ordering application to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
choices.explanation: Moving to DynamoDB requires a data-model and application rewrite rather than isolating reporting reads.

choices.solution: Schedule the reporting queries for non-peak hours.
choices.explanation: Moving reports to off-hours prevents employees from performing the required business-hours queries.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs an application on a large fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads and writes entries into an Amazon DynamoDB table.

The size of the DynamoDB table continuously grows, but the application needs only data from the last 30 days. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and development effort.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Use an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the complete solution. Redeploy the CloudFormation stack every 30 days, and delete the original stack.
choices.explanation: Recreating the infrastructure every month risks deleting required recent data and incurs unnecessary deployment work.

choices.solution:
Use an EC2 instance that runs a monitoring application from AWS Marketplace. Configure the monitoring application to use Amazon DynamoDB Streams to store the timestamp when a new item is created in the table.

Use a script that runs on the EC2 instance to delete items that have a timestamp that is older than 30 days.
choices.explanation: A monitoring instance and custom deletion script add cost and maintenance for functionality supplied by DynamoDB TTL.

choices.solution: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a new item is created in the table. Configure the Lambda function to delete items in the table that are older than 30 days.
choices.explanation: Deleting old items on every stream event requires custom querying and deletion logic; native TTL expires items without that worker.

choices.solution: Extend the application to add an attribute that has a value of the current timestamp plus 30 days to each new item that is created in the table. Configure DynamoDB to use the attribute as the TTL attribute.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB TTL is purpose-built for automatic expiry. Store an expiration timestamp on each item and configure that attribute as the table TTL to remove data older than 30 days with minimal operational effort.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to export its database once a day to Amazon S3 for other teams to access. The exported object size varies between 2 GB and 5 GB.

The S3 access pattern for the data is variable and changes rapidly. The data must be immediately available and must remain accessible for up to 3 months.

The company needs the most cost-effective solution that will not increase retrieval time.

Which S3 storage class should the company use to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
choices.explanation:
S3 Intelligent-Tiering is designed to optimize costs by automatically moving objects between two access tiers: frequent and infrequent access. It is suitable for data with unknown or changing access patterns.

With S3 Intelligent-Tiering, Amazon S3 automatically and transparently moves objects between access tiers based on changing access patterns. It is cost-effective for a wide range of storage access patterns.

The objects can be immediately accessed, and the storage cost is lower than using S3 Standard, making it a suitable choice for varying access patterns.

choices.solution: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
choices.explanation: Glacier Instant Retrieval has retrieval charges and a 90-day minimum duration, making rapidly changing access patterns less economical than automatic access tiering.

choices.solution: S3 Standard
choices.explanation: Standard provides immediate access but continues charging the frequent-access storage rate when objects become infrequently accessed.

choices.solution: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
choices.explanation: Standard-IA retrieval charges and a fixed storage-class choice are less suited to this unpredictable, rapidly changing access pattern.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has 700 TB of backup data stored in network attached storage (NAS) in its data center. This backup data need to be accessible for infrequent regulatory requests and must be retained 7 years.

The company has decided to migrate this backup data from its data center to AWS. The migration must be complete within 1 month.

The company has 500 Mbps of dedicated bandwidth on its public internet connection available for data transfer.

What should a solutions architect do to migrate and store the data at the LOWEST cost?

choices.solution: Order AWS Snowball devices to transfer the data. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation:
A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers.

The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings.

Which solution will meet these requirements? Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.

choices.solution: Deploy a VPN connection between the data center and Amazon VPC. Use the AWS CLI to copy the data from on premises to Amazon S3 Glacier.
choices.explanation: At 500 Mbps, transferring 700 TB takes well over a month even before network overhead; VPN does not increase the bandwidth.

choices.solution: Provision a 500 Mbps AWS Direct Connect connection and transfer the data to Amazon S3. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: A 500-Mbps link still cannot move 700 TB in one month, and provisioning Direct Connect adds cost and lead time.

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data and deploy a DataSync agent on premises. Use the DataSync task to copy files from the on-premises NAS storage to Amazon S3 Glacier.
choices.explanation: DataSync cannot overcome the 500-Mbps bandwidth limit, which is insufficient for this migration deadline.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company wants to experiment with individual AWS accounts for its engineer team. The company wants to be notified as soon as the Amazon EC2 instance usage for a given month exceeds a specific threshold for each account.

What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution:
Use Cost Explorer to create a daily report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances.

Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.
choices.explanation: Cost Explorer reports do not provide the proposed native SES threshold-alert mechanism; Budgets supplies managed alerts.

choices.solution:
Use Cost Explorer to create a monthly report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances.

Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.
choices.explanation: A monthly report delays detection and does not itself send a notification when the threshold is crossed.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Budgets to create a cost budget for each account. Set the period to monthly.

Set the scope to EC2 instances. Set an alert threshold for the budget.

Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.
choices.explanation: AWS Budgets is a cost management service that allows you to set custom cost and usage budgets that alert you when you exceed your thresholds. In this case, you can create a monthly budget specifically for EC2 instances, and when the usage exceeds the defined threshold, it triggers an alert.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report with hourly granularity. Integrate the report data with Amazon Athena.

Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an Athena query. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.
choices.explanation: Custom report ingestion, Athena queries, and scheduled alert logic require more work and cost than a managed budget.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A medical research lab produces data that is related to a new study. The lab wants to make the data available with minimum latency to clinics across the country for their on-premises, file-based applications.

The data files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that has read-only permissions for each clinic.

What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic
choices.explanation:
This option provides a way to present an S3 bucket as a file system to on-premises applications. Each clinic can deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway as a VM on-premises, allowing them to access the data in the S3 bucket as if it were local files.

It minimizes latency because the data is cached locally, and read-only permissions can be controlled at the S3 bucket level.

choices.solution: Migrate the files to each clinic's on-premises applications by using AWS DataSync for processing.
choices.explanation: DataSync creates transfer jobs and copies rather than a transparent locally cached file share backed by the S3 dataset.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.
choices.explanation: Volume Gateway exposes block storage, not a file interface to the existing S3 objects.

choices.solution: Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to each clinic's on-premises servers.
choices.explanation: Remote EFS access requires network connectivity and migrating the S3 files, and lacks the proposed local file-gateway cache at each clinic.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a media application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data.

The solution must be fully managed.

Which AWS solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol.

Connect the application server to the file share.
choices.explanation: Volume Gateway provides iSCSI block volumes, not an SMB file share.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Configure tapes to use Amazon S3.

Connect the application server to the tape gateway.
choices.explanation: Tape Gateway presents virtual tapes to backup software, not a shared SMB filesystem.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance.

Connect the application server to the file share.
choices.explanation: A Windows file server on EC2 requires the company to operate, patch, and protect the server.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server.

Connect the application server to the file system.
choices.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed file storage service that supports the SMB protocol. It provides a native Windows file system experience and is designed to be accessed by SMB clients.

This option meets the requirements for a fully managed shared storage solution accessible via SMB.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company's security team requests that network traffic be captured in VPC Flow Logs. The logs will be frequently accessed for 90 days and then accessed intermittently.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements when configuring the logs?

choices.solution: Use Amazon CloudWatch as the target. Set the CloudWatch log group with an expiration of 90 days
choices.explanation: Expiring the log group after 90 days deletes records that must remain available for intermittent access.

choices.solution: Use Amazon Kinesis as the target. Configure the Kinesis stream to always retain the logs for 90 days.
choices.explanation: Kinesis retains streaming records rather than providing the proposed inexpensive long-term log-storage lifecycle.

choices.solution: Use AWS CloudTrail as the target. Configure CloudTrail to save to an Amazon S3 bucket, and enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail records API activity and is not a destination for VPC Flow Logs.

choices.solution: Use Amazon S3 as the target. Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the logs to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.
choices.explanation:
Amazon S3 is a scalable and cost-effective object storage service. Enabling an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition logs to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days is a suitable solution.

This approach allows you to store the logs in a cost-effective manner, automatically moving them to a lower-cost storage class after the initial 90 days.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to design a system to store client case files. The files are core company assets and are important.

The number of files will grow over time. The files must be simultaneously accessible from multiple application servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances.

The solution must have built-in redundancy.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
choices.explanation: EFS provides elastic shared file storage mountable by multiple EC2 instances. Regional EFS replicates data across Availability Zones for redundancy.

choices.solution: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
choices.explanation: Ordinary EBS volumes are AZ-scoped block devices and do not provide a shared elastic filesystem for multiple application servers.

choices.solution: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
choices.explanation: Deep Archive requires restoration before access and is unsuitable for an actively shared file repository.

choices.solution: AWS Backup
choices.explanation: AWS Backup protects data in other storage services; it is not a live filesystem that application servers can mount.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is implementing new data retention policies for all databases that run on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must retain daily backups for a minimum period of 2 years.

The backups must be consistent and restorable.

Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create a backup vault in AWS Backup to retain RDS backups. Create a new backup plan with a daily schedule and an expiration period of 2 years after creation.

Assign the RDS DB instances to the backup plan.
choices.explanation: AWS Backup centrally schedules daily RDS recovery points and applies a two-year retention policy; native automated RDS backup retention alone cannot retain backups that long.

choices.solution:
Configure a backup window for the RDS DB instances for daily snapshots. Assign a snapshot retention policy of 2 years to each RDS DB instance.

Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to schedule snapshot deletions.
choices.explanation: RDS automated backup retention is limited to 35 days, and DLM does not manage RDS snapshot retention.

choices.solution: Configure database transaction logs to be automatically backed up to Amazon CloudWatch Logs with an expiration period of 2 years.
choices.explanation: Transaction logs alone are not consistent, directly restorable daily database backups.

choices.solution:
Configure an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication task. Deploy a replication instance, and configure a change data capture (CDC) task to stream database changes to Amazon S3 as the target.

Configure S3 Lifecycle policies to delete the snapshots after 2 years.
choices.explanation: DMS change records in S3 are not native RDS snapshots and require custom reconstruction to restore a database.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company provides an online service for posting video content and transcoding it for use by any mobile platform. The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so that multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing.

As the popularity of the service has grown over time, the storage costs have become too expensive.

Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

choices.solution: Use AWS Storage Gateway for files to store and process the video content.
choices.explanation: A file gateway adds an appliance and cache layer when workers can download objects directly from S3 for processing.

choices.solution: Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.
choices.explanation: Volume Gateway exposes block volumes and adds gateway management instead of economical object storage for the video archive.

choices.solution: Use Amazon EFS for storing the video content. Once processing is complete, transfer the files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
choices.explanation: EBS retains provisioned-volume costs for completed videos; S3 is the more economical durable object repository.

choices.solution: Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.
choices.explanation: Amazon S3 is a highly durable, scalable, and cost-effective object storage service. It is well-suited for storing large amounts of video content at a lower cost compared to Amazon EFS.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company's compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months.

Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.
choices.explanation:
AWS Backup will automatically take full backups of the DynamoDB table on the schedule defined in the backup plan (the first of each month). The lifecycle policy can transition backups to cold storage after 6 months, meeting that requirement.

Setting a 7-year retention period in the backup plan will ensure each backup is retained for 7 years as required. AWS Backup manages the backup jobs and lifecycle policies, requiring no custom scripting or management.

choices.solution:
Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months.

Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
choices.explanation: Native DynamoDB on-demand backups cannot be transitioned into S3 Glacier by an S3 Lifecycle rule.

choices.solution:
Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month.

Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
choices.explanation: Native DynamoDB backup APIs do not supply the proposed cold-storage transition; AWS Backup's advanced DynamoDB backup lifecycle is required.

choices.solution:
Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression.

Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.
choices.explanation: The native DynamoDB create-backup command has no cold-transition and seven-year-expiration options.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application. The simulation application runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes.

The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system. The company maintains two synchronized file systems.

This strategy is causing data duplication and inefficient resource usage. The company needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
choices.explanation: Moving desktop and simulation applications to Lambda and replacing their files with S3 calls requires code and execution-model changes.

choices.solution: Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon FSx File Gateway for storage.
choices.explanation: Containerizing both applications changes deployment, and FSx File Gateway does not provide a shared NFS/SMB multiprotocol dataset.

choices.solution:
Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances.

Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to exchange data between the applications.
choices.explanation: SQS supplies messages rather than the NFS and SMB filesystem interfaces that the unchanged applications require.

choices.solution:
Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances.

Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.
choices.explanation: FSx for NetApp ONTAP exposes the same data through NFS and SMB, allowing Linux simulations and Windows visualization to share storage without application code changes.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets.

A solutions architect needs to determine the most efficient way to obtain this report information.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
choices.explanation: Athena needs billing data export and table setup before queries; Cost Explorer can produce the report more directly using configured user cost-allocation tags.

choices.solution: Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
choices.explanation: Cost Explorer can report costs grouped by activated cost allocation tags, but AWS billing does not automatically attribute costs to IAM users. This answer requires resources to have an activated user or department tag; without attribution metadata the question is underspecified.

choices.solution: Access the bill details from the billing dashboard and download the bill.
choices.explanation: The bill download is organized by billing dimensions and does not by itself attribute resource costs to individual users.

choices.solution: Modify a cost budget in AWS Budgets to alert with Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
choices.explanation: A budget alert monitors thresholds rather than producing a detailed historical cost report grouped by users.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand.

The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long-term commitment.

Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Dedicated Instances only
choices.explanation: Dedicated tenancy adds cost without a requirement for isolated hardware.

choices.solution: On-Demand Instances only
choices.explanation: All On-Demand capacity misses the Spot savings available for part of an elastic fleet.

choices.solution: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
choices.explanation:
On-Demand Instances: These instances are charged per hour or per second of usage, without any upfront payment or long-term commitment. While they offer flexibility, they are usually more expensive compared to other purchasing options.

Spot Instances: These are spare compute capacity in the AWS cloud available at a lower price compared to On-Demand Instances. However, they can be terminated by AWS with little notice if the capacity is needed elsewhere.

Spot Instances are suitable for workloads that are fault-tolerant and can handle interruptions.

choices.solution: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: Reserved Instances require the long-term commitment the company wants to avoid.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS.

The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
choices.explanation: Snowball is a temporary offline migration device, not a permanent automatically synchronized backup gateway.

choices.solution: Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on- premises systems with local access to the data.
choices.explanation: Snowball Edge provides temporary local device access but not the ongoing managed backup relationship after the device is returned.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally.

Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
choices.explanation: Cached volumes keep only a subset locally; the requirement is to maintain the complete primary dataset on premises.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage.

Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
choices.explanation: Stored Volume Gateway retains the complete dataset locally and uploads asynchronous EBS snapshot backups to AWS, preserving local access while automating cloud backup.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The application's database storage continues to grow over time.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Spot interruptions are unsuitable as the sole capacity for an uninterrupted legacy workload, and S3 is not a drop-in relational database.

choices.solution: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
choices.explanation: On-Demand database pricing misses reservation savings for a database used continuously.

choices.solution: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
choices.explanation:
Using Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances for the application layer provides cost savings compared to On-Demand Instances while ensuring availability for the 24/7 runtime. Migrating the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances provides a fully managed relational database service with automatic scaling capabilities.

Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and cost efficiency. Reserved Instances provide cost savings compared to On-Demand Instances over an extended period, making them suitable for applications with continuous operation.

Amazon Aurora, being a fully managed service, offloads much of the operational overhead associated with managing a traditional database, making it a cost-effective choice for growing database storage. =====================================================================================================

choices.solution: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.
choices.explanation: On-Demand application pricing misses reservation savings for the continuously running application tier.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data.

The solution must be fully managed.

Which AWS solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
choices.explanation: DataSync transfers files; it does not expose a mountable SMB filesystem.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance.

Connect the application server to the file share.
choices.explanation: A Windows server on EC2 requires patching, management, and availability configuration.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server.

Connect the application server to the file system.
choices.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed file storage service that is compatible with the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol, making it suitable for use with SMB clients, including Windows-based systems. With Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, you can create a file system that can be mounted on application servers, providing shared storage for the gaming application.

Amazon FSx for Windows File Server handles the management aspects such as server provisioning, maintenance, and backups, making it a fully managed solution.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket.

Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.
choices.explanation: S3 exposes object APIs rather than a native SMB share that the clients can mount.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises.

The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally.

Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Amazon S3 File Gateway
choices.explanation: File Gateway presents NFS or SMB, not the required iSCSI block volumes.

choices.solution: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
choices.explanation: Tape Gateway supplies a virtual tape library, not online iSCSI primary storage.

choices.solution: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
choices.explanation: Stored volumes keep the full dataset locally rather than only recently accessed data.

choices.solution: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes
choices.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway provides a hybrid cloud storage service that enables on-premises applications to use cloud storage seamlessly. Volume Gateway offers two modes: cached volumes and stored volumes.

In the cached volumes mode, the entire dataset is stored in Amazon S3, and the most frequently accessed data is cached on-premises. This allows the company to keep recently accessed data locally, minimizing the need for on-premises scaling.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days.

The company's finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts. The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS.

The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs.

Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.
choices.explanation: The selected reservation analysis should use consolidated billing to account for pooled usage and reservation benefits, rather than examining one account in isolation.

choices.solution: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.
choices.explanation: Use the payer account to obtain organization-wide RDS reservation purchase recommendations based on consolidated usage.

choices.solution: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
choices.explanation: The RDS reservation purchase recommendation check identifies potential savings for sustained On-Demand database usage; an idle-instance check addresses a different issue.

choices.solution: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
choices.explanation: Idle-instance recommendations target little-used databases, not the active high-performance instances described.

choices.solution: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.
choices.explanation: Redshift Reserved Node Optimization applies to Redshift, not RDS for Oracle.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
An image hosting company uploads its large assets to Amazon S3 Standard buckets. The company uses multipart upload in parallel by using S3 APIs and overwrites if the same object is uploaded again.

For the first 30 days after upload, the objects will be accessed frequently. The objects will be used less frequently after 30 days, but the access patterns for each object will be inconsistent.

The company must optimize its S3 storage costs while maintaining high availability and resiliency of stored assets.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Move assets to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves eligible objects between access tiers as access changes, avoiding manual access-pattern predictions.

choices.solution: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up incomplete multipart uploads.
choices.explanation: A lifecycle AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule removes unused multipart parts that otherwise continue to incur storage charges.

choices.solution: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up expired object delete markers.
choices.explanation: Delete-marker cleanup helps versioned deletion bookkeeping, not the storage charged for incomplete multipart uploads.

choices.solution: Move assets to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Standard-IA has retrieval charges and does not automatically adapt to each object's inconsistent future access pattern.

choices.solution: Move assets to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA reduces AZ resilience, contrary to the requirement for highly resilient core assets.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has an aging network-attached storage (NAS) array in its data center. The NAS array presents SMB shares and NFS shares to client workstations.

The company does not want to purchase a new NAS array. The company also does not want to incur the cost of renewing the NAS array's support contract.

Some of the data is accessed frequently, but much of the data is inactive. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that migrates the data to Amazon S3, uses S3 Lifecycle policies, and maintains the same look and feel for the client workstations.

The solutions architect has identified AWS Storage Gateway as part of the solution.

Which type of storage gateway should the solutions architect provision to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Volume Gateway
choices.explanation: Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block storage rather than the clients' existing NFS and SMB shares backed by S3 objects.

choices.solution: Tape Gateway
choices.explanation: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library, not a live NAS filesystem interface.

choices.solution: Amazon FSx File Gateway
choices.explanation: FSx File Gateway caches an FSx filesystem rather than migrating the repository into S3 with S3 Lifecycle policies.

choices.solution: Amazon S3 File Gateway
choices.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway provides on-premises applications with access to virtually unlimited cloud storage using NFS and SMB file interfaces. It seamlessly moves frequently accessed data to a low-latency cache while storing colder data in Amazon S3, using S3 Lifecycle policies to transition data between storage classes over tim

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has an application that is running on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect has standardized the company on a particular instance family and various instance sizes based on the current needs of the company.

The company wants to maximize cost savings for the application over the next 3 years. The company needs to be able to change the instance family and sizes in the next 6 months based on application popularity and usage.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Compute Savings Plan
choices.explanation:
Compute Savings Plans provide significant cost savings over On-Demand pricing in exchange for a commitment to a consistent amount of compute usage (measured in $/hr) for a 1 or 3 year period. They offer flexibility by allowing you to switch between instance families, sizes, and AZs (Availability Zones) while still benefiting from the savings plan pricing.

This aligns well with the company's requirement to change instance family and sizes based on application needs.

choices.solution: EC2 Instance Savings Plan
choices.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans bind the discount to a selected family and Region, so a later family change loses that flexibility.

choices.solution: Zonal Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: Zonal reservations constrain capacity to a specific AZ and instance configuration rather than permitting the planned family changes.

choices.solution: Standard Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: Standard reservations do not provide Compute Savings Plans' flexibility across instance families.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company collects data from a large number of participants who use wearable devices. The company stores the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table and uses applications to analyze the data.

The data workload is constant and predictable. The company wants to stay at or below its forecasted budget for DynamoDB.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use provisioned mode and DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA). Reserve capacity for the forecasted workload.
choices.explanation: Standard-IA increases per-request charges and targets storage-heavy, infrequently accessed tables, which is not established for this constant analysis workload.

choices.solution: Use provisioned mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs).
choices.explanation:
In provisioned mode, you provision a specific amount of read and write capacity, which allows you to manage costs more effectively based on your expected workload. This approach is suitable when your workload is predictable, as you can provision the capacity to meet your known requirements.

DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (Option A) is designed for cost savings on long-term storage and retrieval of infrequently accessed data, and it might not be the best fit for a constant and predictable workload.

choices.solution: Use on-demand mode. Set the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) high enough to accommodate changes in the workload.
choices.explanation: On-demand capacity does not use configured RCUs and WCUs as proposed; predictable traffic is more economical with provisioned capacity.

choices.solution: Use on-demand mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) with reserved capacity.
choices.explanation: Reserved capacity applies to provisioned mode, not on-demand billing.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company hosts a serverless application on AWS. The application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database.

The company notices an increase in application errors that result from database connection timeouts during times of peak traffic or unpredictable traffic. The company needs a solution that reduces the application failures with the least amount of change to the code.

What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Reduce the Lambda concurrency rate.
choices.explanation: Reducing concurrency can throttle legitimate requests rather than efficiently sharing database connections.

choices.solution: Enable RDS Proxy on the RDS DB instance.
choices.explanation: RDS Proxy is a fully managed, highly available database proxy that can handle database connections for serverless and highly scalable applications. It helps manage database connections efficiently, reducing issues related to connection timeouts and errors.

choices.solution: Resize the RDS DB instance class to accept more connections.
choices.explanation: A larger instance increases ongoing cost without pooling the burst of short-lived Lambda connections.

choices.solution: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand scaling.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB requires changing the data model and application instead of adding a proxy to the existing database.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company stores its data objects in Amazon S3 Standard storage. A solutions architect has found that 75% of the data is rarely accessed after 30 days.

The company needs all the data to remain immediately accessible with the same high availability and resiliency, but the company wants to minimize storage costs.

Which storage solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Move the data objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Deep Archive requires restoration before reads, violating immediate accessibility.

choices.solution: Move the data objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
choices.explanation: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA): This storage class is designed for infrequently accessed data but still provides low-latency and high-throughput performance. It maintains the same high availability and durability as S3 Standard, making it suitable for data that is accessed less frequently.

choices.solution: Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ and reduces resilience compared with Standard.

choices.solution: Move the data objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA reduces AZ resilience and incurs retrieval costs even during the initial frequent-access period.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company hosts a multiplayer gaming application on AWS. The company wants the application to read data with sub-millisecond latency and run one-time queries on historical data.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use Amazon RDS for data that is frequently accessed. Run a periodic custom script to export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: RDS alone does not supply sub-millisecond cached reads, and a custom export script adds maintenance.

choices.solution:
Store the data directly in an Amazon S3 bucket. Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy to move older data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long- term storage.

Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
choices.explanation: S3 is not a sub-millisecond operational database, and Deep Archive objects must be restored before Athena can query them.

choices.solution:
Use Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for data that is frequently accessed. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using DynamoDB table export.

Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
choices.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX): DynamoDB is a highly scalable and low-latency NoSQL database, suitable for frequently accessed data. DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a caching layer that provides sub-millisecond read latencies for DynamoDB.

Export Data to Amazon S3: Use DynamoDB table export to periodically export historical data to an Amazon S3 bucket. This allows you to store historical data in a cost-effective manner while still benefiting from DynamoDB for frequently accessed data.

Amazon Athena for One-time Queries: Amazon Athena allows you to run SQL queries directly on data stored in Amazon S3. By using Athena, you can perform one-time queries on the historical data without the need to manage a separate database.

choices.solution:
Use Amazon DynamoDB for data that is frequently accessed. Turn on streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams.

Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read the data from Kinesis Data Streams. Store the records in an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB without DAX does not supply the requested sub-millisecond read cache, and this option omits a historical SQL query engine.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has an application that collects data from IoT sensors on automobiles. The data is streamed and stored in Amazon S3 through Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.

The data produces trillions of S3 objects each year. Each morning, the company uses the data from the previous 30 days to retrain a suite of machine learning (ML) models.

Four times each year, the company uses the data from the previous 12 months to perform analysis and train other ML models. The data must be available with minimal delay for up to 1 year.

After 1 year, the data must be retained for archival purposes.

Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
choices.explanation: Monitoring trillions of objects incurs Intelligent-Tiering per-object charges when the access timeline is already predictable.

choices.solution: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
choices.explanation: Per-object monitoring adds cost, and Intelligent-Tiering's optional archive tiers can archive by inactivity before the required immediate-access year ends.

choices.solution: Use the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
choices.explanation: Immediate Standard-IA placement incurs retrieval charges during the first month of daily model-training reads.

choices.solution: Use the S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days, and then to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
choices.explanation:
S3 Standard Storage Class: Use S3 Standard for the first 30 days because it's the default storage class for frequently accessed data. This is suitable for the initial period when you need quick and frequent access to your data.

S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) Storage Class: After the initial 30 days, transition the data to S3 Standard-IA. S3 Standard-IA is designed for data that is accessed less frequently but still requires quick retrieval when needed.

It's more cost-effective for data that is accessed less often compared to S3 Standard. S3 Glacier Deep Archive: After 1 year, transition the data from S3 Standard-IA to S3 Glacier Deep Archive using an S3 Lifecycle policy.

S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the most cost-effective option for long-term archival storage. This is suitable for storing data that you need to retain for compliance or archival purposes but don't need to access frequently.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is planning to migrate a commercial off-the-shelf application from its on-premises data center to AWS. The software has a software licensing model using sockets and cores with predictable capacity and uptime requirements.

The company wants to use its existing licenses, which were purchased earlier this year.

Which Amazon EC2 pricing option is the MOST cost-effective?

choices.solution: Dedicated Reserved Hosts
choices.explanation:
A Dedicated Host is a physical server with EC2 instance capacity fully dedicated to your use. When you launch instances on a Dedicated Host, those instances run on the dedicated hardware of that host.

Dedicated Hosts provide control over the placement of instances for compliance, licensing, or regulatory requirements. You can purchase Dedicated Hosts on a reservation model (Reserved Hosts) or pay for them on-demand.

The host remains dedicated to you for the specified term in the case of Reserved Hosts. Dedicated Hosts can be useful for workloads with specific licensing models tied to physical sockets or cores.

choices.solution: Dedicated On-Demand Hosts
choices.explanation: On-Demand Dedicated Hosts cost more than host reservations for predictable continuous usage.

choices.solution: Dedicated Reserved Instances
choices.explanation: Dedicated Instances do not provide the same host/socket/core visibility and placement control needed for this licensing model.

choices.solution: Dedicated On-Demand Instances
choices.explanation: Dedicated Instances lack explicit host-level licensing control, and On-Demand pricing misses predictable-usage reservation savings.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 Linux instances across multiple Availability Zones. The application needs a storage layer that is highly available and Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX)-compliant.

The storage layer must provide maximum data durability and must be shareable across the EC2 instances. The data in the storage layer will be accessed frequently for the first 30 days and will be accessed infrequently after that time.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Glacier.
choices.explanation: S3 exposes object APIs rather than a POSIX filesystem, and Glacier archival access requires restoration.

choices.solution: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
choices.explanation: S3 Standard-IA remains object storage rather than the shared POSIX filesystem required by the application.

choices.solution: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS Standard-Infrequent Access (EFS Standard-IA).
choices.explanation:
Amazon EFS provides scalable and highly available file storage in the cloud. The Standard storage class is designed for frequently accessed data, making it suitable for the initial 30 days of frequent access.

You can create a lifecycle management policy for EFS that automatically transitions infrequently accessed files to the EFS Standard-Infrequent Access (EFS Standard-IA) storage class. This helps optimize costs by moving less frequently accessed data to a lower-cost storage tier.

choices.solution: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS One Zone-Infrequent Access (EFS One Zone-IA).
choices.explanation: One Zone EFS places data in one AZ and reduces resilience compared with the required regional filesystem.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use Lustre clients to access data.

The solution must be fully managed.

Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.solution: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
choices.explanation: DataSync copies files but does not expose a managed mountable Lustre filesystem.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol.

Connect the application server to the file share.
choices.explanation: File Gateway supports NFS/SMB file shares, not the Lustre client protocol.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server.

Connect the application server to the file system.
choices.explanation: EFS uses NFS and cannot be configured as a Lustre server.

choices.solution:
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server.

Connect the application server to the file system.
choices.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed service that provides high-performance shared storage. It is specifically designed to be used with Lustre, making it a suitable solution for Lustre clients.

Fully Managed: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed service, meaning that AWS takes care of maintenance, updates, and other operational tasks, reducing the management overhead for the company.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has a business system that generates hundreds of reports each day. The business system saves the reports to a network share in CSV format.

The company needs to store this data in the AWS Cloud in near-real time for analysis.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create a scheduled task that runs at the end of each day.
choices.explanation: A daily transfer waits until day-end rather than making new reports available in near-real time.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Update the business system to use a new network share from the S3 File Gateway.
choices.explanation: the business system already writes CSVs to a network share. S3 File Gateway exposes an SMB/NFS share, but files written there are asynchronously uploaded into S3, so the application can keep behaving like it is writing to a normal file share.

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create an application that uses the DataSync API in the automation workflow.
choices.explanation: A custom DataSync automation application adds development and administration work.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint. Create a script that checks for new files on the network share and uploads the new files by using SFTP.
choices.explanation: A polling script and SFTP uploads add custom transfer maintenance compared with writing directly to a File Gateway share.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is storing petabytes of data in Amazon S3 Standard. The data is stored in multiple S3 buckets and is accessed with varying frequency.

The company does not know access patterns for all the data. The company needs to implement a solution for each S3 bucket to optimize the cost of S3 usage.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

choices.solution: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
choices.explanation:
S3 Intelligent-Tiering: This storage class is designed to automatically and dynamically move objects between two access tiers - frequent and infrequent access - based on changing access patterns. It is a good fit for data with unknown or changing access patterns.

It provides cost savings compared to S3 Standard while maintaining low-latency access to frequently accessed objects.

choices.solution: Use the S3 storage class analysis tool to determine the correct tier for each object in the S3 bucket. Move each object to the identified storage tier.
choices.explanation: Analyzing and manually moving objects adds management work when Intelligent-Tiering adapts automatically.

choices.solution: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
choices.explanation: A fixed archival-class choice incurs retrieval charges and does not adapt to unknown access patterns.

choices.solution: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone- IA).
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA reduces AZ resilience and does not adapt when frequently accessed data changes.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is running a custom application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. The application has frontend nodes that need to run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and backend nodes that need to run only for a short time based on workload.

The number of backend nodes varies during the day. The company needs to scale out and scale in more instances based on workload.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
choices.explanation: Fargate requires containerization and does not supply the same EC2 Spot pricing for the existing short-lived backend nodes.

choices.solution: Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Spot Instances for the backend nodes.
choices.explanation:
Reserved Instances (RIs) for Frontend Nodes: Since the frontend nodes need to run 24/7, Reserved Instances provide a significant cost savings compared to On-Demand pricing. RIs are a commitment to a consistent usage pattern, making them suitable for instances that need to run continuously.

Spot Instances for Backend Nodes: Spot Instances are a cost-effective option for workloads that can be interrupted or are flexible regarding availability. As the number of backend nodes varies during the day, using Spot Instances allows you to take advantage of spare capacity at a lower cost.

Spot Instances are suitable for short-lived, scalable, and flexible workloads.

choices.solution: Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Reserved Instances for the backend nodes.
choices.explanation: Spot can interrupt the continuously required front end, while reservations are inefficient for short-lived variable backend capacity.

choices.solution: Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
choices.explanation: Spot is unsuitable as the sole guaranteed front-end baseline, and Fargate requires changing the backend deployment.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to store data from its healthcare application. The application's data frequently changes.

A new regulation requires audit access at all levels of the stored data. The company hosts the application on an on-premises infrastructure that is running out of storage capacity.

A solutions architect must securely migrate the existing data to AWS while satisfying the new regulation.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
choices.explanation: Explanation: CloudTrail management events don't capture object-level (data) access, so they can't satisfy "audit access at all levels of the stored data." CloudTrail data events, which log individual object-level API activity on the S3 bucket, are needed instead.

choices.solution: Use AWS Snowcone to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.
choices.explanation: Management events do not audit individual S3 object reads and writes, so this misses the required data-level access trail.

choices.solution: Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
choices.explanation: Transfer Acceleration can speed object uploads but lacks DataSync's managed dataset transfer, verification, and incremental synchronization workflow.

choices.solution: Use AWS Storage Gateway to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail management events omit object-level data access, regardless of how the files reach S3.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A manufacturing company has machine sensors that upload .csv files to an Amazon S3 bucket. These .csv files must be converted into images and must be made available as soon as possible for the automatic generation of graphical reports.

The images become irrelevant after 1 month, but the .csv files must be kept to train machine learning (ML) models twice a year. The ML trainings and audits are planned weeks in advance.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Launch an Amazon EC2 Spot Instance that downloads the .csv files every hour, generates the image files, and uploads the images to the S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Hourly polling delays images and requires maintaining a worker instead of reacting immediately to each upload.

choices.solution: Design an AWS Lambda function that converts the .csv files into images and stores the images in the S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function when a .csv file is uploaded.
choices.explanation: S3 object-created notifications invoke Lambda to convert each uploaded CSV into an image without waiting for a polling schedule.

choices.solution:
Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 1 day after they are uploaded.

Expire the image files after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Use prefix or tag filters to archive the CSV files and expire images after 30 days. Glacier Flexible Retrieval is suitable when training and audits are planned ahead.

choices.solution:
Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded.

Expire the image files after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle transitions into One Zone-IA require objects to be at least 30 days old, so the proposed one-day transition is invalid.

choices.solution:
Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded.

Keep the image files in Reduced Redundancy Storage (RRS).
choices.explanation: Standard-IA transitions require a 30-day object age, and retaining images in RRS misses the requested inexpensive expiration after one month.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company that uses AWS is building an application to transfer data to a product manufacturer. The company has its own identity provider (IdP).

The company wants the IdP to authenticate application users while the users use the application to transfer data. The company must use Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) protocol.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
choices.explanation: DataSync does not provide the required AS2 business-to-business transfer protocol.

choices.solution: Use Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task for IdP authentication.
choices.explanation: AppFlow integrates SaaS data flows but does not supply an AS2 endpoint.

choices.solution: Authenticate application users with the company's existing IdP. Use AWS Transfer Family AS2 servers or connectors with trading-partner profiles and certificates for the data transfer.
choices.explanation:
Transfer Family provides managed AS2 exchange. The application handles end-user IdP authentication separately; an AS2 server does not support a Lambda custom identity provider like an SFTP server.

AS2 certificates and trading-partner agreements secure the transfer.

choices.solution: Use AWS Storage Gateway to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool for IdP authentication.
choices.explanation: Storage Gateway presents storage interfaces, not AS2 transfers or the proposed application IdP integration.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
