A solutions architect is designing a RESTAPI in Amazon API Gateway for a cash payback service. The application requires 1 GB of memory and 2 GB of storage for its computation resources.

The application will require that the data is in a relational format.

Which additional combination ofAWS services will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Amazon EC2
choices.explanation: EC2 requires server provisioning, patching, and capacity management.

choices.solution: AWS Lambda
choices.explanation: Lambda runs the API business logic without provisioning or patching application servers.

choices.solution: Amazon RDS
choices.explanation: RDS provides a managed relational database, reducing database infrastructure administration.

choices.solution: Amazon DynamoDB
choices.explanation: DynamoDB is a non-relational database and does not meet the relational-format requirement.

choices.solution: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Services (Amazon EKS)
choices.explanation: An EKS cluster introduces Kubernetes platform management unnecessary for this small API compute workload.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS Organizations to run workloads within multiple AWS accounts. A tagging policy adds department tags to AWS resources when the company creates tags.

An accounting team needs to determine spending on Amazon EC2 consumption. The accounting team must determine which departments are responsible for the costs regardless ofAWS account.

The accounting team has access to AWS Cost Explorer for all AWS accounts within the organization and needs to access all reports from Cost Explorer.

Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.solution: From the Organizations management account billing console, activate a user-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.
choices.explanation: While AWS provides AWS-defined tags, the use of a user-defined tag provides flexibility in terms of naming and tagging conventions. Activating the tag at the Organizations management account level ensures that the tag is applied to resources across all member accounts.

choices.solution: From the Organizations management account billing console, activate an AWS-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.
choices.explanation: department is a company-defined tag, not an AWS-generated cost-allocation tag.

choices.solution: From the Organizations member account billing console, activate a user-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by the tag name, and filter by EC2.
choices.explanation: Organization-wide cost allocation tags are activated through the management account, not separately through this member account.

choices.solution: From the Organizations member account billing console, activate an AWS-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.
choices.explanation: The tag is user-defined, and a member-account report does not provide centralized organization-wide activation and reporting.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company stores raw collected data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is used for several types of analytics on behalf of the company's customers.

The type of analytics requested determines the access pattern on the S3 objects. The company cannot predict or control the access pattern.

The company wants to reduce its S3 costs.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use S3 replication to transition infrequently accessed objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
choices.explanation: Replication creates object copies; it does not automatically tier the originals according to access patterns.

choices.solution: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
choices.explanation: A fixed Standard-IA transition cannot adapt to unpredictable access and can incur retrieval charges when data becomes hot again.

choices.solution: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
choices.explanation:
S3 Intelligent-Tiering is designed to optimize costs by automatically moving objects between two access tiers: frequent and infrequent access. It is well-suited for scenarios where access patterns are unpredictable.

Using S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering allows you to take advantage of automatic cost savings based on actual access patterns without the need for manual adjustments.

choices.solution: Use S3 Inventory to identify and transition objects that have not been accessed from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
choices.explanation: Inventory lists objects and metadata; it does not track last-access patterns or transition objects by itself.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company wants to migrate 100 GB of historical data from an on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has a 100 megabits per second (Mbps) internet connection on premises.

The company needs to encrypt the data in transit to the S3 bucket. The company will store new data directly in Amazon S3.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use the s3 sync command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket
choices.explanation: For this one-time 100-GB transfer, the AWS CLI s3 sync command uses HTTPS and the existing internet connection without deploying a transfer agent or VPN. Future data is already written directly into S3, so ongoing synchronization infrastructure is unnecessary.

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the on-premises location to an S3 bucket
choices.explanation: DataSync supports secure verified transfers, but deploying its agent and configuring locations and a task adds overhead for this small one-time migration. CLI HTTPS transfer meets the stated requirements more simply.

choices.solution: Use AWS Snowball to move the data to an S3 bucket
choices.explanation: An offline device adds shipping and handling overhead for a dataset small enough to transfer over the existing link.

choices.solution: Set up an IPsec VPN from the on-premises location to AWS. Use the s3 cp command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket
choices.explanation: A VPN adds networking setup when AWS CLI HTTPS or DataSync already encrypts data in transit.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is looking for a solution that can store video archives in AWS from old news footage. The company needs to minimize costs and will rarely need to restore these files.

When the files are needed, they must be available in a maximum of five minutes.

What is the MOST cost-effective solution?

choices.solution: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and use Expedited retrievals with provisioned retrieval capacity.
choices.explanation:
For the archive retrieval tiers in these choices, Glacier Flexible Retrieval Expedited retrievals typically take 1-5 minutes for objects smaller than 250 MB. Provisioned retrieval capacity makes expedited capacity available predictably.

The question must assume appropriately sized archives; five minutes is not a universal completion guarantee for large videos. Glacier Standard retrievals take hours.

S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is a current alternative with millisecond access but is absent from these choices.

choices.solution: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier and use Standard retrievals.
choices.explanation: Standard Glacier Flexible Retrieval restores typically take hours, exceeding the five-minute maximum.

choices.solution: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
choices.explanation: Standard-IA provides immediate access but has higher storage cost for rarely restored archives.

choices.solution: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA).
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA has higher archive storage cost and lower AZ resilience than the selected Glacier storage.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company uses on-premises servers to host its applications. The company is running out of storage capacity.

The applications use both block storage and NFS storage. The company needs a high-performing solution that supports local caching without re-architecting its existing applications.

Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Mount Amazon S3 as a file system to the on-premises servers.
choices.explanation: S3 is object storage and does not directly provide the applications' existing local cached NFS interface.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to replace NFS storage.
choices.explanation: S3 File Gateway exposes NFS or SMB file shares backed by S3 with a local cache.

choices.solution: Deploy AWS Snowball Edge to provision NFS mounts to on-premises servers.
choices.explanation: Snowball Edge is a transfer/edge device rather than the long-term managed gateway for this hybrid storage architecture.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replace the block storage.
choices.explanation: Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes and stores managed backups in AWS.

choices.solution: Deploy Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volumes and mount them to on-premises servers.
choices.explanation: EFS access over the network does not provide local caching or solve the block-storage requirement.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has Amazon EC2 instances that run nightly batch jobs to process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that uses On- Demand billing.

If a job fails on one instance, another instance will reprocess the job. The batch jobs run between 12:00 AM and 06:00 AM local time every day.

Which solution will provide EC2 instances to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
choices.explanation: A continuously billed commitment is inefficient for six hours of daily interruption-tolerant work compared with Spot capacity.

choices.solution: Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
choices.explanation: A reservation commits to instance usage beyond this short nightly window and misses available Spot savings.

choices.solution:
Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances.

Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
choices.explanation:
Spot Instances: Spot Instances allow you to bid for unused EC2 capacity at a potentially lower cost than On-Demand pricing. This can result in significant cost savings for batch jobs that are fault-tolerant and can be interrupted or retried.

Scaling Policy: Setting a policy to scale out based on CPU usage ensures that additional Spot Instances are launched when the demand for processing power increases during batch job execution. This helps in handling varying workloads efficiently.

choices.solution:
Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Increase the instance size.

Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
choices.explanation: Increasing instance size keeps On-Demand pricing and does not exploit the job's retry tolerance.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A social media company is building a feature for its website. The feature will give users the ability to upload photos.

The company expects significant increases in demand during large events and must ensure that the website can handle the upload traffic from users.

Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST scalability?

choices.solution: Upload files from the user's browser to the application servers. Transfer the files to an Amazon S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Proxying uploads through application servers creates a bandwidth and compute bottleneck.

choices.solution: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file gateway.
choices.explanation: File Gateway supplies NFS/SMB interfaces, not a public browser upload endpoint.

choices.solution: Generate Amazon S3 presigned URLs in the application. Upload files directly from the user's browser into an S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Amazon S3 Presigned URLs: This approach allows the client (user's browser) to directly upload files to Amazon S3 using a presigned URL generated by the server. This offloads the file transfer process from the application servers and enables a direct upload to S3 from the client side.

choices.solution: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file system.
choices.explanation: Browsers cannot directly upload over the EFS NFS protocol; an application intermediary would still be required.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company needs to configure multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers.

On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database
choices.explanation: A dedicated Aurora cluster adds storage and compute cost for an environment used only a few hours daily.

choices.solution: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances
choices.explanation: Explanation: Since each environment is only used for half of the workday, a standard RDS for PostgreSQL instance that gets stopped when not in use is cheaper than running Aurora continuously - Aurora costs more than standard RDS and this workload doesn't need Aurora's extra performance/availability features.

choices.solution: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database
choices.explanation: On-Demand Aurora still requires a provisioned cluster; Single-AZ RDS is sufficient for these nonproduction databases.

choices.solution: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select
choices.explanation: S3 Select does not host a PostgreSQL database or support the developers' PostgreSQL schema.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company is designing a new web application that will run on Amazon EC2 Instances. The application will use Amazon DynamoDB for backend data storage.

The application traffic will be unpredictable. The company expects that the application read and write throughput to the database will be moderate to high.

The company needs to scale in response to application traffic.

Which DynamoDB table configuration will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
choices.explanation: Provisioned autoscaling reacts after demand changes and remains bounded by the chosen maximum, risking throttling during unpredictable surges.

choices.solution: Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard table class.
choices.explanation:
On-demand capacity mode allows DynamoDB to automatically scale read and write capacity based on actual application traffic. It eliminates the need for manual provisioning of read and write capacity, making it well-suited for unpredictable workloads.

DynamoDB Standard Table Class: The DynamoDB Standard table class provides general-purpose storage with consistent, single-digit millisecond latency. It's suitable for a wide range of applications, including those with unpredictable traffic

choices.solution: Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
choices.explanation: Standard-IA has higher read/write request pricing and provisioned scaling limits for this moderate-to-high access workload.

choices.solution: Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class.
choices.explanation: Standard-IA trades cheaper storage for higher request charges and is unsuitable for the stated high access rate.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company wants to add its existing AWS usage cost to its operation cost dashboard. A solutions architect needs to recommend a solution that will give the company access to its usage cost programmatically.

The company must be able to access cost data for the current year and forecast costs for the next 12 months.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Access usage cost-related data by using the AWS Cost Explorer API with pagination.
choices.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer is a tool provided by Amazon Web Services (AWS) that allows users to visualize, understand, and manage their AWS costs and usage.

choices.solution: Access usage cost-related data by using downloadable AWS Cost Explorer report .csv files.
choices.explanation: CSV downloads require report generation and ingestion instead of directly retrieving and forecasting costs through an API.

choices.solution: Configure AWS Budgets actions to send usage cost data to the company through FTP.
choices.explanation: Budgets actions do not provide the proposed FTP usage-data export or forecasting API.

choices.solution: Create AWS Budgets reports for usage cost data. Send the data to the company through SMTP.
choices.explanation: Email reports require parsing and do not provide the desired programmatic historical and forecast retrieval.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A data analytics company wants to migrate its batch processing system to AWS. The company receives thousands of small data files periodically during the day through FTP.

An on-premises batch job processes the data files overnight. However, the batch job takes hours to finish running.

The company wants the AWS solution to process incoming data files as soon as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients that send the files. The solution must delete the incoming data files after the files have been processed successfully.

Processing for each file needs to take 3-8 minutes.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

choices.solution:
Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch.

Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.
choices.explanation: Nightly processing violates immediate handling, and Glacier adds restore delays plus a self-managed FTP server.

choices.solution:
Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch.

Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.
choices.explanation: The workflow still waits for nightly processing and retains an EC2 FTP server to maintain.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch.

Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.
choices.explanation: Transfer Family does not use EBS as its managed backend, and S3 event notifications cannot arise from EBS file creation.

choices.solution:
Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed.

Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.
choices.explanation:
Transfer Family provides a managed FTP endpoint backed by S3. Object-created events invoke Lambda immediately; the stated 3-8 minute processing duration fits Lambda's 15-minute timeout.

Delete the input only after successful, idempotent processing.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company wants to build a logging solution for its multiple AWS accounts. The company currently stores the logs from all accounts in a centralized account.

The company has created an Amazon S3 bucket in the centralized account to store the VPC flow logs and AWS CloudTrail logs. All logs must be highly available for 30 days for frequent analysis, retained for an additional 60 days for backup purposes, and deleted 90 days after creation.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
choices.explanation: Keeping the logs at Standard pricing after day 30 misses savings during their infrequent-access period.

choices.solution:
Store logs in S3 Standard initially. Transition them to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and expire them after 90 days.

Do not transition them to Glacier at the same time they expire.
choices.explanation: Standard serves the first month's frequent analysis, then Standard-IA reduces storage cost for the next 60 days. Glacier Flexible Retrieval has a 90-day minimum storage duration, so a 60-day archive incurs early-deletion charges; a transition at expiration adds no useful retention.

choices.solution: Transition objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
choices.explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval has a 90-day minimum storage duration; deleting only 60 days after transition incurs early-deletion charges.

choices.solution:
Transition objects to the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class 30 days after creation. Move all objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class after 90 days.

Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA reduces resilience, and transitioning to Glacier on the same day as expiration incurs unnecessary operations and minimum-duration charges.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A recent analysis of a company's IT expenses highlights the need to reduce backup costs. The company's chief information officer wants to simplify the on-premises backup infrastructure and reduce costs by eliminating the use of physical backup tapes.

The company must preserve the existing investment in the on-premises backup applications and workflows.

What should a solutions architect recommend?

choices.solution: Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
choices.explanation: NFS changes the existing tape-backup interface instead of preserving the virtual tape library workflow.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
choices.explanation: EFS is a filesystem, not a virtual tape library compatible with the existing tape backup application.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the iSCSI interface.
choices.explanation: EFS does not expose an iSCSI interface.

choices.solution: Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface.
choices.explanation:
AWS Storage Gateway provides a hybrid cloud storage service that enables on-premises applications to seamlessly use cloud storage. The iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface of AWS Storage Gateway is designed to integrate with existing backup applications that use tape-based workflows.

It emulates a tape library, allowing you to store virtual tapes in Amazon S3 or Glacier, providing a cost-effective and scalable alternative to physical tapes.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has a financial application that produces reports. The reports average 50 KB in size and are stored in Amazon S3.

The reports are frequently accessed during the first week after production and must be stored for several years. The reports must be retrievable within 6 hours.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Use S3 Standard initially. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition reports to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days, explicitly allowing objects smaller than 128 KB.
choices.explanation:
Glacier Flexible Retrieval standard restores typically complete within 3-5 hours, while Deep Archive cannot meet a six-hour requirement. The 50 KB reports need an explicit lifecycle size-filter or transition-default override because current lifecycle defaults block transitions below 128 KB.

Assess per-object request and metadata overhead for small files.

choices.solution: Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 7 days.
choices.explanation: Standard-IA requires a 30-day object age for lifecycle transitions and bills these 50-KB objects at its 128-KB minimum size.

choices.solution: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to transition the reports to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) and S3 Glacier.
choices.explanation: Objects smaller than 128 KB are not automatically tiered by Intelligent-Tiering, and its tiers are not configurable Standard-IA transitions.

choices.solution: Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
choices.explanation: Deep Archive standard retrieval generally takes around 12 hours, exceeding the six-hour requirement.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company needs to optimize the cost of its Amazon EC2 instances. The company also needs to change the type and family of its EC2 instances every 2-3 months.

What should the company do to meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Purchase Partial Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term.
choices.explanation: Standard reservations lack the required freedom to change instance families regularly, and a three-year commitment is less flexible.

choices.solution: Purchase a No Upfront Compute Savings Plan for a 1-year term.
choices.explanation: A Compute Savings Plan provides flexibility across EC2 instance families, sizes, Regions, operating systems, and compute services while still providing a commitment discount. A 1-year No Upfront plan best matches the need to change instance type and family every few months.

choices.solution: Purchase All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 1-year term.
choices.explanation: An upfront Standard reservation still constrains the instance configuration rather than allowing repeated family changes.

choices.solution: Purchase an All Upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan for a 1-year term.
choices.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to a selected family and Region, even with an upfront payment.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company hosts multiple applications on AWS for different product lines. The applications use different compute resources, including Amazon EC2 instances and Application Load Balancers.

The applications run in different AWS accounts under the same organization in AWS Organizations across multiple AWS Regions. Teams for each product line have tagged each compute resource in the individual accounts.

The company wants more details about the cost for each product line from the consolidated billing feature in Organizations.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.solution: Select a specific AWS generated tag in the AWS Billing console.
choices.explanation: A product-line tag applied by the teams is user-defined, not AWS-generated.

choices.solution: Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Billing console.
choices.explanation: Choose the user-defined resource tag that identifies the product line for cost allocation.

choices.solution: Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Resource Groups console.
choices.explanation: Resource Groups organizes resources but does not activate the tag for billing cost allocation.

choices.solution: Activate the selected tag from each AWS account.
choices.explanation: The management account activates consolidated cost-allocation tags for organization reporting.

choices.solution: Activate the selected tag from the Organizations management account.
choices.explanation: Activate the tag in the Organizations management account so consolidated billing can attribute eligible resource costs by product line.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A financial services company launched a new application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses the application to track stock market trends.

The company needs to operate the application for only 2 hours at the end of each week. The company needs to optimize the cost of running the database.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL database cluster.
choices.explanation:
Use a compatible Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL engine version with minimum capacity set to zero ACUs and automatic pause/resume. The database scales for its short weekly workload and incurs no instance-capacity charges while paused; storage charges remain.

A nonzero minimum would continue incurring idle compute cost.

choices.solution: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora MySQL database cluster.
choices.explanation: Provisioned Aurora incurs idle compute charges unless explicitly stopped; compatible Serverless v2 auto-pause can reduce compute to zero between uses.

choices.solution: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs MySQL. Purchase an instance reservation for the EC2 instance.
choices.explanation: An EC2 reservation commits to usage despite the database running only two hours weekly and leaves database administration to the company.

choices.solution: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses MySQL container images to run tasks.
choices.explanation: Operating MySQL containers requires database persistence, backup, and availability management instead of a managed database.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs an application that uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The application receives traffic only on weekdays during business hours.

The company wants to optimize costs and reduce operational overhead based on this usage.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use the Instance Scheduler on AWS to configure start and stop schedules.
choices.explanation: Instance Scheduler: The AWS Instance Scheduler is a solution that allows you to schedule the start and stop times of your Amazon EC2 and RDS instances. By configuring start and stop schedules, you can ensure that resources are only running during the required business hours, thereby optimizing costs.

choices.solution: Turn off automatic backups. Create weekly manual snapshots of the database.
choices.explanation: Disabling backups risks data protection and does not remove idle database compute charges.

choices.solution: Create a custom AWS Lambda function to start and stop the database based on minimum CPU utilization.
choices.explanation: A custom CPU-based scheduler adds code and can misinterpret a temporary low-utilization interval; the usage timetable is already known.

choices.solution: Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances.
choices.explanation: An upfront reservation commits to usage outside business hours rather than removing unnecessary running time.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has 5 PB of archived data on physical tapes. The company needs to preserve the data on the tapes for another 10 years for compliance purposes.

The company wants to migrate to AWS in the next 6 months. The data center that stores the tapes has a 1 Gbps uplink internet connectivity.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? [Historical question: Tape Gateway on Snowball Edge is no longer available; the listed offline option cannot be deployed today.]

choices.solution:
Read the data from the tapes on premises. Stage the data in a local NFS storage.

Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
choices.explanation: Even an ideal 1-Gbps link needs substantially more than six months to transfer 5 PB.

choices.solution: Use an on-premises backup application to read the data from the tapes and to write directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation: Reading and uploading tapes through the existing 1-Gbps connection cannot meet the migration deadline.

choices.solution:
Order multiple AWS Snowball devices that have Tape Gateway. Copy the physical tapes to virtual tapes in Snowball.

Ship the Snowball devices to AWS. Create a lifecycle policy to move the tapes to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
choices.explanation:
This is the historical offline-transfer answer, but Tape Gateway on Snowball Edge was discontinued in March 2024. None of the listed choices currently solves the stated 5 PB migration in six months over a 1 Gbps link: transferring 5 PB continuously would take roughly 463 days before overhead.

Use a current physical-transfer service or increase network capacity.

choices.solution:
Configure an on-premises Tape Gateway. Create virtual tapes in the AWS Cloud.

Use backup software to copy the physical tape to the virtual tape.
choices.explanation: An online Tape Gateway still sends the dataset through the insufficient 1-Gbps uplink.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing a disaster recovery (DR) strategy to provide Amazon EC2 capacity in a failover AWS Region. Business requirements state that the DR strategy must meet capacity in the failover Region.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Purchase On-Demand Instances in the failover Region.
choices.explanation: Unreserved On-Demand capacity is subject to availability at failover time.

choices.solution: Purchase an EC2 Savings Plan in the failover Region.
choices.explanation: Savings Plans provide billing discounts but do not reserve physical capacity.

choices.solution: Purchase regional Reserved Instances in the failover Region.
choices.explanation: Regional Reserved Instances provide discounts without guaranteeing capacity in a selected failover AZ.

choices.solution: Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.
choices.explanation:
A Capacity Reservation allows you to reserve a specific amount of EC2 instance capacity in a given region without purchasing specific instances. This reserved capacity is dedicated to your account and can be utilized for launching instances when needed.

Capacity Reservations offer flexibility, allowing you to launch different instance types and sizes within the reserved capacity.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A research company uses on-premises devices to generate data for analysis. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to analyze the data.

The devices generate .csv files and support writing the data to an SMB file share. Company analysts must be able to use SQL commands to query the data.

The analysts will run queries periodically throughout the day.

Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon S3 File Gateway mode.
choices.explanation: S3 File Gateway exposes an on-premises file share backed by S3 for collecting the CSV files.

choices.solution: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon FSx File Gateway made.
choices.explanation: FSx File Gateway uses an FSx Windows backend rather than writing CSV objects into S3 for Athena queries.

choices.solution: Set up an AWS Glue crawler to create a table based on the data that is in Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: A Glue crawler discovers the CSV schema and creates Data Catalog tables.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon EMR cluster with EMR File System (EMRFS) to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
choices.explanation: An EMR cluster adds compute and management overhead for periodic SQL queries that Athena runs serverlessly.

choices.solution: Set up an Amazon Redshift cluster to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
choices.explanation: A Redshift cluster adds warehouse compute cost for occasional queries directly over the S3 dataset.

choices.solution: Setup Amazon Athena to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
choices.explanation: Athena queries the CSV data in S3 using the cataloged schema without provisioning database servers.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company will migrate 10 PB of data to Amazon S3 in 6 weeks. The current data center has a 500 Mbps uplink to the internet.

Other on-premises applications share the uplink. The company can use 80% of the internet bandwidth for this one-time migration task.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Configure AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 and to automatically verify the data.
choices.explanation: The usable 400-Mbps link cannot transfer 10 PB in six weeks, even with optimized managed transfers.

choices.solution: Use rsync to transfer the data directly to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: rsync does not directly target S3, and the network bandwidth remains far too low.

choices.solution: Use the AWS CLI and multiple copy processes to send the data directly to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation: Parallel copies cannot increase the total 400-Mbps bandwidth available for this enormous dataset.

choices.solution:
Order multiple AWS Snowball devices. Copy the data to the devices.

Send the devices to AWS to copy the data to Amazon S3.
choices.explanation:
With only a 500 Mbps uplink bandwidth shared among other on-premises applications, transferring 10 PB of data over the internet would be impractical and time-consuming. AWS Snowball provides a physical device that can be shipped to the company to facilitate faster initial data transfer.

Historical-service limitation: Snowball Edge is available only to eligible existing customers since November 7, 2025; new customers need a current physical-transfer or online-transfer alternative.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A solutions architect is designing an application that will allow business users to upload objects to Amazon S3. The solution needs to maximize object durability.

Objects also must be readily available at any time and for any length of time. Users will access objects frequently within the first 30 days after the objects are uploaded, but users are much less likely to access objects that are older than 30 days.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Glacier after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Glacier archival access requires restoration and does not keep objects immediately available.

choices.solution: Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Storing objects in S3 Standard ensures low-latency access and high durability. After 30 days, transitioning objects to S3 Standard-IA allows you to take advantage of a lower storage cost for objects that are less frequently accessed.

choices.solution: Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA reduces resilience to an AZ loss, contrary to maximum durability for these objects.

choices.solution: Store all the objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
choices.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring fees before a fixed 30-day transition when the access pattern is already known.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company stores a large volume of image files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The images need to be readily available for the first 180 days.

The images are infrequently accessed for the next 180 days. After 360 days, the images need to be archived but must be available instantly upon request.

After 5 years, only auditors can access the images. The auditors must be able to retrieve the images within 12 hours.

The images cannot be lost during this process. A developer will use S3 Standard storage for the first 180 days.

The developer needs to configure an S3 Lifecycle rule.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA can lose data if its AZ is destroyed, violating the requirement that the images not be lost.

choices.solution: Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA reduces resilience, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval does not provide instant access after day 360.

choices.solution: Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
choices.explanation: S3 Standard-IA keeps multi-AZ durability for the infrequently accessed period. Glacier Instant Retrieval meets the instant-access requirement after 360 days, and Deep Archive is the lowest-cost tier that still supports retrieval within 12 hours for long-term audit data.

choices.solution: Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
choices.explanation: Glacier Flexible Retrieval requires restoration, violating instant availability during years one through five.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company has a large data workload that runs for 6 hours each day. The company cannot lose any data while the process is running.

A solutions architect is designing an Amazon EMR cluster configuration to support this critical data workload.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: A long-running cluster incurs instance costs during the 18 hours each day when the workload is idle.

choices.solution: Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: A transient EMR cluster avoids paying for idle capacity between six-hour daily runs. Keep primary and core nodes on On-Demand instances so data is not lost, and use Spot only for replaceable task nodes.

choices.solution: Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance and the core nodes and task nodes on Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: Core nodes store HDFS data; Spot interruption of core capacity creates data-availability and loss risk.

choices.solution: Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance, the core nodes on Spot Instances, and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
choices.explanation: The cluster remains billed while idle, and interruptible core nodes expose its stored data to failure risk.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs a website that stores images of historical events. Website users need the ability to search and view images based on the year that the event in the image occurred.

On average, users request each image only once or twice a year. The company wants a highly available solution to store and deliver the images to users.

Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

choices.solution: Store images in Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: EBS plus an EC2 web server adds provisioned storage, compute, and maintenance costs for rarely accessed images.

choices.solution: Store images in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
choices.explanation: EFS and an EC2 server add filesystem and compute costs unnecessary for simple image objects.

choices.solution: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard. Use S3 Standard to directly deliver images by using a static website.
choices.explanation: Standard has a higher storage rate than Standard-IA when images are requested only once or twice annually.

choices.solution: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use S3 Standard-IA to directly deliver images by using a static website.
choices.explanation: S3 Standard-IA is highly available and cost-effective for objects read only once or twice per year. EBS/EFS require servers or file-system capacity, and S3 Standard costs more for infrequent access.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company uses AWS Cost Explorer to monitor its AWS costs. The company notices that Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage and snapshot costs increase every month.

However, the company does not purchase additional EBS storage every month. The company wants to optimize monthly costs for its current storage usage.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution: Use logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs to monitor the storage utilization of Amazon EBS. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: EBS Elastic Volumes cannot shrink existing volumes, and storage utilization does not explain accumulating snapshot retention.

choices.solution: Use a custom script to monitor space usage. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
choices.explanation: Custom monitoring adds work, and EBS volume size cannot be reduced in place.

choices.solution: Delete all expired and unused snapshots to reduce snapshot costs.
choices.explanation: One-time deletion reduces current cost but does not automate retention to prevent continued snapshot accumulation.

choices.solution: Delete all nonessential snapshots. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create and manage the snapshots according to the company's snapshot policy requirements.
choices.explanation: Delete nonessential snapshots and use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to automate snapshot creation and retention. EBS volumes cannot simply be shrunk with Elastic Volumes, and manual cleanup has more operational overhead.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company performs tests on an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table. The tests run for 4 hours once a week.

The company knows how many read and write operations the application performs to the table each second during the tests. The company does not currently use DynamoDB for any other use case.

A solutions architect needs to optimize the costs for the table.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Choose on-demand mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
choices.explanation: On-demand mode does not accept provisioned RCU/WCU settings; known throughput can be scheduled in provisioned mode for the test window.

choices.solution: Choose provisioned mode. Update the read and write capacity units appropriately.
choices.explanation:
Provisioned capacity fits the known request rate. Schedule capacity increases before each weekly test and reduce capacity to the supported minimum afterward.

Year-long reserved capacity is poorly utilized by a workload running only four hours per week; compare actual on-demand prices for the workload.

choices.solution: Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 1-year term.
choices.explanation: A one-year reservation commits to capacity far beyond four hours of weekly testing.

choices.solution: Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for a 3-year term.
choices.explanation: A three-year capacity commitment is even less suited to the infrequent test schedule.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company performs periodic financial assessments of its AWS costs.

The company recently identified unusual spending. The company needs a solution to prevent unusual spending.

The solution must monitor costs and notify responsible stakeholders in the event of unusual spending.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use an AWS Budgets template to create a zero spend budget.
choices.explanation: A zero-spend budget alerts on any spending, which is unsuitable for an existing application with legitimate recurring cost.

choices.solution: Create an AWS Cost Anomaly Detection monitor in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.
choices.explanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection is designed to identify unusual spend and send alerts to stakeholders. A zero-spend budget is for detecting any spend, not anomalies in an existing workload.

choices.solution: Create AWS Pricing Calculator estimates for the current running workload pricing details.
choices.explanation: Pricing Calculator estimates planned cost rather than detecting anomalous actual spending.

choices.solution: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor costs and to identify unusual spending.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch billing thresholds are not the usage-pattern anomaly model provided by Cost Anomaly Detection.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A company runs an SMB file server in its data center. The file server stores large files that the company frequently accesses for up to 7 days after the file creation date.

After 7 days, the company needs to be able to access the files with a maximum retrieval time of 24 hours.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

choices.solution: Use AWS DataSync to copy data that is older than 7 days from the SMB file server to AWS.
choices.explanation: Copying older files alone does not specify the storage class, ongoing SMB interface, or retrieval workflow needed to meet the requirement.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
choices.explanation:
S3 File Gateway preserves the SMB interface and caches recent files locally. An S3 Lifecycle rule can transition older objects to Deep Archive for low-cost retention.

Archived objects must be explicitly restored before the gateway can read them; use standard retrieval and an operational restore process consistent with the 24-hour window.

choices.solution: Create an Amazon FSx File Gateway to increase the company's storage space. Create an Amazon S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data after 7 days.
choices.explanation: FSx File Gateway uses FSx storage, so an S3 Lifecycle rule cannot transition its filesystem data.

choices.solution: Configure access to Amazon S3 for each user. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days.
choices.explanation: Direct S3 access changes the existing SMB workflow and requires per-user access configuration.

Design Cost-Optimized Architectures.question:
A solutions architect needs to copy files from an Amazon S3 bucket to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and another S3 bucket. The files must be copied continuously.

New files are added to the original S3 bucket consistently. The copied files should be overwritten only if the source file changes.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.solution:
Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system.

Set the transfer mode to transfer only data that has changed.
choices.explanation: AWS DataSync supports S3 and EFS locations and can transfer only changed data. That avoids custom Lambda/EC2 synchronization logic and prevents unchanged destination files from being overwritten.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS Lambda function. Mount the file system to the function.

Set up an S3 event notification to invoke the function when files are created and changed in Amazon S3. Configure the function to copy files to the file system and the destination S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Custom Lambda copying requires code, retries, EFS connectivity, and handling object sizes and function execution limits.

choices.solution:
Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system.

Set the transfer mode to transfer all data.
choices.explanation: Transferring all data adds unnecessary scanning and rewriting work when only changed files should be copied.

choices.solution:
Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in the same VPC as the file system. Mount the file system.

Create a script to routinely synchronize all objects that changed in the origin S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket and the mounted file system.
choices.explanation: An EC2 synchronization script requires server maintenance and custom scheduling and error handling.
